Crossing the bridge and merging with the city traffic, the streets alive for the weekend with people cramming into bars and restaurants and the early nightclub regulars already queuing. Lena felt the warmth of the evening wrap around her in a comforting blanket, so content that she would’ve let Kara drive for hours, take her anywhere she wanted to, her eyelids growing heavy.

     

                When they finally pulled up outside Lena’s apartment, the street was dark and the fragrant smell of the magnolias flooded in through the car windows as they sat in the dark interior. Lena’s dark hair curled in tangled knots around her face, hiding her from Kara as she stared straight ahead for a moment. 

     

                “Do you want to get dinner?” Kara blurted out. “We don’t have to go out , if you don’t want to; we could just … order in.”

     

                “I- yeah, sure. Ordering in sounds good!”

     

                Climbing out of the car, keeping her head ducked down, Lena grabbed the keys from the centre console and fished her phone out of her jacket pocket before she climbed the front steps and unlocked the door. The house was dark inside and she could feel Kara behind her, feel the itchiness of the red welts she knew peppered her cheeks and throat, her stomach aching slightly.

     

                Sighing as she stepped inside, Lena hesitated at the light switch. “Okay, I need you to not freak out for a second, okay?”

     

                “Is everything okay?” Kara cautiously asked.

     

                Turning on the lights as she replied, Lena turned, “yeah, I-”

     

                “Oh my God! What the hell happened to your face?”

     

                Opening and closing her mouth as she flushed, Lena gave her a helpless smile, spreading her hands in a sheepish manner. “So … I might be slightly allergic to peanuts.”

     

                “You what? Slightly? Lena, you’re … covered in hives!”

     

                “It’s fine,” Lena quickly assured her, reaching out to pull her inside and shut the door, “it just … makes me a little itchy. It’s not like I’m going to go into anaphylactic shock or anything.”

     

                Lena let out a weak chuckle, scratching at her cheek before she dropped her hand, her smile wilting. Kara was giving her an incredulous look that made Lena wince faintly, shifting uncomfortably from foot to foot.

     

                “You’re … allergic to peanuts and you … ate a peanut butter sandwich. What is wrong with you? Why would you do that? Oh my God, that’s so … stupid.”

     

                With an embarrassed smile on her face, Lena kicked her running shoes off on the mat and shrugged again, “you were really excited for me to try it so … I didn’t want to ruin your fun.”

     

                Groaning as she pinched the bridge of her nose and hung her head, Kara let out a sigh of laughter. Looking up, she shook her head and gave Lena an exasperated look of amusement. 

     

                “Was it even worth it?”

     

                Hesitating, Lena pursed her lips as her eyes narrowed. “Honestly … it was kind of disgusting.”

     

                “You ate all of it!”

     

                “I didn’t want to be rude,” Lena dismissively replied, reaching out for Kara’s hand, “now, come on, what do you want for dinner?”

     

                Sighing as she shook her head, Kara followed her upstairs, still astounded at Lena’s complete nonchalance, while they put ideas out there for food. Lena wasn’t particularly hungry, her stomachache putting a damper on their meal plans, but she wanted Kara to stay for dinner anyway, and as she showered, the bathroom door open as Kara lounged on the bench at the end of her bed, they decided on a nearby Jamaican restaurant that was a little more upscale than Kara’s usual takeout joints.

     

                Pink and soft from the shower, the welts of hives still livid on her pale skin, Lena curled up on the sofa as they shared curry goat, fried plantains and Escovitch fish, watching a movie that Kara had picked on the wide TV. Uncharacteristically tired, and irritable from her itchy skin, Lena had to fight back the urge to fall asleep there and then, the night still relatively early.

     

                Kara ended up leaving just after ten, assuring Lena that she’d be fine to catch a cab. She still looked annoyed by the rash on Lena’s skin as she shook her head and gave her a parting kiss, Lena’s lips still tingling as she faintly smiled into it.

     

                Back inside, Lena poured herself a cup of coffee and carried it up to her office, Kara’s Polaroid camera in hand from where she’d coaxed it from her. She was determined to fix it for her, and at her work table in her office, Lena disassembled it, neatly lining up each screw and piece from the inside before she looked up independent camera stores that would sell spare parts, making notes of the addresses. The plastic pieces were salvageable, and Lena didn’t think it would be too hard to replace the rest, even if she had to buy a secondhand one of the same model online and gut it for replacement parts. 

     

                Staying up until past midnight dithering around in her office, absentmindedly itching her welts as her stomach cramped and coffee buzzed in her veins, she finally crashed and plodded downstairs with an air of exhaustion about her, making a mental note to never eat peanuts again. No matter which pretty girl asked her to.

    Chapter 10

                Monday was Kara’s first day of work, and they had dinner afterwards at a Korean barbecue restaurant while she skirted around the topic of her job, but was quietly pleased about something. Lena was content to let her keep her thoughts to herself, as unusual as it was for Kara, and chalked it up to excitement for her first day back after her break. 

     

                It was a busy week for Lena, and it made it harder to fit in moments with Kara, who was also exhausted from her long days and the commute out to the base and back, but they still managed to find the time. After Korean barbecue, there was pizza late one night at Lena’s office, her eyes burning as she stayed glued to her computer screen, while Kara rewrote an article she was working on from the sofa. There had been a night spent curled up on Lena’s sofa, watching a movie as they ate ramen and mochi from a takeout Kara had swung by on her way home.

     

                It wasn’t until the weekend that they really had much time, Lena’s Saturday morning taken up by an important meeting with an overseas associate, before her afternoon and Sunday was freed up. Sunday afternoon, they walked along the bay wall, eating gelato as the sun left dappled shadows on the sidewalk as it filtered through the overhanging trees, their leaves so deeply green that they looked blue.

     

                Lena was grateful for the chance to get outside and stretch her legs, breathing in the briny air as children screamed and laughed on the playground, dogs barked and chased after tennis balls or begged for attention from them - she loved to watch Kara sink to her knees to ruffle their fur under their chins as their tongue lolled - and seagulls wheeled about, their keening cry oddly comforting. It was a warm day and they walked and walked, occasionally holding hands, pointing out things of interest to each other and just enjoying the pleasure of company. They didn’t even have to talk; Lena just enjoyed being beside her.

     

                Kara didn’t stay for dinner that night, grimly explaining to Lena that Nia and Querl were moving into their own apartment together and she’d offered to help, and Lena assured her that it was fine with an odd sense of amusement. No one had ever worried that she might be offended at being left alone; Lena didn’t know any different. Perhaps a part of her even craved the loneliness, until Kara came along, but she would survive a night on her own. Besides, she already had plans.

     

                She’d ordered four separate broken Polaroid cameras online while at work, and at the long table in her attic, she sat at the stool, surrounded by the disassembled pieces of cameras. There was an open tutorial on the laptop screen before her and Lena stared at it intently while she sipped her Aperol Spritz and followed the steps to reassemble it. 

     

                The evening was warm, the sky a gentle violet through the open windows as a sweet breeze brought in the faintly spicy smell of magnolia and heated tarmac. She had a record on downstairs that just managed to reach her on the fourth floor, and she was happy to sit there all afternoon as the hours dragged on, determined to get the camera working again.

     

                Her paperwork was piled on her desk, forgotten about as the camera occupied her attention, and Lena picked at a light dinner of figs and soft cheeses as she worked, letting her mind wander as her capable hands moved of their own accord. It was slow work, and satisfying as each fiddly piece was slotted into place, and the sun hadn’t even fully set by the time Lena had a fully assembled camera before her.

     

                Pointing the lens of the camera towards herself, Lena smiled, her eyes crinkling as she cocked her head to the side slightly and snapped a photo to see if it was working. Her stomach soared with triumph as she let out a quiet laugh, black spots momentarily blinding her from the flash before the camera chugged out a square film. Setting the camera down safely, Lena held the square in her hands, beneath the desk where it was darker, and waited for the photo to reveal itself. She brought it back out to find her smiling face staring back at her and was filled with smug satisfaction.

     

                Tidying up the detritus of the other cameras, Lena tucked the pieces safely into a little box in case of another emergency one day, surprising herself by the advanced planning of a day where she clearly envisioned herself and Kara still being … was friends still an appropriate word? She then wiped the camera over, removing any lingering scuff marks before she set it down safely on the table and smiled in anticipation of giving it to Kara again.

     

                She didn’t see her until Tuesday after work, Lena hurrying to that small Chinese restaurant that was Kara’s favourite, hoping to beat her home with the surprise. On her drive home, the food on the passenger seat, Lena found herself smiling slightly, and perhaps even more surprising was because of the simple act of buying something she knew Kara liked. She had never imagined it would be so satisfying to buy dinner for someone, and it made her feel good to do it, a sign that she was paying attention, that she cared enough to take note of what Kara did and didn’t like.

     

                Humming to herself as she laid the table at home, changed into something a little more casual, the mid-March weather confusing as it lingered in the overcast chill of winter and the muggy heat of summer. Lena was quickly realising that it was always vaguely warm in National City, even as north as it was. The air was always somewhat dense, a muggy feeling that she imagined might be suffocating in summer, but was welcome in early spring, after so many years of the bitter Metropolis winters. 

     

                She was just opening two beers - the kind that Kara liked to drink, although Lena thought it was a bit sour - when there was a knock on the door. Smiling, she put the bottle opener down on the counter and crossed the kitchen to step out into the hallway, pulling open the door to reveal Kara, still dressed in her fatigues, looking a little frazzled.

     

                “Hi! Sorry, I didn’t have time to change,” Kara wearily greeted her, giving her a quick peck, which still managed to surprise Lena, before she stepped inside. “I got held up at work and then I had to stop off- I got Chinese food for dinner.”

     

                Lifting the plastic bag, Kara kicked her heavy boots off inside the door and Lena let out a choked laugh. “I also got Chinese food for dinner.”

     

                Eyebrows rising a fraction, Kara’s face split with a smile as she laughed, “well … I guess we won’t be going hungry.”

     

                Giving her an appraising look in her uniform, Lena wasn’t quite sure what to make of it. Kara wore it well, perfectly at ease in the uniform she’d worn nearly every day for seven years, but the sight of it was like a reality shock for Lena. Kara’s work seemed so distant to their moments spent together, some intangible thing that was mentioned in passing but held no importance in their relationship. To see her wearing her uniform was a stomach-lurching reminder that she could be gone at any moment, whisked away overseas to the middle of a warzone. 

     

                Smile faltering as her eyes clouded with unease, Lena turned around and made for the stairs, “hang on a second, I’ll be right back. Beers are in the kitchen and the food is on the dining table.”

     

                Taking the steps two at a time, she bounded up to the fourth floor to fetch the camera, the knot of unease releasing slightly, and she hid it behind her back as she reached the ground floor again, a mischievous smile on her face as she rounded the archway to the dining room. Kara was sitting at what had become her seat, shifting the containers she wanted closer to her plate, and she looked up as Lena lingered in the doorway.

     

                “I have something for you.”

     

                Holding the camera up, Lena smiled at the look of utter joy that illuminated Kara’s face. She swiftly rose from the table as her mouth fell open, rounding the end to stop before Lena, reaching for the camera with tender surprise in her blue eyes.

     

                “You- you fixed it?”

     

                “I did. Now, give me a salute.”

     

                Kara chuckled at the order, lazily snapping to attention as she smiled, trying not to laugh as Lena took her photo. She clung to Lena’s arm as the camera started printing, a palpable air of excitement surrounding her that made Lena’s stomach knot itself with nervous delight, and they both stared at the photo as it developed.

     

                Looking up at Lena, Kara’s eyes creased at the corners and she reached up to cup her face in her rough palms. “You,” she murmured, “are a wonder.”

     

                And then Kara kissed her as surprise flashed across Lena’s face at the compliment. It was such a silly thing, a fleeting moment of joy that had brought forth kind words, and Lena already knew she was a wonder - of course she did, everyone knew it - but no one ever told her that. It was an unspoken truth but to hear it said made her heart twinge slightly with gratitude, and she closed her wide eyes and melted into the kiss for a fleeting moment before Kara pulled back.

     

                “Thank you,” Kara whispered, her fingertips softly grazing Lena’s cheek, “you don’t know how much this means to me.”

     

                “I do,” Lena murmured, wanting her to know that she didn’t take the sentimental value of it for granted, that she knew why something as small as a camera meant so much to Kara.

     

                A smile twitched at the corner of Kara’s mouth and she nodded, taking the camera from Lena and turning it over in her hands and Lena stepped away, giving her a moment. And she was glad that she could give it to Kara, that she’d grazed her knees and skinned her palms climbing up and down the rocks, that her eyes had been sore and bloodshot from the gritty water as she’d stirred up dirt, the dank taste filling her mouth, trying to find the camera. She would’ve done it again in a heartbeat, just for this moment.

     

                “Come and sit,” Lena gently ordered her after a moment, “tell me about your day.”

     

                Kara looked up and smiled at her before reclaiming her seat and setting the camera down nearby, reaching for a container and opening it to a waft of steam and spices. “It was good! Not really anything exciting.”

     

                As she scooped food onto her plate, Lena arched an eyebrow as she smiled slightly. “What, is it confidential?”

     

                Shrugging indifferently, Kara opened a container of noodles. “I mean … kind of . We’re not supposed to talk about things that aren’t published yet. Especially when … well, we need permission from a Public Affairs Officer and PSYOPS to clear it for release.”

     

                “Oh. Is it like … a propaganda thing?”

     

                With a scoff of laughter, Kara shook her head as she smiled at her plate, “is that what you think I do? Write military propaganda?”

     

                Softly sighing, Lena spread her hands helplessly, “I don’t know, Kara. I don’t know much about how the military works internally or what exactly you do . But it’s the military, right?”

     

                “I know you don’t exactly like the idea of it, but … no, we’re not allowed to spread propaganda. We have as much journalism integrity as the others and it’s against the Department of Defence’s public affairs programs for us to … you know, influence opinions, misinform the public to benefit the military.”

     

                “So … you just tell it as it is?”

     

                “Essentially.”

     

    Clearing her throat, Lena gave Kara a wry smile as she reached for her beer, “well, I can see this is … a sore topic, so …”

     

                Sighing, Kara pinched the bridge of her nose, “sorry, I just- I get this shit from my family all the time. They don’t understand why I …”

     

                “To be honest, Kara, I don’t understand it either. What would possess someone to go over there, to a war zone of their own creation, to- to sit around in the sand waiting for someone to tell them what to do.”

     

                “Money, mostly,” Kara murmured, the tips of her ears reddening as she speared a dumpling on her fork.

     

                Lena had nothing to say to that, sitting in her million-dollar house, bank accounts filled with more money than she could use as she pretended that she had to run her company, when she never had to work a day in her life. Shifting uneasily, she took a sip of beer, grimacing as she set it back down.

     

                “Does it bother you?” Kara asked after a long moment. “What I do.”

     

                Mouth thinning, Lena’s expression softened with an aching look in her eyes, “I’d be lying if I said it didn’t, but … I think it bothers you too. I can’t picture you over there.”

     

                “I’m lucky I’m a journalist.”

     

                “It’s still dangerous.”

     

                “It could be worse.”

     

                “At least you’ll probably never have to go back.”

     

                Kara gave her an uneven smile as she met her eyes, “yeah, maybe. If I do … at least it won’t be for a while.”

     

                Lena’s mouth twitched and some unreadable expression crossed her face, noticed by Kara, who reached out to touch the back of her hand. “It upsets you.”

     

                Rolling her eyes as she tried to feign nonchalance, Lena scooped up a forkful of garlic vegetables off her plate and gave Kara a thin smile. “It’s fine. I mean can I really be upset about your job requirements when we’ve only known each other for … what? Two months?””

     

                “Don’t do that,” Kara murmured as she frowned.

     

                “Do what?”

     

                “Don’t brush me off; you’re allowed to be upset about it.”

     

                Lena didn’t look at her as she replied just a little too fast, her voice light and high-pitched. “I’m not upset.”

     

                “It’ll be months, at least. We could have … five, six months.”

     

                A rueful smile curled Lena’s lips as sadness welled in her green eyes. Six months. It seemed like a long time to them, then and there, but in the grand scheme of things, it was no time at all. Their time together could be even shorter, another month if they desperately needed Kara out there somewhere, and Lena didn’t find any comfort in the fact that even at the end of her active duty contract, they could send her anyway. Nothing was certain and she didn’t like that, not knowing. 

     

                And what would happen if they did deploy Kara again? Against all signs that she was done, that she would probably spend the rest of her service time in an office at the nearby base, until her twenty-sixth birthday came and went and the date of her enlistment passed by, they could deploy her at the drop of a hat. She could be sent back to Afghanistan, or maybe Iraq again. There was no saying how long for, and Lena would go back to her loneliness, perhaps talking to Kara every now and then, when one of them had the time, this brief fling reduced to nothing.

     

                “We don’t- we don’t have to do this, you know,” Kara whispered as they ate in tense silence, her shoulders taut as she spoke to her plate.

     

                Her voice was strained, as if it pained her to speak the words, and Lena looked up at her quickly, her eyebrows furrowing together as her jaw tightened. The meaning behind Kara’s words were plain, but she could tell how reluctant Kara was to say them, but understood why. Why it would be easier for them to let go of the tenuous relationship they were slowly figuring out, caught somewhere between casual and serious, neither one of them taking the risk to make a commitment.

     

                “You’re mad,” Kara stated.

     

                With a snort of laughter, Lena sucked on the inside of her cheek and shook her head, a bright, wounded look in her eyes, even as amusement softened the sharpness of her features. “Well … yeah.”

     

                “I just- I don’t want you to feel pressured …”

     

                Letting out a frustrated sigh, Lena rolled her eyes, “Kara … I have never let anyone pressure me into anything . I’m too stubborn for that. I get it, I’m not the best at relationships or … whatever, and there’s a lot you don’t know about my life that’s just … so fucked up, but I’m trying to make it work, the way I know how. I’ve never wanted to try and make something work before, but I am . I like you.”

     

                Kara opened and closed her mouth a few times before she climbed to her feet and sank into a crouch before Lena’s chair, a tender look in her mournful eyes as her lips curled into a smile. Taking Lena’s face in her hands, she stroked her cheek and fixed her with a stern look.

     

                “I didn’t mean it like that. That’s not- I know you’re trying to make it work but … all I’m saying is that- if you don’t want things to go past this … I get it. I wouldn’t hold that against you. But I take it seriously, okay? So if you do want it to work, even with … my job and everything, then I’m all in. Is- is that alright with you?”

     

                Lena let out a breathless laugh, leaning forward to press her forehead to Kara’s as she closed her eyes, the tension bleeding out of her as she swallowed thickly. Nodding, she let out a faint sigh. “Yeah, that’s alright with me.”

     

                “Good.”

     

                Pulling back, Lena gave her a ghost of a smile and tucked a strand of hair behind her ear, fixing her with a piercing stare before tugging on the arm of Kara’s shirt. “Eat your dinner before it gets cold.”

     

                With a shuddering laugh, Kara climbed back to her feet and sat back down on her chair, picking up her fork as she glanced sideways at Lena. Hesitating, she gave her a crooked smile.

     

                “So … we’re okay?”

     

                “Yeah, we’re okay.”

     

                Nodding, satisfied with the vague admission that they were both on board for seeing this through, to whatever end, Kara dug into her food with enthusiasm. Lena felt a sense of relief and wonder inside her, some knot loosening with the knowledge that they were on the same page. A part of her had been worried that she was getting too attached to Kara, filling the emptiness inside her with the only person she had, and that Kara was more indifferent about it, her state of kindness and easy friendship extended to everyone in equal measures. It was no small relief to Lena to know that Kara intended to stay, to know that she didn’t view it as something casual and fleeting.

     

                Lena didn’t want to rush into anything by any means, but the uneasiness that she’d felt at Kara’s potential deployment, at the uncertainty of their time together, was quietened for the time being. Even if she did go again, perhaps she would still be able to have her in some capacity, as far apart as they would be. They wouldn’t have to give it up entirely.

     

                Dinner was more relaxed after that, the air cleared between them and the conversation less strained, and afterwards, they watched episodes of TV shows Kara had fallen behind on - only the ones she hadn’t promised to watch with Alex though - while Kara curled up in borrowed clothes, her head in Lena’s lap. She spent more time tracing absentminded circles on the bare skin of Kara’s arm than focusing on what they were watching, but Lena enjoyed it anyway. It felt normal . Like they were a proper couple and they did that every night.

     

                But as the night dragged on, Kara had to go, her uniform bundled up under her arm as she carried the plastic bag of takeout that Lena had insisted she take home for Alex - but only after Kara had demanded she take a couple to make sure she had a proper meal to eat - and a yellow cab idled on the curbside. Lena kissed her goodnight and Kara thanked her again for fixing her camera, and as she shut the door behind her, Lena wondered what it would be like if they were a proper couple.

    Chapter 11

                Friday morning, Lena was coming out of a strategy meeting, after spending an hour pushing her new long-term plan of action to promote L-Corp’s ethically oriented approach to cleaner energy practices in manufacturing. The relevant department heads were all there, new plans to boost social media presence and environmental initiatives, as well as a decision for a press conference on Lena’s behalf to implement the company’s vision, and she was feeling rather pleased with herself as she swept out of the office.

     

                Jess greeted her outside of the conference room with a pressed juice and a tablet, “how did it go?”

     

                “Perfectly,” Lena lightly replied, a smile twitching her lips. “Remind me to speak with Sam on Monday about the budgeting for the new social media campaign; I don’t have time today. Where am I needed next?”

     

                “Conference room three on the Operations and Supply Chain floor. I left you a ten minute window to freshen up. There was also a phone call for you on your private cell.”

     

                “Did you take a message?”

     

                “It was Kara Danvers. She said she’d call back at lunch.”

     

                Lena glanced sideways at Jess, trying to maintain her aloofness as she held out her hand, “I’ll just call her back now.”

     

                “Of course.”

     

                Taking her cell phone, Lena stopped in the wide hallway and gave her assistant a smile, “thanks, Jess.”

     

                Nodding, Jess strode towards the elevators and pushed the button as the flow of employees dispersed back to their own floors. Opening the door to an empty room, Lena dialled Kara’s number and took a sip of her juice as it rang.

     

                “Hi! Sorry, I didn’t realise you were in a meeting. Your assistant seems nice!”

     

                “Hi, it’s fine,” Lena said with a smile, “and she is. I wouldn’t survive without her, but don’t tell her that.”

     

                “You should tell her that,” Kara chided her.

     

                Rolling her eyes as she bit back a smile, chewing on the paper straw, Lena shook her head, eyeing the sprawling city through the full-length windows taking up the complete back wall. “Okay, okay. What did you call for?”

     

                “Dinner. Tonight. Alex really wants to meet you and I’ve held her back for as long as I could, but after the other night, I thought that … well, maybe it’s not such a bad idea. If you want to. Of course you don’t have to, but I’m already going out for drinks with her and Kelly after work tonight so I thought … maybe you’d want to come too.”

     

                “Dinner? With your sister?” Lena echoed, her stomach flipping with nerves as her mouth went dry.

     

                “Yeah. Just the four of us. It’ll be public so you can always make an excuse and bail if you want.”

     

                Kara laughed but Lena didn’t take it as a joke, she might actually need an escape route. She was no good with people, but especially not the adored sister of someone she actually liked. It sounded like her worst nightmare, but she knew that it would mean a lot to Kara, could sense it in the anxious tone of her voice as she worried that Lena would say no. And if it was important to her, it was important to Lena.

     

                “Dinner sounds great. If you haven’t settled on a place yet, I can get my assistant to book something. We can meet there.”

     

                “Okay, but nowhere too fancy.”

     

                Shaking her head slightly as her eyes closed, Lena softly sighed, “okay, fine. I’ll text you the details. Do you want me to get my driver to pick us all up?”

     

                “We’ll be fine. I’ll talk to you later. Bye!”

     

                The call ended after that and Lena’s brow puckered as she sucked on her straw, exiting the room to find Jess waiting at the elevator, the hallway now empty, leaving them to climb into the next one that arrived. Rubbing at a tender spot above her left eyebrow, Lena pursed her lips.

     

                “Jess? Would you mind looking for a restaurant for dinner tonight? Table for four. Nothing too upscale, but a little nicer than casual dining. Maybe a bistro or a nice bar.”

     

                “Any preference for food?”

     

                Contemplating, Lena’s mouth thinned, “nothing specific. Could you also fetch me something a little more casual from home. But not too casual.”

     

                “Right. How about those plaid grey slacks with the cream cuban shirt you had for that office weekend retreat last April?”

     

                “Perfect. With the black mules.”

     

                “Of course, Miss Luthor.”

     

                Pushing the button for the tenth floor, Lena bit her lip and looked at Jess as the doors slid shut. “Thank you, Jess. I don’t know how I’d survive without you.”

     

                She watched surprise flash across her assistant’s face and turned to face the closed doors as the elevator started moving. Lena bit back a smile at Jess’ quiet thanks and she turned her attention back to the upcoming meeting.

     

                The rest of her day passed by quickly, Jess making a reservation at a Mexican restaurant a few blocks away, Lena’s afternoon meetings wrapping up quickly with seeming progress as departments set forth their plans while she listened and occasionally chimed in with her thoughts, the palpable air of unease from the lower level employees oddly amusing to her. 

     

                Knocking off a little early, Lena changed in the private bathroom outside her office, spraying herself with perfume and reapplying her lipstick before fussing over her appearance in the mirror. Finding herself nervous, and nitpicking as a result of that stomach-churning feeling, Lena lingered for a few minutes longer before exhaling roughly and shaking her head.

     

                Pulling her wool coat over her outfit, an unnecessary layer given the mild weather, Lena grabbed her bag and told Jess to leave early before breezing past her.

     

                She left her car at the office and walked the few blocks, still early for the time she’d given Kara, enjoying the last of the sunlight as broad strokes of tangerine painted the sky between the mirrored skyscrapers.

     

                The Mexican restaurant was a narrow space, dimly lit with marimba music spilling out onto the street as Lena opened the door. The walls were mustard yellow, turned amber in the glow of lights and the floor was Saltillo terracotta tiles, a variety of tequila, from top to bottom shelf stuff, lining the walls behind the length of wood, painted and stained a rich green.

     

                Giving her name at the door, Lena handed over her coat and opted to sit at the bar while she waited, ordering a Paloma cocktail, the pinch of salt cutting through the sweetness of the grapefruit as she smoothed her clammy palms over the thighs of her pants. She wished she’d had more time to prepare herself for meeting Kara’s sister, the unease eating away at her as she felt her heart flutter in her chest like a caged bird, so fragile and frantic.

     

                “Hey!”

     

                At the sound of Kara’s quiet, yet delighted voice, Lena turned on the stool and felt a nervous smile break out across her face, some of the tension fading. It was Kara , she was comfort and kindness, and if her sister was half as friendly as her, Lena had nothing to worry about.

     

                “Hi,” Lena murmured, somewhat shy as her eyes quickly darted behind Kara as she leaned into the kiss heading her way.

     

                With a quick laugh, her arms closing around Lena, Kara’s breath tickled her ear, her voice full of surprised amusement as she replied. “You’re nervous.”

     

                Giving her a wan smile, Lena shrugged, “a little.”

     

                Nose wrinkling, Kara grabbed her hand and gently tugged her, not caring that it was clammy and cold as she squeezed comfortingly. Filing back towards the door where a couple were handing in their coats, Lena swallowed thickly as she watched their attention land on her.

     

                Kara dropped her hand and gestured to Lena before pressing her hand against her lower back, and Lena paled slightly. She could face down a room of investors, the whole board and give a speech to a crowd, but she was overcome with a sudden bout of shyness in the presence of Kara’s sister. And Lena knew that stemmed entirely from her fear that Alex would think she wasn’t good enough. If there was one thing Lena was insecure about, it was that, the leftover remnants of her childhood where she’d always tried so hard, but had fallen short in every way.

     

                “This is Lena,” Kara beamed, before waving to the two women, “and this is Alex, and Kelly.”

     

                Surreptitiously wiping her palm on her pants Lena reached out, a tentative smile on her lips as she shook Alex’s hand and then Kelly’s. The latter put her at ease, although it wasn’t as if Alex was being rude, but there was the need to impress Kara’s sister that made Lena feel like she was wilting beneath her scrutinising stare.

     

                “It’s nice to meet you both,” Lena honestly said, because it was, even if she was wracked by nerves.

     

                “Likewise,” Alex said over the din of conversation and music, a smile reaching her brown eyes. “Shall we sit?”

     

                Leading them to the table reserved for them, Lena found herself against the wall with Kara beside her, a solidly reassuring presence, and she dropped her shoulders and raised her chin slightly at the touch of Kara’s hand on her knee.

     

                “You look beautiful by the way,” Kara murmured, a pleased look on her face as she smiled at Lena.

     

                “You too.”

     

                “This place is nice,” Kelly noted as she looked around, “what’s the food like?”

     

                She directed the question at Lena, who hesitated before giving her a sheepish smile. “I’ve never been before. My, uh, my … assistant booked it, so I don’t know.”

     

                Lena could feel herself flush at the admission and shifted in her seat, while Kara squeezed her knee again.

     

                “Well, the menu looks good!” she enthusiastically commented, nodding as she read the menu. “Shall we order drinks first?”

     

                Ordering a strawberry margarita for herself, Lena winced when she was asked for ID, fishing it out of her purse and handing it over as she pressed her lips into a flat line of dismay. She caught Alex biting back a smile and couldn’t help but let out a breathless scoff of laughter, rolling her eyes as she relaxed.

     

                “They’ll let me run a business but I still can’t buy alcohol unquestioned,” Lena sighed.

     

                “How old are you anyway?”

     

                “Twenty-four.”

     

                Letting out a low whistle as she perused the menu, Alex’s eyebrows rose. “You must be pretty smart to be managing such a big company. And pretty serious.”

     

                “I’m a bit of a workaholic.”

     

                “How do you manage to fit a girlfriend into that?”

     

                Kara muffled a cough and leant forward, “oh, we, uh, we’re not-“

     

                Covering Kara’s hand with her own, soothing her flustered panic at the seriousness of the label slapped onto their relationship, Lena smiled slightly. 

     

                “Honestly, I work too much, so it’s been good, actually.”

     

                “So, tell me about yourself.”

     

                The waitress returned with a tray holding their drinks and Lena took a sip, salt crystals bitter on her lips as she scrambled for something to say. Anything of note.

     

                “Geez, Alex, it’s not a job interview,” Kara muttered with vague embarrassment as she nudged her glasses up her nose.

     

                “It’s okay,” Lena lightly assured her with a quick smile. “There’s not really much to tell anyway.”

     

                Pressing her lips into a flat line as she thought, a furrow between her eyebrows, Lena shrugged. 

     

                “I run my family’s company; I guess you both already know about … all of that. I, uh, I moved to National City a few months ago for a fresh start. I studied bioengineering and computer science at MIT. I have two PhD’s, and I graduated a few years early.”

     

                “Two PhD’s?” Kelly echoed, a look of astonishment on her face. “Jesus. I knew you were smart but …”

     

                Shrugging, Lena gave her a reserved smile, “my family was big on education. Boarding school, aptitude testing and extracurricular classes and all of that.”

     

                “She used to fence,” Kara gushed, “and was a national chess champion. And a rebellious cellist.”

     

                Fighting back a flush at the praise, Lena took another sip of her drink to mask her discomfort. Her achievements had never been something to be praised before, only expected, and she found the attention a little daunting.

     

                “What about you two?” Lena asked, raising her eyebrows in polite curiosity, “I heard you’re a pharmacist and a psychologist.”

     

                The attention was momentarily shifted from her and the conversation flowed naturally, back and forth with surprising ease, Lena warming up to them by the second round of drinks (her third) and as plates of food filled the table, Lena forgot what she was so worried about.

     

                She was hoping she wasn’t deluded into thinking that Alex liked her, as much as she could like someone she barely knew, and as she took a bite of her chicken enchilada, Alex’s eyes lit up with glee.

     

                “How’s the food? Lena?”

     

                “It’s good,” she hummed appreciatively.

     

                “The chicken’s cooked properly?”

     

                Feeling a slow flush spread up her neck and turning her face red, Lena let out a snort of laughter, while Kara choked on her mouthful and had to force it down, letting out a wheezing cough.

     

                “Alex!”

     

                “What? It’s a genuine question.”

     

                Covering her mouth as she smiled, Lena arched an eyebrow at Kara in a playful look of accusation. “You told her?”

     

                Wincing, Kara gave her an innocent look, blue eyes wide and childlike as she smiled widely. Lena laughed again and gave Alex an exasperated look, shaking her head. 

     

                “We also heard about the peanut butter as well,” Alex said, trying to hold back her laughter as Kelly nudged her, lips pressed together as she ducked her head. “Kelly’s allergic to blueberries. Do you know what she did when I put them in her pancakes? She didn’t eat them.”

     

                “Mm, maybe I’ll consider that next time,” Lena hummed, smiling as she reached for her drink.

     

                She was teased mercilessly over dinner, but Lena was surprised to find that she didn’t mind it. It wasn’t malicious, it was usually self-deprecating too, and it actually helped her relax and enjoy herself, finding that she could give it as well as she could take. Above all, Lena appreciated the fact that it seemed like Alex’s way of slowly embracing her for Kara’s sake, and took a liking to her and Kelly the longer that dinner progressed.

     

                Once they’d cleared their plates and dessert was on its way, Kara excused herself to go to the restroom, her eyes anxiously on Lena’s face as she judged whether she was okay to be left alone, and Lena quickly reassured her as Kelly slipped out of the booth to go with her. She didn’t know whether it was a calculated move, but she knew what came next from the way Alex straightened in her seat, the sharp suspicion in her brown eyes as she ran a hand through her long hair on top. 

     

                Neither of them spoke for a moment as Lena touched a fingertip to her sweating glass, eyes glued to the pale pink drink, before she glanced up at the subtle shift in Alex’s posture. Quietly clearing her throat, Alex gave her a curious stare and propped her elbows on the table.

     

                “So … you like her?”

     

                A crooked smile of embarrassment crossed Lena’s face as she looked down at her drink and slumped in her seat, finding herself in unfamiliar - although expected - waters. In a way, she knew Alex had been holding out for this moment all night, to ask Lena some questions without Kara’s presence nervously fluttering around to stop her the moment she got a little too close to pushing.

     

                “Yeah, I really do,” Lena quietly replied, exhaling slowly as her shoulders dropped.

     

                Hesitating, a slow smile spread across Lena’s face and she looked up at Alex with a wry look, her green eyes flashing. “Is this the part where you tell me I’m not good enough for her?”

     

                She tried not to sound too bitter, amused by the prospect, but it was still there, an edge to her words as Alex slowly sat back, surprise flashing across her face. “No. I don’t even know you. Even then, Kara’s a grown adult; she can make her own decisions.”

     

                “Oh.”

     

                With a snort of laughter, Alex gave her a bewildered look, “what? Were you expecting the Spanish Inquisition?”

     

                Shrugging half-heartedly, Lena sheepishly smiled, “I wouldn’t have been surprised.”

     

                “Listen, all I want for her is for her to be happy. If that’s you … I’m sure there’ll be time for us to get to know each other better. But … for what it’s worth, you’re not bad - for a billionaire.”

     

                Closing her eyes as she wrinkled her nose, letting out a quiet groan, Lena shook her head and then laughed. Alex chuckled too and took a sip of her beer, her expression softening slightly as she tipped her head to the side. She was only four years older than Lena, but she felt so much more composed, at ease with herself, and Lena found it intimidating. Yet it was oddly reassuring at that moment, to see Alex seem so blasé at her presence.

     

                “I actually looked you up online, you know. I hope that’s okay.”

     

                Opening and closing her mouth, Lena didn’t have time to mention that it didn’t matter what she thought because it was already too late, and she was silent as Alex continued.

     

                “Your brother was a lot older than you.”

     

                “Mm.”

     

                “You don’t have any other siblings?”

     

                “Nope. No family.”

     

                “Just your mom then?”

     

                Sighing softly, Lena’s cheek dimpled as she grimaced, “we’re … estranged . I see her maybe … five, six times a year at board meetings and galas. Otherwise we don’t talk.”

     

                She didn’t mention that Lillian had been calling her a lot lately, all of the phone calls ignored and sent straight to voicemail, which then went ignored. It didn’t matter that Lena changed her number every couple of months; her mother still got ahold of it again, and Lena still refused to pick up the calls.

     

                “Well … that sucks.”

     

                “Not really,” Lena scoffed, “my mom’s kind of a bitch.”

     

                “I guess the holidays will be spent with us then; that makes it easier.”

     

                Lena’s stomach lurched at the presumption that she’d be around long enough for that, that they’d all be together, with Kara, and it was daunting yet heartwarming. She smiled slightly, dipping her head in silent agreement, wondering what it would be like to go home somewhere for the holidays, to make gingerbread and eat turkey and celebrate the new year with people. It was far off, but the idea was disquieting as much as it was comforting, something that Lena craved but had no certainty of.

     

                “You’re worried,” Alex noted, “I can tell.”

     

                With a pained smile, Lena shrugged, brushing her hair out of her face. “I’ve … never been with someone long enough to ever consider the holidays. I just- I think I’d like to, but … I’ve never been good at … this whole thing. Never made it to meeting anyone’s family before either, actually.”

     

                Expression softening, Alex gave her a gentle smile, “Lena, she is … the last person who would ever hurt someone. You’re a smart girl, and I know that … if you don’t have anyone, you probably look out for yourself first, and that’s fine, but … please don’t break her heart.”

     

                “I- what? I wouldn’t-“

     

                “She’s too naïve. I love her, God, I love her but she’s too sweet, even after everything she’s been through, and she trusts people too easily. It’s not a bad thing, but I worry about her. You don’t know what she was like as a kid, when she was adopted; she’s changed a lot since then. But with this whole army thing … she doesn’t have many friends outside of it, much of a life with the- the deployments and the little time she’s home. Since she’s met you, she’s been different though. I don’t know what it is, but something’s shifted, and she’s always been an optimist but she’s been happier lately, in a different way.”

     

                Cutting off, Alex sighed heavily and gave her a pleading look as she leant forward, hands on the table as if she was going to seize Lena’s hands and beg her.

     

                “I just- I guess what I wanted to tell you was … please don’t break her heart, okay?”

     

                Blinking in surprise, Lena’s mouth fell open as her eyebrows rose, and she found herself speechless for a moment. 

     

                “Oh … this isn’t how I thought this conversation was going to go. Um … I just- I’m not. I’m not going to break her heart. I could live a thousand lifetimes and not deserve her, so … I don’t plan on screwing that up.”

     

                Giving her a perplexed look, Alex opened her mouth to reply when the waitress showed up with their dessert. Lena left her sopaipillas untouched as she looked at Alex with an anxious look on her face, biting her bottom lip as she waited for her reply.

     

                “I don’t know what you think you’ve done to not be deserving of her, and that’s your business, but … for what it’s worth, I think you’re good for her.”

     

                They didn’t have time to continue the conversation as Kara and Kelly reappeared a minute later, apologetic for taking so long because Kelly couldn’t find her lipstick to reapply. Lena had the sneaking suspicion that she’d waylaid Kara in the restroom to give Alex the time to say her piece.

     

                All through dessert Lena was more subdued, preoccupied with her thoughts as she mulled it all over. Alex’s words confused her, and there was the strangled feeling in her chest at the fact that she thought Lena was good enough. She barely knew her but had already given her approval, purely based on the fact that Kara was happy. Lena wished it had been that simple for her growing up, that happiness was the benchmark of whether someone was good enough. 

     

                It weighed heavily on her mind as she ate her food and finished her drink, and then paid the bill as it was set down on the table. The protests that they would split it fell on deaf ears and Lena didn’t want to pretend like it wasn’t pocket change - less than pocket change to her - and whether it was the distant look of preoccupation in her eyes, or the reluctant realisation that Lena didn’t even have to check the bill to know that it wouldn’t be an issue of whether she could afford it.

     

                Slipping out of the booth, they all gathered their coats at the door and stepped outside. Lena’s driver was waiting and she winced at how pompous it was going to sound as she turned to the trio.

     

                “Do you need a ride home?”

     

                “We can do a ride share,” Kelly said, her phone in hand as she opened an app.

     

                “I have a car.”

     

                “Don’t tell me you’re going to drive home,” Kelly exclaimed, shock colouring her words as she looked at Lena with incredulity.

     

                Closing her eyes as she wrinkled her nose, Lena sighed. “It’s … my personal driver.”

     

                There was a moment of silence before both women let out snorts of laughter, and then again when they realised Lena was serious.

     

                “You have a driver?” Alex sceptically asked.

     

                “He’s … right there,” Lena said, jerking her thumb towards the nondescript black car waiting for her.

     

                “Alright then.”

     

                The four of them piled into the back of it and buckled in, and Lena felt embarrassed as the car jerked into motion and Alex and Kelly looked around with interest.

     

                “Was he outside that whole time?” Alex asked.

     

                “No. He doesn’t just … wait around for me. I mean, he would if I asked him too. I usually drive myself around though, unless I’m drinking.”

     

                “So … you just have him on standby?”

     

                Grimacing, Lena shrugged noncommittally, “basically.”

     

                “God, I would kill to be rich.”

     

                “If you wind up dead, we’ll know who to blame,” Kelly said, leaning over to whisper to Lena.

     

                The car ride was quick and full of chatter and laughter and Lena was tired in a satisfied way, the tequila warming her stomach and her eyes leaden and the feeling of contentment at the night having gone well leaving her more affable than usual.

     

                Pulling up outside Kara’s building, they all tumbled out and Lena was surprised at the hugs she was given, the ease at which the affection was given and the gratitude for the night out and how good it was to finally meet her. They’d already made slapdash plans for dinner or drinks another time, and Lena found that she didn’t dread the idea.

     

                Walking into the lobby of the building after saying goodnight, Alex and Kelly tactfully gave her a moment alone with Kara, but not before Lena caught the sly smiles of satisfaction on their faces. Kara must’ve noticed too because she shook her head and sighed softly as she turned her attention to Lena.

     

                “I had a really good time,” Lena whispered, smiling at her, “thank you for inviting me.”

     

                Eyebrows rising in surprise, Kara rubbed her upper arms and gave her a scrutinising look, “yeah? It was okay?”

     

                “Mhm, they’re both lovely. It was nice meeting them.”

     

                “I’m glad you came,” Kara said, her shoulders dropping slightly as she seemed to perk up at Lena’s admission that she’d had fun. And then she hesitated, her nose wrinkling with a pained look as she grimaced. “And listen, I’m not stupid, I know Alex got you alone to talk to you so … whatever she said, you can just ignore it, okay?”

     

                Lena let out a shuddering laugh at the anxious look in Kara’s eyes and reached up to lace her fingers behind her neck. “We had … a good talk. I’ll keep it to myself, but I like her. I can see why she’s so important to you.”

     

                Her relief was palpable and Lena’s smile grew before she leaned in and kissed her. She could taste the cinnamon and tequila on Kara’s lips and pressed herself against her for a fleeting moment before pulling back.

     

                “And you’re important to me too, you know that, right?” Lena haltingly said, uncertainty on her face.

     

                With a pleased smile as she looked down, glasses slipping down her nose, Kara nodded and peeked back up at her. “Yeah, I do.”

    Chapter 12

                The next morning saw Lena in her office at L-Corp, despite the fact that it was a Saturday, no one except security was there and she could’ve easily left things until Monday. Lena liked the solitude though, a coffee bought on her way over sitting next to her keyboard as the early morning sunlight pooled across her back and desk, just warm enough to combat the chill that emanated from the tiled floors of the clinically cold office.

     

                L-Corp’s lawyers had finished combing through a few documents that had been left on her desk, and she signed each page with a flourish as she rewatched the new advertisement on repeat on her computer screen, making notes on changes for the media department. It was quiet and productive, no meetings to pull her from her work, and while Lena knew she could’ve delegated more to other departments and heads, she appreciated the fulfilment hard work brought her. 

     

                Without her job, she would’ve had nothing to strive for, no competitive drive to best other rival tech companies, no creative outlet for her new plans to further technology in a greener way. She knew that was the real reason she threw herself so wholly into her work, for a distraction from the boredom that would’ve consumed her otherwise. Most people would probably have been content to have a bank account full of more money than they’d ever need to do whatever they wanted, but Lena craved the intellectual stimulation too.

     

                Even a few drinks the night before that had left her feeling groggy with exhaustion at five o’clock that morning hadn’t been enough to deter her from checking in on things. Although, she could feel herself flagging now, needing more coffee to sustain her as her sore muscles ached from her sunrise workout in the basement. 

     

                Finishing off signing the stack of contracts, she leaned back in her seat and closed her eyes, breathing slowly as she sifted through the mental list she’d made for herself. Jess tried to organise things according to relative importance, but sometimes Lena preferred to do it her own way. 

     

                As she decided to tackle the budget spreadsheets for the quarterly meeting that would be coming up in a few weeks, as well as the reevaluated budget for the next quarter, Lena’s phone rang on her desk.

     

                Picking it up she smiled at the sight of Kara’s name and quickly answered. “Good morning!”

     

                “Morning! You sound happy.”

     

                “It’s been productive.”

     

                There was a second too long pause on the other end. “You’re at the office?”

     

                “Yeah, I was just signing some contracts and going over the budget. Why?”

     

                “I’m outside your house. I knocked but … well, I guess that’s why you didn’t answer. I should’ve known you weren’t just having a lie-in for a change.”

     

                Lena straightened up as her face softened with surprise, “oh, well … I’ll be there soon.”

     

                “No, no, you’re busy.”

     

                “See, the good thing about running your own business is that you get to choose your own hours.”

     

                She heard a faint sigh on the other end and grinned as Kara relented. “Alright. But I don’t have anything planned, just so you know. You’re going to be stuck with my company.”

     

                “Sounds perfect. I’ll see you soon.”

     

                Shuffling everything into a resemblance of a neat pile, Lena grabbed her bag, finished off her coffee and dumped it in the trash before stalking out.

     

                Passing by security in the lobby, she gave them a quick smile and said goodbye before breezing out onto the sidewalk, where her car was parked out front in her spot. The sky was overcast now, the threat of rain on the horizon and Lena was all too eager to get home.

     

                It was spitting with rain as she parallel parked outside and she shivered at the drop in temperature as she climbed out of the Tesla. Her face brightened with a smile at the sight of Kara dressed down in jeans and a woollen shirt worn soft, huddling in the alcove of the stoop with flowers in hand.

     

                Smiling, Kara quickly descended the steps, rain flecking her glasses, and stooped to kiss Lena - once, twice - and then presented her with the flowers.

     

                “This is a nice surprise,” Lena said, taking the bouquet of tulips as she flushed with delight. “Thank you.”

     

                “I wanted to see you.”

     

                Kara said it simply, as if it was really that easy, that they should be allowed to drop by on each other whenever they felt like it for the pleasure of their company. It jolted through Lena, the knowledge that they could, that if she wanted to, she could probably drop by Alex’s apartment unannounced to see her.

     

                “I also brought … breakfast burritos,” Kara enthusiastically exclaimed, lifting the bag. “Sausage and egg. No salsa. Light on the Tabasco.”

     

                “You’re amazing,” Lena groaned, a flutter in her chest as she smiled, fishing her keys out of her pocket and mounting the steps.

     

                Kicking off her boots inside the door, she sighed at the relief that joke brought, and moved through to the kitchen with Kara trailing after her. Setting the flowers in a vase of water, Lena fetched two bottles of coconut water from the fridge and walked through to the living room, collapsing onto the sofa as she grumbled.

     

                “God, I don’t want to move for the rest of the day.”

     

                “Then don’t,” Kara said with a quiet laugh, sitting down beside her and removing their food.

     

                Lena straightened up as Kara handed her burrito over and she rubbed at her tired eyes before unwrapping it. Taking a bite, Lena sighed and chewed and swallowed, before looking at Kara with a tender look of expectation on her face.

     

                “So, what do you want to do today?”

     

                Looking at her, Kara’s eyebrows rose and she swallowed her mouthful, her eyes shifting to the window and back again.

     

                “I guess anything outside is out of the question.”

     

                “At least I won’t have to water my garden today.”

     

                Giving her a crooked smile, Kara quirked an eyebrow as she tilted her head to the side. “That almost sounds like optimism. I know that can’t be true.”

     

                “A very rare occasion, I can assure you. So … what’s the plan? What childhood milestone have I missed out on that can be remedied at home?”

     

                “I’m not sure about milestones, but we could always watch the shockingly long list of movies you haven’t seen.”

     

                Pouting slightly as she set her burrito down in her lap and reached for her drink, Lena scowled. “You’re really going to make me waste my time on these?”

     

                “It’s not a waste of time! Cinema is a form of art; you like art. It’s a visual medium!”

     

                “Okay, but if I’ve read the novel, we’re not watching the movie. Nine times out of ten it’s a lousy adaptation.”

     

                “Fine, I’ll compromise there. But … have you watched the Lord of the Rings before?”

     

                Scoffing, Lena rolled her eyes, her cheeks turning pink, “of course not, but I’ve read the books so it’s off the table.”

     

                “No way! I won’t budge on that one. Between the three movies, it won seventeen Oscars. Eleven for the last one alone!”

     

                Shifting on the sofa, one leg up on the cushions while the other was on the rug, Lena narrowed her eyes as her mouth thinned and she begrudgingly relented.

     

                “Okay, fine. I’ll watch them, but just so you know, I was obsessed with the book series growing up and if the movies suck, I’ll never trust your judgement again.”

     

                Grinning, Kara nodded, “that’s fair.”

     

                “What else are we going to watch?”

     

                Eyes widening, Kara paused as her mouth opened. “Oh. No, that’s it. That’s going to take eleven hours.”

     

                “Eleven hours? On three movies? What could possibly take that long?”

     

                “You’ve read them; you tell me.”

     

                Rolling her eyes again in feigned exasperation, Lena climbed to her feet and set her food down. “Okay, okay. You find it on the TV; I’m going to put something comfortable on. Do you want to get out of your jeans?”

     

                “Sure, if you’ve got anything to spare.”

     

                Clucking her tongue, Lena shook her head with amusement as she left the living room and jogged upstairs. She was quick as she changed into her loungewear and then plucked the little box tied with ribbon from the floor. The cashmere loungewear that she’d ordered for Kara had been delivered on Thursday and Lena had been waiting to see her to give it to her, feeling the stirring of excitement in her stomach as she grinned at the thought.

     

                Back downstairs, she found the heavy curtains drawn, casting the room in darkness, and Kara perched on the edge of the sofa, a slack look on her face as she searched for the first movie. 

     

                Moving over to the sofa, Lena leant over the back and deposited the box in Kara’s lap, biting back a smile as she braced herself against the back. Kara looked down at the box and then up at Lena, a questioning look in her eyes.

     

                “What’s this?”

     

                “Well, open it and you’ll find out,” Lena said, gently squeezing her shoulder.

     

                Setting the remote down, Kara pulled the end of the ribbon and watched the bow come undone before she pulled off the lid and nudged tissue paper aside.

     

                “It’s your pants!”

     

                “It’s your pants.”

     

                “For me?” Kara asked with elated surprise, holding them up in one hand.

     

                Nodding, Lena smiled at the mild look of shock on her face before it crumpled into a shy smile, rosy-cheeked and sweet.

     

                “Thank you,” Kara quietly exclaimed, hugging them to her chest, “that was really thoughtful.”

     

                Fiddling with a strand of her blonde hair, Lena nodded again, enjoying the sense of satisfaction at the touched look of delight that softened Kara’s face. Her blue eyes shone with adoration and Lena liked that she could make Kara feel that way and thought that she should do it more often.

     

                “Thank you,” Kara said again, pushing herself up off the seat to kiss Lena.

     

                She disappeared to get changed, looking pleased when she came back in, and she kissed Lena on the cheek as she sat down beside her and pulled up the movie.

     

                Despite her griping, Lena did enjoy herself, mostly because of Kara’s running commentary as they ate, but also because the movie was well-made. Still, she took it upon herself to point out the differences to the book, her nitpicking inaccuracies getting so particular that Kara couldn’t help but laugh, nudging her as she rolled her eyes and called her out on her derision.

     

                It was nearly lunchtime by the time they finished with the first one, which Lena admitted had been good, and they busied themselves in the kitchen, making coffee and raiding the fridge for snacks. As Lena poured the coffee into a French press, plunging it down as the coffee grounds were strained, she had the sense that Kara wanted to say something.

     

                Looking up at her, she gave her a warm smile, watching as Kara nearly arranged thick cuts of ham on wholemeal bread. The never before used sandwich press was radiating heat, waiting for the grilled ham and cheese sandwiches that Kara had volunteered to make, and a slight crease formed between Lena’s eyebrows.

     

                “You okay?”

     

                “Hm? Yeah, I, um … never mind.”

     

                Nodding as her mouth turned down at the corners in a curious manner, Lena poured coffee into two cups, adding oat milk to hers and creamer to Kara’s. She didn’t press the matter, knowing Kara would tell her in her own time; if there was one thing Kara was doing, it was being quiet.

     

                It only took a few minutes, as she put the buttered sandwiches in the machine and pressed them between the hot plates as the pepper jack and cheddar sizzled. As Lena poured veggie chips into a bowl and opened a tub of hummus, Kara cleared her throat, garnering her attention.

     

                “Actually,” Kara blurted out, fiddling with the knife in her hand as she looked down at the sandwich press. “I wanted to talk to you. About last night.”

     

                “Okay.”

     

                “It’s, um, about … what Alex said. About you being my girlfriend. I know we haven’t talked about that properly or anything, so I was just wondering …”

     

                The expectant look of open interest on Lena’s face softened into a gentle look of understanding as she cocked her head to the side.

     

                “Oh, well, we’re dating, right? I mean … you’re not seeing anyone else, are you?”

     

                A sudden feeling of dread pooled in Lena’s stomach at the lurching realisation that perhaps she’d gotten ahead of herself. They’d never mentioned anyone else, but Lena hadn’t exactly posed the question before either.

     

                “No, no, I’m- I’m not, but I just wasn’t sure how you felt about it. You know … labels.”

     

                She smiled helplessly as she rubbed the back of her neck and shrugged. A smug smile curled Lena’s lips as her eyes shone wickedly and she reached out to pull Kara closer, a goading look on her face as her grin widened.

     

                “Are you asking me to be your girlfriend?”

     

                Making a choking sound of embarrassment, Kara’s eyes furrowed upwards in an aching look of longing. “It sounds so childish when you say it like that.”

     

                “I like it,” Lena murmured.

     

                Looking down to hide her smile, she placed her hand on Kara’s waist, the thin cashmere sweater wrinkling to expose a finger of tanned skin, warm beneath Lena’s touch. She let out a snort of laughter and pressed her lips together as her cheeks dimpled with the effort of keeping her laughter at bay.

     

                “What?”

     

                Giving Kara a wry smile, she laughed again. “Nothing. It’s just … funny. I haven’t had a girlfriend since junior high.”

     

                Sighing, Kara gave her a stern look, “childish.”

     

                “I don’t care,” Lena murmured, enjoying Kara’s evident embarrassment, “I’ll take it.”

     

                “Yeah?” Kara scoffed with laughter.

     

                With a lazy shrug, Lena gave her an affronted look. “You sound surprised. Were you expecting me to run?”

     

                “Kind of,” Kara sheepishly admitted, “but only because I was setting myself up for disappointment.”

     

                Laughing, Lena shook her head and kissed her roughly, before she pulled back and narrowed her eyes. “You’re going to burn our grilled sandwiches.”

     

                “Oh! Shit.”

     

                With another quiet laugh, Lena carried their coffee into the living room and came back for the chips, eating a carrot one as she carried the bowl, while Kara quickly followed with two very toasted sandwiches.

     

                There was something soothing about their conversation in the kitchen, and, as Kara pressed play on The Two Towers, Lena leant against her, curled up with her knees to her chest and her plate on top. The press of Kara’s shoulder against her felt like an indulgence, and Lena couldn’t stop her lips from twitching with faint smiles as she thought about something so childishly simple as having a girlfriend.

     

                They were well into the afternoon by the time they got halfway through Return of the King , a four-hour monster that they were struggling to get through.

     

                At some point during the second film, after they’d finished eating and were fixated on the battle scenes, they’d shifted, both of them stretched out on the wide sofa on their sides, fitting together as Kara laid her head on Lena’s chest. It had surprised her at the time, Lena stiffening as she made to sit up before realising what Kara was doing, and as she settled back down, forcing herself to relax, Lena found herself at a loss. No one had ever cuddled up with her in such an innocently intimate manner.

     

                “Your heart is beating really fast,” Kara murmured, her voice rough from disuse, and Lena let out a breathless laugh, letting her arm settle around Kara’s shoulders.

     

                Each time one of them got up to move, using the bathroom of fetching water or ordering the pizza they’d settled on for dinner, they’d returned to that position, and each time, it had given Lena a little thrill. She trailed absentminded patterns on Kara’s back and Kara breathed in the smell of her detergent from the laundromat and the expensive French perfume, as content as Lena felt.

     

                Both of them tired from a long week and the lethargic day on the sofa, they slowly drifted off to sleep, Kara first and then Lena, without even meaning to. She never usually gave herself the opportunity to nap, the handful of hours she caught each night sustaining her as she overworked herself, but Lena didn’t even remember drifting off, so peaceful with Kara’s weight draped over her, that the next thing she knew, she was jolting awake to a dark room.

     

                The TV screen was black, the movie over and ending missed, and the golden light that had seeped through a crack in the curtains was gone. The house was still as it could only be at night, nothing stirring and the only sounds being the old bones of the structure settling with the occasional cream and groan. 

     

                And fast asleep on her chest was Kara, her glasses askew and her lips parted, a youthful slackness to her face as she breathed deeply. Blearily blinking back sleep, Lena smiled dopily to herself, reaching down to brush a strand of hair off Kara’s face.

     

                Her phone was on the floor beside her and Lena squinted at the harsh light that lit up the blackness, finding it past midnight already: they’d slept for hours.

     

                Her back protested and she sighed before gently reaching down to shake Kara awake. “Kara.”

     

                She quietly laughed as Kara groaned, a pucker wrinkling her forehead as her eyelashes fluttered. Quietly calling her name again as she lightly brushed her hand down her arm, Lena watched as Kara bolted upright a moment later, the movement so abrupt and forceful that she thought she was going to launch herself off the sofa from the momentum.

     

                “Hey,” Lena murmured, her voice warm as her smile froze for a second.

     

                Turning to look at her, Kara blinked owlishly, a distant look in her eyes, her pupils wide and her face taut. It took her a moment, but then her whole body went slack and she nudged her glasses up, exhaling as she rubbed at her eyes, still half asleep.

     

                “What time is it?”

     

                “Past midnight,” Lena whispered, brushing Kara’s hair off her shoulder as her expression softened. “Come on, let’s go to bed.”

     

                Looking a little lost, Kara looked at her for a moment before pushing herself to her feet. Pressing her hand to her back, Lena led her upstairs, all the way up to her bedroom without giving it a second thought, pulling the heavy covers back and guiding Kara onto the high mattress. Rounding the bed, Lena pulled back her own side and climbed into bed beside her. The mattress was big enough that she couldn’t feel Kara, but her skin prickled with the sensory awareness of someone else beside her and Lena closed her eyes as she pummelled the pillow into shape.

     

                “Goodnight,” she whispered, even though Kara was already asleep again.

     

                The room was still for a few minutes, the even sound of Kara’s breath surprisingly not disturbing at all as Lena sank into the mattress, waiting for sleep to claim her. And then she jerked at the heavy weight of an arm flopping over her waist as Kara mumbled in her sleep and shifting closed. Smiling to herself, Lena shuffled backwards, feeling her solid warmth at her back, and soon drifted off to sleep.

     

                Grey light flooded into the room as a light rain pattered against the windows and Lena was blinded as she woke, her eyes narrowing to slits as she turned her head and pulled the blankets up over her head. The sun hadn’t fully risen yet, indicating that it was still early, and Lena let out a vexed sigh at having forgotten to close her curtains before going to bed.

     

                As she took a moment to lay there with her eyes closed, waking up slowly, she could feel the warmth of Kara’s knee against her thigh and slowly lowered the blankets to look at her. She hadn’t taken her glasses off before falling into bed the night before, and they were wonky on her face as her blonde hair splayed across the pillows in a golden halo around her head. 

     

                Slowly propping herself up on her elbow, Lena watched her for a moment, a funny feeling in her chest at the knowledge that she’d slept beside her. That had never happened before; Lena didn’t let anyone into her bed, her bedroom, her house . She’d never slept beside anyone, even when she’d been in casual flings with other people - she’d always gone home, or ended up on their couch, unable to sleep with the thought of someone else beside her, breathing and taking up space. But her sleep had been restful, and she marvelled at that as she reached over to try and ease Kara’s glasses off her face before she bent the arms.

     

                As if she could sense Lena’s stare, or her close proximity, Kara woke the moment Lena touched her glasses, bolting upright and smacking her forehead on Lena’s chin with a solid smack. Cursing, Lena jerked back, rubbing her chin as she grit her teeth.

     

                “Shit,” she hissed.

     

                “Ow! What the- oh my God. I’m so sorry,” Kara cringed, a hand clapped to her forehead as she blinked rapidly, still half asleep as she looked at Lena.

     

                With a burst of laughter, Lena flopped onto her back, “good morning. I bet that was a nice wake-up.”

     

                “I’ve had worse,” Kara said with a sheepish smile, pulling her hand away to reveal a small red circle. 

     

                Lena tutted and reached over to smooth her thumb over the sore spot, while Kara looked at her with a curious look in her eyes.

     

                “Your eyes are especially green in the morning - did you know that?”

     

                “Mm, I did , because I do, in fact, have green eyes.”

     

                “Always so sarcastic,” Kara chided as she smiled, leaning down to kiss her.

     

                Closing her eyes, Lena kissed her back until she felt Kara pull away, and then she stretched her arms upwards, grumbling at how much she ached. “Coffee?”

     

                “Mm, please.”

     

                Climbing out of bed, she padded downstairs and set the machine on with two mugs underneath. It felt odd to have the second one there, filled with the strong coffee filtered through the machine, and Lena smiled at the sound of heavy footsteps plodding downstairs, an unusual sound in the usually empty big house.

     

                Glancing over at Kara, she watched her stretch, shirt riding up, and snagged the two cups off the machine and fetched the steamed milk. As she filled the cups, turning the dark espresso a tawny colour, she felt Kara’s arms wrap around her waist and her head on her shoulder. Feeling her cool fingertips dig into the bare skin of Lena’s stomach, she shivered slightly at the touch of Kara’s lips on her neck, rolling her head to the side as her eyelids fluttered.

     

                “If this is the good morning I get, you should stay over more often,” Lena laughed breathlessly as Kara pulled back.

     

                “Sorry about that. I guess I was more tired than I thought.”

     

                “You don’t need to apologise,” Lena quickly assured her, turning around and holding up a cup of coffee for her. “It was … actually nice waking up beside someone. Never done that before.”

     

                “Never?”

     

                “No. When people snore or toss and turn, it irritates me.”
