                Looking a little abashed, Kara winced, “I didn’t talk in my sleep, did I?”

     

                “You do that?” Lena chuckled. “That’s cute. But no, you didn’t.”

     

                “Good,” Kara weakly laughed, ruffling her tousled hair. “Sometimes … it can be a bit intense. Or so Alex tells me.”

     

                Lena could sense there was something more to it, but she didn’t press as she watched Kara, taking a sip of her own coffee. After a moment, Lena arched an eyebrow in question. “Breakfast?”

     

                Humming, Kara pursed her lips and smiled, “how about I make us pancakes?”

     

                “Sounds perfect.”

     

                Kara kissed her and directed her to a stool, and Lena was all too eager to obey, hands wrapped around her coffee cup as her eyes tracked Kara. She raided the pantry and the fridge and cupboards, pulling out stainless steel mixing bowls and free-range eggs, heating butter in a pan and mashing bananas, and Lena admired her ease. She moved around so effortlessly confident as if she lived there and spent every Sunday making them pancakes.

     

                Watching her sift the flour into a bowl of oats, Lena felt buoyed by happiness, a strange thing to be feeling so early in the morning, yet there it was. She felt happier than she’d been in a long time - perhaps ever. Each day she spent with Kara seemed to drag her further away from the stifling loneliness and bitterness that had made her so irate and resentful for most of her life.

     

                The kitchen was soon filled with the heavenly smell of cinnamon and Lena watched as Kara flipped pancakes in the large pan, tossing it one-handed and expertly catching it as she showed off for Lena's sake. Once there was a decent stack, Kara presented the heaped plate to her and set down a bottle of maple syrup before taking a seat beside her. 

     

                “These are really good,” Lena said, her voice coloured with surprise as she looked at Kara.

     

                “You sound surprised.”

     

                “I am. Not because you’re a shit cook, but I’ve never really liked pancakes that much.”

     

                “What if you’d hated them?” Kara spluttered.

     

                Shrugging, Lena cut another piece and held it halfway to her mouth, “I would’ve eaten it, obviously.”

     

                “You really need to stop eating everything I make you. Do you have any other allergies I should be aware of? Foods you don’t like?”

     

                Rolling her eyes, Lena chewed her mouthful and frowned, in deep thought for a moment. “No other allergies and I don’t like pickles. That’s it.”

     

                “That’s it?”

     

                “Basically.”

     

                “Okay, well, no pickles I can manage. When we get cheeseburgers I’ll just eat yours for you.”

     

                With a quiet, shuddering laugh, Lena shook her head as she smiled and cut another bite of her pancake.

     

                Once they were finished eating, Lena insisted that Kara take the first shower while she loaded the dishwasher, arguing that it was only fair, seeing as Kara had cooked for them. Instructing her to take what she wanted from the closet, she listened to the footsteps retreat upstairs and hummed to herself as she stacked plates in a neat row.

     

                Heading upstairs once the machine was on, a low rumble drifting after her, she found Kara standing in the middle of her closet, towel drying her hair as she looked at Lena with raised eyebrows. Half-dressed, her jeans buttoned up as she browsed the row of shirts, blouses, sweaters and t-shirts, Kara looked almost alarmed.

     

                “You have … so many clothes.”

     

                “I’m very into sustainable fashion,” Lena said with a crooked smile, “I donate all of my clothes to charity when I’m done with them.”

     

                “If only you were a few inches taller,” Kara heavily sighed, reaching out to let a satin dress slip through her fingers.

     

                Lena stepped inside to fetch something for herself, and that close to Kara, she could smell the spice of her soap on her skin, clean and fresh, and felt a slow flush creep over her. She couldn’t explain why she liked it so much, just like she had a hard time explaining why she liked anything personal she shared with Kara. 

     

                Pulling a grey long-sleeved shirt off a hanger, Kara dragged it on, the sleeves baring her wrists as she tugged at the short bottom, and she shook her head, grimacing. Lena was too busy eyeing the taut muscle of her bicep where the shirt clung to it, just a little too tight, but she wasn’t complaining.

     

                Snapping herself out of it, Lena took her damp towel off her and dumped it in the laundry basket on her way into the bathroom, the mirror and glass already fogged up. The water was hot but she didn’t linger, not wanting to waste a single minute in Kara’s company. She dressed quickly and put her bedraggled hair up before making her way back downstairs.

     

                Kara was in the living room, two cups of tea on the coffee table and the TV rewound to the last scene she remembered watching, and she smiled at Lena and jerked her head in a beckoning gesture. Flopping down beside her, Lena dragged the throw blanket off the back of the sofa and spread it over their laps as she cuddled up beside Kara, who put her arm around her, picking up the remote.

     

                “Ready?”

    Chapter 13

                Lena was at the office before the sun was even up on Thursday, typing away at her computer as streaks of pink gave a rosy tint to the lavender sky behind her, the view wasted on Lena, who didn’t even turn around to appreciate it. There were dark circles under her eyes from two sleepless nights, not entirely concealed by makeup, and she was slumped with exhaustion, already disgruntled at the fact that her day had barely started.

     

                She was on her second coffee already and the air outside was muggy as it seeped in through the open balcony door. The following week held a board meeting and Lena was working overtime - more so than usual - to get everything prepared for it, her days completely filled up with meetings with different department heads to go through their strategies and figures with a fine-toothed comb.

     

                When her phone buzzed on her desk, she cast it a cursory glance and then picked it up to hide in her drawer, not in the mood for distractions, but paused at the name on the screen. She’d anticipated a dinner proposal from some overseas business associates in a different timezone, but Kara was up early for work and Lena slowly exhaled. As busy as she was, she knew she was going to be in a foul mood all day, and Lena allowed herself the small indulgence of hearing Kara’s voice as she read the text.

     

    [Kara]: hi! busy tonight? have a good day xx

     

                Dialling her number, Lena pressed the phone to her ear and closed her eyes as she slumped in her chair. Her eyes were heavy and her shoulders ached from the tension of the permanent hunch behind her desk, and she rubbed at a kink in her neck as she listened to the ringing.

     

                “Hi! You were already awake, right?” Kara anxiously greeted her.

     

                “Unfortunately,” Lena grumbled, “I’m already at the office.”

     

                “Already? Geez, it’s not even seven o’clock; how long have you been there?”

     

                “Since five. There’s a big project meeting next week that I need to prep for. Which means … a full day.”

     

                Reaching for her coffee and taking a sip, Lena listened to Kara’s disappointed reply. “Damn. Alex told me this morning that Cirque du Soleil is in town and wanted to know if we wanted to go with her and Kelly tonight. I’ll tell them you can’t make it, but maybe we can go next week after your meeting is over.”

     

                Sitting up straight in her chair, Lena set her cup down as she frowned. “No, no, tonight is fine.”

     

                “You’re going to be exhausted! It’s fine, they won’t mind.”

     

                “I can guarantee you that if I’m not at the circus tonight, I will be at the office. Probably until after midnight.”

     

                “You need to sleep more.”

     

                Ignoring the chastisement, Lena considered for a moment, wondering how early she could leave without hindering her productivity. “What time is the show?”

     

                “There’s one at four forty-five, another at six-fifteen, and then eight-thirty.”

     

                “How about we meet there at six? I’ll send my driver to come and pick you all up.”

     

                “Six. Perfect.”

     

                “Send me through the address and the ticket site.”

     

                “It’s okay! We can buy them when we’re there.”

     

                “My treat.”

     

                With a snort of laughter, Kara pointedly replied, “it’s always your treat.”

     

                “Kara, I can promise you, me buying tickets to the circus is not a big deal.”

     

                Hesitating, Kara sighed, “okay, but next time-“

     

                “Sure,” Lena lied.

     

                “Okay, I really have to go before I get pulled over for using my phone.”

     

                “Wha- go! Before you end up wrapped around a tree.”

     

                “It’s hands-free and I’m a good driver!”

     

                Smiling to herself, Lena shook her head, “mhm, I’ve been in the car with you.”

     

                With a weary sigh, Kara clicked her tongue. “Fine. But now I really have to go. I’ll see you later; have a good day!”

     

                “You too.”

     

                The line went dead and Lena felt buoyed by the warm feeling in her chest from the short conversation. Taking a few minutes more to finish off her coffee, which was already bordering on lukewarm from neglect, Lena climbed to her feet and walked a few steps to stretch out her legs before taking her seat again.

     

                The rest of her morning dragged, tedious phone calls, too many rejections of drafted proposals and finalised figures that she started to get frustrated with each person that came before her, sending them back with notes for corrections and elaborations. 

     

                Only Jess and Sam were spared from her irritation, the three of them spending the hours either side of lunch locked in Lena’s office, occupying the couch, coffee table and ottomans as they shuffled through stacks of paperwork. Jess fetched them lunch that Lena barely touched, and produced anything that Lena required, from pens to specific documents to little flagged stickers.

     

                Her afternoon was spent trying to focus on the droning explanations of various project meetings, which she technically didn’t have to concern herself with going to, but did anyway. After her brother had tanked their family’s reputation - personal and business-wise - Lena had taken a vested interest in rebuilding it once she’d assumed control of L-Corp. 

     

                She put more time and effort into running the business than any other CEO she knew, never giving the Board of Directors a chance to consider replacing her. As the majority shareholder and Chairperson, it would’ve been a difficult decision for them to make anyway. The only person who would be able to veto her was her mother, and Lillian seemed to be indifferent to Lena’s plans for L-Corp, which was just fine with Lena.

     

                Jess had secured six tickets at Lena’s request - four for her personal use and two so that Jess could go on a night of her choosing - and at five-thirty, Lena realised that she needed to leave soon or she’d be late to meet everyone. There wasn’t time for her to go home and change, and she’d mercifully worn slacks and a shirt that day - not too dressy - so at quarter-to, Jess grabbed her bag and coat for her and Lena made her way outside to her car.

     

                Putting in the address Kara had sent her, Lena made her way to the arena and went towards the valet parking entrance for VIP parking. Handing over her keys, she messaged Kara to let her know she was there.

     

    [Kara]: we’re at the main entrance

     

                It took Lena a few minutes to locate them through the flow of other ticket holders, but she caught sight of Kara first, a few inches taller than Alex and Kelly and craning her neck as she tried to spot Lena. There were warm greetings all around and they talked about their day as they joined the crowd heading towards the doors.                 Showing her ID, Lena was handed four tickets and directed towards the doors, and they stepped inside to the smell of buttered popcorn and the chilled air pumped through the vents. Lena eyed the concession stands and turned around raising her eyebrows.

     

                “Drinks? Snacks?”

     

                Kara looped her arm through Lena’s and dragged her over to the stand selling fresh popcorn. Squeezing Kara’s arm in a reassuring manner as Lena tapped her credit card at every stall, buying nachos, giant soft pretzels and cotton candy, chilli dogs and three beers - she was driving - she handed out the snacks without a word and then glanced around for the entrance for their seat section, dismissing the thanks from everyone with a vague sense of embarrassment.

     

                “Which section are we in?” Kara asked, looking over Lena’s shoulder at the tickets. “A2. A2? Is that at the very front? Lena, how much did you spend on these tickets?”

     

                She lowered her voice to a hush, scandalised as she tried to pluck one from her hands, the price printed on the little slip. With a faint smile, Lena pressed the tickets against her coat, hiding the details as she gave Kara a reproving look.

     

                “It’s fine, Kara.”

     

                “Lena, that's a lot of money,” Kara softly exclaimed, a pained look on her face.

     

                “Then it’s a good thing I can afford it, right?” Lena murmured, her lips twitching with a faint smile as she reached out to gently tug on the end of Kara’s braid. “Besides, I didn’t pick them; Jess did.”

     

                “And what did you tell Jess?”

     

                Shrugging indifferently, Lena gave her a wolfish smile, “to buy the best seats they had.”

     

                “You’re a nightmare.”

     

                “I’ve never been to the circus before,” Lena stated matter-of-factly, jerking her chin up in a haughty manner, “I wanted to have good seats.”

     

                With a scoff of laughter, Kara rolled her eyes as Lena displayed the tickets for the usher and the four of them were waved through. Wide steps descended through the dark arena, and Lena followed the guide lights down to their seats.

     

                “Have you really never been to the circus before?”

     

                “I’ve never done anything fun before. Well … normal fun. Paris Fashion Week? Yes. Skied the Valais region in Switzerland? Every year since I was six. A circus? Not a chance.”

     

                Alex scoffed from behind her, “I bet you grew up with a butler, right?”

     

                Grinning over her shoulder, Lena rolled her eyes, “not a butler, but … we had staff.”

     

                “Jesus,” Kelly muttered, her eyebrows rising.

     

                “Why do you even work?” Alex asked, frowning, “if I was you … I’d never work a day in my life. I’d have a private jet and a house in every country, and I’d spend a week in each of them every year.”

     

                Shrugging as they reached the bottom and were directed towards the small block of seats arranged in rows, they found their seats in the third row and shuffled across to fit.

     

                “I like my job,” Lena said with a grave look of deep thought, “but … I guess it helps that it’s a choice. I don’t need it, so if I didn’t like it … I wouldn’t do it.”

     

                Lena made no apologies for her fortune, was completely unabashed when it came to spending money, and wouldn’t pretend otherwise for the sake of a few hundred dollars for a circus show. It was such an inconsequential number, an infinitesimally small amount that it made her feel a little guilty that it would be considered an extravagant cost to the other three women. Lena was generous to a fault anyway, filthy rich but not snobby, but she’d never had anyone to indulge in small treats - most people she was acquainted with having their own money or people she had no interest in beyond work.

     

                “Simple enough,” Kelly said with a quiet laugh, taking a sip of her beer.

                “But … it’s the circus .”

     

                “At least I was never afraid of clowns as a child.”

The lights dimmed shortly after, plunging the arena into darkness and her curiosity was piqued as a large spotlight lit up the centre of the ring as the show started.

She’d seen the ballet at The Royal Opera House in London’s Covent Garden and Shakespearean plays at the Ancient Greek Epidaurus Theatre, in preserved ruins, but Lena was no less fascinated by the performance before her. There was a subtle beauty to the aerial show as trapeze artists swooped overhead in extravagant costumes and acrobats tumbled and contorted. It was captivating and not what she’d expected at all.

     

                Once it was over, they exited the arena to the darkness of night, a faint breeze chilling them after the warmth of so many bodies packed into one place, and Lena let Kara loop her arm through hers as she led them towards her parked car.

     

                “So, what did you think?” Kara asked.

     

                “It was good! I’m surprised.”

     

                “Surprised?” Kelly asked from her right, “it’s an award-winning performance troupe.”

     

                “Well of course I’ve heard of it before, but I thought it’d be … cheesier.”

                “I could eat.”

                “You look exhausted.”

                “At this time?” Alex sceptically asked.

                “What?”

Although,” Lena paused, letting out a short laugh as she covered her mouth, cheeks dimpling, “I, uh, I did kind of get into trouble once for sneaking out.”

     

                Turning in her seat, Kara leaned away from her to give Lena a surprised look. “So you were a troublemaker.”

     

                “Barely,” Lena rolled her eyes, “I had … one friend. I say friend, but it was sort of a rivalry. I was only thirteen at the time - she was sixteen - and it was towards the end of my senior year. For graduation, all the girls planned on skipping classes for the day and my friend, Andrea, convinced a few girls to sneak out to the woods to drink. We needed to get alcohol for that, obviously, and she was a lot more bossy than I was so I just went along with it. I was pretty shy when I was younger, and younger than the other girls, so I was just glad that someone liked me enough to be friends - I say friends but I was more of an entertaining pet to her. But of course I went along with it.”

     

                Pausing, Lena let out a snort of laughter and then wrinkled her nose in a sheepish manner. “I shouldn’t laugh, but, well, anyway, Mount Helena’s was in Vermont. Middle of nowhere. The only place nearby was a convenience store a mile down the road at a truck stop, and they were pretty relaxed about the girls who’d sneak out of the school. So we get there and there’s this guy blocking the door and we were kind of just like … um, okay? It was weird but we went inside anyway and there was this other guy just … covered in blood. Apparently we’d walked into the middle of a robbery and everyone was just silent and we were all looking at each other, pretending that we hadn’t just walked into the middle of a robbery. Andrea and I had no clue what to do, and I was scared shitless, so we just walked to the back of the store, talking loudly about what we were going to get. And this place was trashed . The shelves had been knocked over and there was blood everywhere. We grabbed as many bottles of wine and six-packs as we could carry and made our way to the counter, but then we realised the cashier couldn’t serve us because he was literally being held at gunpoint. I don’t know what would’ve happened if he’d tried to card us, but, anyway, we just threw some money on the counter and told them we were going. And they just … let us go? And were so casual about it too, like, they told us to have a good night. We ran the whole way back to school.”

     

                “You just left that guy to get robbed?” Kara asked, appalled as she looked at Lena with shock.

     

                “The police were pulling up when we left; he was fine . We did go back a few weeks later though and he was still there, which was a bit awkward.”

     

                “How-” Kara started, before closing her eyes and holding up a hand, “you know what, actually, I don’t want to know.”

     

                “Boarding school,” Lena said with an indifferent shrug, taking a sip of her iced tea.

     

                She footed the check again, all but shoving a handful of folded bills into their waitress’ hands, enough for a generous tip on top of the cost, and climbed to her feet before anyone could protest. Donning her coat and grabbing her bag, Lena reached for Kara’s hand and led her out onto the street, walking down the street to the arena where her car was parked.

     

                “We can just catch a cab, you know,” Alex assured Lena.

     

                “It’s no problem. Really.”

     

                “You live on the other side of Downtown,” Kara pointed out, bumping her shoulder.

     

                “I need to swing by the office anyway, so it’s just a little bit past that.”

     

                “The office? At this hour?”

     

                Bumping her shoulder in return, Lena grimaced, “okay, that’s a lie, but I don’t mind driving you. Unless you’d rather me call my driver …”

     

                “I’ve been catching cabs for years ,” Kara sighed.

     

                “Why are you so stubborn?” Lena lamented, “take the free ride. Alex?”

     

                Shrugging, Alex gave her a wry smile as Lena glanced over her shoulder with raised eyebrows, “I am curious about what kind of car you have.”

     

                “It’s just a Tesla.”

     

                “Just a Tesla. I guess that is pretty modest for your kind.”

     

                Lena didn’t spill the fact that she had half a dozen others in a storage facility near the docks, various super cars, SUV’s and coupes all hidden beneath covers, collecting dust in favour of the everyday use of Lena’s Tesla, which was more appropriate for her clean energy campaign. The electric car was modest in comparison, but Lena preferred it, although she had been eyeing the new electric Porsche Taycan Turbo S, sleek and fast, a nice indulgence for a quarter of a million.

     

                The arena parking lot was anything but empty as they wound through the cars making a belated exit, the post-show traffic jam having vanished while they ate, Lena felt irritation coil in her stomach at the sight of a few news reporters and journalists lingering about smoking, a few packing away camera equipment while vans emblazoned with KPJT News and KSFZ were parked nearby.

     

                As the four of them strolled past, the white halo of light from a streetlight illuminated them and Lena heard the excited mutters and cursed them for it, knowing she’d been recognised. A shout to catch her attention went ignored as she turned her head in the opposite direction and hunched her shoulders, the starburst of a camera flash blinding her peripheral, and Lena blinked rapidly while Alex grumbled behind her, the other three women having turned to see what the fuss was about.

     

                “For fuck’s sake,” Lena muttered, tugging a little more insistantly on Kara’s hand as she took longer strides, feeling uncomfortable and self-conscious.

     

                “What’s that all about?” Kelly asked, her tone perplexed.

     

                With a breathless huff of laughter, Lena shook her head and rummaged through her bag for her car card. “Must be a slow news day.”

     

                “Oh! I guess you would kind of be … a celebrity. That’s weird. Does it happen often?”

     

                Shrugging nonchalantly, Lena gave Kelly a grim smile, “often enough to be annoying . Especially … well, after. ”

     

                “Right.”

     

                Lena was grateful she dropped the topic then and as they neared her car, she unlocked it and slid behind the wheel, her lips twitching with a tired smile at the quiet exclamations at the novelty of the car. 

     

                Kara tuned the radio into a pop station as she peeled out of the parking lot, glaring at the camera crew as they finished packing up, and indicated for a right turn at the traffic lights. They talked quietly in the back, and Kara softly sang along to the songs beside Lena, her voice smooth and surprisingly good, easing the knot in Lena’s stomach as she drove towards Alex’s.

     

                She didn’t go upstairs, pulling up outside the building and brushing off the gratitude piled on her by the other women as they thanked her for the night. Lena was just grateful for the company, surprised at how much she liked Alex and Kelly, and not just because of Kara. There was a sense of comfort and ease with them, no pressure to perform or to meet any expectations, and she wondered if perhaps she’d just been acquainted with the wrong crowd her whole life. 

     

                Lingering in the front seat for a minute longer, Kara turned to face Lena and gave her a tired smile. “Thank you for coming.”

     

                “I had a really good time,” Lena admitted, reaching out to brush her fingertips over the back of Kara’s hand.

     

                “Me too. Thank you.”

     

                She reached out to brush Lena’s hair out of her face, her fingers a featherlight touch on her cheek as she smiled faintly. “And thank you for not being scared off by Alex.”

     

                With a quiet laugh, Lena’s eyes closed and she smiled, “I like her. Both of them. A lot, actually.”

     

                “I’m glad.”

     

                Lena could sense that Kara really meant that, glad that the people in her life could get along, spend the time to get to know each other. It was a thought that Lena liked too. 

     

                They were both silent for a long moment and then Kara sighed heavily. “Alright, I’d better go inside. Message me when you get home, okay?”

     

                “I will.”

     

                “And no more work tonight; you need some sleep.”

     

                “Mm,” Lena hummed in agreement, although she was still deliberating on whether or not she’d give in to that desire, her eyes burning as she looked at Kara with a tender expression.

     

                Kara leant across the centre console and kissed her slowly before giving her a quick peck, her eyes crinkling at the corners as she smiled.

     

                Saying goodnight, Kara slipped out of the car and gently shut the car door before hurrying to the lobby, where Alex and Kelly were climbing into the elevator.

     

                Lips tingling, Lena smiled to herself as she drove home, warmed by Kara’s concern for her. When she arrived home, Lena messaged her as she made her way upstairs, her footsteps slow and heavy, and when she reached the third floor she couldn’t muster the energy to go up another flight and work until the early hours of the morning. Heeding Kara’s orders to sleep, she fell into bed on the side that Kara had slept on earlier that week and breathed in the lingering smell of her and was asleep, fully-clothed, before she could even reconsider.

    Chapter 14

                An unknown number illuminated Lena’s private cell phone and she frowned as she declined it, setting it back down and turning her attention back to her computer screen. Only to be disturbed by it vibrating again, the sound grating on the desk. With a sigh, Lena snatched it up and jammed against her ear as she answered it.

     

                “Yes?” she asked in a clipped tone.

     

                There was a momentary pause and a snort of laughter. “Do you always answer the phone with such lovely manners?”

     

                Mouth opening and closing, Lena bristled, pulling the phone away from her face to stare at the screen before she put it back to her ear. “Who is this?”

     

                “It’s me . Alex.

     

                Lena let out a breathless laugh, pressing her fingers to her mouth as she relaxed in her chair. “Oh. Alex, hi. Sorry, I just- I’m funny about who I gave my personal cell to.”

     

                “I hope you don’t mind, I asked Kara for it.”

     

                “No, that’s fine.”

     

                “Great. Well, so, you know James? And his girlfriend, Lucy? They’re in town for the weekend so James can see Kelly, but Kara doesn’t know yet. Neither does Kelly. It’s a surprise, so we’re all meeting at this bar we go to. Al's. I thought you might like to come and meet her friends - some of her other ones that actually live here are going to be there too - and I thought you could also get her there for me.”

     

                Blinking in surprise, Lena hesitated. Things at work had slowed down after the quarterly board meeting, where her mother had been mercifully absent on account of her being in Morocco for business. It had all sailed through smoothly, profits up and costs down, new plans greenlit and her position as the head and primary owner of the company further solidified.

     

                “Yeah, I can get her there,” Lena said with conviction.

     

                “Perfect! I’ll text you the address of the bar.”

     

                “Sounds good.”

     

                “Alright, bye.”

     

                Hanging up, Lena frowned for a moment and then sent Kara a text asking her if she wanted to meet her after work tomorrow night. Enjoying the feeling of planning a surprise she knew Kara would enjoy, work seemed to go faster and her good mood seemed to be infectious throughout the rest of her meetings, the tension dissipating as she doled out compliments with caution.

     

                Picking out her outfit that night, she slept relatively early and spent a little extra time in the morning doing her hair and makeup before getting her driver to take her in so she wouldn’t have to drive home.

     

                The day dragged by as her excitement made her usual unbreakable concentration vanish, and she changed and left the office earlier than she’d planned for the week to find Kara waiting outside. The sun was just starting to sink, the air warm enough for Lena’s dress as she stepped outside smiling. Wary of employees staring after her, she kissed Kara quickly, ensuring her back was to the glass front of the office building, before lacing their fingers together.

     

                “You look nice,” Kara said, eyeing the casual sundress and the oversized leather jacket with surprise.

     

                “So do you,” Lena said, squeezing her hand. “How was work?”

     

                “Good! It went fast so I can’t complain. I did want to talk to you about something though.”

     

                A flash of uneasy surprise crossed Lena’s face as she turned to look at Kara, eyebrows raised as a seed of doubt planted itself in her mind. “Oh. Um, sure, what’s up?”

     

                “Can we get Chinese food for dinner?” Kara asked, a hopeful look on her face.

     

                Bringing them to a stop in the middle of the sidewalk, Lena blinked at her, her face blank. “That- that’s what you want to talk about?”

     

                “Yeah,” Kara said, her forehead slightly creasing with confusion, “I’ve been craving it all day and I thought you might already have reservations so-”

     

                Tipping her head back as she exhaled slowly, Lena’s shoulders dropped as the sudden bout of tension fled her body. Letting out a rough sound of exasperation, she shook her head and chuckled.

     

                “Jesus, Kara, don’t do that! I thought it was something serious!”

     

                “Chinese food is serious,” Kara said, cocking her head to the side as she stared at Lena with bewildered surprise, tugging them back into motion. “What? Did you think I was going to break up with you before dinner.”

     

                Rolling her eyes, Lena turned her head to stare through the windows of an electronics store, a brooding look on her face. The truth was that she was always half-expecting bad news, she just couldn’t help herself, and she hated to admit that she was so insecure. Kara seemed to sense that and squeezed her hand reassuringly before leaning in to loudly whisper in her ear.

     

                “I’d at least wait until after .”

     

                A bark of laughter forced its way up Lena’s throat as her eyes creased at the corners. Clouded expression brightening, Lena bumped Kara’s shoulder and smiled as she dropped a kiss on the side of her head, the warmth in her chest a comforting reassurance as they made the walk towards Kara’s favourite restaurant.

     

                Seated at what had quickly become their table during Lena’s lunch breaks, they ordered half a dozen dishes, and while Kara was using the restroom, Lena slyly messaged Alex to let her know that they’d be a bit late. 

     

                Full of orange chicken, Lena had to force herself to move once they were finished, otherwise they would be late . Outside, she tugged Kara along at a brisk pace, furtively checking the map on her phone to ensure they were going in the right direction. She’d looked it up beforehand, but Lena wasn’t used to walking around National City.

     

                “Are we in a rush?” Kara asked with amusement as Lena increased her pace to make it across a flashing pedestrian sign.

     

                Lena gave her a shrug as she slowed her pace, trying to look indifferent. In fact, she was feeling a little nervous about meeting Kara’s other friends, but recognised the appeal of it; she knew she kept Kara away from them sometimes, their late night dinners cutting into nights Kara would’ve otherwise spent at the bar or at someone’s apartment playing board games and drinking. Lena was shockingly optimistic that perhaps she’d tag along to these nights if they liked her, so things would be easier for Kara.

     

                Squeezing Kara’s hand, Lena gave her a thin smile. She was bolstered by the fact that she’d already met Alex and Kelly, and subsequently managed to charm them enough to warrant more nights out at restaurants and bars. She was mildly confident tonight would go just as well. There was something else on her mind though, weighing her down as she worried at the thought, picking through the idea before she brought it up, but now was as perfect a time as any.

     

                “So, I’ve been thinking,” Lena started, her voice slow and uncertain as they stepped around a cordoned off construction area.

     

                “That’s dangerous.”

     

                “Only for stupid people,” Lena scoffed, rolling her eyes as she smiled before she turned solemn and squeezed Kara’s hand. “The annual Luthor gala is coming up next month … I was wondering if maybe you’d want to come. With me. As my girlfriend.”

     

                Surprise lit up Kara’s face. “Oh. Are you sure? I mean … I’d love to, but I know how you feel about the public eye.”

     

                “Well, we’ve already gotten appearances in a dozen magazines and newspapers in the city, and half of the west coast gossip blogs. And my entire company already knows because they’re even worse than the gossip blogs. More importantly though, I want you to come.”

     

                “Mm, I get weird looks whenever I stand outside your building. They must be wondering what someone like you sees in my scruffy self.”

     

                With a scoff of laughter, Lena stopped and grabbed Kara’s face, giving her a bruising kiss before touching their foreheads together for a brief moment. “If they have to wonder, they clearly don’t know you.”

     

                “I wonder myself too, sometimes,” Kara shrugged as they picked up the pace again. 

     

                She didn’t say it in a self-deprecating way, more openly curious, but Lena rankled at the words anyway, a disgruntled look on her face. Lips twitching as she pouted slightly, Lena made a low noise of annoyance at the back of her throat.

     

                “Why? Do you think I’m too prissy to date someone with no trust fund?”

     

                “Not prissy, no. But … I don’t really have anything to offer you, do I? I’m not as rich as you.”

     

                Letting out a quiet chuckle, Lena arched an eyebrow and leant in close, “oh, baby, no one is as rich as I am. I’m clearly not after money.”

     

                “So … why then?”

     

                “Do you really want to know?”

     

                Slowing, Kara shrugged, giving her a guarded look even though she was aiming for carelessness. With a quiet laugh, Lena dropped her hand as they stopped in the mouth of an alleyway, reaching out to grab Kara’s jacket and pull her a little bit closer before she brushed a strand of hair out of her face. Kara leant into her touch as her eyes creased at the corners.

     

                “You’re incredibly kind,” Lena said with a grave look on her face, her green eyes mystified and a flicker of something else in them, something just as guarded and doubtful as the look in Kara’s. “You make me laugh, you make me feel … light . I value that a hell of a lot more than money.”

     

                “Only someone rich would say that,” Kara teased, but Lena could see that she was pleased.

     

                “So?” Lena asked, eyebrows raised expectantly, “will you come with me? It might be the first gala I enjoy .”

     

                “Of course I will.”

     

                Kara threw an arm around Lena’s shoulders and grinned as they set off down the street, the sky a deep blue and the fluorescent lights of storefronts and signs cast a pleasant glow over the shadowed street. Lena leant into Kara as she smiled.

     

                “I’ll have Jess arrange everything with you. Alex and Kelly are welcome as well, of course.”

     

                Lena’s bubble of excitement at Kara’s agreement was subdued as a irate expression darkened her face, her lips twisting in a bitter, rueful smile. “There’s just one other thing; technically, it’s a family event, not L-Corp, so my mother is … somewhat obligated to be there. And, well, you know how I feel about my mom. Just … please don’t take it the wrong way when I try to keep you far away from her. It really has nothing to do with you.”

     

                Nodding slowly, Kara gave her an understanding smile. “That’s fine. If you don’t want me to meet her, then I respect that, but if we can’t help bumping into her, it’s no big deal for me. I’m great with parents, for the record, but even if she hates my guts … well, I’m not trying to date her , right?”

     

                “Right.”

     

                Her smile was hesitant but she felt less tense. Relief that Kara wasn’t going to try and coerce her into introducing her to Lillian made her relax slightly, but Lena knew that her mother had a habit of trying to involve herself in her daughter’s life whenever she could. It had only gotten worse over the last two years since Lex’s death, as if trying to compensate for the lack of a son to dote on, but as far as Lena was concerned, it was two decades too late for Lillian to pretend that she cared about her daughter.

     

                Five minutes later, they walked into the mouth of a wide alley and Lena felt uneasy as she looked at the grimy walls, the glass-strewn asphalt and the graffiti. There was a metal door set into a building at the end of it, a dumpster overflowing with trash, and she stopped in her tracks, glancing down at her phone hidden in her pocket.

     

                “Hey!” Kara exclaimed with surprise, looking at Lena, “how’d you know about this place?”

     

                “Alex told me about it,” Lena said, relieved she’d brought them to the right place, although it was worlds away from anything she’d frequented before, and not entirely nice.

     

                Walking down the alleyway as Kara followed after her, scoffing as she said, “so you and Alex talk now?”

     

                Gingerly pulling the door open, Lena smiled over her shoulder before stepping inside. Her shoes clung to the sticky floor and the smell of stale beer and grease perfumed the air as loud music drowned out most of her reply.

     

                “I mean, not often, but it was necessary.”

     

                “Why?”

     

                “To bring you here tonight.”

     

                Kara’s face darkened with confusion as they stepped into the full bar, cracked booths and worn pool table, a scarred bar - well-stocked - and a jukebox in one corner. It was dingy and half-full and Lena watched as realisation dawned on Kara’s face, her attention snagged by a crowded table in the middle of the room.

     

                “Oh my God! James! Lucy!”

     

                Her shout cut through the din of the bar as she quickly crossed the room, Lena following at a slower pace as she smiled to herself, watching Kara wrap her friends in tight hugs as they all laughed. Lena caught Alex and Kelly’s eyes, raising her hand in a slight wave as she smiled and nodded, catching Alex’s appreciative wink.

     

                Two other people were at the table as well, and Lena took them to be Nia and Querl, Kara’s National City friends. There were greetings all around as Lena hung back apprehensively before Kara stepped back and pressed a hand against her lower back, ushering her forward slightly.

     

                “Everyone, this is Lena! And this is Lucy, Nia, Querl and James.”

     

                Lena shook hands as she was introduced to everyone one by one, smiling and nodding, before she found herself parked on a stool beside Kelly with Kara sandwiching her in on her other side. Kelly tugged on the sleeve of her leather jacket and nodded approvingly.

     

                “Nice jacket.”

     

                Lena’s smile was smug and she leant forward as Kara spoke. “So, when did you guys get here?”

     

                “This morning,” Lucy grinned, “we wanted it to be a surprise for you two.”

     

                She pointed at Kara and Kelly, and Kara looked indignant as she looked around in surprise, before turning sharply to Lena. “Even you knew?”

     

                With a crooked smile, Lena shrugged, gently elbowing her, “well, someone had to get you here. Now … drinks?”

     

                Taking orders for everyone, she was joined at the bar by James, his brawn and height imposing but his wide smile warm. She was carded and paid with her credit card as he leant against the bar beside her, studying her closely.

     

                “So, how’d you manage to impress Jukebox?”

     

                “Jukebox?” Lena echoed with confusion.

     

                “Kara,” James chuckled as they both glanced over at her, “get her to tell you the story.”

     

                “Oh. Okay. Um, well … I don’t know, we met in a coffee shop and here we are. I must’ve done something right.”

     

                He smiled, a fond look on his face that touched Lena - he clearly cared about his friend a lot, both of them bonded over their time spent overseas. “Mhm. I’ve never seen her so happy, which is saying something. It’s good that she’s met someone.”

     

                With James carrying the tray of drinks back over to the table, Lena climbed back onto her stool and reached for her gin and tonic before turning to Kara with a curious look on her face. “Hey, why do they call you Jukebox?”

     

                Flushing, Kara tipped her head back and groaned as everyone else laughed. Rolling her eyes she fixed Lena with a slightly embarrassed look of exasperation. “So, you may or may not have realised that I like to sing.”

     

                “Considering that it’s almost impossible to listen to a song without you joining in on it, yes, I have.”

     

                “Well, when we all enlisted we had to do basic training together, and our Drill Sergeant used to get angry when I would sing, like … all the time. So one day he’d had enough, and he locked me in one of the lockers and made me stand in there all day while he got people to slide quarters in through the gaps. He said if I wanted to be a jukebox so badly then here was my chance. Every time someone posted a quarter through the gap I’d have to sing whatever song they requested, and when our Sergeant yelled change I’d have to change songs. Since then I haven’t been able to shake the nickname,” Kara shrugged, laughing as her cheeks turned rosy and she winced. “It’s hard to shake a nickname in the military once you’re given one.”

     

                Lena let out a surprised bark of laughter, a bewildered look of incredulity on her face as she shook her head. She also made a mental note to take Kara to a karaoke bar one night; she did have a surprisingly good voice and Lena knew she’d enjoy it.

     

                The rest of the night was filled with such stories, the four soldiers - former and present - reminiscing, while Nia and Querl talked about their jobs and stories from game nights or other nights out. There was so much history within the small group and Lena was quietly surprised at how easily them welcomed her in, so much friendliness heaped onto her as they took it in turns ordering rounds - Lena had opened a tab earlier, and they quickly got over their pride to take advantage of it - and she felt the pleasant hum of alcohol in her veins, leaving her susceptible to easier smiles and quicker laughter, her eyes growing heavy and her movements a little slower. 

     

                They stayed until closing time, the early hours of the morning clearing the place out as they grew rowdier over shots, the jokes and digs soon involving Lena. It was clear that they thought she was a prissy rich girl, based on reputation alone, but it was well-intentioned and Lena rolled her eyes at the jibes about her slumming it with them. She didn’t mention how horrified she was by the bathroom stalls.

     

                At closing time, they were all turned out into the back alley, the air cold enough to make her shiver in her dress as she clung to Kara’s arm, lips trembling. James and Lucy caught a cab back to their hotel, and Nia and Querl back to their apartment, all four of them giving Lena warm hugs, while the four women lingered as they waited for Lena’s driver, who arrived a few minutes later. 

     

                All of them slumped in the back, words slightly slurred and eyes lidded, they all murmured about how much fun it had been and how tired they were as they slowly crept through the city to Alex’s apartment.

     

                “God, I hate how tired drinking makes me,” Lena mumbled. “I could fall asleep right now.”

     

                “You can crash at my place,” Alex offered.

     

                “Oh, no, it’s okay. I don’t want to intrude. Besides, my house isn’t far.”

     

                “It’s on the other side of the city,” Kara interjected.

     

                Head lolling to the side as she looked at her, Alex smiled, “you’re not intruding. Honestly. You’re welcome any time.”

     

                Kara brushed Lena’s hair off her shoulder and kissed her temple, her lips warm and soft, and she whispered quietly to her. “You can go home if you want to, but you can stay over.”

     

                “I’ve never seen your apartment before,” Lena mused.

     

                “Not my apartment,” Kara chuckled, “you’d probably be horrified though.”

     

                Snorting, Lena rested her head on Kara’s shoulder as she closed her eyes, humming. “I’m not as snobby as you think I am, you know.”

     

                “I know.”

     

                Lena was silent for a long moment before she spoke, her voice a little too loud in the confines of the car. “I’ll stay. Thank you.”

     

                As her driver pulled up outside, Lena wound the partition down and told him she would call him in the morning to be picked up before she climbed out of the car and wrapped her arm around Kara’s waist, burrowing into her warmth as she walked towards the apartment lobby. The cold seemed to make her mind sharper and she bundled into the elevator with the other three women and watched as Alex jammed her thumb into the button for the seventh floor.

     

                It was a modern apartment, small but homely with an open kitchen and living room, a table for four wedged in between, and a short hallway with two doors leading off it. To the right of the front door was a small bathroom and a hallway closet and Lena looked around with interest, seeing hints of Kara in the coat hanging on the hook, the framed Polaroids and the abandoned romance novel.

     

                They said goodnight and Kara towed her down the hallway to her bedroom, flipping the light on to illuminate a space barely big enough to hold the double bed. There was a narrow shelf filled with books, shoe boxes of photographs and a few CD’s and stiff paint brushes. Shuffling down the side of the bed, which was pushed up against the wall, the sheets rumpled, Kara eased a drawer open and rifled through it, pulling out a few articles of clothing as Lena looked around with interest.

     

                “Here,” Kara murmured, handing her a t-shirt and a pair of sweatpants.

     

                The t-shirt was faded from too many washes, from an Eagles concert a few years prior, and the sweatpants were all bobbly from wear. They smelled of Kara’s laundry powder and Lena stripped off her jacket and dress before changing into them, enjoying the feeling of the sweatpants pooling around her ankles, too long for her stature.

     

                “Which side do you sleep on?” Lena asked, raking a hand through her hair.

     

                Kara let out a soft laugh and gave her a wry smile as she pulled her t-shirt on, “when I get to sleep in a proper bed, sides are the least of my worries. You take whichever side you want; I’ll be right back.”

     

                She watched Kara slip out into the hallway and pulled the covers back, crawling onto the bed and flopping down on her back as she pinched the bridge of her nose, unsure if she’d be able to get her eyes open again. The mattress was cheap but soft, the pillow beneath her smelling like Kara, infinitely comforting, and her faded sheets were soft beneath her fingers as she lay there, listening to the sounds from the bathroom and the traffic outside. It was different from her own neighbourhood, the sounds louder, the apartment noisier with other people inside it.

     

                Kara returned a few minutes later with a glass of water and two aspirin in her hand, kneeling on the edge of the mattress as she jostled it slightly leaning over to Lena. “Here. Take these now so you don’t wake up with a hangover.”

     

                Lena moaned and forced herself to open her eyes to the bare lightbulb overhead, blindingly bright as she moved slowly. Swallowing them down and draining the glass, the lingering taste of tequila on her lips, she flopped back down and smiled sleepily at Kara.

     

                With a small smile, Kara switched her light off and sank down onto the bed beside Lena, her silhouette visible as she removed her glasses before pulling the covers up and turning on her side to face Lena. The curtains weren’t dark enough to blot out the lights outside and Lena reached out to trace the outline of Kara’s lips with her fingertip.

     

                The mattress groaned as Kara propped herself up on her elbow and hovered above Lena, her mouth hot and tasting of minty toothpaste as she kissed her. Reaching up to tangle her hands in Kara’s hair, she was all fingers and thumbs, brushing the back of her neck and her cheeks lightly.

     

                Pulling back, Kara stared down at her for a moment longer before kissing her again, gentle and lingering, before she whispered goodnight and settled back down on her back. Eyes closing, Lena whispered it back and rolled over onto her stomach, throwing an arm across Kara’s stomach as she pressed her face into the cotton of her shirt, feeling Kara’s warm hand on her back. Cuddled up against her, Lena was asleep within minutes, a peaceful look on her face as she slept soundly.

    Chapter 15

                The following Wednesday, the tickle that had been irritating the back of Lena’s dry throat all week had developed into a full-fledged cold. Her alarm had gone off and Lena struggled to sit up, a pounding headache behind her eyes as her whole body ached and she let out a hacking cough. Groaning, Lena threw the covers back and forced herself out of bed, so lethargic that her whole body sagged and she struggled to open her eyes.

     

                She’d slept in later than usual, although not late enough to warrant her emergency alarm to go off, and after making it downstairs, the lurching steps making her feel dizzy, she shivered as she padded into the kitchen. Pouring a glass of water from the refrigerated pitcher, Lena knocked back two pills and braced herself against the counter, eyes closed as the strange sensation of a hot flush washed over her, quickly replaced by another shiver. The floor was cold beneath her bare feet and she pressed cool fingers to her burning forehead.

     

                Deliberating whether or not she should go into work, the weekend only a few days away, Lena let out a raspy sigh, knowing that she would only suffer for it and end up losing more days of work the following week. It had been a long-time coming, overworking herself to the brink of exhaustion that no amount of coffee, green juices and multi-vitamins could help keep at bay, and with the turning of the seasons as spring edged towards summer, the temperature still a little confused as it slipped between overcast showers and muggy heat, Lena knew she would be pushing her luck to go into the office. She was just thankful it was after the quarterly board meeting instead of before.

     

                With her mind reluctantly made up, she plodded back upstairs and messaged Jess to cancel her meetings and take the day for herself, before collapsing back into bed. Feverish and cold, she curled up beneath the blankets and was asleep before she knew it, her mind dragging her into unconsciousness as her leaden body sank into the wide mattress. The curtains blotted out the sunrise outside and Lena slept fitfully, a fever burning through her as she tossed and turned, the damp blankets twisting around her limbs.

     

                The incessant buzzing of her phone woke her up just before twelve. Groggy and hot, Lena struggled upright, blinking back sleep as she pinched the bridge of her nose and felt on the end table for her phone. She didn’t check who it was before answering it and pressing it to her ear.

     

                “Hello?” she rasped, her voice husky and hoarse.

     

                “You sound awful. Are you okay?”

     

                Lena eased herself back down onto her pile of pillows, half-propped up with the blankets in a pool across her waist, as Kara’s soothing voice washed over her. 

     

                “Yeah, I just- I guess I’m a bit drained. I think I’m coming down with something.”

     

                “Are you okay? What is it? The flu? You didn’t go into work did you?”

     

                She smiled wanly at the worry in Kara’s voice, brushed damp strands of hair out of her face as sweat beaded along her hairline. Her pale cheeks were flushed with colour and Lena’s mouth was dry as she licked at her cracked lips.

     

                “Nothing serious; just a slight cold and a fever, I think. And no, I’m not at the office; even I’m not that selfish to spread the flu around to get some paperwork out of the way.”

     

                “Good. You need rest and fluids.”

     

                “Don’t worry,” Lena assured her, “I’ll be at Al’s tonight. Seven on the dot, as promised.”

     

                Kara let out a scoffing laugh on the other end of the phone. “Like hell you will! You better stay in bed; I’ll be right over once my shift finishes.”

     

                “No, no, go out with your friends. I’ll be fine, I promise,” Lena pleaded, her voice scratchy, making her dissolve into a bout of coughing.

     

                “They’ll understand. Besides, you should have someone to look after you when you’re sick.”

     

                Sighing, knowing it was a lost cause to argue, Lena conceded the point. “Okay. Okay, I’ll see you later then. Have a good day.”

     

                “Stay in bed. I mean it.”

     

                “Yes, boss.”

     

                With a quiet chuckle, shot through with relief and a little bit of worry, Kara sighed. “Okay. Now I really have to go.”

     

                “Okay,” Lena murmured. “Bye.”

     

                “Love you, bye.”

     

                There was a second of silence as the words hung heavily between them, Lena’s lips parting in surprise, while she waited for Kara to say something, to retract it or laugh it off. And then the line went dead and Lena frowned with a faint smile playing on the corners of her mouth as she looked down at the dark screen of her phone. Her heart stumbled in her chest as a flush of warmth washed over her feverish skin, an almost giddy feeling in her chest.

     

                After a few minutes of sitting with it, Lena dragged herself out of bed and into the shower, standing beneath the lukewarm stream of water as her whole body fought against the effort of staying upright. Dressing in clean loungewear, she made her way downstairs and was halfway down the bottom flight when the front door opened and her housekeeper stepped inside with her arms laden with bags.

     

                They looked at each other for a moment, both surprised, as Lena had forgotten she would be there, and her housekeeper was unused to seeing her there during the daytime. Giving her a crooked smile as she clutched the bannister and trudged down the rest of the steps, Lena raked a hand through her wet hair.

     

                “Hi, Eve.”

     

                “Miss Luthor. Sorry, I thought you’d be at work today.”

     

                Waving a hand, Lena’s cheek twitched with a half-smile. “I think I’m coming down with something. You can take the day if there’s nothing urgent. I don’t want you to catch it.”

     

                “Oh, no, it’s okay. I’ve just got your grocery shopping and I’m picking up the laundry; I’ll leave the vacuuming so you can rest.”

     

                Nodding as she smiled slightly with gratitude, Lena blinked and stepped forward, “here, let me give you a hand.”

     

                “No, no, you go on ahead, ma’am.”

     

                “It’s fine,” Lena assured her, taking a full bag and then relieving her of another before walking to the kitchen.

     

                She set them down on the counter and then refilled her water from the fridge, swallowing another two pills to take the edge off her headache. It did little for the fever and her congested head, which throbbed in sync with her heartbeat, and her hand trembled slightly as she pressed her palm to her forehead and closed her eyes.

     

                Eve worked around her, stowing vegetables in specific drawers and shelves, refilling containers with new bags of muesli and kale chips and other snack foods. She actually had the chance to refill some of the untouched containers now that Kara was over often, making good use of the kitchen as she taught Lena some of the basics, even though she was still mostly banned from helping.

     

                The sun was harsh outside and Lena couldn’t bear to turn around, leaning against the counters as she drank her water and cast furtive glances at her housekeeper. This was the longest the two of them had ever been in the same room, and she felt uncomfortable in her own house as she watched the blonde woman go about her duties. 

     

                “Are you feeling okay? Can I get you anything?” Eve asked after their eyes met as she folded all the tote bags inside one of them.

     

                Giving her a quick smile, Lena nodded, “I’m fine. Thank you, Eve.”

     

                “I’ll just get the laundry and be out of your hair then.”

     

                “Thank you. And, hey, Eve .. thank you for the chilli last night. It was delicious.”

     

                Beaming, Eve nodded and left her to it, her footsteps vanishing upstairs to Lena’s bedroom to raid the laundry basket. Refilling her glass at the sink, Lena sipped it slowly and waited for the footsteps to come back down, looking up as Eve poked her head in through the open archway.

     

                “Feel better soon. And let me know if you want me to pick you up anything from the store.”

     

                “Thanks, Eve. Have a good weekend.”

     

                The door shut a few moments later and Lena walked up to the fourth floor to claim her laptop from the work table where she’d been parked all night combing through blueprints and schematics before she went back down to her bedroom to work from the comfort of her own bed.

     

                Stepping inside, she smiled slightly at the turned-down sheets, a draft of fresh air worming through the heavy drapes through the open windows, and eased the door shut with her foot. Slipping in between the smoothed sheets, Lena logged in and read through her emails, responding to one off Sam and asking Jess to reschedule one of the meetings for the free slot on her schedule next Tuesday.

     

                The hours slipped by easily, spent laid out in bed sipping sparingly from her water as hunger evaded her and her body alternated between the sweats and intense shivering that couldn’t be dissuaded by the thick blankets and the heating wafting from the vents.

     

                She didn’t even realise how late it had gotten until there was a muffled knock from the front door downstairs. Glancing at the clock, Lena realised it must’ve been Kara and she tumbled out of bed, moving quickly despite herself, and was rounding the bottom of the second staircase when the door opened.

     

                “Hello?” Kara called out.

     

                Lena smiled as she stepped onto the top step, the wood groaning beneath her feet, and she wrapped her arms around herself, feeling cold even as her feverish cheeks and bright eyes told a different story.

     

                “Hi,” she rasped, her voice deep and quiet.

     

                Descending the steps, she moved over to Kara, who was still in her fatigues and carrying a brown paper bag. A tender look of concern softened her face and she clucked her tongue as she took in Lena’s dishevelled appearance. “Oh, you don’t look well at all.”

     

                Lena grimaced and rolled her eyes as she stepped off the staircase and Kara met her at the bottom, reaching out to lay her cool hand against her burning forehead. Eyes fluttering closed at how soothing it felt, Lena’s lips twitched with a smile.

     

                “You’ve got a raging fever. Have you taken anything for it?”

     

                Shrugging, Lena rubbed a hand over her face, “just Tylenol.”

     

                “And for your cold?”

     

                Shaking her head, Lena gave her a wry smile, “I don’t get sick.”

     

                “Oh, honey, well you are now. You should’ve stayed in bed; you look white as a ghost.”

     

                “I think that’s just my normal complexion, actually,” Lena said with a droll smile.

     

                Kara gave her an exasperated look, hefting the bag in her arms to shoo her with the other hand. “Come on. Do you want me to make you a bed on the sofa, or are you going back upstairs?”

     

                “Sofa.”

     

                Shuffling into the living room, Lena muffled her coughs with the crook of her elbow and stood by with a peculiar expression on her face as Kara moved the decorative pillows out of the way, retreating upstairs to a spare room and coming back with thick pillows as she made up a small bed for Lena, facing the TV.

     

                Lena watched on with a peculiar expression on her face, amused and bewildered, lips pressed into a flat line as her eyebrows drew together and her cheeks dimpled. Kara raised her eyebrows expectantly as she caught the look on her face.

     

                “What is it?”

     

                With a strained smile, vaguely embarrassed as she looked away, lacing her fingers behind her neck, Lena let out a huff of laughter. “It’s nothing, I just- no one’s ever looked after me when I’ve been sick before.”

     

                Kara reached out to guide her down onto the sofa, shaking out the throw blanket as she pursed her lips in a troubled look. “Never?”

     

                “The nuns weren’t exactly caring at boarding school, and … well, my mom wasn’t very maternal so …”

     

                Tucking her in, Kara gave her a sad smile, pity flashing in her blue eyes, and ducked down to kiss Lena’s burning brow. She wrinkled her nose as she pulled back with an apologetic look on her face. “Sorry, I can’t risk getting sick. And … you have me to look after you now.”

     

                A slight smile twitched Lena’s lips as she closed her eyes, “that’s a new feeling for me.”

     

                “Lucky for you, I have the best remedy for being sick.”

     

                Opening her eyes to slits, Lena let out a quiet laugh, “oh yeah?”

     

                “Mhm. First things first, you need electrolytes. I wasn’t sure what Powerade flavour you preferred so I got a red and blue one. More Tylenol. Zinc lozenges. Echinacea tea - I’m assuming you have honey. Obviously chicken noodle soup. A book and trashy magazines. Oh, and an orange; vitamin C is good for you.”

     

                Growing more touched and amused with each revealed item, neatly stacked on the coffee table, Lena couldn’t help but smile, watching as Kara lined them all up and then crumpled the paper bag. 

     

                “Thank you,” Lena murmured, her voice thick with emotion as she reached out to brush Kara’s arm. 

     

                “Here, have a drink,” Kara murmured, picking up the bottles and waving them both, “which one?”

     

                “Red.”

     

                Nodding, Kara set the blue bottle down and twisted off the cap before handing it to Lena. Taking a sip, she watched as Kara opened the pack of lozenges and popped one out, handing the little wrapped square to Lena. Putting the lid back on the bottle, Lena set it on the floor beside her and unwrapped the lozenge, the taste of cherry on her tongue as she popped it in her mouth.

     

                “Right, I’ll go and warm your soup up. I’m going to assume you haven’t eaten anything today?”

     

                At Lena’s sheepish expression, she sighed and shook her head, muttering under her breath as she carried the plastic container and tea out of the room with her. Reaching over to the coffee table, Lena picked up the book and read the title. All the Lives We Ever Lived: Seeking Solace in Virginia Woolf. A memoir. Then she reached for the magazine, her eyes scanning the front page before she flipped through and found a quiz on personality types.

     

                Kara returned a few minutes later with a steaming bowl of chicken noodle in one hand and a mug of tea in the other. Glancing up from the magazine, Lena gave her a scrutinising look as Kara set the tea down on the coffee table.

     

                “What personality type are you?”

     

                “What?”

     

                “Personality type. There’s a quiz,” Lena said, tapping the magazine.

     

                Kara took it from her lap and set the bowl of soup in its place before sitting at Lena’s feet and letting her put them in her lap. Shaking out the magazine, Kara read it for a few minutes, tallying up points as Lena spooned soup into her mouth.

     

                “Type D,” Kara declared after a few minutes. “What did you get?”

     

                “Type A.”

     

                Kara’s eyes found the section and she let out a quiet laugh, “yeah, that sounds about right.”

     

                Scoffing and then dissolving into coughs as she held her bowl up out of harm’s way, Lena gave her a narrow-eyed look of doubt.

     

                “What’s that supposed to mean?”

     

                “Workaholic. Ambitious. Dominant. Stubborn.”

     

                Rolling her eyes, Lena took another sip of soup and jerked her chin towards Kara. “What’d it say about you?”

     

                “Compassionate. Dependable. Stable. Consistent. Wow, these are some great qualities.”

     

                “They are,” Lena lightly replied, her face softening as she reached out a hand. “Now, let me do the fashion style quiz.”

     

                Handing it over, Kara turned the TV on and flipped through the channels before settling on a home renovation one. After a few minutes, she slipped away to shower and put her uniform in the laundry before returning in pyjamas and settling down beside Lena.

     

                Spending the rest of the evening fussing over her, making sure she ate all of her soup, took pills as soon as she could and drank her tea with honey, Kara was restless and a little distracted. She’d made a quick dinner of pasta for herself, goading Lena into having a small bowl full, but she’d picked at it with a brooding look on her face. Lena watched and waited, drinking her Powerade and throat lozenges, the scratchy feeling soothed, while she made some headway into the book.

     

                It was nearly ten o’clock and Lena was sweating beneath the blankets, even as her teeth chattered and her heavy eyes slipped closed. Kara kept replacing the warm damp cloth on her brow after wringing it out in cold water, softly murmuring to Lena as her fingertips brushed her cheeks.

     

                “Hey,” Lena eventually said, her voice a low murmur as her lips trembled. Her eyes were closed and she couldn’t look at Kara as she spoke. “We can talk about it. It’s eating you up, I can tell.”

     

                With a soft sigh, Kara kissed her brow and sat back down at her feet, rubbing at her tired eyes as she leaned back in the seat. Letting out a small groan of laughter, Kara shook her head and pressed her lips together.

     

                “About the phone?”

     

                “Mm.”

     

                “I’ve been trying to pretend that you didn’t hear it,” Kara sheepishly replied, her voice small and shy.

     

                Lena cracked open an eye and looked at her, taking in her rosy cheeks and the helpless look of embarrassment. Kara rubbed at a spot above her eyebrow as she ducked her head and shrugged noncommittally.

     

                “Sorry, I just- I don’t want to make you uncomfortable by coming on too strong. You can just … forget I said it.”

     

                Giving her a confused look, Lena pushed herself up, removing the cloth from her brow, and gave Kara a small smile as she reached out to lay a heavy hand on her arm.

     

                “Don’t apologise,” Lena murmured, “please never apologise to me for how you feel, okay? I- I want you to be honest with me, and I don’t want you to ever feel like you can’t tell me things because of … well, how I am. And I’ll always be honest with you too, which is why I- I hope you can understand that I … need more time.”

     

                “Yeah, no, of course,” Kara said with a crooked smile, “I don’t want you to think that you have to say it back. We both know how much I like to overuse the word, and I know it’s different for you.”

     

                “Okay,” Lena hedged, “but … how did you mean it. Because you say it about … everything, and you know I do care about you too but … are you saying- do you … love me or is it just … because I know that I love you. That’s easy. But what we’re saying is …”

     

                With a pained look on her face, Kara reached for Lena’s hand and cradled it in hers, kissing her knuckles as she stared at her. “I’m in love with you, so … yes, it’s different. I love you, and you can take your time. As much as you need to figure things out. I just- I’m not very good at keeping my feelings to myself - maybe it’s a byproduct of my job, but … I just don’t like wasting time.”

     

                Lena’s eyes prickled slightly at Kara’s admission of the truth, and her throat tightened as an ache flared to life in her chest. No one had ever said those words to her before in a way that had ever held any conviction, and it was an unfamiliar feeling. Smiling, Lena raised their entwined hands and pressed a kiss to the back of Kara’s.

     

                “Thank you. I- I know I’m not the … easiest person to love.”

     

                Kara was already shaking her head before Lena could even finish speaking, her lips curling into a bewildered half-smile and she let her fingertips rest against Lena’s cheek as she looked at her with piercing sincerity.

     

                “No. Loving people is one of the only things I know how to do well, and loving you? It’s one of the easiest things in the world. Easier than breathing. I promise you that it is not … difficult or- or hard. Okay?”

     

                “Okay,” Lena whispered, her voice cracking slightly.

     

                She tried to brush it off as the urge to cough, clearing her throat as she quickly swiped her hand across her eyes before settling down on the pillows and letting the fluttering in her chest ease her doubts. Making her more tea, Kara returned and climbed over her, settling down beside Lena as she enveloped her in a hug, kissing her cheek and soothingly rubbing her arm as Lena sniffed and they watched TV in silence.

     

                Kara ended up staying over that night to make sure Lena had someone to look after her, and they went to bed not long after their conversation, Lena’s eyes heavy-lidded from the drowsy side-effects of the pills, and Kara needing to get up early in the morning. 

     

                Lena tossed and turned all night, guiltily keeping Kara up as she alternated between kicking off the blankets, sweating buckets, and then shivering so violently as she burrowed up against her that Kara woke to the clammy feeling of her at her back. Still, she didn’t complain in the slightest, wrapping her in her arms when Lena was cold and ensuring the covers were off her when she woke to her restless shifting as Lena muttered to herself, eyes rolling beneath closed lids.

     

                Half-asleep, Kara would whisper quiet reassurances to her, picking up the glass of water on the end table and making her take sips when Lena was lucid, and more pills in the early hours of the morning. She would be exhausted at work, but Kara cared more about Lena than her lack of sleep.

     

                It didn’t stop the dark circles from appearing beneath her eyes though, and when her alarm went off at five o’clock, she sighed listlessly, pushing herself up. Lena woke with the sound of it too, her fever breaking sometime during the night, and while she still felt awful, she was marginally better than yesterday and wracked with guilt at the exhaustion on Kara’s face.

     

                With the enticing offer of borrowing her Tesla to drive into work, Lena managed to coax Kara back to bed for a while longer, and as she fell asleep quickly, Lena remained awake, staying as still as possible as she let Kara sleep. She took full advantage of the comforting feeling of being in the arms of someone who loved her, and soon enough, she drifted off again too.

    Chapter 16

                The Thursday evening before the gala, Lena was stepping into the small designer boutique that she’d made Jess pull a few strings to open for her after hours, smiling at the attendant as Kara, Alex and Kelly filed in after her. Setting her handbag down beside a small loveseat, Lena shed her coat and turned to look at the other women, who were all looking around with apprehension.

     

                “I took the liberty of putting a rack together with all of our best pieces,” the woman said, wheeling it out to the middle of the small store. “Can I offer you refreshments?”

     

                Lena accepted the glass of sparkling water and stepped up to Kara, who was already rifling through the array of dresses. There was a growing look of trepidation on her face and Lena gave her arm a squeeze as she raised her eyebrows encouragingly.

     

                “See anything you like?”

     

                Eyes widening a fraction as she flipped a price tag over, Kara leant in to Lena, her voice hushed as she replied. “Lena, this dress is a thousand dollars; none of us can afford this.”

     

                Pressing her hand against Kara’s back, Lena smiled slightly at her scandalised tone, “you don’t have to - I’m paying.”

     

                “I can’t let you do that.”

     

                Sighing, Lena grimaced, “at the risk of sounding too snobby, I won’t comment on the prices, but … would it help to know that these dresses are the product of sustainable fashion? The designer also made the outfit I’m wearing, and it’ll be good publicity for the company so …”

     

                “No one will be looking at us; they’ll be too focused on you.”

     

                Tugging a soft velvet dress out, eyeing the deep burgundy and thin straps, Lena smiled. “Not if you’re wearing this.”

     

                Pursing her lips, Kara eyed the dress and Lena took it off the rack. “At least try it on.”

     

                Sighing, Kara took the dress off her and fixed her with an exasperated look. Grinning, Lena took a seat on the loveseat, sipping her sparkling water as Kara moved towards a changing room at the back. Glancing over at Alex and Kelly, who were busy whispering over other dresses, Lena was content to wait for them to choose.
