                After an hour of combing through the racks, and Kara relenting and settling on the dress Lena had picked out, they left the shop with a bag each - save for Lena, who already had hers sorted out - and went to a nearby bistro for dinner. 

     

                Lena was tired after a day of busy planning for the charity gala, on top of her usual workload and the lingering symptoms of her cold that she couldn’t seem to shake, and she went home afterwards. Kara went with her and they watched TV in bed, the curtains drawn and the lamps on as Lena pores over paperwork and Kara flipped through a borrowed book.

     

                Friday was a blur and Lena was stuck at the office late, which meant that she didn’t see Kara all day, or the morning after. She stayed at Lena’s place a few times a week now, evidence of her scattered throughout the house in the signs of a spare toothbrush in the holder in the bathroom, one of her shirts found beneath Lena’s bed where it had accidentally been kicked, and her preferred brand of oat milk in the fridge. It was a surprisingly easy adjustment, Lena barely even recognising that Kara spent nearly half of the week at her apartment, cooking dinner and watering her plants and working out in her gym in the basement. Somehow, it didn’t feel like an intrusion; it felt like some life had been breathed into the house.

     

                She missed her that Friday night, the bed feeling cold and empty with so much space to herself, and Lena woke on Saturday morning tired from a restless night. As busy as her day was, all the last minute arrangements needing to be overseen as Jess conferred with her mother on her behalf, Lena had promised Kara breakfast.

     

                Driving to a small café in Chinatown, near Alex’s place, Lena stepped into the narrow place wedged in alongside the faded signs of Chinese businesses. A faded sign for Coca-Cola was stuck on the window outside, which was obscured with a layer of bacon grease and fryer oil inside. The floor was peeling linoleum that the chair dragged on as she pulled it out, leaning across to kiss Kara.

     

                The coffee they ordered was caustic and Kara ordered eggs, putting ketchup on the scrambled mass as the grey light filtering through the grimy windows cast a sallow light over the diner. Kara’s cerulean eyes were flinty, her hair a dishwater blonde and the circles under her eyes lavender as it washed the golden tan from her skin.

     

                Sitting across from her, Lena watched as Kara poured too much creamer in her coffee and was startled by the thought that crossed her mind. Stiffening slightly in her chair as the unbidden thought of how much she loved Kara crossed her mind, Lena looked at her with parted lips and tender surprise in her green eyes.

     

                Looking up, Kara caught her staring and smiled sweetly as she picked her coffee up and held it in her palms. And for a moment, Lena thought she was brave enough to say it, until she took too long and the moment passed. Reaching across the table with her fork, Lena stole a mouthful of eggs and winked as she pulled back chewing, Kara letting out a laugh as she set her cup back down. 

     

                Lena realised she never wanted to go another day without hearing that laugh. Kara was simply more alive than anyone she’d ever met, and as she sat with the weight of her revelation sitting comfortably in her heart, Lena was content with taking her time; she had all the time in the world to say it.

     

                She had to run after breakfast, an apologetic smile on her lips as she kissed Kara quickly as she dropped her off outside Alex’s after insisting on driving her home. The rest of her morning and lunchtime was spent overseeing the arrangements of flowers around the open venue hall, watching as a stream of caterers rushed through the lobby, led towards the kitchens by Jess and the venue coordinator and debated the position of the stage and podium.

     

                By the time Lena left to shower before her hair and makeup appointments, she was weary and mildly stressed, wondering if she should have opted for cotton napkins instead of linen and if the white flowers were too muted with the almost austere minimise of the large room. Lillian would no doubt voice her opinions when she inevitably tracked Lena down later on in the evening, but so far she’d been able to avoid all her calls about it.

     

                Trying to push it to the back of her mind, Lena allowed herself a break to relax as her hair was made into neat waves and her makeup applied with the tickling touch of a dozen brushes. She was running late by the time she changed into the charcoal grey dress, of a similar style to Kara’s but satin and shorter. Her lipstick was a deep crimson that would match though, as were her nails, and she couldn’t help but smile as she thought of Kara, eager to see her in the dress again.

     

                Her car was already waiting outside and as soon as she was done, Lena slid into the back with a quick apology to her driver before they set off through the city. The sleek car stopped outside ten minutes later than the promised time and Lena was a little flustered as she rang the buzzer and Kelly let her upstairs.

     

                She held a bouquet of burgundy calla lilies in hand and the elevator let her out on Alex’s floor, she cleared her throat and knocked on the door. It only took a moment for Kara to open it, a bright smile on her face as she gave Lena an appraising look, her blonde hair twisted into a messy chignon and her face surprisingly bare of her glasses.

     

                “You look beautiful,” Kara said by way of greeting, leaning in to carefully kiss Lena, trying not to get red lipstick on her mouth.

     

                “So do you. But no glasses?”

     

                Nose crinkling, Kara shrugged, waving her inside, “I thought it’d be a nice change for tonight. I rarely get to dress up like this.”

     

                “We should find more reasons to do it more often,” Lena murmured, easing the door closed. “These are for you, by the way.”

     

                Kara beamed as she reached for the flowers, a perfect complement to her dress. “They’re beautiful, thank you.”

     

                “Not in comparison to you.”

     

                The smile on her face wavered for a second before she turned around and made for the kitchen to set the flowers in a vase. Lena’s skin prickled with wary unease as she moved through the apartment after Kara, the muffled voices of Alex and Kelly coming from behind a closed door, and her face clouded with worry as she lowered her voice.

     

                “Hey, is … everything okay?”

     

                Shutting off the tap, Kara turned to give Lena a bright smile, the earlier look gone so fast that Lena almost believed she’d imagined it.

     

                “Fine! I just- I had to go into work earlier for a bit so I’m running behind. Sorry.”

     

                “Oh. Well, that’s no problem. We’re not in a rush,” Lena assured her with a gentle smile.

     

                Nodding, Kara set the flowers in the vase and then clapped her hands together as she turned with a sheepish smile on her face. “Five minutes, I promise. Do you want a drink while you wait?”

     

                Waving a hand dismissively, Lena moved over to the sofa and took a seat. Fiddling with the diamond necklace around her throat, she brooded in silence, unsure what was unnerving her, only that Kara seemed off. There was a slight tension to her shoulders, an almost guilty tautness to her face as she looked at Lena. 

     

                Pushing it aside, Lena patiently waited, listening to the muffled remarks of three women vying for the bathroom mirror before they all filed out five minutes later. Falling into easy conversation, compliments doled out freely to each of them, they all piled into the elevator and then out into Lena’s car.

     

                By the time they reached the venue, photographers were already milling about outside while reporters lurked about, scribbling down details of the event to spin a story out of. Most of the guests were already there, composed of a few high-ranking L-Corp employees, local socialites and celebrities as well as a host of the wealthy and upper class, on a scale of new millionaires to old money billionaires.

     

                Her driver opened the door and held out a white-gloved hand to help her out, and Lena was momentarily dazzled by the cameras, the excitement of the president of the Luthor’s charity fund having arrived drawing them closer. Tossing her hair back, Lena eyed the cameras with disdain before reaching a hand out for Kara, who stepped out behind her.

     

                “Just ignore them,” Lena murmured, her head close to Kara’s as her lips barely moved.

     

                Squeezing Kara’s hand, Lena quickly breezed past the reporters, snatches of questions and the sound of her own name falling on deaf ears. There were a few bystanders too, including one man who shot her a look of pure hatred, stepping forward, only to be stopped by security. He spat at Lena’s feet but she didn’t even look at him. Doormen opened the glass doors to the foyer and Lena stepped inside to the background strains of classical music.

     

                Letting out a pent up breath, Lena’s stiff posture relaxed minutely as she turned to give the three women strained smiles of apology. “Sorry about that.”

     

                “So, I guess that’ll be on the front page tomorrow, huh?” Alex asked.

     

                “Probably,” Lena sighed. “It’s the first time it’s ever been held in National City. And only the second since filling my brother’s shoes.”

     

                The sympathetic looks given to her only made Lena grimmer. It was no surprise that she hated the lack of privacy afforded to her in such public settings. Usually, Lena could avoid it for the most part, aside from the occasional photographer parked outside L-Corp when they were releasing something big, but it was still tedious when the moments occurred.

     

                “How about a drink?” Lena sighed, gesturing towards the wide-open doorway of the ballroom.

     

                Weaving their way through the throngs of people, they were soon set upon by a server holding a tray of champagne flutes. Snagging one, Lena drained half of her glass in one mouthful, aware of the stares sent her way as people took note of her arrival.

     

                “Hey, easy,” Alex cautioned her.

     

                “I really hate these things,” Lena grumbled, draining the rest of her glass and setting it down on the closest standing table, a few people already clustered around it.

     

                Looping her arm through Kara’s, Lena’s eyes restlessly darted around the room, an anxious look in them as she swallowed. Kara didn’t have to ask to know that Lena was trying to spot her mother, and when she stiffened a moment later, Kara followed her line of sight to single out the woman she was staring at.

     

                With a look of curiosity on her face, Kara’s head tilted to the side as she surveyed Lillian. “That’s your mom?” Kara whispered in surprise.

     

                “Mm,” Lena sourly hummed, tugging on Kara’s arm, “let’s go this way.”

     

                “Your mom’s kind of hot,” Alex whispered, scandalised.

     

                Kelly ribbed her as she snorted with laughter and Lena shot them both a withering look. Giving her a sheepish smile, Alex shrugged. “We’ll leave you to … mingle,” Alex said with an airy wave of her hand. “I see canapés over there.”

     

                Nodding distractedly, Lena pulled Kara through the room, snagging herself another glass of champagne as they passed by a server dressed in white. People turned to nod and raise their glasses at her, calling out gratings and stepping into Lena’s path to steal a few minutes of her time. Forcing herself to relax, to be polite and charming, Lena smiled and made witty remarks and introduced each of them to Kara in turn, a challenge in her green eyes as she smiled sharply.

     

                Managing to shake off the crowd after the first round, Lena found Jess in a corner, talking to Sam, and Lena steered Kara towards them.

     

                “Please tell me it’s going well,” Lena sighed as she pressed her lips into a flat line.

     

                “I think we’re going to beat last year’s sum,” Jess encouragingly replied.

     

                Exhaling, Lena nodded and took a sip of champagne before blinking and turning to Sam. “Oh, sorry, hi, Sam. This is Kara, my girlfriend. Kara, this is Sam, my CFO.”

     

                Recognition lit up Kara’s blue eyes and she smiled brightly as she thrust out a hand. “It’s good to meet you; Lena’s told me a lot about you.”

     

                “Really?” Sam said with disbelief.

     

                Rolling her eyes, Lena licked her red lips, eyes still warily darting about, and finished off her champagne. “Of course I have,” Lena brusquely replied.

     

                “Oh. Well, I’m sorry, Kara, but we haven’t heard much about you. Our boss is a little bit mysterious at work,” Sam said in a stage whisper, her hazel eyes shining with amusement. “It’s like pulling teeth trying to get her to talk about anything other than work.”

     

                With a quiet laugh, Kara eyed Lena, who flushed with indignation, and pressed her hand against her back. “Maybe we all need to go out for drinks one night then, so we can talk about something else,” Kara said with a smile.

     

                “Well we’re not at work now,” Lena said, “so, Sam, how’s your daughter doing?”

     

                Kara lingered on the edges of the conversation, uncharacteristically quiet as she let Lena do all the talking for once, playing the part of host as she kept the talk of L-Corp to a minimum. It was fascinating to watch the change, the confidence and directness at odds with the gentler, sadder version of Lena that lived in Kara’s mind. She enjoyed it though, shaking hands with the big shot CEOs of recognisable brands as they bragged about the big donations they’d made towards the charity.

     

                Platters of food circulated through the room at regular intervals and Lena fought back a smile at the look of delight on Kara’s face when she noticed the dumpling Lena had added to the menu especially for her. All the while, Lena stayed on the move, circling as she kept Kara beside her as a buffer, occasionally catching sight of Alex and Kelly and stopping to make sure they were okay.

     

                After a little more than an hour of chatter and canapés, the crowd was directed towards a large dining room and guests were seated at their name cards. With a sheepish look on her face, Lena directed everyone to a table occupied by acquaintances she could stomach spending three courses with, including Jess and Sam, keeping it to herself that she should’ve been sitting at the table with their mother and the board.

     

                “Andrea,” Lena curtly greeted a woman as she took her seat, shaking out the linen napkin and draping it over her lap. “I was shocked to hear you would be here.”

     

                “Lena. Long time,” Andrea drawled, her eyes shifting over the three women seating themselves beside her. Narrowing her eyes slightly, she smiled as she pointed at Kara. “And you must be the girlfriend.”

     

                With a bright smile, Kara rose halfway from her seat to shake hands with Andrea. “Kara.”

     

                “A pleasure.”

     

                “Um, how do you two know each other?” Kara cautiously asked.

     

                “Boarding school,” Lena said as her lips twisted slightly. “Andrea is my oldest friend.”

     

                “She says that but this is the first time I’ve seen her in five years,” Andrea said with a reproving stare.

     

                Rolling her eyes, Lena turned to give Kara a thin smile, “never go into business with friends.”

     

                The conversation became more relaxed as the table filled, Jack Spheer making an appearance and sitting beside Andrea’s fiancé, the only two men at the table. It was a strange gathering of people, but Lena would rather wade through business talk for the next two hours, as opposed to sitting beside her mother as she tried to show an interest in Lena’s life.

     

                The first course of var salmon with grapefruit, fennel and radish passed by quickly and Lena barely picked at her food. Her appetite eluded her and she sipped slowly at her wine instead, careful not to toe the line of intoxication, but needing something to distract herself with as she paid little attention to the conversation. 

     

                Occasionally, Kara would set her hand on Lena’s knee for a brief moment as if comforting her, and Lena would turn to Sam on her right and ask her a question, or enquire about Andrea’s wedding plans or Jack’s new venture into medicine, now that he’d sold Spheerical Industries over to her.

     

                The second course was lamb with caramelised shallots, mint and peas, and Lena managed to get half of it down but gave her dessert of apricot soufflé with almond ice cream to Kara to finish off. Once the plates were cleared away, Lena sighed and resigned herself to another hour of mingling before it was time for her speech and then she could slip away. Climbing to her feet, she took Kara’s hand in hers and followed the trickle of guests back across to the ballroom. 

     

                As she stepped out of the dining room, Lena softly cursed and turned around, trying to duck out of the flow of people before Lillian could see her. Kara made a quiet sound of protest as Lena tried to hide behind the bulk of a tall man she thought might’ve been a local football player, wincing slightly as he walked right past her. As a last resort, Lena tried to hide behind Kara too, but it was no use.

     

                “Don’t let her see you,” Lena hissed, tugging Kara along as she ducked her head down.

     

                “I flew all this way and my own daughter can’t even take the time to say hello to her mother.”

     

                Lena tensed up at the sound of Lillian’s voice behind her and slowly turned around as she dropped Kara’s hand. Exhaling through her nose as her eyes shuttered, Lena pursed her lips before finally meeting Lillian’s eyes.

     

                “Mom.”

     

                “You didn’t sit at our table for dinner; I was hoping to talk to you.”

     

                With a small shrug, Lena looked away, trying not to look too much like a sullen teenager as she folded her arms over her chest. She hated that her mother was able to bring that out in her, even though Lena hadn’t lived at home in years. 

     

                “I’m busy tonight,” Lena murmured, “whatever you have to say can wait. I’ll call you tomorrow; we can arrange a meeting.”

     

                Letting out a soft chuckle, Lillian smiled widely as she arched an eyebrow, “no you won’t. You can’t even be bothered to pick up the phone when I call you.”

     

                “Yeah, well, like I said; I’m busy.”

     

                “Mm, right. With your girlfriend, I presume?” Lillian asked, her attention drawn to Kara, who lingered behind Lena, restless with uncertainty. 

     

                Giving her a cool, appraising look, Lillian smiled faintly as Kara stepped around Lena and held her hand out. “Kara Danvers, ma’am,” Kara introduced herself.

     

                Briefly shaking her hand, the amusement on Lillian’s face only seemed to grow as her attention fell back on her daughter. Kara swallowed thickly, rubbing her palms together as she anxiously eyed Lena, wondering if she should slip away and remove herself from the awkwardness of the conversation, or if she should stick it out beside Lena for support.

     

                “Well … I’m surprised. This is the first time you’ve ever brought a date to one of our galas. It must be serious.”

     

                “What do you have to say?” Lena bluntly asked, a weariness to her face as she tilted her head to the side and gave her mother an expectant look. “If you’re here to fish for information about my relationship, I’m not going to bite. So just say your piece and go.”

     

                Looking mildly taken aback, Lillian gave her a reproving look and arched an eyebrow. “What? Am I not allowed to say hello?”

     

                “You never just say hello. And you’ve always made such a show of keeping your distance that I’m surprised you’d even want to.”

     

                Clicking her tongue, Lillian’s mouth thinned with disapproval as she reached out to brush a strand of Lena’s hair back into place. It was almost a maternal gesture, but Lena knew her mother was lacking in that department. 

     

                “It’s not fair for you to put all the blame on me; I’ve tried to reach out to you and make amends. And you chose to move the company’s headquarters all the way out here, making it nigh on impossible to see you anymore.”

     

                “Oh, please,” Lena scoffed, clenching her teeth, “don’t act like you’re so cut up about your estranged daughter. You’re only here for the gala; I bet you’ve got the jet booked for tomorrow morning.”

     

                “Well, of course; business comes first. But that doesn’t mean I don’t want to see you. We could get breakfast at the hotel-”

     

                “I don’t want breakfast, mom,” Lena tightly replied, a flush of frustration adding some colour to her cheeks as she tried to maintain her composure. 

     

                Lillian looked genuinely wounded for a brief moment, opening her mouth to speak before her eyes caught on someone behind them and she straightened slightly, a placid smile on her lips as she beckoned. “The photographer’s here; make sure you smile this time. All the press could focus on last year was how miserable you looked.”

     

                Scowling, Lena forced herself to uncross her arms and turned to face the woman approaching with a large camera in her hands. Suppressing a sigh, she smiled faintly as she stood beside her mother, both of them looking decidedly uncomfortable, hands clasped in front as Lena was dwarfed by Lillian’s stature.

     

                “Maybe … a little closer?” the photographer suggested.

     

                Lena bit back a complaint and shifted an inch closer, her smile tight as the camera flash blinded her. She reflexively took a step back as soon as it was over, looking at the tiled floor as she blinked rapidly. Unfortunately, her mother had more ideas.

     

                “Miss Danvers, perhaps you’d like some photos?” Lillian suggested.

     

                Taken aback at the suggestion, she looked at Lena with a wary look on her face as she hesitated. Lena scoffed and quirked an eyebrow as she gave Lillian a wry smile. “What’s your angle?”

     

                “Why are you always looking for the worst in me?” Lillian admonished her, looking faintly peeved, even as she masked it with a tense smile. “Really, Lena, you’re so set on making me out to be this bad person. It’s a charity event, for God’s sake.”

     

                “So, what, good publicity? You’re going to exploit my relationship now?”

     

                With an exasperated sigh, Lillian fixed her daughter with a sharp look, a muscle twitching in her jaw as she lowered her voice. “Please, Lena. Can’t we just take some photos without making a fuss of it?”

     

                “Lena,” Kara murmured, gently laying a hand on her arm, “it’s fine. I’ll take the photo.”

     

                Looking at her, Lena’s gaze softened, the sharp set of her face relaxing into a warm look of affection. Swallowing thickly, hating every moment of it, she nodded and stepped up beside Lillian as she felt Kara press her hand against her back. It was comforting, solid , and Lena’s smile was more genuine as she ignored her mother’s presence. After a few flashes, she pulled away blinking.

     

                “Okay, that’s enough.”

     

                Fixing her with a long stare, piercing and intimidating to Kara, who nervously stood by, Lillian let out a faint sigh and reached out to touch Lena’s arm for a fleeting moment. Her voice was curt and aloof as she spoke. “I’ll leave you to your night then.”

     

                Nodding, Lena looked down at the floor until Lillian vanished, and then she let out a pent up breath, deflating. “I’m sorry,” she murmured, looking up at Kara to give her a defeated look as her shoulders drooped.

     

                Reaching out to take her hand, Kara smiled unevenly, squeezing as she led Lena towards the door to the ballroom. “Hey, don’t worry about it. It wasn’t so bad. I mean, she ignored me for the most part, so I feel like I got off easy.”

     

                Giving her a grim smile of appreciation at the feeble attempt to lighten the mood, Lena squeezed Kara’s hand in return. “You actually did get off easy; she’s usually a lot more insufferable.”

     

                Lena looked up and deflated at the sight of Alex and Kelly making their way towards them. Holding out a glass of champagne, Alex gave her a sympathetic smile.

     

                “So, how was she?” Kelly quietly asked.

     

                “On her best behaviour,” Lena snorted, shaking her head and raising the glass to her lips. “Well, I have a speech to make in ten minutes, so I should probably go and find my publicist and assistant.”

     

                Touching Kara’s arm, Lena gave her a small smile, “you’ll be okay?”

     

                “Of course! Don’t worry about me. But good luck though.”

     

                Making a face, Lena let Kara kiss her on the cheek before she disappeared through the crowd. Taking a sip of champagne, she set her nearly full glass down, not wanting to be sloppy when she addressed everyone, and was tracked down by Jess, who always seemed to know her needs before Lena did.

     

                Running through the speech prepared for her off to the side of the stage, Lena waited until she was introduced a few minutes later by her mother. Lillian gave a glowing statement about the charity organisation and Lena, before she stood before the small podium and recited the words she’d memorised.

     

                Walking off to the sound of polite applause as she announced the figure raised from the generous donations and thanked everyone, Lena sagged as exhaustion washed over her. With one more quick circuit of the room, Lena sought out Kara and gave her a pleading look as she quietly asked her if they could leave.

     

                Bidding Alex and Kelly to stay awhile and enjoy the open bar, Lena hugged them both and found Jess before leaving to thank her for her help and give her Monday off. Whisking Kara through the lobby, Lena stepped out into the warm night and into the car waiting for her, buckling her seatbelt as she tipped her head back against the headrest.

     

                With a heavy sigh, Kara turned to look at her as the car pulled into traffic. “That was … eventful.”

     

                “Mm.”

     

                Lena looked up as Kara covered her hand with hers, a questioning look on her blue eyes. “Are you okay?”

     

                “Just tired,” Lena murmured, her voice rough with exhaustion.

     

                “So, your mom …”

     

                “Yeah. She’s a bit overbearing; I guess that’s what happens when you always get your own way.”

     

                “So, she just … what? I mean, does she actually want to see you or …”

     

                Closing her eyes, Lena swallowed thickly. “I don’t know. Honestly, I don’t really care. I spent most of my life without her in it; sometimes it feels like we’re strangers. And I know I’m supposed to love her because she’s my mom, but it’s just … how do you love someone who didn’t love you? Not until my brother died and she had an empty spot that she needed to fill. Now, it’s like … she’s so eager to know what I’m doing and to make up for what she missed and … I don’t like it. I made my peace with the fact that I’d never measure up to Lex years ago and it feels wrong to watch her try so hard. So now I just avoid her.”

     

                “Oh. Well … you’re not supposed to love anyone. Just so you know. So, just because she barely raised you … you don’t owe her anything.”

     

                Meeting Kara’s eyes, Lena straightened up, blinking back the heaviness in her eyes as her heart thudded in her chest. Opening her mouth, she drew in a shuddering breath and ran her thumb over Kara’s knuckles.

     

                “I-“ Lena hesitated, a lump in her throat that she couldn’t speak around, couldn’t bring herself to speak the words she’d never said to anyone in any way that was meaningful.

     

                Sighing, Lena deflated and slumped against the seat again as she smiled faintly, her eyes closing. Squeezing Kara’s fingers, she relinquished her hold on her.

     

                “Thank you for tonight,” Lena murmured. “You made it bearable.”

     

                “Of course,” Kara lightly replied.

     

                The rest of the drive back to Lena’s house was quiet and when her driver stopped outside, she quietly thanked him and slid out behind Kara. Fitting her key into the lock, she opened the front door and stepped into the empty house.

     

                “Mm, I can’t wait to get into bed,” Lena murmured, scrubbing a hand over her face as she kicked off her heels, her feet aching on the narrow rug after so long spent standing in the teetering stilettos.

     

                As she switched on a light and locked the door, Kara inhaled quickly and opened her mouth, clutching her purse in hand as she took a step towards Lena.

     

                “Can we- can we talk about something first?”

     

                Giving her a tired smile, droll and faintly amusement, Lena stretched her arms and sighed. “Are you finally going to tell me what’s been bothering you all night?”

     

                With a strained smile, Kara kicked her shoes off and raked a hand through her hair. Lena paused at the conflicted look on her face and quickly set her purse down on the sideboard beneath the gilt mirror, a panicked feeling in her chest that made her heart spasm.

     

                “Hey, it’s okay,” Lena murmured, crossing the few feet between them to cup Kara’s shoulders as she gave her a tender smile. “It’s been a long night; why don’t we wait until the morning?”

     

                Swallowing thickly as she hung her head, Kara let out a pent up breath and pinched the bridge of her nose. “No. No, I should tell you now. I- well, you know that I had to go to work earlier. It was just- it was because they wanted to let me know that I … got promoted.”

     

                “Promoted?” Lena echoed, her eyebrows rising a fraction as the corners of her lips curled upwards. “That- that’s amazing, right? You should’ve told me earlier! We could’ve celebrated more.”

     

                At the agonised expression on Kara’s face, as she bared her teeth in a pained look of defeat, Lena’s enthusiasm guttered as her stomach dropped. The smile on her lips wilted as her hands slid down Kara’s muscled arms to grip her biceps.

     

                “Isn’t it?” Lena asked, her voice pitching with uncertainty as her expression clouded.

     

                “I- yes, but … no. You- you don’t understand; I’ve been transferred. The new platoon ships out to Afghanistan in a month.”

     

                Kara’s miserable words took a moment to sink in, a slow look of understanding dawning on Lena’s face as dread settled over her, cold and all-encompassing. The blood drained from her face, leaving her ghostly pale, her dark lips parted and her eyes wide with disbelief. Her head pounded and her throat was painfully dry. Lena felt like throwing up and swallowed hard when her mouth filled with moisture, licking her lips as she shook her head.

     

                “No. No, no, this- this isn’t how it’s supposed to happen. You said we’d have a- a year. At least. We have months left.”

     

                Despite her iron will, Lena couldn’t fight back the tears that flooded her eyes as they breath gusted out of her, her chest so painfully tight that she had to resist the urge to sink to the floor and curl in on herself. Drawing in a shallow, quick breath, Lena’s bottom lip trembled as she looked away, blinking rapidly as a lump formed in her throat.

     

                “I’m sorry,” Kara apologised, her voice small and barely above a whisper, her chin dimpling with the effort it took not to cry, even as tears spilt down her cheeks.

     

                Choking on a suppressed sob, Lena squeezed her eyes shut and shook her head, the set of her face taut as she exhaled slowly. Opening her eyes, a silver sheen of tears making them bright, she looked at Kara with such gut-wrenching sorrow that Kara sagged where she stood, devastation written on her face. Crossing over to her, Lena wrapped her in a tight hug, holding her as if it was the last time.

     

                “It’s okay,” Lena whispered, her voice wavering even as she said it. She didn’t sound convinced at all as fear took root in her heart and left her trembling as she clung to Kara like a lifeline. “It’s okay, you don’t have to apologise. It’s not your fault.”

     

                “I know this isn’t what you wanted,” Kara whispered.

     

                “We knew it could happen. Eventually. We just- we were supposed to have more time.”

     

                Returning the hug, stroking Lena’s dark hair as she let out a small breath, Kara looked up at the high ceiling as more tears trickled down her cheeks and dripped onto Lena’s hair. “I know. I didn’t think- I only found out today.”

     

                Lena was wracked with a silent sob, all pretences of composure gone as she stopped trying to keep it together. It was difficult for her to fall apart, but at that moment she just didn’t have the energy to keep that carefully crafted mask in place. Her knees gave out and she slowly sank to the wooden floor, dragging Kara down with her as she quietly sobbed, her tears dripping into Kara’s lap as her dark hair fell in a curtain around her face.

     

                A small sound of surprise fell from Kara’s lips and she buried her face in Lena’s hair, cradling her close as she rubbed her back. It was a few minutes of silence, save for their quiet, shuddering breaths and Kara’s murmured reassurances, before Lena looked up, a scowl on her face as she took Kara’s face in her hands.

     

                “I love you.”

     

                A sad smile softened Kara’s mournful face as she leaned into Lena’s touch and covered her hand with her own. “You don’t have to say it because-”

     

                “No,” Lena sharply cut her off, “I love you. I should’ve said it sooner; I shouldn’t have wasted time. This changes nothing. ”

     

                “It’s okay. We have time. I’m still here.”

     

                A strangled sound passed through Lena’s lips and she leaned in to kiss Kara roughly, desperation seizing her, even as her bottom lips wobbled as another sob worked its way up her throat. Sniffing, Lena pulled back and touched their foreheads together, her fingertips brushing Kara’s wet cheeks as she breathed slowly.

     

                A few minutes later, Lena pulled back, digging the heels of her palms into her eyes as she swallowed and sighed. There was a hollow feeling in her stomach and her voice was raspy as she spoke. “We should go to bed.”

     

                Faces splotchy and breaths uneven, they made their way upstairs to wipe off their makeup and slip into pyjamas. Splashing cold water on her face, Lena stared at her wan reflection in the mirror, her eyes bloodshot and a tremor to her hands as she squeezed toothpaste onto her toothbrush.

     

                Slipping downstairs to fetch them both water, Lena stood in the dark kitchen for a few minutes, struggling with the effort it took not to dissolve into tears again, before she made her way back upstairs. Stepping into the bedroom, the room where she’d never shared with anyone else, in the house where she was all alone, Lena paused in the doorway to look at Kara, who was slipping her contacts into the container she’d kept in her purse. 

     

                Handing her a glass, Lena climbed into bed beside her and took a sip of her own before setting it aside and switching off the light. The sheets slithered as Lena shifted beneath them, burrowing her face into the front of Kara’s shirt and feeling her arms encircle her in return. They didn’t say anything for a long while, Kara silent as a wet patch spread across the front of her shirt and Lena’s shoulders shook. Kara’s own tears ran down her temples as she stared up at the ceiling.

     

                Her voice cracked when she eventually spoke, Lena’s eyes squeezed tightly shut as she listened, clutching fistfuls of her shirt. “I’m going to come back, Lena.”

     

                Lena nodded, her lips parting as she drew in a ragged breath. She already knew that Kara would come back to her, one way or another. It was the how that scared her. She didn’t know how to say that though and pressed her lips into a flat line.

     

                She lay there for hours like that, even when Kara eventually drifted off to sleep, her breaths listless and shallow, until dawn was only a couple of hours away and her mind finally succumbed to the exhaustion of the past day. And still, Lena didn’t let go of Kara, clinging to her as the crushing realisation that they were running out of time cast a pall even over her sleep, bad dreams leaving her restless and troubled long after she woke to the pink sunrise outside.

    Chapter 17

                Giving up on sleep, Lena slipped out of bed and left Kara to sleep as she made her way downstairs to brew coffee. Filling a mug, she carried it all the way up to her office and took a seat behind her desk. She didn’t even attempt to do any work, just idly spun her chair as she stared out of the arched windows, watching the sunrise over the city. Exhaustion made her eyes gritty and heavy, her whole body aching, but Lena knew that sleep would elude her for the rest of the day as her mind reeled from last night.

     

                Sipping her bitter coffee as the knot in her stomach made her feel nauseous, Lena brooded over things, trying to convince herself that Kara would be fine, that it would just be a few months spent reporting on patrols and political strife before she was shipped back home and her active duty was up. Things would be normal then - they’d never have to be parted again. But that was a big if , because as many times as she told herself that Kara was safe as a reporter, she knew it was a lie. That if was enough to sow seeds of doubt and worry and make her chest ache from the constricted feeling of panic as she breathed shallowly.

     

                Half of the morning had been lost to the harrowing thoughts that consumed her, her coffee growing cold as she sipped it, numb to her surroundings as her eyes stared blankly ahead and the lines of light crept across the room. It was nearly midday when Kara’s footsteps thudded up the stairs and her blonde head appeared from the staircase, her eyes widening over the edge of the floor before she hurried up the last few steps.

     

                “Oh, there you are. I didn’t know where you’d gone.”

     

                “I didn’t want to wake you,” Lena murmured, looking down at the gritty dregs of coffee as she flicked her thumb against the glazed ceramic, the sound dully ringing out as a wretched look clouded her face.

     

                With a faint sigh, Kara crossed over to the desk and leant against it, folding her arms over her chest as she assessed Lena’s appearance, seeming unsatisfied with what she saw there. “You look tired.”

     

                Reaching out, Kara caressed her cheek, a flicker of concern in her blue eyes as Lena glanced up and gave her a sad smile. The circles beneath her eyes made Kara’s stomach clench with guilt and Lena raked a hand through her hair.

     

                “I couldn’t sleep properly. For obvious reasons.”

     

                “Yeah,” Kara heavily sighed as her mouth thinned.

     

                Uncurling herself from her ball, Lena set her bare feet on the wooden floor and climbed to her feet. “Come on, let’s make breakfast.”

     

                Kara followed her down three flights of stairs and into the kitchen, wide shafts of warm sunlight sweeping in as the sweltering July sunshine baked the city outside. It was mercifully cool inside the house but Lena still pulled open the double doors to listen to the birdsong and the rustling leaves of the trees shading her terrace. Rinsing out her mug, she set fresh coffee on to brew and pulled open the fridge door.

     

                “What do you want to eat?”

     

                “What do you want to eat?” Kara chuckled, coming up behind Lena and wrapping her arms around her waist as she kissed the side of her neck.

     

                Trying not to sound too bitter as she replied, Lena grimaced. “No, it’s fine. I’ll make breakfast; I’ll have to go back to relying on my housekeeper for the pity meals she leaves behind if I don’t learn now.”

     

                Kara’s grip loosened as she pulled back, her voice a whisper as a wince marred her gentle face. “I’m sorry.”

     

                “Don’t apologise,” Lena quietly scoffed, a flicker of frustration burning within her as she concentrated her anger on the military. “It’s not your fault; they shouldn’t be allowed to- to just tell you you’re being promoted and then ship you off. You should have a say in it. You should get longer than a month .”

     

                Despite her efforts, her tirade came out sounding sour and resentful as she pulled a carton of eggs from a shelf and kicked the door shut with a little more force than was necessary, rattling the contents of the fridge. She glanced at Kara and frowned at the shamefaced expression on Kara’s face as she looked at Lena with pleading eyes and fiddled with her fingers.

     

                “What?” Lena asked, brushing past her and stooping to pull a frying pan out of a cupboard. “How do you want them?”

     

                “Fried.”

     

                Nodding, Lena set the pan down on the stovetop and picked up the egg carton again before glancing over her shoulder. “Well? What’s bothering you?”

     

                At the expectant look on Lena’s face, eyebrow arched and eyes appraising, Kara looked at the floor and nudged her glasses up her nose. Every inch of her was bristling with nervous tension as she scuffed a bare foot along the floor, mouth opening and closing as she hid behind a curtain of messy blonde hair.

     

                “I- well, they- they don’t just … promote you. You- you need to apply when a spot opens up and go before the board to, uh, answer some questions. Sergeant is a non-commissioned officer rank so … well, you don’t have to do officer’s training but you still have to go for the job and get a certain amount of points to get put on the recommended list.”

     

                Confusion furrowed Lena’s brow as she turned around, “but … you didn’t apply. Can they even promote you if you didn’t do the interview?”

     

                Kara’s silence was damning as she shifted uneasily beneath Lena’s confused stare, unwilling to look her in the eye as realisation dawned on her face. Mouth opening and closing, Lena’s eyebrows drew together as she cocked her head to the side. “Oh.”

     

                “Lena-”

     

                “No,” Lena quietly cut her off, the softness quickly hardening as the stab of betrayal hit home. “Tell me you didn’t.”

     

                Reaching out for her, Kara glanced up with a beseeching look of guilt on her face and Lena stepped back against the counters, her mouth falling open as her stomach swooped and the breath was expelled from her lungs. Finding it hard to catch her breath, Lena grabbed a fistful of her shirt, right over her heart as it raced at the implications behind Kara’s words, and the carton of eggs slipped from her fingers and struck the floor, yellow yolks oozing out of the cracked shells as she raked a hand through her hair and let out a quiet, hysterical laugh.

     

                “Oh my God.”

     

                “I- I wanted to tell you,” Kara started.

     

                Closing her eyes, Lena held a hand up and slowly turned around to brace herself against the edge of the counters. Breathing in and out slowly, she blinked away the burning pressure behind her eyes as she licked her lips, feeling the cold touch of eggs against her feet as neither of them moved.

     

                “Just … tell me this; if you didn’t apply for the promotion … would you still be going?”

     

                She could feel Kara’s reluctance to admit it, but she was honest when she finally replied, her voice barely audible. “No.”

     

                Shoulders drooping as she hung her head and expelled a small breath, Lena jumped at the warm touch of Kara’s arm on her shoulder. Whirling around, her eyes blazing with wounded anger, Lena skittered away.

     

                “Don’t touch me,” she snapped, her cheeks a blotchy red as her heart pounded in her chest, the deafening sound of it in her ears as her whole body felt suffocatingly hot.

     

                “I’m sorry, Lena,” Kara whispered, wrapping her arms around herself as she stood in the middle of the kitchen with a lost look on her face. Her eyes were bright with a film of tears and her skin looked grey with nauseous regret. “Please, just … let me explain.”

     

                As angry as she was, Lena was mostly just confused and hurt, and her voice cracked as her face crumpled with a wounded look. “You lied to me.”

     

                “I know but-”

     

                “I’ve been honest with you about everything ,” Lena said, gesturing widely, “and you couldn’t even tell me about something that involves me . Our relationship. Do you know how unbelievably selfish that is?”

     

                Clenching her hands into fists, Kara squeezed her eyes shut, “I was going to tell you! I just didn’t know when the right time would be. But this is my job , Lena. I’ve been doing this for years and I didn’t know if you and I …”

     

                “If we what?”

     

                “It would’ve been too much too soon!” Kara protested, “it’s barely been five months since we met and I didn’t know how you’d handle it off the bat if you knew that I’d be gone again soon. I didn’t want you to shut me out.”

     

                Kara’s breath hitched and she clamped her lips together, the guilt clawing at her as Lena wiped at her wet cheeks.

     

                “You should have trusted me.”

                

                “I do trust you.”

     

                As Kara surged forward with an agonised look on her face, Lena held a hand up to keep her at bay, looking at the floor as she swallowed thickly. “Just … tell me one thing; when did you know? That you were up for a promotion.”

     

                Silent for a moment, Kara drew in a deep breath and gave Lena a rueful look. “There was talk when I got back, before I met you. I went for the interview three months ago.”

     

                Nodding as she let the words sink in, Lena pressed her lips into a flat line and struggled with herself for a moment before speaking. The effort it took to keep her voice relatively stable was evident in the hoarse, strained whisper.

     

                “I’d like you to leave.”

     

                “Lena, please don’t do this,” Kara quietly begged.

     

                Lena didn’t look up from the floor to meet her gaze, stewing in her anger and hurt and disbelief as she clenched her trembling hands into fists. “I don’t want you in my house.”

     

                Somehow, it was worse that she didn’t shout. Kara would have preferred it if she lashed out at her, out of control as she let a torrent of anger spill out and find the weak spots in Kara’s armour. Instead, she was calm - although the tremor in her shoulders spoke of the effort it was taking - and her voice was firm, if not loud, and Kara knew that Lena’s mind was made up. Trying to reason with her would be futile in such a cool and collected manner, so, after a moment of hesitation, Kara slowly turned.

     

                She didn’t bother to change out of her pyjamas, didn’t even have any clothes but what she’d had on the night before, and stepped outside after a moment of hesitation, glancing back over her shoulder to see that Lena hadn’t moved an inch. Lena only moved once the door shut, quickly storming out of the kitchen and down the hallway to turn the lock and brace herself against the doors as she gritted her teeth, eyes smarting with tears.

     

                Her calm façade disintegrated and she let out a breathless sob as she turned away from the door, covering her mouth with a hand. Swallowing around the lump in her throat, she stalked back into the kitchen and grabbed the roll of paper towels, cleaning up the mess as her vision blurred with tears and her anger made her clench her teeth so hard that her jaw hurt.

     

                Padding upstairs once she was done, Lena roughly stripped off her pyjamas and stepped beneath the stream of water before it even had the chance to warm up, goosebumps rippling across her skin as she shivered and scowled at the wall. It quickly heated, but even that did little to help work the pent up tension in her knotted muscles as her tears were washed down the drain. She was tired and worried and mad and she stood beneath the water with her arms wrapped around herself as her breaths hitched with quiet sobs.

     

                After she’d mustered up the energy to scrub herself clean and wash her hair, Lena shut off the water and changed into clean clothes. Settling for tea in the hopes that it would quell some of the discomfort in her churning stomach, Lena made her way back up to her office and started up her computer with the intention of losing herself in work until the simmering anger twisting inside her abated. 

     

                And then her attention snagged on the framed photo on her desk, the only personal touch and a recent addition at that. It was the Polaroid of Kara she’d taken on their picnic and Lena reached out to trace Kara’s face with one finger, her head aching at the warm smile on Kara’s face. Exhaling until the air in her lungs was spent, Lena’s shoulders drooped and she slunk down in her chair, picking up the frame and drawing her knees to her chest.

     

                Trying not to cry again, so much confusion and anguish bottling up inside her, she wallowed in her misery and anger, knowing that it was really directed at the unfairness of the situation. She was mad that Kara would do something like that, but could Lena really expect her to change her plans for her? The unfairness of the situation still left her bitter and churlish as she thought about how their time together had been cut short though, the other half of their year together slipping through her fingers as she clutched the photo.

     

                After an hour of sitting in her chair, Lena grew restless and paced the length of the office, circling around the armchairs and the workbench, her eyes skimming the rows of books as she occasionally snagged one and flipped through it, hoping that it would consume her attention. Then she made her way downstairs, each step creaking and heavy, and made a fresh cup of tea to actually drink this time before she took a seat outside, closing her eyes to the sunshine as it warmed her cold skin.

     

                Once she’d tended to her little collection of herbs and drained her tea, Lena went inside and plodded all the way back upstairs to fetch her phone. She was torn between leaving a message for Kara and leaving it a while longer, the twisting feeling uncomfortable to hold within her as she silently fumed, alone with no one to voice her frustrations to, save her own mind. It was better that way, so she didn’t say things she regretted, and as she set her phone back down, Lena took a deep breath.

     

                In her mind, she took what had happened and put it into a box. A box with a tight lid. And then she dropped the box into a deep oubliette, right beside the other sealed boxes of bad memories, where she wouldn’t stumble upon them unwillingly. It landed somewhere next to her father’s last words and her searing loneliness and all the other things she would rather have forgotten about, yet couldn’t bear to live with.

     

                And then she felt the tension bleed out of her and a flicker of regret well up inside her. Lena regretted losing her temper earlier, even if it was justified, and she was seized with the gripping fear of lost time wasted on stewing in her feelings instead of just talking. She hadn’t given Kara the chance to explain properly, and no matter how upset she was, she owed her that much, at the very least. 

     

                It was something that needed to be done face to face though, and she sighed with soft resignation as she went to put shoes on and snagged her car keys off the console before unlocking the door and yanking it open.

     

                Lena let out a yelp of surprise, her hand flying to her mouth as her eyebrows shot up, nearly tripping over Kara, who was sitting on the top step of the stoop.

     

                “Fuck,” Lena swore, pressing a hand to her racing heart as Kara quickly scrambled to her feet.

     

                She retreated a few steps, looking up at Lena with a wounded plea on her face. Lena appreciated the distance as she fiddled with her keys and frowned at Kara with sceptical green eyes. Swallowing, Lena gave her a disgruntled look as her mouth turned down at the corners.

     

                “You scared me,” she admitted after a moment. “Have you been sitting outside the whole time?”

     

                “Oh, um, yeah,” Kara mumbled, ruffling her messy hair as she sheepishly winced. “I just- I didn’t want to leave you alone, so I thought I’d just … hang around until you were ready to talk. I also didn’t have any shoes or money to get home so …”

     

                “It’s been like … four hours. Why didn’t you just knock?”

     

                Kara opened and closed her mouth before a bewildered look crumpled her brow. “You … you told me to go.”

     

                “Right. Well … I was about to come and see you. To talk.”

     

                Nodding, Kara looked at her with wide, nervous eyes, twisting the hem of her shirt in her hands as uncertainty flashed across her face. Rubbing at the back of her neck, Lena’s lips twitched slightly and she swallowed her pride enough to turn and jerk her chin towards the door.

     

                “Do you want to come in? Have something to eat and drink?”

     

                “Sure.”

     

                Fetching two bottles of coconut water from the fridge, Lena set one down before Kara and then set about making them sandwiches from the packet of shaved ham in the fridge. Kara took a seat on one of the barstools and Lena hovered on the other side of the counter, her sandwich untouched as she folded her arms over her chest and eyed Kara.

     

                “So,” Lena slowly said, taking in the wary flicker in Kara’s eyes as she looked up at her and swallowed. 

     

                “I’m sorry,” Kara hoarsely replied, her voice earnest and pleading.

     

                “Yeah, me too.”

     

                Surprise flashed across Kara’s face at Lena’s words and she straightened, her head tilting to the side as her face furrowed. Lena let out a quiet laugh, her eyes closing for a moment as her cheeks dimpled.

     

                “What?”

     

                “Nothing. You just- you didn’t do anything .”

     

                With a heavy sigh and an even heavier heart, Lena’s hard stare softened into doleful yearning. “I … reacted badly. I didn’t even give you a chance to explain, and it’s your job so … I’m sorry for that.”

     

                “You have every right to be mad. I should have been honest from the start, but I- I just thought that … maybe you wouldn’t think it was worth it. Us . If you knew from the start … can you honestly say you would’ve let things go this far?”

     

                “Honestly? I can’t say for sure. I know it wasn’t intentional, but … you know how I feel about relationships. Love . And being lied to. I’ve been in over my head from the second I let you sit down at my table in that café. But you could have told me a month ago, you could have told me when we talked about you possibly being deployed again; I wouldn’t have gone anywhere. I wish you’d believe me when I say that I’m not going to leave.”

     

                Lena’s eyes were glassy with tears and she fiddled with the bottle cap of her water as she felt the shaky feeling in her chest, a precursor to the urge to cry as her throat constricted. Running a hand over her face, Kara softly sighed and slumped in her seat.

     

                “I should have trusted you more. I’m sorry.”

     

                The silence stretched between them, neither of them knowing what to say next, and Lena was itching to reach out for Kara, to hold her and never let her go. After a moment, Lena exhaled, weary as the tension inside her broke and dissipated.

     

                “So … where does that leave us?” Kara eventually asked.

     

                Lena shrugged. She sighed and after a pause placed both of her hands on the counter. Kara hesitated, then slotted her fingers in Lena’s and squeezed gently. Lips twitching with a rueful smile, Lena returned the squeeze.

     

                “I’m not mad that you went up for the promotion. I just wish you would’ve told me, because … I tell you everything . I mean, I told you I love you, and I’ve never said that to anyone so it just- it feels like you still doubt how seriously I take all of this.”

     

                “I don’t doubt you, Lena. I just- I didn’t want to be the one to break your heart.”

     

                “My heart’s always at least half-broken anyway,” Lena said with a wan smile as she squeezed Kara’s hand again.

     

                Letting out a defeated breath, Kara’s mouth thinned. “Come here.”

     

                Rounding the counter, Lena let Kara wrap her in a tight embrace and buried her face into her shoulder. The release inside her was almost immediate, her body going slack as the fight drained from her and sadness engulfed her. Blinking back tears again, Lena swallowed and clutched her tightly, her voice muffled when she finally spoke.

     

                “We’re okay, aren’t we?”

     

                “Yeah,” Kara lightly murmured, “of course we are. I love you.”

     

                Turning her head on Kara’s shoulder, Lena pressed a gentle kiss to the side of her neck and closed her eyes as she let out an airy sigh. “I love you too.”

     

                She stayed in the circle of Kara’s embrace for a few more minutes, relishing the feeling of being held by her, of her solid presence that was a reassuring reminder that she was still there. And even when she left, things would work out in the end. Lena had no doubt about it, because to believe anything else would break her heart entirely.

    Chapter 18

                The next week was a blur. Kara was constantly busy with work, coming home late in the evenings, worn out in her fatigues, eyes ringed with dark circles and shoulders bowed beneath the weight of guilt and sadness. Lena tried to keep herself busy at the office, staying only as long as Kara was at work, before coming home to soak up as much time with her as possible. Still, the days ran through her fingers like sand, slipping away to nothing as a week passed and left them with three more before she had to say goodbye.

     

                Lena kept her emotions on a tight leash around Kara, quiet and thoughtful and smiling even if it was laced with sadness, but at L-Corp, she found herself irritable and short-tempered, snapping at her staff over the slightest delays or mistakes in projects. She wasn’t sleeping well, up half of the night fretting over Kara’s deployment while the soldier slept beside her, slipping out of bed in the middle of the night on more than one occasion to pad downstairs to cry in the bathroom without rousing Kara.

     

                But she found herself gravitating towards Alex too, a small solace in the midst of so much anger and sadness. Alex was about to lose her sister, and she knew how it felt better than Lena did, having done it multiple times before. She and Kelly became nearly permanent fixtures at Lena’s brownstone that week, the four of them having dinner together so that Kara didn’t have to split her time between her sister or her girlfriend. It made it almost ironic that those nights, sitting on the small back patio in the warmth of the summer nights while they drank pitchers of sangria and pimms and ate aglio olio or grilled clams and mussels and ears of corn as the sunset cast a golden tint over the small corner of greenery, were some of the best nights of Lena’s life.

     

                There was an overwhelming sense of sadness growing inside Lena, festering like a wound, as the day of the deployment grew closer with each passing day. She had always been alone, had found it comforting in its own way, the detachment from having to concern herself with other people’s wants and needs and thoughts and feelings, but now, she couldn’t imagine ever going back to that again. She didn’t want to be alone; the highlight of her day was listening to Kara’s rambling thoughts, memorising the minute changes in her expressions and fetching fresh coffee or ordering takeout before Kara even realised that she wanted those things. It was almost cruel that it would get torn away from her as soon as that clarifying moment had hit her.

     

                Still, on Friday night, Lena found herself at Alex’s apartment for a change, typing away on her laptop as she waited for Kara to come home from work. It was a cramped apartment, filled with all of Alex and Kara’s belongings, traces of Kelly scattered throughout it as well, and seeming even smaller with the three women crowded before the sofa. 

     

                After checking the financial dashboard, reading over the KPI’s, data points and the quarterly revenue in regards to the annual target, Lena got stuck into a proposal on a carbon emission free project for a hydrogen storage technology. Alex asked the occasion question about her job and her clean energy goal, Lena launching into long-winded explanations of nuclear modular batteries she’d developed using a gas cooling method as a way to provide a heat and power source without relying on carbon emissions. Ever the scientist, Alex actively listened, something that caught Lena off guard but was appreciated nonetheless.

     

                She was just detailing the environmental and economic benefits of the upcoming roll-out for computers with her new clean energy batteries when the sound of a key scraping in the lock caught her attention. Her eyes dragged towards the door and a smile curled her lips as she watched Kara push the door open. Finishing off her explanation, she watched as Kara shuffled over the threshold, groaning and calling out a greeting. She was late.

     

                The trio chorused their own hello’s back to her, Lena closing her laptop and Kelly looking up from a dense psychology book on PTSD. Kara gave Lena a tired smile as she kicked off her boots inside the door.

     

                “Hey,” Lena murmured, “you’re late. How was work?”

     

                “Busy, busy, busy,” Kara sighed, walking over to the sofa and ducking down to kiss her. “You?”

     

                Shrugging half-heartedly, Lena smiled grimly. “The same. We got takeaway; leftovers are in the fridge.”

     

                “Please tell me it’s something good.”

     

                “Pizza,” Alex said as she switched the TV over to a crime documentary. “Lena splurged on the gourmet stuff for us.”

     

                Cheek dimpling with an exasperated smile, Lena climbed to her feet and touched Kara’s hand as she scooted behind her. “I’ll heat some up for you if you want to jump in the shower.”

     

                Nose wrinkling slightly as she smiled, making her glasses crooked on her face, Kara fleetingly cupped her cheek. “You’re a gem.”

     

                She turned the oven on with some difficulty and transferred a whole pizza onto a tray before setting it in to reheat, glancing back over her shoulder as she shut the door on the warm air flooding out. 

     

                “Hey, Alex, do you mind if I make some coffee?”

     

                Sighing heavily, Alex glanced over at her with an irate pointed look. “I told you, you don’t need to ask,” Alex said, waving a hand dismissively at the kitchen. “Just take whatever you want; you know where everything is.”

     

                Nodding, Lena took a clean cup out and looked back over at her and Kelly sitting in companionable silence. “Either of you want a cup?”

     

                “Please,” Kelly called back, not raising her head as she flipped the page.

     

                Alex similarly replied, distracted as she took in the bloody crime scene displayed on the screen. Fetching three more cups, Lena put a pot on to brew, wincing slightly at the swearing coming from the bathroom as the water ran cold as she filled the machine. 

     

                She bustled about quietly in the kitchen, pouring bitter coffee into four cups and adding cream and sugar according to everyone’s tastes. As she set the cups down on the coffee table, Alex murmured her thanks and leaned towards Kelly.

     

                “I bet you ten dollars it’s the boyfriend.”

     

                With a snort, Kelly shook her head. “I’m not falling for that again; no deal.”

     

                Looking up at Lena, Alex arched an eyebrow in a challenge. “Lena? Ten bucks?”

     

                Rolling her eyes, Lena sighed and reached for her bag set down beside the sofa, plucking ten dollars out of her purse and handing it to Alex.

     

                “I’m going to assume you’ll win,” Lena said with a withering look, “but I’ll take the odds on the slight chance that this time you’re wrong.”

     

                Kara walked out of the hallway, towelling the ends of her wet hair, pink and soft and clad in worn pyjamas and smiled as she watched Lena close her purse and stow it back in her handbag. 

     

                “Is she trying to con you again?”

     

                “There are many mistakes I’ve learnt from,” Lena sighed, moving towards the oven to remove the pizza. “But my competitive streak always wins me over. It’s a good thing I was never overly into gambling or I’m sure my fortune would be gone by now.”

     

                “You’d think you would’ve learnt after the last three losses,” Alex laughed as Lena ushered Kara to the sofa and brought her a stacked plate. “I’m surprised your pride hasn’t been permanently wounded.”

     

                “Oh man,” Kara chuckled, shaking her head as she lifted a slice of pizza off the plate. “She’s going to bleed you dry by the time I get back.”

     

                The four of them watched the TV with rapt attention as Kara ate her and Kelly closed her book around one finger to hold her spot, waiting for the reveal of the murderer. When it was announced as the boyfriend, Lena colourfully swore, burying her face in her hand as she groaned.

     

                “You’re cheating!” Lena protested. “You must’ve seen them before.”

     

                “Or most crimes are committed by men, and most murders are committed by a spouse or family member. Easy deduction; you’d think a scientist could figure that out.”

     

                “Well, I err on the side of a businesswoman and engineer rather than a scientist,” Lena countered. “Aren’t there any games for that?”

     

                Kelly chuckled, opening her book again and reaching forward for her coffee. “I’m sure you’d beat us all at Jenga.”

     

                “Jenga is luck,” Kara countered, “there’s no real strategy to it.”

     

                “Monopoly then,” Kelly shrugged. “Business. Finances. Investment.”

     

                Cocking her head to the side, Lena raised her eyebrows. “Monopoly?”

     

                “We should play it sometime,” Kara smiled, gently nudging her. “In teams, so I can win too. I bet you’re ridiculously good at it.”

     

                “I don’t know, I’ve never played,” Lena admitted.

     

                “What?” Alex snorted. “Who hasn’t played Monopoly before?”

     

                “You can’t really play it by yourself,” Lena said with a wry smile, her eyes shining with amusement even as she shifted with embarrassment.

     

                She watched as Alex’s surprise melted into a pitying look, reaching for her own coffee so she didn’t have to see the identical look on Kara’s face. They forgot that this was new for her, the nights spent in a cluttered apartment with friends, making bets on documentaries and teasing each other. Growing up, she’d lived in a quiet house - until tempers got out of control and then she wished the silence would return.

     

                “We can play it when we go and visit mom,” Alex offered, her voice softening slightly.

     

                “You’re going to visit your mom?” Lena asked, a look of surprise on her face as she turned to look at Kara.

     

                “Oh! Right, yeah, I forgot to tell you earlier. My mom called while I was on the way to work. She usually comes to the city to see us every couple of months, but when I’m being deployed I usually go and spend a week or so with her up in Midvale. I was going to see if you could maybe step away from the office for a couple of days if you wanted to come too.”

     

                “You- you want me to meet your mom?” Lena hesitantly asked.

     

                Giving her a crooked smile, her blue eyes alight with hope, Kara fiddled with her last slice of pizza as she shrugged nonchalantly. “Of course I do! I mean … I met yours.”

     

                “Ours isn’t as scary as yours,” Alex chimed in from the other sofa.

     

                With a snort of surprised laughter, Lena clamped her lips together and frowned as her cheeks dimpled. She was quiet for a moment, her heart fluttering with the nervous thought of meeting Kara’s mother, unfamiliar territory that Lena was admittedly terrified of.

     

                “She can’t be nearly as bad as mine,” Lena said with an apprehensive smile twitching the corners of her mouth. “So, of course I’ll come.”

     

                Surprise flashed across Kara’s face, her cheeks lifting as her lips pulled into a smile, her brows drawing together and then upwards in a tender look of happiness.

     

                “Really? I know you’re busy, so you can just come for a- a day or two. Maybe on the weekend so you don’t have to skip work.”

     

                “I can come for the whole time,” Lena assured her, laying a hand on Kara’s knee. “I think a break is well overdue.”

     

                “I’m coming too, if that helps,” Kelly said, and Lena found that it did offer her some comfort, knowing she wasn’t going to be thrust into the family dynamic without backup.

     

                “When are we going?”

     

                “In a week, I think,” Kara said, stifling a yawn as her eyes creased. “I haven’t booked tickets yet, but we’ll get the train up to Oregon. The house is big enough for us all.”

     

                Brushing her fingertips against the side of Kara’s neck, Lena smiled softly at her as she tipped her head to the side. “Tired?”

     

                “Mm. I think it’s time for bed.”

     

                She rubbed at her eyes beneath her glasses, shoulders curving with exhaustion, and Lena squeezed her shoulder as she climbed to her feet. Collecting the empty coffee cups and Kara’s plate, she left them in the sink and ran a hand through her hair as she watched Kara stand up.

     

                “I’ll see you both in the morning,” Lena called out to Alex and Kelly.

     

                They replied in kind, wishing them a goodnight, and Lena followed Kara down the hallway. She stopped in the bathroom first, brushing her teeth shoulder to shoulder with Kara in the cramped space, before applying a number of skincare products and then making her way into the small bedroom.

     

                Climbing into bed, she waited as Kara shut the door and slipped her glasses off, blinking owlishly as her bad eyesight blurred the room. Switching the lights off, Kara jostled the mattress as she sank down onto it, blankets slithering as she gravitated towards Lena and wrapped an arm around her waist. Lena shivered at the touch of her lips grazing her neck and smiled as her eyes shuttered.

     

                “Thank God for the weekend,” Kara murmured.

     

                “That bad, huh?” Lena whispered to the dark.

     

                Humming, Kara pressed her face into her shoulder blade. “It’s just … a lot to get done. And not enough time.”

     

                “If there’s anything you need to get done outside of work … I can do it. I mean, I can get someone to do it because I’m not good at the whole … normal life thing.”

     

                With a quiet bark of laughter, Kara kissed her shoulder. “It’s fine. It’s just me stressing myself out unnecessarily.”

     

                “Over what?”

     

                “I don’t know … making sure I have everything packed and- and meeting with a notary public to arrange my will. Just in case. And Alex is too nice to tell me she wants to give up the lease here so she can move into a new place with Kelly, but I might just pack everything up anyway and … put it in storage or find a roommate that will charge cheap rent and see me a couple of months out of the year. Stupid stuff.”

     

                “I- Kara, you can just stay with me, you know.”

     

                “I know, but I should have a permanent home for myself. For my things, you know?”

     

                Letting out a soft sigh, Lena squeezed her eyes shut, unwilling to think about the other aspect of the conversation too. She couldn’t comprehend how it must feel for Kara to write up her own will, knowing that she could very well die before making it back.

     

                “I’ll get my lawyer to meet with you next week,” Lena murmured after a pause. “Not the company one, but my personal one. They can arrange your will.”

     

                With a strained laugh, Kara squeezed her tighter for a moment. “It’s not even worth the cost,” she weakly replied. “I don’t really have savings, or anything important.”

     

                “I’ll arrange it,” Lena firmly assured her. “Don’t worry about things like that; I’ll take care of it, okay?”

     

                “Okay,” Kara murmured.

     

                Twisting in her arms, Lena propped herself up on her elbow and stared down at the shadowy outline of Kara’s face as the neon glow of outside seeped through the curtains. The traffic blared and sirens wailed and Lena thought for a moment about how different it was to her quiet street, in a neighbourhood with wide sidewalks strewn with magnolias and trimmed hedgerows, instead of the car alarm and drunken shouts. 

     

                She would never demean Kara for her life but Lena would also do anything within her power to make things better. Laying in silence for a moment, she tried to puzzle out a solution for Kara’s problems, and for Alex’s too, and sighed softly before leaning in to kiss Kara.

     

                “Goodnight.”

     

                “Night,” Kara whispered, her voice thick with sleep. “I love you.”

     

                “I love you too.”

     

     

                Lena woke early the next morning, slipping out of bed and leaving Kara to sleep a while longer, her face slack and youthful as she sprawled across two thirds of the mattress, blankets twisted around her legs. Smiling softly as she eased the door shut behind her, Lena stepped out into the hall, the apartment shadowed as blue pre-dawn light filtered in through the windows. The traffic outside was a constant low hum and she only dared to turn on one light, not wanting to wake anyone else.

     

                Still, she knew Kelly was an early riser, leftover from her military days, so Lena quietly tiptoed around the kitchen, setting a pot of coffee on to brew and raiding the fridge. She’d watched Kara make pancakes half a dozen times by now and it didn’t seem so hard, especially not for someone who knew how to measure parts to the dot, and after rummaging around in a draw for a whisk and finding a large enough bowl to mix the batter in, Lena got started on breakfast.

     

                It was easy and left her mind to wander as she dumped the dry ingredients into a bowl and set a skillet over a low heat to warm the pan. She’d never relished the comforting act of chores, how washing the dishes by hand or following a recipe could be soothing, helping unwind some of the tension she always seemed to hold within her, but in the silence of the early morning, she appreciated it then. Her mind started straying to topics she would have rather avoided though, and Lena shook her head to clear it before she took to quietly humming as she ladled thick batter into the pan.

     

                She was nudging one with a spatula as the edges firmed when strong arms wound around her waist from behind and Kara pressed up against her back. “Mm, you’re in a good mood this morning.”

     

                “Jesus,” Lena softly swore as she startled in Kara’s embrace, “you scared the shit out of me.”

     

                Quietly laughing, Kara kissed the side of her neck and perched her chin on Lena’s shoulder as she eyed the pan. Smiling as she worked the spatula under one of the misshapen lumps and flipped it, Lena almost preened with pride as she leaned back against Kara.

     

                “I’m making pancakes.”

     

                “So I see,” Kara murmured, her voice laced with warm amusement. “I’m having a bigger impact on you than I thought.”
