                Her quick laugh was flat and she watched as Kara’s mouth opened and closed soundlessly for a moment. “Did he- did he … hit you?”

     

                Lena’s eyes burned furiously behind her sunglasses as she looked at Kara, a scowl marring her pretty face as her lips twisted in a bitter smile. “Only sometimes.”

     

                She watched as surprise flashed across Kara’s face, as if she’d been expecting a no, and let out a breathless laugh as she swallowed thickly. “Not as often as Lex. I think that’s why my mom resented me so much; her prodigal son, their son, was on the receiving end of all his cruelty, while I, his darling daughter, was the favourite. Lionel spoiled me, and she spoiled Lex. He was everything to her in a way I could never be, and she never truly held me in the same regard as Lex. I still got everything I wanted, of course, especially after my dad died and I was just … there . The rift got wider after that.”

     

                Squeezing Kara’s arm, Lena gave her a small smile, vulnerable and nervous. Kara had to know it wasn’t something she ever spoke about - not with anyone - and Lena felt her stomach knot as her hands trembled, palms clammy.

     

                “That’s when you- you left?”

     

                Shrugging nonchalantly, Lena chewed on her bottom lip as she looked back ahead. “We used to argue all the time; eventually I just stopped showing up. I used my inheritance to buy my own place, I finished my second PhD. I should have been graduating high school - if I was normal - but instead … I rebelled the only way I knew how. That was six years ago now, and then … when Lex went off the rails, she tried to fix things. She was CEO for a while before she got them to instate me. Since then … she’s been trying to make things right, but I- it’s too late, you know? I don’t need anything from her anymore. And now that I have you …”

     

                Lena trailed off and raised Kara’s hand to her lips, pressing a kiss to the back of it as her eyes crinkled. “I’m not so lonely anymore. Not so closed off from everyone.” Letting out a quick laugh, Lena wrinkled her nose as she shrugged. “I mean, I can’t blame her for everything though; she was awful to me and I was a bitch to her. I would say I’m surprised she didn’t cut me off the minute my dad died, but I think … that would be dishonest, considering she’s always given me the best of everything, paid for college, was fine when I came out. We’re just … too different - or maybe we’re too alike, and that’s why we clash so much. Anyway, it’s been six years since I’ve had any sort of relationship with her, and what we had then wasn’t much to begin with.”

     

                Mouth flattening into a grim line, Kara’s face was grave as they walked on, the town behind them now, the roads more overgrown with trees and shrubbery as they walked past neighbourhoods and outlying stores.

     

                “You’re not obligated to love her just because she adopted you and paid for things,” Kara murmured, squeezing Lena’s hand.

     

                “I know,” Lena whispered, a constricting feeling in her throat that made her chest ache as she drew in a shallow breath. “There’s just- there’s a part of me that loves her anyway. We’ll never see eye to eye, but … for the last few years, we’ve only had each other. Doesn’t change anything though.”

     

                “Well, you have me now. And my family too.”

     

                A crooked smile curled Lena’s mouth as she nodded, that ache in her chest twinging slightly. It was so easy for Kara to offer her love freely, for Alex and Kelly, and even Eliza, to open their arms to her, but she didn’t know how to explain that it wasn’t that no one had ever done that for her before, but that Lena didn’t know how to let them. It was still uncomfortable to admit things to Kara, but she was working on it, peeling back the layers and the walls, knowing that it would only harm her, in the long run, to hold back now. Already, Lena felt so changed by knowing her.

     

                It left her with a heavy mind, weighed down with thoughts and doubts and snippets of memories that she hadn’t thought of in a long time. Ahead of them, Alex and Kelly laughed and bumped each other, arms around shoulders or waists or faces pressed into the crook of a neck, so effortlessly affectionate that it made Lena prickle with jealousy. But with Kara’s hand in hers, she felt anchored, steady in the place she was right now as she breathed in the late summer air, cooler than California’s, and enjoyed the walk.

     

                Once they reached the white house atop the small hill, they put the pie in the fridge and Alex made lemonade before the four of them retreated to the back porch. Kelly sat on the steps, legs stretched out into the sun, while Lena resumed reading her book and Kara listened to a podcast with earphones plugged in. 

     

                As the afternoon wore on, Alex wanted to go for a walk, and as Kara suggested clam chowder for dinner, Kelly stayed back to help her while Lena joined the other sister. Shoes in hand, she walked along the shore with Alex, tensing every time frigid water swept over her bare feet, her teeth soon aching from clenching with that prickle of fear as the wind tousled her hair. She made small talk with Alex, neither of them feeling the pressure to speak unless posed a question, and Lena was starting to feel tired from the languid day spent doing nothing in the warmth. It always made her tired to be unproductive, and by the time they turned and walked back home, she was loose-limbed and warm to the touch, the sunshine doing her some good as her body took a break.

     

                Eliza was home just before dinner, sweeping in with the smell of medical grade bleach, antiseptic and a faint coppery tang of blood. Still dressed in her scrubs, she kicked off her running shoes and gave them all a weary smile as she hung up her coat in the hallway. She went upstairs to shower and change while Kara stirred the pot and Lena helped Kelly lay the table. 

     

                “Any good cases today?” Alex called over her shoulder as Eliza reappeared in the kitchen, comfortable and clean in a cardigan and loose loungewear.

     

                “Nothing exciting. An appendectomy.”

     

                “Oh, you’re a general surgeon?” Lena asked with interest.

     

                “She’s head of the department,” Kara chipped in, smiling as she ladled the creamy broth into bowls.

     

                “Kara said your mother is in medicine too,” Eliza queried, a mild look of interest on her face as she took a seat at the table.

     

                Giving her a wan smile, Lena airily waved a hand and took the plate of buttered slices of baguette off Alex to set it down on the table. “She used to practice but she’s in biomedical engineering now. Lab stuff.”

     

                “Oh? Which company?”

     

                “Cadmus.”

     

                “Oh.”

     

                Lena masked a cringe at the surprised recognition colouring Eliza’s voice, and she ducked her head as she took her own seat. Clearing her throat, Lena smiled grimly and fiddled with her fingers in her lap as she looked anxiously at Kara’s back, quietly urging her to come and alleviate some of the tension welling up in Lena’s chest.

     

                “Is that a big company?” Kara asked, setting a bowl down before Eliza and Lena before taking a seat next to her mother. 

     

                “It’s … yeah, kind of. It’s a subsidiary of L-Corp, for medical stuff.”

     

                “So, your whole family are just geniuses then?”

     

                Shrugging, Lena sullenly picked up her spoon as she tried to compose her face into a neutral expression. Kara lightly touched her shoulder before sinking down onto the chair beside her with her owl bowl, smiling brightly as she picked up her spoon.

     

                “Is it good?”

     

                “Delicious,” Lena murmured, despite not even having a bite yet.

     

                Kara squeezed her knee beneath the table and Lena quickly scooped a bite of potato and creaming broth, swallowing it before anyone could ask her any further questions about her family. That didn’t deter Eliza from asking about her though.

     

                “So, Lena, you’re CEO of L-Corp?”

     

                “Only for the last two years.”

     

                “And you’re … twenty-four?”

     

                “Mhm. I, uh, well, it got handed to me. I was actually getting into genetic engineering but … well, it didn’t pan out with- with the CEO thing.”

     

                Eyebrows rising in surprise, Eliza’s mouth turned down at the corners, impressed as she nodded. “So, you went to college then?”

     

                Flushing until she could feel the tips of her ears warming, Lena let out a strained laugh. “I did. I studied a few things.”

     

                “She’s being modest,” Kara said, clicking her tongue as she rolled her eyes. “She had two PhD’s by the time she was eighteen. She skipped a lot of grades at boarding school and joined that genius society and everything. Chess champion, fencing master, cellist, all of that.”

     

                “I bet you can even ballroom dance,” Alex snorted.

     

                Letting out a quiet scoff of laughter, Lena looked up at the ceiling and sighed, the knot in her chest easing up at the gentle teasing. “In my defense, it was a requirement at boarding school, so I didn’t have a choice with that one.”

     

                “You can ballroom dance and you never told me?” Kara exclaimed, “you have to show me some moves.”

     

                “I’m good,” Lena objected, holding her hands up defensively.

     

                “Come on,” Kara wheedled, giving her a pleading look, “just for a second.”

     

                Rolling her eyes, Lena sighed, “after dinner.”

     

                Placated, Kara smiled and dipped a slice of baguette into the chowder and the conversation moved on. Listening, Lena picked up on new snippets of information about everyone - Kelly’s brother, Alex’s job, Eliza’s patients, Kara’s childhood and mutual friends - and filed it all away accordingly as she followed along with the conversation.

     

                She helped Alex clean up after dinner, the sound of the TV and conversation drifting in from the living room as they opened a bottle of white wine and Kara fetched the glasses. The sky was starting to turn a deep blue outside, the trees turning to hazy shadows as cicadas picked up a droning song, and Lena was up to her elbows in suds as she passed each clean bowl over to Alex, who dried them and put them away. It was a companionable silence and they worked quickly and efficiently, soon rejoining the others in the living room.

     

                Collapsing down beside Kara on the sofa, Lena was handed a glass of wine and nestled against her girlfriend as Kara pressed a hand against her back, nodding to something Kelly was saying. Eliza was sifting through a stack of developed polaroids from the day as she nursed her own glass of wine on Lena’s other side.

     

                “Come on then, show us your dance moves,” Alex said, shaking Lena’s shoulders as she passed behind her and sprawled in an armchair.

     

                “Well … we don’t have music,” Lena protested.

     

                “Don’t let that stop you,” Alex snorted, pulling out her phone and connecting to a speaker as she thumbed through her collection. “Ah, here we go. A classic.”

     

                The first notes of Chasing Cars by Snow Patrol sounded from the small speaker housed on the sideboard and Lena bit back a groan, giving Kara a resigned look before she climbed to her feet. Setting her wine glass down, she held a hand out to Kara.

     

                “Come on then.”

     

                Kara laughed, pink-cheeked and uncrossed her legs as she scrambled to her feet, setting her own drink down. Taking Lena’s hand, she let her lead her into the small open space of the living room, to the left of the sofa, Kara’s worn socks sliding on the wooden floorboards. Gripping Kara’s hand in her left, she directed her other to her shoulder and splayed her hand across Kara’s lower back.

     

                “Alright, I’ll lead then,” Lena said, feeling her cheeks colour slightly. “It’s one, two, three, four. One, two, three, four.”

     

                The flash of a camera going off caught her attention and her head whipped around to find Kelly holding Kara’s polaroid camera, chugging out a photo. Shoulders slumped, Lena gave her a pointed look.

     

                “Come on - no photos.”

     

                “You guys look cute,” Kelly softly pleaded her case, holding her hands up defensively as a small square printed from the mouth of the camera.

     

                Rolling her eyes, Lena led Kara in a quick circle, quietly chuckling as a burst of loud laughter fell from Kara’s lips, her eyes and nose wrinkling with delight. “You’re actually a good dancer,” Kara said with surprise.

     

                “Of course I am,” Lena crookedly smiled, “I could never be anything less than the best, even in ballroom dancing lessons. Too bad I never dance.”

     

                “Well, we should go sometime,” Kara said, an earnest look on her face that made Lena readily agree, even though there were few things she could imagine being worse than that.

     

                She pulled Kara closer for a moment, swaying as the music played on, before relinquishing her hold on her and gently jerked her chin before sitting back down on the sofa. Kara nestled in beside, pulling a blanket off the back of the sofa and spreading it over their legs.

     

                They ended up having an early night, laying in bed with the lights off as they whispered to each other, Kara lazily stroking Lena’s arm as they closed their eyes to the bedroom, minds a little heavy after a few glasses of wine. Lena’s voice took on a gravelly tone as she felt her eyes prickling with tiredness, too much sun and not enough stimulation or caffeine leaving her spent. She fell asleep pressed up against Kara’s back that night, and even though they both knew that soon enough they’d wake up alone in different beds in different countries, it was enough that Lena woke up beside Kara the next morning.

     

                She woke early to the deep blue pre-dawn light outside, a chill to the day, which hadn’t yet been warmed by the sunshine, and Lena eased out of bed, leaving Kara to sleep. She donned Kara’s faded blue fleece and pulled the patchwork blanket from the end of the bed, wrapping it around her shoulders and shoving her feet into slippers. 

     

                Quietly sneaking downstairs, Lena slipped outside into the cold morning, everything still hidden in shadow, save for the lightening colour of the sky. Easing the screen door shut, Lena walked over to the steps and sat down, running her fingertips over the peeling paint and splinters of worn wood as she leaned against the post of the porch and listened to the soothing ebbing and flowing of the ocean. The wind chimes tinkled quietly above her and her breath misted faintly as she closed her eyes. It was colder than the last two days had been, and, this far north, Oregon was already inching towards autumn.

     

                Eliza found her there thirty minutes later, the warm glow of the kitchen lights switching on inside the house, unbeknownst to Lena, as the older woman readied herself for a thirty-hour shift at the hospital. A draft sweeping in through the open door caught her attention and after setting coffee on to brew she went to investigate, finding Lena’s small frame bundled up on the steps.

     

                Lena didn’t stir at the sound of the screen door opening and closing, didn’t so much as turn or open her eyes, expecting Kara or Alex or Kelly, quiet as they swelled in the cotton wool haze of sleep that they hadn’t shaken off yet. The sound of Eliza’s gentle voice startled her slightly as she took a seat beside Lena, her hand on her shoulder as she lowered herself down.

     

                “Are you okay, sweetie?”

     

                Tilting her head to the side, she watched that flicker of alarm in Lena’s eyes, taking in the barely concealed flinch at the unexpected touch. Lena cleared her throat, rough from disuse, and raked a hand through her dark hair.

     

                “I’m fine. Just … trouble sleeping.”

     

                She unwrapped the blanket to share it with Eliza, draping it over both of their knees and wrapping her arms tightly around herself. Neither of them spoke for a moment but Lena could feel Eliza watching her from the corner of her eyes. Anxiously cracking her knuckles, she waited for the inevitable talk, for whatever reason it was this time, and swallowed thickly. 

     

                The silence stretched on between them for a few minutes longer, and Lena didn’t know how to fill it. This was the first time she’d truly been alone with Eliza, with no one about to intrude on the moment, and she was tense with anticipation.

     

                “Lena,” Eliza haltingly started, “I don’t want to pry … I only know as much as Kara’s told me, which isn’t a lot - she values your privacy too much - but I- I understand that … you don’t have much family.”

     

                Lena ducked her head, dark hair falling in a curtain around her face, effectively hiding her from Eliza’s perceptive stare. Her shoulders were hunched, muscles tense beneath the fleece, and she felt the prickling feeling of tears in her eyes, a muscle twitching in her jaw as she clenched her teeth, trying to fight back the feeling. It weighed heavily in her chest and she drew in a deep breath, blinking hard.

     

                “I’m fine,” Lena echoed, her voice scratchy and uncertain. She rubbed at her eyes, briefly, nonchalantly, clearing her throat softly. “I just- I don’t … I don’t want her to go.”

     

                Her voice broke at the end and it was an effort to draw in shuddering breath as her eyes filled with tears. The pressure in her chest built painfully, constricting her throat and making it hard to breathe, to fill her lungs with oxygen as she felt the knot inside her unravelling. 

     

                “Oh, honey,” Eliza murmured, reaching out to soothingly rub her back.

     

                The gesture only served to force a pitiful sob from Lena’s lips, forced up her throat and falling before she could stifle it behind her hand. All of a sudden, Lena felt like she was six years old, so young and vulnerable and scared , hot tears spilling down her pale cheeks as her eyes over-filled. It had been a childish thing to say, yet it seemed like it had been a reminder to Eliza of just how young Lena was - younger than either of her daughter’s, for all her maturity and haughty bearings - and she softly exhaled, as if the air had been knocked from her lungs, and shifted closer to the young woman.

     

                Lena covered her face with her hand, turning aside as Eliza wrapped an arm around her and pulled her closer. Breathing in the smell of her detergent, of the clinging sharpness of antiseptic that was vaguely familiar, a scent from her childhood when Lillian had still been a practicing surgeon, for a moment, Lena was struck with the sudden thought that this was what it was like to have a mother. Someone to comfort you when you were upset. It made her want to cry even more.

     

                “I know, I know,” Eliza whispered, and Lena had no doubt that she did.

     

                She would understand very well what it meant for Kara to leave, to be gone for months at a time, her safety never guaranteed. Lena wondered how she’d been able to bear it, waiting for a deployment to end with bated breath, unable to rest not knowing where she was or what she was doing. Lena knew she was looking at her inevitable future, no matter how short it was. She couldn’t imagine spending years fretting over a child.

     

                “I’m scared,” Lena whispered, her eyes screwed shut as she took comfort in Eliza’s motherly embrace, steadying herself as she breathed slowly. “I- I don’t want to be alone.”

     

                Gently pushing her back, Eliza cupped her cheeks in her strong surgeon’s hands, fixing her with a hard stare, insistent and stubborn and so much like Kara’s that Lena realised she had more of her adoptive mother in her than she’d imagined. 

     

                “Listen to me,” Eliza urged her, “you won’t ever be alone again, alright? I know it’s hard, believe me, I do. And it doesn’t get any easier, you just- you get used to it. But you have to hold onto the hope that she’ll come home, and you don’t have to do it alone.”

     

                Nodding, Lena reached up to wipe at a stray tear and let out a breathless sob, “I know, it just hurts. I miss her so much and she hasn’t even gone yet. I don’t know what I’m going to do without her.”

     

                A faint smile graced Eliza’s trembling lips and she thumbed away a few of Lena’s tears, clicking her tongue in a sympathetic manner before brushing dark hair out of her pale face. “You’ll do what you did before her. And at first, you’ll cry yourself to sleep every night and you’ll worry about her constantly. That worry won’t ever go away, but you’ll get to talk to her and you’ll forget about it for a moment, because you’ll know she’s safe. And there’ll be times you won’t hear from her for a week, and it’ll be hell , but you just have to tell yourself that no news is good news.”

     

                Lena was silent as she listened to the woman’s advice, occasionally wracked by the shiver of a suppressed sob. She felt less alone as she sat there, listening to the soft sound of Eliza’s voice as she coached Lena, gently rubbing her back as she laid it all out, months of deployments lending her the weary air of someone used to that dread and fear. She carried it around every day that Kara was gone, for years.

     

                They stayed outside as the dawn swept in, the sun behind the house but the sky above the ocean the palest shades of lavender and peach and pink as the waves slowly materialised, an inky pool roiling back and forth. 

     

                “I’m happy she found you, you know,” Eliza said after a long stretch of silence. “I’ve always worried about her; she lost her parents so young, and I tried to fill that gap as best as I could-”

     

                “She loves you,” Lena murmured. 

     

                Eliza chuckled quietly, propping her chin in her hand as her face softened. “She’s always been good at that,” she agreed, “that’s why I’m happy she has you. I worried with her joining the army and missing out on a normal college life that she wouldn’t have the time to find someone to put all of that love into, and someone to give it back . Kara’s the kind of person that needs that. I can see now that I was worried for nothing.”

     

                With a soft sigh, relieved and content, Eliza gently squeezed Lena’s arm. “She’s never been good at keeping secrets, my girl, so I knew immediately that she’d found someone. The way she talked about you on the phone … I would believe she fell for you the minute she first saw you.”

     

                Choking on a quiet laugh, a warmth spread through Lena’s chest and she stared out at the sea, watching the sky turn the black water to indigo to stone as it lightened. The day was warming as the sun blanketed the seaside town in its warmth, birds coming to life and the smell of morning dew leaving the air fresh and heady with the scent of pine and damp sand.

     

                “Come on. I’ve got to get to work and you’re freezing.”

     

                Eliza cupped the back of Lena’s head for a moment before standing up and vanishing inside. Lingering a moment longer, Lena watched the sea oats and the long grass sway with the gusting wind before she climbed to her feet, sand grinding underfoot on the steps where it had accumulated overnight, before following Eliza inside.

     

                She folded the blanket over her arm, screen door squeaking as she eased it open and closed. Scrubbing a hand over her face, Lena judged that Kara would be up soon and made for the staircase, shutting herself in the bathroom to wash her face before she slipped into the bedroom and returned the blanket to the foot of the bed.

     

                Sinking onto the mattress, jostling it slightly, Lena laid a hand on Kara’s arm and watched as she inhaled deeply and blinked. A smile curled her mouth and she groaned, burrowing back into the pillows.

     

                “Your hands are cold,” Kara mumbled.

     

                “I was outside. Talking to your mom.”

     

                “What’d she say?”

     

                “Not a lot,” Lena hedged. 

     

                She watched her for a moment, Kara still lingering in sleep as she slowly coaxed herself awake. Smiling faintly, Lena pressed a kiss to her shoulder and ran her hands through her silky hair, waiting patiently. After a long moment, Kara let out a rough sigh and rubbed at her eyes before easing herself up.

     

                “Mm, I’m going to miss sleeping in,” Kara muttered, blinking owlishly and then slipping on the glasses that Lena handed her. “I’m going to miss sleeping next to you.”

     

                “Me too,” Lena sadly whispered. “You know what you won’t miss? My cooking. But you may as well make the most of it while you can. What can I do you for? Bacon? Pancakes? I’m getting good with the pancakes.”

     

                Kara let out a snort of laughter, “go on then, I should make the most of them while I can.”

     

                Lena tugged on her hand and pulled her from bed and Kara stumbled towards her, enveloping her in a hug. Her pyjamas were rumpled and she was so warm, the extra few inches of height she had on Lena made it seem like she was engulfing her. Pressing her face into the side of Kara’s neck, Lena closed her eyes and felt the ridges of her spine through her t-shirt and she felt her chest ache slightly. Kara’s stomach rumbled then, breaking them both apart as they laughed, and Lena towed her toward the door.

     

                In the kitchen, Eliza was finishing a bowl of granola and smiled at Kara as she stepped inside, making a beeline for the coffee pot and filling two cups. She added a dash of cream to her own and stirred in a sugar before pulling out the ingredients and bowls and pans for Lena, who washed her hands and listened to the conversation. 

     

                Nudging Kara into a chair, Lena cracked eggs and measured flour with a doubtful look on her face as she frowned and murmured to herself. At some point, the conversation tapered off without her realising as Kara and Eliza observed her, the latter looking fondly amused.

     

                “Turn the heat down a little,” Eliza coached.

     

                Lena, who had been leaning down to look at the blue flames on the stove as she fiddled with the knob, jerked up and blinked before following the instructions. Laying strips of bacon down on the sizzling butter while the pan cooled slightly, she then set a dollop of pancake batter in another pan and sheepishly smiled over her shoulder.

     

                “Kara’s been teaching me how to cook.”

     

                “An essential skill,” Eliza approvingly replied, nodding her thanks as Kara poured more coffee for me.

     

                “Eliza taught me everything I know,” Kara explained with a warm smile at her mother. 

     

                “Maybe I could do with a lesson or two,” Lena laughed.

     

                She left batter and strips of cooked bacon for Alex and Kelly for their own breakfast before setting a plate down in front of Kara and sitting across from her. Eliza had to leave for work shortly after, for a long shift that meant they wouldn’t see her until the following night, and possibly not until the next morning once she’d slept it off.

     

                The sound of her car tires crunching down the driveway retreated, leaving the two young women alone in the kitchen, and Lena studied the faint signs of Kara’s weariness on her face. She knew she was enjoying being home, that her healthy tan from a summer of hiking and walking around a base in the middle of the desert made her glow, but there were faint thumbprints of purple beneath her eyes and a slope to her shoulders as the reality of her departure weighed her down. 

     

                Lena resolved not to say anything more on the subject and resolutely picked at her breakfast, barely touching what she’d made. Time was slipping by too fast for her liking, and she knew she couldn’t properly enjoy being in Midvale, knowing each day brought Kara closer to leaving her.

    Chapter 22

                It was dusk, on their last night in Midvale, and Lena was stretched out on her back on a plaid blanket covering a damp patch of grass. Kara was beside her, warm and thoughtful with her arms folded behind her head, listening to the sounds of rolling waves a dozen feet away from them. The tall grasses of the dunes and the canopy overhead rustled, a harmonising sigh with the singing cicadas, as they watched the sky slowly darken. It was dark enough that the first stars had started to appear, tiny pinpricks of silver against the velvety backdrop of approaching night.

     

                “I’ve always liked the stars,” Lena murmured, “maybe it’s because I’ve never lived anywhere where you could see them that well, never really been anywhere you could see them. Metropolis, London, Hong Kong. They’re so polluted that it almost became a novelty for me; it was always the best part about skiing trips, getting to see the stars from the lodge at the top of the mountain.”

     

                “Mm, it’s one of the good things about this place. It’s not so busy, I feel like … I didn’t appreciate that when I was younger. It was one of the things that made me want to leave, but now … I wish I could come back more often.”

     

                “We can come here more often when you get back,” Lena whispered, brushing aside the intrusive ‘if’ that tried so hard to sow seeds of doubt in her mind. “I can’t remember the last time I’ve ever felt so relaxed.”

     

                “Shocking,” Kara mockingly gasped, laughing as Lena ribbed her. “You always seem like the absolute pinnacle of calm, what with you running a multi-billion-dollar company and literally never leaving your office. I’m surprised I haven’t caught you sneaking off texts to Sam to ask for meeting updates.”

     

                Lena softly laughed, closing her eyes as her cheeks dimpled. “Ah, well, just because you didn’t catch me, it doesn’t mean I wasn’t . Seriously, though, it’s been nice to just … not think for a few days.”

     

                “Mm. And back to reality tomorrow. And then … one week.”

     

                A lump lodged itself in Lena’s throat as Kara spoke, and she couldn’t even form a reply, letting the silence stretch on between them as she swallowed three times, trying to force it down. It was painful, it made it hurt to breathe, and Lena gouged half moons into her palms as she curled her hands into fists and clenched her teeth to stop her bottom lip from wobbling. 

     

                They stayed there for another hour, stargazing and listening to the sea, while the night grew colder and they huddled up next to each other for warmth. She didn’t want the moment to end, but of course it had to, and it was with bitter regret that Lena folded the sandy blanket, slightly damp, while Kara packed up her camera and the stack of polaroids and slipped the thermos of hot coffee into her backpack. Brushing blades of grass and little burls off the back of her sweater, Lena followed her down the sandy path to the beach and followed the coastline home to the house.

     

                It was a quiet night, a certain air of solemnity to it, finality , even though none of them wanted to admit it. They sat outside on the porch, Alex grilling steaks and burgers and ears of corn while Kelly mixed Sangria and they listened to the radio. Eliza had the night off and joined them, amused by their antics and bickering, everyone laughing and trying to make the most of their dwindling time left in Midvale. 

     

                After devouring a Boston cream pie and tidying up the condiments and stacking the plates in the dishwasher, they all turned in relatively early, knowing there would be a lot to do in the morning.

     

                Lena rose first, quietly laying out her clothes and packing away the smattering of perfumes and lipsticks and lotions that had been strewn throughout Kara’s bedroom over the week, before she made her way downstairs. They weren’t leaving until the afternoon, but she was already mourning the slice of peace she’d been able to carve out there. In a week, she’d felt more at home there than she ever had growing up, and it left Lena brooding and quiet as she made tea in the kitchen and curled up on the sofa as early rays of sunlight lifted the grey veil of dawn.

     

                Kara didn’t stay in bed, and Lena heard her voice preceding her as she conversed with Kelly. She smiled when Kara kissed her softly, perching on the arm of the chair and picking up the book in her lap to look at the cover.

     

                “You’re all packed?” Kara asked as she set it back down.

     

                “Mostly. You?”

     

                Shrugging indifferently, Kara’s cheek dimpled, but not quite with a smile. “It won’t take me long.”

     

                A thump sounded upstairs and they both turned their eyes upwards to the ceiling as Kelly walked in with two mugs of tea and a concerned frown on her face. “What’s your mom doing?”

     

                Shrugging again as she took the cup, Kara flopped down onto the sofa and switched the TV on. Listening to the morning news, she looked up as Eliza entered the room with a battered cardboard box in her arms and frowned.

     

                “What you got there?”

     

                “Lena, come here a second, sweetie. I have something for you to see,” Eliza said, tearing Lena’s attention away from the TV as she set the box down on the rug and opened it up.

     

                Curious, Lena pushed herself out of the armchair and moved over onto the sofa, craning her neck to watch as Eliza pulled out a thick photo album and set it down heavily on the coffee table. Smiling mischievously, she pulled another one out as Kara groaned loudly, tipping her head back against the sofa as she closed her eyes.

     

                “I thought you might like to see some photos of Kara when she was younger.”

     

                “No, no, no,” Kara grumbled, covering her face with a hand. “She does not need to see those!”

     

                With a snort of laughter, Lena eagerly leaned in closer and picked up the first one as Eliza took a seat beside her. “Oh, yes, I do.”

     

                “Well … I haven’t seen any of yours.”

     

                “I don’t think there are any,” Lena said, rolling her eyes. “Actually, that’s a lie, I know we have some horrible , ugly staged ones. Ugh. I’m sure you could just Google me when I was younger and find some paparazzi photos from events. You know, if you’re that desperate to see me with braces and plaid.”

     

                “Maybe I am,” Kara challenged her, smiling as she threw an arm around Lena’s shoulders and looked over her shoulder as she opened the album to the first page.

     

                The first photo of Kara was her with heavy bangs and a timid air about her that was palpable through the page, her arms wrapped around herself as she smiled meekly while Alex sat beside her, grumpy and as far away from her as she could get on the sofa. A scoff of laughter fell from Eliza’s lips as she shook her head.

     

                “This was when Alex met Kara for the first time, and let me tell you, she was not happy about having a new sister. Jeremiah and I had already signed the adoption papers, and Alex knew about it, but … well, two teenage girls under one roof.”

     

                The next page was Kara sitting on the steps of the back porch, shielding her eyes from the sun as she squinted and smiled, a melting ice cream in hand and her shoulders slightly sunburnt. There were polaroids that Lena assumed had come from Kara’s camera, of Alex going through an edgy stage, chopping her hair off with chokers and Barenaked Ladies band shirts, both of them in soccer uniforms, Kara slowly outgrowing Alex, going from her little sister to a gangly, smiling teenager with a wide smile. Kara with rescue dogs the summer she’d volunteered at the shelter and from a summer vacation to the Grand Canyon one year, standing in a ravine of orange stone with an azure sky overhead.

     

                There was Kara dressed in a baseball uniform, resting a bat on her shoulder as she smiled and Eliza laughed as Kara groaned, bringing forth a story. “Kara decided to take up baseball when she was fourteen - she enjoyed watching the games with Jeremiah and thought she’d try out for the junior league. This was just before her first and only match. She swung at the ball and ended up throwing the bat instead, knocking the pitcher out cold.”

     

                Wincing, Kara gave Lena a sheepish smile as she shrugged helplessly, “I decided to stick to watching it after that.”

     

                There were more photos, of Alex in a NCU sweatshirt, Kara in a cheerleader’s uniform that Lena couldn’t stop laughing at, and various ones sent home from their travels around Europe, looking tanned and happy in Rome and Budapest and St Petersburg. Alex came down in the middle of it, and the trio regaled Lena and Kelly with stories - the latter already familiar with most of them - filling the living room with their laughter and clamouring voices talking over one another.

     

                At breakfast, Kara cleared her throat as she let her spoon clatter against the rim of the empty cereal bowl, and leaned back as she rested her arms on the back of the chair. “So … I actually have something to talk about. I didn’t want the hassle before we came here, but … I’m moving out.”

     

                She directed her words at Alex, who choked on her coffee as her eyebrows flew up. “You what?”

     

                “Yeah, well, I felt like it was a good time to do it, before I leave. You know, in case you and Kelly- well, whatever you want to do, you won’t have to worry about me.”

     

                “Kara-”

     

                Holding a hand up to cut her sister off, Kara smiled slightly, “I know, I know. But don’t worry, you’re not kicking me out; I’m moving in with Lena.”

     

                “Oh,” Kelly murmured, her eyes widening as she quickly glanced at Alex.

     

                “I’ve got the space,” Lena explained with a shrug as she smiled at Kara and brushed her hair out of her face. 

     

                “And because I’ll be gone, it’ll be a while before we actually get to live together, so, well, I know it seems a bit rushed, but it’s something for the future.”

     

                “Right. Well, I think it’s great,” Alex enthusiastically replied, looking at Kelly and Eliza as she nodded encouragingly. 

     

                Lena didn’t miss the eager spark in her brown eyes as she looked at her girlfriend, already making plans to follow through on moving in together, like Kara had guessed they’d been wanting to do for a while but had been too guilty to do.

     

                Smiling brightly, Kara nodded and picked her cup up, cradling it between her hands. “Right? It’s going to be a busy week, packing it all up, but it’ll free up my room to … I don’t know, sublease or whatever you wanted to do with it. I know the lease finished up a while ago so ...”

     

                Rolling her eyes, Alex smiled thinly, “yes, Kara, Kelly and I do want to move in together. You don’t have to hint.”

     

                “Good, good,” Kara nodded as Kelly quietly laughed.

     

                Lena squeezed her hand under the table and bit back her own smile before taking a sip of her tea. She left Alex and Kara to clean up with Eliza, giving the three of them some of the last few moments as a family that they would have for a while, and vanished upstairs with Kelly, showering and dressing for the flight and making sure she hadn’t left anything behind. 

     

                Once she was done, she knocked on the door frame of Alex’s room, curiosity getting the better of her as she peered around the place, taking in the purple walls and rock bands postered on them. It was bare in comparison to Kara’s, with so much of her stuff housed in her own apartment, Lena guessed, and Kelly looked up from the bag she was packing and beckoned her in.

     

                “How’re you holding up?” Kelly gently asked, raising her eyebrows as she glanced at her and folded a t-shirt. 

     

                Shrugging, Lena sank onto the bed and grimaced. “You met Alex once you were already out of the army, right?”

     

                “Yeah. It was actually Kara who introduced us.”

     

                “Oh, really? She didn’t mention that.”

     

                Wariness flickered in Kelly’s eyes and her movements slowed. “Did she mention anything else?” she hesitantly asked.

     

                “No. I mean, she’s told me about you, but not really much about what happened over there. She doesn’t … talk about that.”

     

                “Yeah.”

     

                Letting out a strained laugh, Kelly’s smile seemed a little forced and Lena cocked her head to the side, confusion in her green eyes. “What?”

     

                “It’s- I’ll tell you some other time. I need to finish packing.”

     

                Brow creasing faintly, Lena’s mouth thinned and she nodded slowly. “Okay,” she lightly murmured, “I’ll, uh, I’ll let you finish up.”

     

                Kelly gave her knee a quick pat and nodded, not looking up as Lena slid off the bed and left her to it. Puzzled, Lena slowly paced back and forth in Kara’s bedroom as she waited for her to make her way upstairs. Warm arms wrapped around her waist a few minutes later, pulling her back against a solid chest, and Lena smiled as she rested her hands on Kara’s forearms, leaning against her as she stared out the window.

     

                “Hey, was there something you were supposed to tell me about Kelly?”

     

                “Why?” Kara slowly asked.

     

                “I don’t know, we were just talking and she … she just mentioned that you introduced her to Alex and asked what else you’d told me.”

     

                Kara was silent for a moment, swaying them as the weight of her thoughts felt almost tangible to Lena. Finally, she swallowed and licked her lips, her voice quiet from behind Lena. “It’s not something that’s mine to tell.”

     

                “Oh. So, you know what she’s talking about? She did say she’d tell me some other time.”

     

                “Okay, well, just … it’s personal for her, okay?”

     

                “Don’t worry,” Lena quietly scoffed, turning in her arms, “I won’t nag her about it.”

     

                Kara’s smile didn’t quite reach her eyes and she ducked her head to kiss the side of Lena’s neck before hugging her tightly. Pulling back, some of the shadowed emotions hidden in the depths of Kara’s eyes had vanished and her next smile was more convincing, if a little regretful.

     

                “I should pack.”

     

                Everyone was all ready by lunchtime, but the scheduled driver wasn’t coming for an hour or so yet, leaving enough time for the five of them to pack into Eliza’s car and make the short trip into town for a parting slice of pie each. Kara savoured the chocolate pecan but Lena barely touched her slice of apple, her stomach twisting itself into nauseating knots as the pressure in her chest built up, that building anticipation of Kara’s departure feeling more and more real and daunting with each passing moment. Dismissing Eliza’s gently probing questions, she assured her that she was fine and convinced Kara to finish off her slice for her, the lie that she’d eaten too much for breakfast coming far too easily to her.

     

                Back at the house, they all lingered in the living room, the tension in the air unbearable as they all dwelled in relative silence, waiting for the appointed hour for the driver to take them out to the private airstrip for their flight. They watched some daytime TV show and Alex tried to convince Kelly to have takeout for dinner when they got home, while Kara sat close to Eliza in brooding silence. On her other side, Lena was just as quiet, lost in her own thoughts as she stared blankly at the TV screen.

     

                The sound of a car pulling into the driveway caught their attention, and Alex moved first, pushing herself to her feet with a sigh and moving down the hallway to gather her bag, dumped inside the front door. Lena’s lips twitched ruefully and she slowly followed after her, picking up her own bag and stepping outside. Walking down the steps, she greeted the driver and handed off her bag before turning around. 

     

                Kelly came out next, while Kara was already being lectured behind her as Eliza brought up the rear. Lena’s throat tightened and she lingered back as Alex swept past her and gave her mom a brief hug, kissing her dutifully on the cheek.

     

                “See you soon.”

     

                “Have a safe flight. And remember to call.”

     

                “Yeah, okay,” Alex agreed, rolling her eyes as she slid her sunglasses over her eyes and made for the car.

     

                Kelly said goodbye and was quick to join her, before Eliza’s attention slid to Lena. Smiling, Lena stepped forward into her hug, a pang of longing in her chest as she pulled back. 

     

                “It’s so good to know you,” Eliza said with a warm smile.

     

                “You too. And thank you for having me.”

     

                “Of course. Make sure you come and visit soon; you can come up with Alex.”

     

                “Okay.”

     

                “And take care of yourself.”

     

                A small, bewildered laugh surprised Lena as she nodded. She lingered back, uncertain whether or not to intrude on the private moment that followed, and the back of her eyes were stinging with tears as she watched Eliza hug her daughter tightly, her eyes squeezed shut and her fingers whitening with the force of her grip. Pulling back, she cradled Kara’s cheeks in her hands and looked at her, tearfully.

     

                “Make sure you stay out of trouble, okay? Stay safe. I love you. Call as often as you can.”

     

                “I’ll write too,” Kara thickly promised as she nodded.

     

                From Lena’s respectful distance, she could see that she was crying, her shoulders hunched and her eyes downcast. Eliza wiped away her tears as she cried as well, unashamedly.

     

                “Let me know if you need anything sent over. And … just come back. Don’t be a hero; just look out for yourself.”

     

                “Yeah, I will,” Kara mumbled, blinking rapidly.

     

                “Oh, my baby girl,” Eliza clicked her tongue, wiping at Kara’s cheeks and then pulling her into another hug. She kissed her cheeks three times in rapid succession and then drew back, relinquishing her hold on Kara to wring her hands anxiously before her. “You’d better go or you’ll miss your flight.”

     

                No one bothered to mention that it would wait as long as Lena asked it to, and Kara nodded as she slowly withdrew. “I’ll talk to you soon. Love you.”

     

                As Kara reached Lena’s side, she rubbed her back soothingly and they made their way to the car. Lena slid inside first while Kara waved goodbye for a moment before climbing in beside her. She exhaled roughly as she buckled her seatbelt, a faltering look on her face as she tried to remain brave. As Lena laid a hand on her knee, Kara buried her face in her shoulder and tried to steady her breathing for a minute before sitting upright.

     

                They were already passing through Midvale by that point and she looked solemnly out the window, eyes a little red, and watched as it quickly vanished behind them. The drive to the airport seemed longer on the return, everyone silent as they drove down twisting tree-lined roads, the warm day offering a beautiful view as dappled sunlight filtered through the canopy.

     

                The tarmac was hot beneath the soles of her shoes as Lena climbed out of the car, greeting the pilot as she made her way onto the jet, nodding to the air hostess and offering her a small smile as she took her seat. Kara sat beside her and fastened her seatbelt before closing her eyes. As soon as they were in the air, she leaned her chair back and slept for the whole flight home, covered in a blanket as Lena made whispered conversation with Alex and Kelly across the table. There were no rounds of poker and they sipped the champagne with less enthusiasm than the first time.

     

                It was getting dark when they touched down in National City, Lena’s driver waiting for them outside. The air was cold but she kept the window wound down a fraction in the back of the car as they raced towards the smattering of lights and soaring buildings, the sky too veiled to let through all but the brightest of stars. The smell of gasoline and stagnant water and alleyways overflowing with trash was familiar, but it did little to instill comfort in Lena as she leaned her forehead against the window and watched it all flash past.

     

                They went straight to her house, the brownstone dark and empty and quickly coaxed back to life as she flipped the switches and dumped her belongings in the hallway. Shedding her jacket over the back of a dining chair and leaving her bag on the counter, Lena was quick to make a mess before searching the number for the Chinese restaurant Kara favoured.

     

                Placing the order over the phone as she browsed the extensive wine rack in her pantry, Lena let everyone else settle in. It had been a long day, even if it wasn’t yet late, too emotionally draining for anyone to feel like talking much. They were all too busy thinking about the repeat of it all in a week’s time, the thought leaving a sour taste in Lena’s mouth. She didn’t think she’d be able to hold herself together as well as Eliza had. For all her coldness, she cried at the drop of a hat, at the slightest raised tone; Kara leaving would just be another awful moment to add to the locked away collection from her childhood.

     

                Pouring wine for everyone, they all retreated to the front living room, where Kara selected a movie at random and they all cuddled up, waiting for dinner to arrive. At the knock on the door, Lena handed over a wad of bills and they all passed around the white cartons while making the odd comment about what they were watching. It was strange to see Kara so dejected, the mood not quite able to recover from its depressing nature without her natural exuberance and near-constant chattering to keep the silence at bay. 

     

                The absence of her cheerful demeanour left Alex and Kelly leaving early, Lena paying for an Uber for them and waving them off before she locked up and they made their way to bed. Washing up in the ensuite, Lena applied her skincare routine and brushed her teeth before she made her way back into the room, taking in the silhouette of Kara against the darkness of the room. She was sitting on the edge of the bed and looked up as Lena shut the bathroom door behind her.

     

                “Come here,” Kara murmured, and Lena went obligingly, standing between her legs and cupping her face as Kara’s arms encircled her thighs.

     

                Leaning down to kiss her as she raked her fingers through her hair, Lena sighed softly. “I don’t want you to go,” she admitted after a moment.

     

                “I know,” Kara whispered.

     

                She pushed herself up as she captured Lena’s lips with her own, suddenly standing over her, and Lena smiled into the kiss as Kara picked her up with ease. Laying her down, Kara crawled on top of her and peppered her cheeks with gentle kisses as Lena breathlessly laughed at the tickling sensation.

     

                Sobering up a moment later, she slumped against the mattress and Kara raised her head, her features indecipherable in the dark but questioning all the same. “What?”

     

                “We should sleep,” Lena murmured. “It’s been a long day.”

     

                “I don’t want to sleep; I don’t want to lose any more time with you.”

     

                “Baby, I’m tired,” Lena sighed as Kara sat up. She pushed herself to her knees and draped herself across Kara’s back, propping her chin on her shoulder as Kara rubbed at her forehead. “And so are you - you know you are. Why don’t- why don’t you just … let me hold you tonight, and we can talk.”

     

                It was exactly what Kara needed, to be held close and reminded that she wasn’t gone yet , and that even if there was an aching feeling in her chest, things would be okay. It was a comfort for Lena too, as they lay down, entwined with each other, a reminder that Kara was very much still out of harm’s way. She clung to that hope she’d stay that way, even a thousand miles away.

     

                Kara fell asleep first that way, her heavy weight almost pinning Lena, who stared into the darkness, her mind far too occupied to sleep yet. Truthfully, she didn’t want to squander what time they had left either. She wasn’t ready to let Kara go.

    Chapter 23

                The last week went by in the blink of an eye, so full of activity that they never really got to spend any time alone together that wasn’t occupied about Kara’s inevitable deployment in some way, shape or form. Lena was back at the office for most of the week, sticking to shorter workdays so that she could still see Kara, who had been packing up her bedroom at Alex’s and ferrying boxes back and forth to Lena's house in the Tesla. 

     

                Aside from the big business meetings, Lena had spent her every moment with her, trying not to let Kara’s haphazard mess drive her mad as she added her own books to Lena’s meticulously organised library in random order, hung her slim selection of clothes in the designer closet without any arranged category and cluttered Lena’s shower with her favourite bathroom products. It was a big adjustment to live with someone else, but Lena cherished the sniping comments and flashes of irritation over the week, knowing that it would be months before she’d experience them all again.

     

                She had Kara’s friends over for dinner that week, hiring a private chef to cook for them all - Nia and Querl both coming, as well as Alex’s old mentor, J’onn - and she spent her lunch breaks meeting Kara in the coffee shop they first met in, or at the art gallery or a picturesque park for a walk, trying to fill Kara’s last days with colour and life and laughter. There were a lot of photos to savour and capture the memories, and she was grateful for Kara’s old camera, knowing it would offer her small comfort to be reminded of the good times before she left. 

     

                That last night was unbearable though. Kara had gone to Alex’s for a couple of hours, alone, to sort the last few things out. Lena didn’t ask what, was too afraid to know what arrangements had been made - just in case. But she was grateful for that small reprieve, holing herself up in her office, trying to focus on spreadsheets as she scowled and blinked and tried to swallow the sickening stone in her stomach that had been a permanent fixture for the past seven days. She’d tried to ignore the preparations, for the most part, treating it all like some sort of business trip Kara was taking, but the reality of it was frightening. It filled her with so much dread, leaving her numb and pale and quiet. Try as she might to ignore it, in the morning, Kara would be leaving.

     

                They’d eaten out every single night - save the dinner party - to all of Kara’s favourite restaurants and takeout places, and for that last night they’d piled into an old book at the Chinese restaurant they’d first had lunch together at. One last meal together with the four of them. Later on that night, it was just the two of them, and Lena was resolved to make it a meaningful last night.

     

                She filled the deep bathtub with sweet-smelling salts and bubbles, steam rising from the surface and making the bathroom tiles sweat, grabbed two forks for the slice of chocolate and pecan pie she’d had Jess order from an upscale bakery in the city centre, and ushered Kara into the bath to luxuriate to the peaceful tones of Coldplay’s earlier records.

     

                Lena was content to sit on the bathroom floor with a glass of wine, just for the sake of being close to her while she could. Taking in Kara’s cheeks, gently flushed pink, and the way her damp hair curled against her neck and brow, the sight of her without her glasses on and the small scar in the middle of her forehead all memorised until Lena was satisfied that she’d be able to draw her from memory. It was a silly thing to do, knowing they’d get to FaceTime each other and that she had so many photos of Kara, but it put her at ease to know that she was so ingrained in Lena’s mind that she would never forget, no matter how much time passed.

     

                When she finally emerged from the bath, a long while later, soft and warm and still slightly damp, she pinned Lena to the bed where they stayed for hours, until midnight had passed by and they eventually fell asleep, bare skinned and pressed up against each other. Lena was restless, waking often and allowing Kara’s presence to lull her back to sleep for a short while longer, but when the first cracks of dawn filtered through the windows, she woke to the wretched day with silent curses on her tongue. She’d forgotten to close the curtains the night before, and was angry that the day had to be any longer than it had to be.

     

                Slipping out of bed, she drew the curtains angrily, frustration already bringing her to the threshold of tears, before she eased herself back into bed. Sitting upright against the headboard, she watched Kara sleep for a while with the nauseous knowledge that this was the last time she’d see her like that for a while, looking so young and vulnerable and peaceful.

     

                Eventually, Kara stirred, squinting as she tried to make out the dim shapes of the room. Her hand searched blindly next to her, seeking out Lena, who picked it up and lightly kissed the back of it before shuffling over to her side and letting Kara rest her head on her stomach.

     

                “Good morning.”

     

                “No, it’s not,” Kara whispered. “What time is it?”

     

                “Almost eight.”

     

                “How long have you been awake?”

     

                Lena’s voice was faintly hoarse as she let her fingers idly trail through Kara’s hair. “A while. Couldn’t sleep.”

     

                Softly sighing, Kara sat up and stretched, drawing her knees to her chest as she rubbed at her tired eyes. Lena studied her profile, resisting the urge to reach out and just touch her, to convince herself that she wasn’t some made-up person about to vanish beneath her fingertips.

     

                “Do we have time for coffee?” Kara asked, turning to look at her.

     

                Smiling sadly, Lena nodded, “one last one before you go.”

     

                They were heading to Alex’s before the command post, where a bus would take Kara to the plane flying her to Afghanistan. Alex usually went alone, but it went unspoken that Lena would be going to that final point with her this time, saying goodbye to Kara at the very last possible moment. 

     

                But first, coffee. They even managed to get the same table they’d met at, a little bit sticky and the sunlight wasn’t slanting in at the same angle yet, but it was still the same, nevertheless, and Lena smiled lopsidedly as she tilted her head.

     

                “Do you have your camera on you?”

     

                “Always. Why?”

     

                “Do you mind if I take your photo? The lighting is perfect right now,” Lena echoed the words Kara had said to her months ago, the first time she’d ever taken Lena’s photo.

     

                Choking on a laugh, Kara fished the camera out of her backpack and handed it to Lena with a wry look on her face. The look softened into a familiar expression on Kara’s face, one Lena knew very well, one she adored , where she was just about to smile but her mouth was still soft and undecided, but the corners of her eyes were already faintly creasing with the telltale signs of it. Her eyes were a translucent blue and limned with silvery pricks of tears as the old camera flashed and started to chug out a dark square.

     

                While it developed, they sipped their drinks, Lena opting for a chai latte, unable to withstand the jitteriness of caffeine when she already felt like a coiled spring, while Kara savouried the dregs of the last decent cup of coffee she was likely to get until she was back in the States again.

     

                When she flipped the photo over, Lena let out a soft huff of laughter as her eyes burned, staring down at the photo that had perfectly captured the soft golden tones of Kara’s hair and skin, the tenderness of her gaze and the fragile sadness of the morning. She let Kara look at it for a moment before taking a knife from the cutlery stand and roughly sawing through the plasticky layers of the photo, until she was left with an oval, encapsulating Kara’s face and shoulders.

     

                Watching with mild concern and a little confusion, realisation dawned on Kara’s face as she watched Lena reach up and undo the clasp on her locket. Her curiosity piqued, Kara leaned forward to watch her pry it open and felt a stab of disappointment and pity to find both halves of the locket empty. But, as she watched, Lena gently worked the roughly cut photo of Kara into the right half, filling the gift tainted by her brother’s memory with something more deserving of its worth. 

     

                Lena had waited a long time to find someone worth sticking in a locket, and once she’d latched it back around her neck, she smiled and covered it with her hand. “There. Right next to my heart,” she told Kara, her voice hitching slightly.

     

                Finishing off their drinks, they left the café and walked down the baked sidewalk, dodging pedestrians as they held hands, Kara forging ahead, and made for the parked car. Unlocking the Porsche, Lena slid behind the wheel and softly sighed before the passenger door slammed shut and she gave Kara a slight smile.

     

                Driving to Alex’s place, she parked outside and they made their way upstairs, the door yanking open almost immediately, as if Alex had been waiting on the other side for their arrival. She looked pale and resigned, gesturing them inside as she held the door open. Kelly was dressed for work, pushing her clients back a bit later so that she could say goodbye to Kara, and she smiled grimly as she shoved a few files into her handbag.

     

                They made small talk for five minutes before Kara inhaled deeply and then sighed, twisting her hands before her as she tried to muster some enthusiasm. “Well … we should get going then.”

     

                “Come here then, you,” Kelly said, pushing herself to her feet and opening her arms wide.

     

                Smiling, Kara hugged her for a long moment before patting her back and pulling back. Kelly’s eyes sparkled with forced levity as she pointed sternly at Kara. “Do I need to give you the usual speech? Look after yourself, okay?”

     

                “Yes, ma’am.”

     

                “I’ll see you soon.”

     

                “Look after yourself,” Kara nodded, before cracking a smile and jerking her head towards Alex and Lena, “and these two, too.”

     

                Promising that she would, Kelly followed them to the door and clapped Kara on the shoulder before squeezing Lena’s arm encouragingly, pity flashing in her dark eyes. Stepping out into the hallway, Lena lingered as Alex kissed her girlfriend goodbye, murmuring promises to call and see each other later that night before the trio made their way downstairs alone.

     

                It took them an hour to get to Fort Rozz with the inner city traffic, and by the time they reached the command post, there wasn’t much time at all before Kara had to get on the bus to make it to the jet. She had her bursting duffel bag with her, supplies to pack into the heavy chest shipped overseas as well as the necessary military issued items she hadn’t yet packed, and Kara looked tall and severe in her uniform as she climbed out of the car and sighed heavily, weighed down by her bags.

     

                The bus was already there, families and kids saying goodbye to the departing soldiers. They trailed Kara towards it and she dropped her bags off before turning around. Alex stepped forward first, biting her bottom lip as she crushed Kara in a tight hug.

     

                “I don’t have to say it,” Alex murmured, “you already know, just … stay out of trouble. Please just stay out of trouble. And save yourself first, okay?”

     

                Kara laughed weakly, her eyes screwing tightly shut as she stooped over her sister, swaying her slightly. “You got it. Look after each other, okay? I’ll be back before you know it. I love you.”

     

                “Love you too, kid,” Alex gruffly replied, her brows furrowed low over her dry eyes as she pulled back and grabbed Kara’s face in her hands, tipping her head down to kiss her brow. 

     

                She smiled slightly, clapping a hand on each shoulder and giving her a little shake. Kara let out a breathless laugh, nodding; they didn’t have to say much to know. It wasn’t the first time they’d been through this, and while it wasn’t easier , it was familiar. But not for Lena, who felt herself wilt the moment Kara’s eyes slid over to her, her eyes smarting with tears in an instant.

     

                Rushing into Kara’s arms, she buried her face in her shoulder, violently shaking - even though she managed to hold back her sobs, each withheld one making her chest hurt with the effort - and she couldn’t bring herself to speak. Not for the longest moment as soldiers started to board and families said their own last goodbyes.

     

                Gripped with a sudden urgency, Lena pulled back and stared down at the faded asphalt and Kara’s pristine, shining boots. “Just … make it back to me,” she hoarsely ordered her, wrapping her arms around herself. “I don’t care how you do it, just as long as you- you come back, okay?”

     

                “I promise,” Kara murmured, reaching out to cup Lena’s cheek in a rough hand, urging her head up. “Let me look at you before I go.”

     

                Lena looked up at her with gut-wrenching, mournful eyes, looking young and frightened at the uncertainty of it. A faint smile dimpled Kara’s cheek and she swiped the pad of her thumb across Lena’s high cheekbone, brushing away a stray tear that had fallen. 

     

                “I’m going to come home,” Kara quietly assured her, fierce determination in her blue eyes as a pucker formed between her brows. “I know it’s hard for you, but I won’t be the one to hurt you like that, okay? Just … wait for me to come home.”

     

                “Of course,” Lena choked out, her lips pressing into a petulant look as she looked everywhere but at Kara, where she most wanted to look, to drink in the sight of her, savour the last glimpse of her and her touch and her smell. “I love you. No matter what.”

     

                “I love you too,” Kara softly chuckled, jerking her chin in an affectionate manner that managed to coax the barest hint of smile from Lena. “And I’ll call as often as I can. Every day, if possible.”

     

                “Make sure you tell me what you need; I’ll have it sent to the PO Box when you give me the address.”

     

                “I will.”

     

                “And make sure you wear sunscreen, okay?”

     

                Kara’s smile was sad but her eyes sparkled with amusement, squeezing Lena’s arm as she nodded. “I promise.”

     

                Nodding, Lena swallowed thickly, biting on the inside of her cheek, hard enough to taste the coppery tang of blood. Her bottom lip wobbled as she drew in a shuddering breath and gestured toward the bus. “You should go.”

     

                Her stoicism faltered then, hot tears spilling down her cheeks as Kara cupped her face with rough urgency, kissing her hard enough to bruise, and then again, soft and lingering. Caressing Lena’s cheek, she pulled her in for another hug, her voice low and hoarse as she whispered.

     

                “I won’t say goodbye, just … I’ll see you soon.”

     

                She let her go then, stepped back as she blinked furiously, eyes filled with welling tears. Shading her eyes she dawdled as she inched backwards toward the bus, watching as Alex stepped up behind Lena and set a hand on her shoulder.

     

                “I love you both,” she called out, slowly turning and hauling herself onto the bus with the handrail.

     

                Soldiers trickled on after her and Lena tracked her down the centre aisle, until, amid a sea of smiling faces waving and saying last goodbyes out of the small hinged windows at the top of the bus, she saw Kara. Blonde hair pulled back into a neat bun, eyes as blue as empty skies and a smile beaming as bright as the overhead sun. Raising her hand, fingers spread, she blew them both a kiss and leaned against the window, watching them for a moment longer before the doors of the bus hissed shut and the engine grumbled. 

     

                They both lingered there until the bus was out of sight, and only then did Lena lose some of her hard earned composure. A breathless sob was expelled from her lungs and she covered her mouth with a hand, hunching her shoulders as embarrassment washed through her. Stalking off towards the car, she flinched at the hand on her shoulder and shrugged it off.

     

                “I’m fine,” Lena said, her voice cracking as she squeezed her eyes shut and shied away from Alex. “Just … don’t look at me.”

     

                Rubbing furiously at her face, Lena drew in a shuddering breath that hitched on another sob, rummaging around in her handbag as for the car keys as she hurried ahead, desperate to get out of there. Nearing the parked Porsche, her fingers were shaking too badly to unlock the car and she dropped the keys, cursing as she stooped to pick them up.

     

                Alex beat her to them, snagging them off the hot ground and grabbing Lena by the arm as she towed her over to the passenger side. “You shouldn’t drive a Porsche while crying.”

     

                Choking on a laugh, Lena yanked open the door and slid inside, hunching forward and digging the heels of her palms into her eyes. Alex climbed in on the other side and slammed her door shut before adjusting the seat and sighing heavily.

     

                “One minute.”

     

                “What?” Lena asked, looking up with doe-eyed confusion in her damp eyes.

     

                “You have one minute to cry, and then you get your shit together and you can cry yourself to sleep later, okay?”

     

                Lena blinked at the sharpness of Alex’s orders and let out a strangled laugh. And then she found the sound dissolving into hitching sobs as raw pain threatened to overwhelm her. Wiping at her cheeks and struggling to catch her breath, Lena spent the hurried minute reining back in her control as Alex likewise composed herself beside her.

     

                “Alright, minute’s up,” Alex said as she straightened up, raking a hand through her hair and sniffing as she started the engine. Clearing her throat, she fiddled with the radio and pulled into the flow of traffic leaving the post before they hit the highway back into National City.

     

                The drive back home was mostly in silence, Lena staring blankly ahead as she was lulled into a stupor by the motions of the car speeding along, a wide expanse of desert giving way to flat, sprawling neighbourhoods and distant foothills before the city made itself known as a hazy lump on the horizon. Following the curving highway through the haze of dust, Alex took the exits and passed through junctions as skyscrapers and apartment blocks and streets bustling with traffic and business revealed themselves. It was a sunny day, too nice for a goodbye, and Lena stared sullenly at the shining reflections of sunlight off a thousand windows, at the smell of gas and warm bitumen and trees still smelling green in the late summer heat.

     

                When they turned onto Lena’s street, quiet and neat with its rows of magnolia trees out of bloom but still a rich green, shading the cars parks along the sides of the road, the brownstones stretching down each side, ancient and elegant, Lena turned to look at Alex.

     

                “Aren’t you going home?”

     

                “No,” Alex curtly replied, indicating and pulling into the empty spot before Lena’s house. She cut the engine and turned to Lena as she opened the door, sheepishly admitting, “she asked me not to leave you alone.”

     

                Lena swallowed thickly, nodding even though what she wanted more than anything was to be alone. Climbing out of the car, she wearily made her way up the front steps and fished her key from her bag, unlocking the door to let herself in. The silence of the house felt oppressive instead of comforting, like it had used to when she’d first moved in. Now, the stillness of it, the lack of Kara clattering about in the kitchen or the TV, which she always had tuned into some show she’d missed out on, or her loud voice filling the rooms and hallways as she moved about the place with ease, made Lena feel homesick in the place she’d worked so hard to make her home.

     

                “Do you want tea?” Lena belatedly asked as she blocked the doorway for a minute, Alex hovering on the threshold as she waited for her to move.

     

                “Whisky,” Alex said with a quiet laugh.

     

                With a huff of laughter and an agreeing nod, Lena kicked off her shoes, dropped her handbag to the floor and made for the sideboard where her liquor was shelves. Fetching two clean tumblers, she filled them with top shelf whisky and knocked half of hers back in one gulp as Alex fiddled with her glass.

     

                “You know … it helps to talk,” Alex gently prompted her.

     

                A wry smile curled one side of Lena’s mouth and she fingered the edge of the glass as she stared down at the floorboards. “I’ve never been much good at that.”

     

                “Right. It’s just- you’re not alone , Lena. I know you probably don’t give a shit, but I don’t just like you for her benefit - and neither does Kelly, so … you have a family.”

     

                Looking up, mild surprise flashed across Lena’s face and she nodded slowly, a guarded look in her eyes as she took another sip and let the liquor burn its way down her throat.

     

                In the end, she curled up on the sofa and brooded, watching a documentary on the fishing industry as Alex busied herself with tidying up and nosing around the place. Lena was too defeated to tell her to stop, that she didn’t need her laundry done because she sent it to a dry cleaners, that she didn’t want a sandwich because her appetite had vanished to nothing. She still dutifully ate the sandwich and finished off her and Alex’s kombuchas when the latter gagged at the taste of it.

     

                After that, Lena withdrew to her study, where she made the half-hearted effort to answer a few emails and review plans with a contractor for a new warehouse north of the city. Alex eventually came to disturb her, perusing the selection of books, poking around in Lena’s things as Lena watched from the corner of her eyes, sitting with her knees drawn up to her chest on the wide leather desk chair as she chewed the end of a pen and listened to a seminar she’d missed two days before on workplace culture.

     

                Kelly showed up after she’d finished work with a bag of Thai food in hand, and the three of them crowded around one end of the dining table, ignoring the empty place where Kara should have been sitting as they kept up a steady stream of conversation and Lena pushed her food around her plate.

     

                She stayed up until it was an acceptable time to go to bed, although still hours earlier than her usual bedtime, putting her empty tea cup in the sink and drying her hands on a dish towel. Alex and Kelly were stretched out on a sofa, cuddled up with a blanket over their legs as they watched a sitcom, and Lena hovered uncertainly.

     

                “Are you- are you staying tonight?”

     

                “Mm,” Alex hummed in agreement, “unless you want us to leave.”

     

                “I- no, it’s fine. Take whichever spare room you want. They’re already made up.”

     

                Kelly eased herself up and looked at her with sympathy. “You’re off to bed?”

     

                Ducking her head in assent, Lena chewed on her bottom lip for a moment, arms folded over her chest as she scuffed a foot along the floorboards. “Yeah. I’m tired.”

     

                “Alright, well, goodnight.”

     

                “Try and get some sleep.”

     

                She nodded at their advice and murmured similar niceties before vanishing upstairs. Her room was the same as always, the lights dimly flickering on at her arrival to illuminate the wide bed made with clean linens, the antique headboard and the staged decorations. The stack of books with dog-eared corners that she hadn’t finished yet, and the shoes and bags that Alex had left on the bench at the foot of the bed.

     

                And there, in the middle of the bed - something out of place. Lena knew what it was immediately, a photo album with a sealed envelope on top, left as a parting gift.
