                September rolled into October and the autumn chill covered National City in a permanent drizzle, although that sometimes wasn’t enough to dispel the odd humidity, even with overcast skies. Lena took business trips and worked long weeks, pushing through each day with anxious determination. One day closer, one week closer, another month closer. Until it was almost five months until Kara would be home, and October crept to an end.

     

                Her birthday came too quickly for her liking, and felt almost laughable that twenty-five felt too young for how she felt inside. She hadn’t had any thoughts about the day beyond the flight to Midvale at lunchtime, a rare gift to herself to even take that much time off for what was essentially a forgettable day, and so, Lena was making up for lost time at the office when the clock ticked over to midnight. If it wasn’t for the sound of her phone vibrating on the desk, amidst piles of paperwork and empty coffee cups, Lena wouldn’t have even noticed.

     

                Picking up her phone, she frowned down at Kara’s name on the screen, confused about why she would be calling her at that time. It would’ve been just before noon in Afghanistan, while Kara would have still been working, but Lena didn’t question it as she answered, her face already softening with a smile.

     

                “Happy birthday!”

     

                The loudness of Kara’s voice in the stillness of the office was almost deafening in her ear, and a surprised laugh escaped Lena before she could even stop herself. Drawing the phone away from her ear, she winced faintly and then glanced at the time before pressing it back. There was a warm glow in her chest that Kara had called dead on midnight, and Lena closed her eyes as she slumped behind her desk.

     

                “Thanks,” she murmured, “I didn’t expect to hear from you until later.”

     

                “Well, I couldn’t wait that long to talk to you. Not on your birthday. I can’t stay long though; I might get in trouble. I just had to call you though.”

     

                Making a choked sound of surprise as her eyebrows raised, Lena chuckled softly, “Kara Danvers, are you breaking the rules right now?”

     

                “For you, it’s worth it. I’m trying to be sneaky though, but it’s a bit loud.”

     

                “Mm, I can hear voices in the background. You better keep an eye out for your Sergeant or you’ll find yourself tied to the front of a tank for target practice, or whatever morbid punishments they have over there.”

     

                Kara laughed quietly, the sound faintly muffled, and she sighed with amusement before replying. “I just wanted to wish you a happy birthday and tell you that your gift won’t be there until tonight. I thought it’d be better to send it to my mom’s, but hopefully you’ll get it before I speak to you later. Otherwise, I’ll have to wait until tomorrow to see if you like it.”

     

                “If it’s off you, I love it already,” Lena earnestly murmured.

     

                “I hope so, but … anyway, you should go to bed and I have to go. What time are you leaving?”

     

                “Twelve-thirty. I’ve still got some paperwork-”

     

                “Work? Come on, not on your birthday. Take a break!”

     

                Lena snorted as her lips curved with a smile, “it’s just my birthday, Kara. The whole world doesn’t revolve around me, sadly. Don’t worry, it’s from home so no chances of getting shot, and I’m going to bed soon anyway; Alex and Kelly have conned me into breakfast with them.”

     

                “Good. I’m glad you’ll be able to spend it with people.”

     

                “Mm, it makes a change. I think this will be the best birthday I can remember having.”

     

                “Yeah? That’s good. I hope it is too. Look, I’m really sorry to cut it short but someone’s walking past so-“

     

                Lena’s face softened as Kara’s voice pitched to a low murmur, a slight smile twitching the corners of her mouth as she surmised, “you have to go.”

     

                “I’ll talk to you later, okay? Try and enjoy yourself; it is all about you today.” She chuckled and then sighed. “I love you.”

     

                “I love you too.”

     

                She hung up after that and climbed to her feet, stretching out her arms and arching her spine as her spine ached from being slumped in the chair. Closing her laptop screen, she walked over to the rug and sank down to scratch Athena behind her eyes, the dog looking up at her with dark, liquid eyes in the dimness of the loft office.

     

                “Come on, time for bed,” Lena murmured, jerking her chin as she pushed herself back up.

     

                The dog’s claws scratched at the wooden steps as they went down a level and into Lena’s bedroom. Her eyes were stinging slightly and she tumbled into bed, pressure building in her chest as she thought about how Kara had waited until midnight to call her. Lena couldn’t stop grinning to the dark, feeling silly and pink-cheeked at something so childish, but it made her heart swell with happiness and she allowed herself that feeling. After all, she was only just twenty-five - she didn’t have to grow up just yet.

     

                She slept in late, indulging herself in an extra few hours of restless tossing and turning and frequent waking, before she got out of bed for breakfast. Showering and dressing, she put on a thin sweater and jeans and tried to hide the evidence of her exhaustion before knocking back a little cup of espresso in the kitchen and grabbing her keys. She parked her car at L-Corp and walked the few blocks in the cool weather, trying to muster some enthusiasm for her birthday, intent on enjoying it like she imagined Kara would.

     

                They met at an upscale café that Lena had had a few business brunches at, the pair already sitting at a table for four against the back wall as pale sunlight streamed through the wide windows that made the converted space seem airy. It was an old industrial building and Lena passed by exposed piping and brickwork on her way to the table.

     

                “Happy birthday!” Kelly quietly exclaimed at the sight of her, a wide smile lighting up her face.

     

                She pulled out the chair beside her and sank down onto it, feeling vaguely embarrassed as she smiled tentatively as Alex echoed the sentiment.

     

                “Thanks, guys.”

     

                “We do have gifts for you, but we thought we’d wait until tonight,” Alex said with a smile.

     

                “Oh,” Lena murmured, eyebrows rising, “thanks. That’s nice of you.”

     

                Snorting, Alex fished something out her pocket and set it down on the table before Lena with a droll smile. “This one’s for now, though. Just in case.”

     

                Lena burst out laughing at the taser with a little green bow stuck to it, picking it up as she smiled widely, eyes bright with mirth. 

     

                “Next time someone threatens you … give them hell,” Alex sternly told her.

     

                “Thanks,” Lena chuckled, slipping it into her bag with a shake of her head as her shoulders still shook with laughter. “It’s very heartening to know you think there’ll definitely be a next time.”

     

                Alex snorted and gave her a reproving look before sliding a menu across to her. “Yeah, well, I was optimistic in hoping the next one wouldn’t be a gun, so …”

     

                “Come on, let’s order,” Kelly said, gently nudging Lena.

     

                She browsed the menu and settled on shakshuka , while the three of them ordered mimosas, slipping into conversation as they enjoyed their unhurried breakfast. It was still early, and with the whole day and rest of the week stretching out before them, they quickly fell into vacation mode, coming up with plans for Midvale.

     

                “So, what time are we leaving again?” Kelly asked, a hesitant flicker in her eyes.

     

                “Flight is at twelve-thirty. Obviously there’s wiggle room for when someone is late.”

     

                Alex held her hands up defensively, eyes glimmering as she faintly smirked. “No delays this time, I promise.”

     

                “I made her pack her bag this morning,” Kelly laughed.

     

                “Don’t worry, I won’t spoil your birthday,” Alex said, rolling her eyes. “I’ve got the whole day off, so, who knows, maybe I’ll follow you to the office and serenade you with my rendition of ‘happy birthday’ in front of your employees. I’m assuming you won’t be dragged away from your work that easily.”

                

                Rolling her eyes, Lena sighed and gave her a grim look. “I just have to go in for an hour-“

     

                Groaning as she put her head in her hands, Alex laughed, “you make it so easy to pity you, kid.”

     

                “One hour!” Lena protested, gesturing helplessly as she glanced at Kelly. “We’re adults! Who takes work off when you’re a grown adult?”

     

                “You own the business!”

     

                “I like working!”

     

                Kelly laughed and patted her shoulder reassuringly, wincing slightly with amusement as her brow furrowed. “Lena, honey, you need to learn to have more fun.”

     

                “It’s my birthday, you can’t bully me.”

     

                “Alright, I’ll lay off, but only because you’re going to be in for it for the rest of the week. Happy birthday.”

     

                They clinked their half-empty glasses and finished their breakfast and once they were done, Lena walked back to the office. Stepping off the elevator, Lena greeted Jess as her assistant climbed to her feed, gathering up the coffee, newspapers and tablet as she hurried after Lena, who breezed into her office.

     

                Leaving her bag and coat strewn over the sofa, Lena walked over to the desk and smiled at the annual cupcake that appeared on her desk without fail and no further explanation. Sinking down onto her chair, she looked up at Jess and gave her a genuine smile.

     

                “Thanks, Jess.”

     

                Nodding, Jess launched straight into a few pieces of information that she’d prioritised - a rejected offer, a missed call from a high profile investor - as she arranged the newspapers on Lena’s desk for her and nudged the coffee closer. Humming in acknowledgment, Lena swiped her finger in the frosting and caught Jess looking at her strangely for a moment, surprised that Lena was enjoying the cupcake. She realised, perhaps for the first time, that she’d never really had much interest in sugary treats before and couldn’t remember if she’d ever actually eaten the little gift her assistant left her. 

     

                That wasn’t to say Lena wasn’t grateful - she liked to think she showed that gratitude threefold when it came to Jess’s birthday, which Lena did remember and appreciate with some expensive trifle that she picked out herself - but she wondered again at how little she voiced it or showed it. It had never seemed important to her; if everyone was working efficiently, they kept their job, and that seemed like a testament to what she thought of them.

     

                “You know, you can probably take the rest of the week off, Jess,” Lena blurted out, interrupting her. “I won’t be here, there won’t be much for you to manage that admin can’t cover, and any important calls can be fielded by Sam or sent through to my cell.”

     

                “Oh, um, well … I actually used all of my vacation time in March.”

     

                Giving her a wide smile, her eyes creasing at the corners, Lena leaned back in her chair, holding the cupcake up. It was chocolate with cream cheese frosting and a cherry on top and she plucked it off by the stem, smiling wryly.

     

                “I have a newfound appreciation for birthdays,” Lena informed her. “Take the week. You’ll still get paid; I’ll arrange it with the Finance Department.”

     

                “Okay,” Jess warily replied, “um, thank you.”

     

                “I’ll only be here for about an hour, so if I don’t see you before I go … make sure you do something fun.”

     

                “Fun?” Jess echoed, her eyes widening slightly.

     

                Lena laughed, shrugging, “yeah, you spend so much time running around after me, I hope you at least … I don’t know, get a facial or day drink.”

     

                Jess let out a snort of laughter and gave Lena a sceptical look. “Is that your plan for your trip?”

     

                “Maybe,” Lena smiled.

     

                “Who knows, it might surprise you,” Jess said with a crooked smile. “I hope you have a good birthday.”

     

                Lena’s face softened minutely as they broke their unspoken tradition of not vocally acknowledging it, and she smiled shyly as she ducked her head in agreement.

     

                “Thanks, Jess.”

     

                She met with Sam, who gave her a cheerful ‘happy birthday’ and inquired about Lena’s plans for the day, fondly teasing her about coming into the office as Lena rolled her eyes and grumbled until they got back to their conversation. 

     

                It wasn’t so productive, but she spent the full hour she’d allowed herself going over tactics with Sam as the CFO cautioned her about a projected drop in stock value and urged her to pay back investors. Lena had a nagging suspicion the call from the investor was them backing out and she grimaced but agreed with the intention of buying back shares at a low price. The stock market was fickle but Sam navigated it so well that she wouldn’t have been sitting there advising her if Lena didn’t trust her judgment.

     

                Lingering a little longer than she’d planned, Lena eventually had to go as the clock tucked dangerously towards eleven. She’d packed the night before but they still had to get to the private airstrip and get cleared for takeoff, and despite Alex’s assurances that she’d be ready, Lena doubted it.

     

                Leaving her car parked in the underground parking lot, Lena’s driver took her home and she hastily grabbed her bag and bundled Athena into the waiting car before going to fetch her friends. The three of them chatted in the back as Downtown National City retreated and the anticipation of escaping to the seaside made them all excited. Alex and Kelly were practically brimming with it, beaming the whole car ride and laughing loudly and Lena found it bewilderingly amusing but infectious nonetheless.

     

                As they pulled up to the airstrip, Lena’s phone started ringing, and she pulled it out of her pocket to see her mother’s name on the screen. Lips twitching slightly Lena climbed out of the car first and moved off a few steps as she answered.

     

                “Hi.”

     

                “Happy birthday.”

     

                “Right, yeah. Thanks.”

     

                “God, twenty-five,” Lillian sighed, softly musing, “I know you were always away at school for most of them, but how is it possible that you grew up so fast?”

     

                Lena let out a slightly strained laugh, rubbing at her forehead. “Mm, well, I did get a bit of a head start in that area. You know, being a genius and all.”

     

                Lillian laughed, the sound sharp but still warm with amusement. “Do you remember your seventh birthday? We had a tea party for you at The Ritz and you wouldn’t talk to any of the other kids because you said they were all stupid.”

     

                Sniffing derisively, Lena’s eyes creased at the corners as she grinned. “I’m sure I was right.”

     

                “Oh, you were. No one was ever as smart as you, but it did bother me that you never made any friends. You were always so stubborn.”

     

                “Nothing’s changed there. Well, I mean, I have friends now. I think they’re more age appropriate than the adults I was at college with as a kid, so … probably for the best.”

     

                Lillian hesitated slightly, “you’re still going to Midvale today?”

     

                Narrowing her eyes against the pale sunlight, Lena hummed in agreement, watching as their luggage was being hauled onto the small jet. “We just got to the airstrip.”

     

                “Good. Good. Um, so … well, I thought I wouldn’t make it a surprise, because I don’t want to ruin your day if you think it’s a bad idea-“

     

                “Oh?” Lena softly snorted with laughter, “boundaries?”

     

                “Very funny,” Lillian witheringly replied before pressing on. “When I reached out to ask them what they had planned for your birthday and they told me, well, I asked if I might be allowed to come. Now, I’m still in Metropolis, so if you think I’m overstepping, I’ll leave you to enjoy your night, but I thought … seeing as it’s been going … okay …”

     

                Blinking in surprise, Lena’s face quickly crumpled in a confused look. “I- yeah, sure, mom. You can come.”

     

                “Oh. Okay. Great. Well … I’ll see you tonight then. I had the liberty of sending your gift ahead to Eliza’s, but I’ll probably get there first then. If you don’t like it, I’ll get you something else.”

     

                “Sure. Thanks, mom.”

     

                Hanging up, she pocketed her phone and moved towards the plane, gripping the railings as she hauled herself up the steps and into the interior. Sinking down onto her usual seat, she reached for a little pastry from the platter and took a bite from form eclair before feeding half to Athena. The dog wolfed it down and Lena smiled at the air hostess who handed her a glass of Dom Pérignon. 

     

                The flight felt quick as Lena flicked through the latest issue of a business journal and then through a memoir she’d brought along with her. Before she knew it, they were descending through rain clouds, the window spattering with fat droplets of water as they soared down to a lower altitude, and a blanket of green over rocky grey greeted them as they watched the airstrip materialise and touched down after a little turbulence. Lena felt a little queasy and unbalanced after the mild panic, cursing her frequent need to fly and grateful to get onto solid ground as she climbed down the steps.

     

                It wasn’t late, by any means, but the dismal weather and days reaching for winter meant the sun was already setting by the time they pulled up outside Eliza’s house. The lights were on, a cheerful yellow glow welcoming them, and they hurried through the light downpour and inside, shaking off the rain and the cold as their voices filled the hallway.

     

                Eliza poked her head out of the kitchen, a gentle smile, pleased and inviting, on her face as she spread her arms. “You’re here! Come in, come in.”

     

                They shuffled further inside, making the house feel cramped as they kicked off wet shoes and dumped their bags at the foot of the stairs for the time being. Alex hugged her mother, followed by Kelly and then Eliza spread her arms, warmth in the lines of her face as she looked at Lena with sparkling blue eyes.

     

                “And there she is, the birthday girl!”

     

                “Hi, Eliza,” Lena murmured, her cheeks warming with embarrassment at the attention as she ducked her head and briefly hugged her. “Thanks for having me.”

     

                Looping an arm through Lena’s, Eliza patted her hand and led her down the hallway to the living room, “of course, of course. Any time. You’ve spoken to your mother?”

     

                “Mhm, she’ll be here later.”

     

                “Good,” Eliza said, clamping her hands down on Lena’s shoulders as she slipped behind her and urged her forward. 

     

                Lena stepped through the doorway and her eyebrows rose at the sight of dozens of balloons filling the room, as well as banners and streamers and two big numbers displaying ‘25’. It was all a riot of colours and Lena let out a bark of laughter as she was taken aback by the sounds of party poppers and paper horns.

     

                “Surprise!” Alex crowed.

     

                Covering her face with her hands, slightly mortified but genuinely touched by the effort, Lena was only a little baffled as she shook with laughter. Kelly forced a party hat onto her head, the whole thing so silly and childish but unlike anything Lena had ever received in her childhood, and she couldn’t stop smiling as she was ushered down onto the sofa. A smile pile of gifts waited for her, but she was warned not to touch them yet and was brought coffee instead.

     

                “Thank you guys so much,” Lena demurely smiled, nursing the cup between the palms as she looked around, taking in the confetti scattered around the gits and the long strands of tissue paper from the poppers and feeling a rush of love for them. 

     

                It was still a strange feeling, that these people had accepted her so readily, so completely, as if there had been a space waiting for her to fill. She’d never known love like that, had never expected love like that, and it made her eyes sting as she shifted in her seat, rubbing at the back of her neck.

     

                “Of course,” Kelly said, reaching over to squeeze her knee. “It’s just- well … Kara wasn’t sure if you’d ever had a- a proper birthday party so …”

     

                Letting out a quick laugh, Lena’s cheeks dimpled as she shook her head. “I should’ve known she had a hand in this. She’s right though; I’ve never had a party like this.”

     

                She didn’t mention the few birthdays where she hadn’t been away at boarding school, the ones so ostentatious that it fell into a completely different realm of birthday parties. Lena would have picked the banners and balloons and the thoughtfulness of it all over the alternative any day. 

     

                “Well, we’ve got a long night of board games,” Alex said, grinning wickedly as she rubbed her palms together. “Time to bring out that competitive streak.”

     

                “Let me guess, Monopoly is in there?”

     

                “Of course. This time I’m going to win, I swear. But we’ve also got Clue, Trivial Pursuit, Apples To Apples, Pictionary and if everyone’s in for the long haul, Catan.”

     

                “Does your mom like board games?” Kelly asked.

     

                Lena scoffed loudly as her eyebrows rose with incredulity. “I’m sorry, have you met her? The only board game she knows how to play is chess .”

     

                “Well, someone has to come last,” Alex shrugged indifferently, “unless she happens to be a good artist or have encyclopedic knowledge.”

     

                “Ah, well, she does have the latter.”

     

                “Great,” she muttered in reply, “another Luthor genius to put up with. Scratch Trivial Pursuit, babe; I can’t lose to people who don’t even know how much groceries cost.”

     

                Rolling her eyes, Lena gave her a jaded look, “of course I know how much they cost, I just don’t buy them myself. There’s a difference.”

     

                “Oh, please , when was the last time you set foot inside a CostCo?”

     

                “You already know the answer to that, but that’s beside the point - you said no bullying today.”

     

                “Alright, alright.”

     

                There was a lightness in her chest as she sat there with the little party hat on, sipping her coffee and basking in the feeling of appreciation that came from the feeling of love that her new family shrouded her with. Because that was what they were to her, Lena surprisingly realised, which only made her heart ache a little more with fondness for them as outside, the storm raged, churning the waves into frothy whitecaps with the waning light.

     

                Lillian showed up an hour later, just before dinner time, and Lena heard the cheerful sound of Eliza’s voice welcoming her into her home. Climbing to her feet, feeling anxious at the mixings of her two worlds outside of the walls of a hospital, Lena moved down the hallway and hung back for a second with uncertainty on her face. When she caught her mother’s attention, she smiled tentatively, hands in her back pockets as she hunched her shoulders slightly.

     

                “Hi.”

     

                “Happy birthday,” Lillian said as a smile twisted her lips.

     

                “Yeah, thanks.”

     

                “This is a lovely house, Eliza,” Lillian commented, looking around as she shed her coat.

     

                Lena rolled her eyes and smiled crookedly, wondering what her mother’s real thoughts were. It was a spacious house, but Lillian probably would have described it as quaint . Following them through to the kitchen, Lena leaned against the counters as Alex came in, greeting Lillian and then offering up a bottle of wine. Glasses were passed out and Lena sipped the Shiraz in thoughtful silence as she let the chit chat wash over her. In some ways, she was grateful for her mother’s presence - it gave Eliza someone to talk to, aside from her kids.

     

                “Your gift hasn’t arrived yet?” Lillian asked at one point, arching an eyebrow.

     

                “I haven’t opened any yet, but I would assume not,” Lena shrugged.

     

                “Ah, well, it should be here soon then, but here’s another one for when you finally open them, then.”

     

                She took the envelope and murmured a thank you before moving into the living room to put it with the rest of the gifts until she was allowed to open them. They all migrated there with her, taking seats and chatting amicably, and Lena bit back a smile as she watched Lillian process the balloons and banners in silent surprise. Her mother looked very much out of her comfort zone, but was too stubborn and proud to admit that she wasn’t used to ordinary life. 

     

                As she sat and drank her wine, Lena became increasingly aware of the fact that she hadn’t eaten since the bite of cupcake she’d had that morning, and wondered at dinner. They’d decided on Chinese, and she imagined it would be getting delivered soon as it neared six o’clock, the sky outside dark as rain blanketed the house in white noise.

     

                Eventually, there was a knock on the door and the conversation paused as everyone turned their head towards the sound. Lillian cleared her throat as she straightened up, setting her glass down and smiling wryly.

     

                “That’ll be your gift.”

     

                “Or dinner,” Eliza supplied.

     

                “Well, why don’t you get it anyway, just in case,” Lillian suggested, jerking her chin at Lena.

     

                Climbing to her feet, Lena stooped down and set her glass on the coffee table, stepping over a balloon and ducked beneath another one as she made for the open mouth of the hallway. The porch light was on and she raked a hand through her hair as she reached for the handle and yanked it open. She was confronted with the sight of a paper bag smelling of soy and ginger, so full it obscured the delivery person, as well as a bouquet of flowers, and quietly snorted.

     

                “Jesus,” Lena muttered, reaching out to take the food. “Hi, sorry, um, how much do I owe you?”

     

                She turned and set the bursting bag down on the table inside the door and turned back, an expectant look on her face, which turned to blindsided shock as the bouquet was lowered and she was met with a familiar suntanned face and a smile she’d been dreaming of for months.

     

                “I wouldn’t mind a kiss.”

     

                Mouth falling open as she paled, heart thudding in her chest as the breath escaped her lungs, Lena was momentarily blinded by the flash of an old Polaroid camera. No sound escaped her as she stood there for a moment, frozen, willing her brain to comprehend exactly what she was seeing. What she was seeing was Kara , dressed in her fatigues with a heavy military issued bag slung over one shoulder, looking exhausted as her blue eyes filled with tears and she smiled brilliantly at Lena on the doorstep.

     

                “Happy birthday.”

     

                With a strangled sob as the spell was broken by the sound of her voice, Lena launched herself at Kara, slamming into her as she wrapped her arms around her neck and propelled them backwards. The bouquet of flowers got tossed aside as Kara slipped backwards down the couple of steps, stumbling as she wrapped an arm around Lena’s waist and went down hard on the concrete pathway as rain hammered down on them. Wincing as she tried to smile through the pain, Kara let out a tearful laugh as Lena straddled her, gripping the front of her shirt in a white-knuckled grip as she pressed her forehead against Kara’s shoulder and sobbed.

     

                Relief and happiness and a little bit of heartache too were in those sobs, and beneath her touch, Lena could feel Kara shaking too, half-laughter, half-sob, and she clung to her desperately, breathing in the smell of her perfume and the feeling of her arms around her waist. Kara pushed herself up onto her elbows after a minute, pushing Lena up with her, and cupped her face in a calloused hand as she smiled, urging Lena to meet her eyes.

     

                When she finally looked up, hair slowly plastering to her tear-stained face, Lena’s lips trembled as she reached out to cup Kara’s face between shaking hands, letting out a choked laugh as she looked at her as if seeing her for the first time. 

     

                “You’re here?” she choked out, her voice hitching and making it sound like a question as she stared at Kara with mystified eyes.

     

                “I’m here,” Kara quietly agreed, brushing the wet hair out of Lena’s face before she leaned in and kissed her, hard and holding a desperate edge as she pressed them close together before pulling back. Pressing her lips together as she fought back a smile and her eyes creased behind rain-flecked glasses, Kara thumbed her lower lip. “We should get out of the rain.”

     

                Lena’s laugh was almost hysterical as she climbed to her feet, wincing at the blossoming pain in her knees, roughly wiping her cheeks as she struggled to breathe properly. She watched as Kara rescued the abandoned flowers and rubbed at her back, where her bag had gotten wedged between her spine and the ground before Kara gave her a wide smile and reached out to take her hand. Pressing up close beside her, Lena stared up at her with parted lips and disbelief as they mounted the front steps and went inside.

     

                “But … how?” Lena asked as Kara dumped her bag in the hallway, her eyes roaming over every inch of her, taking in the tiredness that must have come from hours spent on a plane. Other than that she was fine. Safe.

     

                “Did you really think I’d miss your birthday?” Kara murmured, her face softening with such intense yearning that it made Lena’s stomach clench.

     

                She swallowed another sob and gripped at the hem of Kara’s shirt as she shook her head, still so confused. Smiling rather smugly, Kara kissed her temple and picked up the Chinese food.

     

                “I’ve missed you,” Lena murmured.

     

                “I’ve missed you, too.”

     

                Smiling widely, Lena took her by the hand and tugged playfully, “come on, come and see everyone.”

     

                Raising their entwined hands to her lips, Kara placed a kiss to the back of Lena’s, still somewhat teary-eyed. She laughed softly and the tension seemed to bleed from her shoulders, and Lena likewise felt that knot that had felt so suffocating for months now loosen in her chest; the relief left her feeling shaky and. It was strange that she’d been able to withstand Kara being gone for months now, but now that she was back, all of Lena’s strength had been leached away in an instant.

     

                They made it through the door at the end of the hallway, damp and shivering as the warmth of the house shrouded them, and Lena let out a frayed laugh as she looked around at everyone. Alex was already on her feet, and Eliza pushed herself up, and she moved aside to let Kara through, her eyes stinging as she watched her sister engulf her, followed by her mother.

     

                Skirting around them, Lena sank down onto the sofa beside Kelly and narrowed her eyes.

     

                “You all knew?”

     

                Shrugging, nonchalantly, Kelly beamed, “yeah.”

     

                “I can’t believe you didn’t tell me,” Lena spluttered, nudging her softly.

     

                “You never asked,” Kelly whispered, her eyes sparkling before she climbed to her feet for her turn.

     

                Reaching for her glass of wine, Lena took a sip and frowned as her lips curled with a smile, a bubble of happiness in her chest as she kept her eyes trained on Kara, greedily drinking in every inch of her. Her skin prickled with the sensation of being watched and she turned to catch sight of Lillian looking at her and gave her a lopsided smile.

     

                Lillian didn’t move as Kara rounded the sofa and gave her a friendly smile, nodding, “Mrs Luthor.”

     

                “You can call me Lillian, you know,” she replied with a thin smile. “How are you, Kara?”

     

                “Good,” she said, flopping down onto the sofa beside Lena and wrapping an arm around her, pulling her closer. “Better now. Thank you for doing this.”

     

                Eyebrows rising to her hairline, Lena whipped her head around to give Lillian a sharp look of incredulity. “You did this?”

     

                “You said this was what you wanted for your gift,” Lillian reminded her. “I pulled some strings.”

     

                A lump lodged itself in Lena’s throat and she swallowed painfully, ducking her head in a quick nod as she smiled slightly. “Thanks, mom.”

     

                Lillian nodded and left it at that, but Lena hoped she knew how truly grateful she was. Alex had relieved Kara of the bag of food and carried it into the kitchen and her shout drifted through, beckoning them to come and have dinner. The six of them squeezed around the table, Lena beside Kara, feeling her hand reassuringly on her knee, while Lillian sat at the head, opposite Eliza, straight-backed and watchful.

     

                Lena got the dumplings first, setting it down before Kara as Alex gave her some wine too, and they all shared out boxes with enthusiasm, a small smile staying firmly in place on Lena’s face as she enjoyed what was ultimately the best birthday she’d ever had. The kitchen was filled with their laughter and loud conversation, and even her mother managed a few quiet laughs and many wry smiles as she found herself thrust into the centre of a family who loved each other without restraint.

     

                After dinner, they were ushered through to the living room, Kara dragging her out of the kitchen by the hand, leaving everyone else to clean up as Lillian helped, the idea of leftovers a novelty for her as she closed containers and shifted things around in Eliza’s fridge to make room for them. Kara looked uneasy as she watched over her shoulder on her way out.

     

                 “This is weird right?” she whispered in Lena’s ear as she towed her over to the sofa.

     

                Flopping down beside her, pressed against her side, Lena quietly laughed. “Not for me - they’ve all met before. And bonded over nagging me to death. You being home is weirder than anything.”

     

                Kara’s fingers lightly brushed her arm as she kissed the side of Lena’s head and exhaled softly. “I wanted to talk to you about that, actually,” Kara murmured, “about going back again.”

     

                Glancing up at her, Lena gave her a strained smile, a plea in her eyes as she felt the tension return to her shoulders. “Can we, uh, talk about it in the morning?”

     

                “Oh. Yeah, sure. Of course.”

     

                “Thanks,” Lena said with an airy sigh of relief, her eyes creasing faintly at the corners as she reached up to touch Kara’s cheek. “It’s not the same on a screen.”

     

                “I know,” Kara mumbled as she touched her forehead against Lena’s.

     

                They sipped their wine and murmured amongst themselves, unable to stop smiling and pressing brief kisses and gentle touches to reassure themselves they were both there, and Lena felt the burning urge to cry again as exhaustion made her reluctant to ever move again. She would have been perfectly content to sit there on the sofa until she died, so long as Kara was beside her, their legs overlapping and her arm around her shoulders as Lena leaned against her chest.

     

                When Alex and Kelly walked back in, the latter carrying another bottle of wine, they sprawled in their own seats and left space for Lillian and Eliza to follow a minute later. Removing her arm from around Lena’s shoulder, Kara leaned forward, excitement making her perk up as she gestured with a hand.

     

                “Go on then.”

     

                She opened the cards first, reading each one silently and lining up a short row along the edge before reaching for the first gift. “Who’s this one off?”

     

                “Us,” Alex said, gesturing to Kelly.

     

                Lena smiled as she lifted the tape and unwrapped it, the thin square revealing itself to be a vinyl of the latest Florence + The Machine album that Alex must have picked out after one late night conversation about music that had revealed the common interest. She thanked them and reached for a similarly wrapped gift to reveal two books of feminist essays and thanked them again, before opening Eliza’s gift - a nice leather planner for work - and then Kara’s, feeling her girlfriend’s restless excitement beside her. 

     

                Kara had gotten them tickets to a TED Talk in National City the next week to watch an economist give a talk, something that Lena knew would be endlessly boring for Kara, which made it all the more sweeter. There was a small potted sage plant as well for her herb garden and Lena cupped the little pot in her hands as she breathed in the sweetness of the soil and the leaves.

     

                “Thank you,” Lena murmured, giving her a quick kiss as she smiled at Kara’s pleased expression. “I love them.”

     

                The thick manila envelope Lillian had handed her upon arrival was left and Lena eyed it sceptically as she picked it up. Lifting the flap, she watched as half a dozen smaller envelopes slid into her lap, each one stamped with a vivid red ‘return to sender’ stamped over the address and let out a bark of laughter.

     

                “Did you really bring all the gifts I had sent back to you?”

     

                Shrugging, Lillian gave her a thin smile as her eyes glinted with mirth. “I thought it might satisfy your curiosity.”

     

                Arching an eyebrow, Lena was reluctant to admit that she was curious, and it was only pride and the simmering anger and resentment towards her mother that had stopped her from opening the gifts and tossing them out. Returning them had been a much clearer message. Still, she picked up one by random and opened the envelope, her eyes scanning the deed she held before she let out a snort of laughter.

     

                “A private island, really?”

     

                “I thought you might vacation there, if you vacationed.”

     

                Kara’s eyes widened as she plucked the deed from Lena’s hands and let out a low whistle, hardly daring to believe she would have received something like that as a gift. The next gift was a hefty addition to Lena’s stock portfolio, and she wondered idly how much money she’d made off of them while the written information had stayed sealed in the envelope. Another held tens of thousands of hectares of land in the Amazon and various other agricultural and ecological places dotted around the planet, an effort on Lillian’s behalf to support Lena’s conservation plan. The other gifts were likewise similar, all of them amounting to a sum of millions , and Lena had to hand it to her mother, she knew her daughter’s interests and had spared no costs trying to win her favour.

     

                “Thanks, mom,” Lena said with amusement hitching the corners of her mouth as she slid everything back into the envelope.

     

                Lillian nodded, waving a dismissive hand, and Lena smiled at everyone else. “And thank you to all of you.”

     

                The warmth in her chest made her cheeks ache as they deeply dimpled with a permanent smile, feeling so spoiled at the effort and kindness gone into making her birthday special. She’d never felt happier in her life, of that she was sure, and that feeling tied to everyone in the room with her, but most importantly, the person beside her. The one who had been taking photos and now hunched over them with Lena, their heads ducked together as they took in the happiness, so obviously written on Lena’s face.

     

                Eliza slipped out into the kitchen while she was preoccupied, and when the lights dimmed a moment later, Lena looked up, confused, before the glow of candles stuck into a cake made her groan. Slinking down in her seat, she laughed and covered her face as everyone sang happy birthday to her, Kara carrying them with her good pitch. As they trailed off, Kara gestured to her with a dopey grin on her face. 

     

                “Make a wish!”

     

                Lena laughed at her naivety but indulged her anyway, thinking carefully for a second. She couldn’t think of anything she wanted; Kara was there with her already. All she could wish for now was that Kara would stay safe and that she’d stay with Lena. Closing her eyes, she thought it, gripped the wish tightly, and then blew out the candles as she squeezed Kara’s knee.

     

                “I’ll get plates,” Eliza said as Kelly picked the cake up and Lillian moved to let Athena outside as the dog lingered near the back door.

     

                Lena climbed to her feet to go and help plate up the cake while Alex refilled wine glasses from her seat. As she moved towards the kitchen door, Lena watched as her mother followed the dog out on the back deck, a flood of cold, rainy air gusting inside briefly.

     

                Returning with two slices of red velvet cake, Lena’s brow creased as she handed one off to Alex and stared at the recently vacated spot where Kara had been sitting. Alex jerked her head towards the screen door, the porch light on outside and the smell of the sea rushing in through the mesh. Lena moved over to it, hesitating as the sound of voices fell on her ears.

     

                “I just wanted to say thank you, for what you did,” Kara slowly said, her voice earnest with gratitude.

     

                “It pays to have friends in high places,” Lillian said, her voice slightly smug and amused. “I’ve known Colonel Haley for years; she owed me a favour.”

     

                “Ah, well, I’m sorry you had to waste it on something so trivial.”

     

                Kara’s soft huff of laughter made Lena’s heart twinge and her brows furrowed together at her mother’s reply. “I’ve never seen her happier; it’s not trivial to her, so it’s not trivial to me.”

     

                “Right. Well, thank you, again.”

     

                There was a brief moment of silence before Lillian spoke. “I hear you’re thinking of reenlisting?”

     

                “Did- did Lena tell you that?”

     

                Lillian laughed at the wary doubt in Kara’s voice, “no, your mom did. I suspected something was off when she almost pulled her stitches after talking to you.”

     

                “Yeah … Lena- she doesn’t- well …”

     

                “She loves you, you know.”

     

                Kara hesitated and let out a choked laugh, vaguely embarrassed. “I- yeah, I do.”

     

                “And do you love her?”

     

                The reply was immediate, full of surprise as if Kara couldn’t believe it would need to be asked. “Of course!” she quietly exclaimed. 

     

                “Good, then you know what’s at stake for her. She’s told you everything, I assume?” There was a slight pause where Lena presumed Kara nodded. “Then, do you have what it takes to be there for her? Not for a month or a year, but a life? One bad experience could set her back decades, and if that bad experience is you-”

     

                A hand on her shoulder made Lena jump slightly, her heart stuttering in her chest, and she turned to look at Alex, who jerked her head over to the sofa, the message clear. Leave them to talk. Lena was reluctant but wasn’t prone to eavesdropping and made her way over to the sofa. Picking up the slice meant for Kara, she gouged a mouthful off the side with a spoon and ate as she thought about what she’d heard. She felt that she should have been annoyed with her mother, but her mood was too good to be soured by any sort of interference right then, and when Kelly walked in and Alex seized Trivial Pursuit from the teetering stack of board games, she resolved to push it aside and enjoy her birthday without letting anything cloud her happiness.

     

                They were all soon back inside, and when Lena raised her eyebrows at Kara’s flushed cheeks, Kara gave her a sweet smile, squeezing her arm before they were ordered to pair up. It went without saying that Alex and Kara chose their girlfriends, leaving their moms to partner up, and it was a close competition as they raced to fill their wheel with the colourful wedges. Kara and Lena clinched a win by one wedge, based entirely on Kara’s knowledge of sporting history and there was a raucous round of complaints and gleeful laughter before they set up Clue.

     

                They cycled through the boardgames for a couple of hours, Eliza winning at Clue, Kelly winning at Monopoly before Lillian won the second, picking it up surprisingly quick, before Alex and Kelly won at Pictionary and Kara got into a heated fight with her sister that resulted in them no longer playing Pictionary. Wine made them all happier, their smiles and laughter coming more easily, and Lena would’ve been content to stay up until midnight, wrapped in the bubble of contagious joy as her birthday passed by, but eventually they packed everything up and her mother left. 

     

                After thanking everyone and saying her goodbyes, Lillian let Lena walk her to the front door as her driver waited outside, headlight illuminating the sprinkling of rain. Lena chewed on the inside of her lip as she hugged her arms to herself and ducked her head, before looking up and giving Lillian a crooked smile.

     

                “Thank you,” Lena started, “I- uh, it means a lot to me. More than you know.”

     

                “Of course,” Lillian said, waving her thanks aside. “I hope you’ve had a good day.”

     

                “The best.”

     

                They hovered awkwardly for a moment on the cusp of goodbye, and Lena surprised them both when she suddenly darted forward and wrapped her arms tightly around Lillian, who let out a soft exclamation of surprise. She returned it a little belatedly and patted her back when Lena started to withdraw, but her delight was unmistakable in the softening of her face as she looked at Lena.

     

                “Thank you,” Lena whispered, her face crumpling as she stared at her, still somewhat confused. “Thank you for bringing her home.”

     

                “Enjoy it,” Lillian told her, her smile thin as her blue eyes flashed. “I’ll speak to you soon. I love you.”

     

                “Alright, sure,” Lena lightly murmured before pausing, hesitating as uncertainty curled through her and she managed a slow and halting response. “I- you- well … you know, I- I love you too. Thanks mom.”

     

                Surprise was slow to flash across Lillian’s face, the loosening of her jaw muscles a telltale sign, and she let out a quiet huff of laughter as confusion filled her bright eyes, before stepping forward and kissing Lena on the cheek. Patting her shoulder, she hesitated but then turned without another word and walked down the steps, towards the waiting car.

     

                She paused to wave as she ducked into the car and Lena raised her hand in reply before opening the screen door and stepping back into the warmth. Kara was waiting for her at the bottom of the staircase, elbows on her knees and a weary slump to her shoulders as she smiled tiredly.

     

                Walking over to her, Lena held her hands out and pulled her to her feet before rising on her tiptoes to bridge the few inches to kiss her. “Come on. You should sleep.”

     

                “I don’t want to sleep,” Kara murmured, cupping the side of her neck. “I want to spend every moment of the next two weeks with you.”

     

                Lena laughed and hummed as her face softened with adoration, “you’ve been on a plane all day; I think falling asleep beside you tonight will be just as perfect.”

     

                “Alright, if you’re sure,” Kara said, looking sheepish but grateful.

     

                They went to say goodnight to the trio, helping tidy things up briefly before they went upstairs to Kara’s room. Bringing her bag with her, Kara set it down heavily and let out a contented sight before turning and collapsing backwards onto the bed, letting out a low groan.

     

                “I’ve forgotten how comfy real mattresses are. God , it’s good to be home.”

     

                Lena laughed and crawled on top of her, pinning her beneath her weight as her body went limp. “Mm, I’ve forgotten how comfy cuddling with you is.”

     

                “Is that the only thing you’ve forgotten?” Kara asked, moving in one fluid motion to flip them over so she was on top of Lena, one hand catching her wrists and pinning them above her head. She leaned down and kissed her slowly, achingly sweet and almost torturous as Lena gave her a resigned look when she pulled back.

     

                “Have I not suffered enough yet?”

     

                “I guess you’ll have to wait a bit longer,” Kara chuckled before climbing off her and slipping off the bed.

     

                She pulled her fatigues off, discarding them on the floor, and changed into pyjamas from a bag that Lena only just realised had been one of Alex’s, filled with Kara’s clothes. Likewise changing, Lena moved to tug on a thin sweater when Kara’s hands cradled her waist and she paused, her arms through the sleeves and an arched eyebrow as she gave her an expectant look.

     

                Kara’s eyes were trained on her stomach - or rather, on the scar - and Lena pulled her head through and let the fabric fall into place. It didn’t deter Kara though, as she pushed it back up and smoothed her thumb over the pink, slightly puckered line.

     

                “I can’t believe I wasn’t here,” Kara miserably murmured.

     

                Lena pulled her hand free and then reached for the lights, pulling her over to the bed. They climbed beneath the blankets, warm and comfortable in each other’s embrace, and she let out a long sigh.

     

                “I was glad you weren’t; I wouldn’t have wanted you to see that.”

     

                “It feels like so long since I last saw you, but it also feels like I never left,” Kara sighed, her voice scratchy. “God, how I’ve missed you.”

     

                Blinking furiously as a sob built in her chest and she let out a tearful laugh, Lena burrowed her face into Kara’s chest. “I can’t believe you’re actually here. Four months! I’ve spent every day wishing for this moment. Some days … it was so unbearable, I didn’t think I could stand it for another second.”

     

                “I don’t think I could’ve stood not seeing you for a minute longer,” Kara chuckled, rolling Lena over and feeling for the short scar in the dark, her fingers warm and gentle on her stomach. “I’ve been worried sick about you - especially after this.”

     

                She shifted down the bed and Lena shivered at the feeling of Kara’s warm lips softly kissing it as she gripped her waist. Closing her eyes, Lena let out a strained laugh, throwing an arm across her face.

     

                “You’ve been worried? I’ve been out of my mind, Kara Danvers,” she sternly told her, dissolving into a fit of laughter as her contrarian emotions swung wildly from one end of the spectrum to the other, like a pendulum. 

     

                Kara moved back up the bed and smiled as she pressed a clumsy kiss to the side of Lena’s mouth. Then she kissed her again, harder this time, and Lena’s lips parted beneath her own before she broke it off a moment later, laughing as she wiped tears from her cheeks. “Sorry, I don’t mean to cry, I just-”

     

                “I know,” Kara murmured. “I know.”

     

                “I love you.”

     

                “I love you too.”

     

                For the first time in as long as she could remember, Lena slept soundly, one arm thrown over Kara’s waist as she pressed up against her back as close as she could, feeling her breaths and the drumming of her heartbeat through the cotton of her shirt. They breathed in unison, both deeply asleep without the weight of concern for Kara’s safety hanging over them, and Lena clutched Kara tightly, as if she was never going to let her go again.

    Chapter 37

                “No!”

     

                The yell tore Lena from her sleep, shooting up in bed, wild-eyed and her heart racing as she immediately became alert. Rubbing at her eyes, she blinked and looked beside her, Kara propped up on her side as she turned away from Lena, head bowed and shoulders tense as her quick, shallow breaths sounded ragged in the ensuing silence.

     

                Lena was hesitant to touch her for a moment as panic settled in, but she slowly placed a hand on her shoulder, feeling her pulse race beneath the cotton. This was something Lena didn’t know how to fix, something she’d only seen the surface of when Kara sometimes jerked away, a cold sweat covering her as she breathed quickly. This was more .

     

                “Hey, you’re okay,” Lena murmured, a concerned look clouding her face.

     

                Kara didn’t shrug her touch off, and after a few moments, Lena felt the tension unwind and she rolled back onto her back. With a subdued sigh, Kara ran a hand over her face and then blinked, her poor vision making her squint as she reached out and fumbled for her glasses before jamming them on her face.

     

                “Good morning,” Kara said, her voice thick with sleep and slightly scratchy as she smiled tiredly, cheeks pink and creased with the seam of the pillows.

     

                It was a clear morning, the sky a pale blue as the early morning sunrise slanted in through the windows. Her hair, her skin and even the freckles on her nose seemed to glow golden as she leaned over and kissed Lena slowly before flopping back down onto her back and holding her arms open.

     

                “Kara-”

     

                “I’m fine , baby. It was just a bad dream,” Kara evasively murmured, unconvincing but her tone firm, broaching no further arguments from Lena as she cuddled up beside her, throwing an arm across her tanned stomach.

     

                “Do you want to tell me about it?”

     

                “No. Not right now.”

     

                There was an undercurrent of pain to her whispered words that made Lena’s throat constrict, but she didn’t push her. She listened to the steady drum of her heart as Kara idley trailed her fingertips over the satin skin of her back, touching her distractedly as she let her fingers drag over her back in a featherlight, ticklish touch. 

     

                They stayed like that for a few minutes, warm and comfortable and reluctant to leave their bed. It would have been enough for Lena to stay there for two weeks, her eyes half-lidded as she luxuriated in the feeling of Kara’s warmth surrounding her, the smell of her on the sheets, her slowing breaths as whatever panic had gripped her slowly retreated.

     

                Absentmindedly running her fingers through Lena’s hair, Kara let out a soft sigh. “We need to talk,” she slowly said, wariness curling around her words as she stared up at the ceiling. “About me reenlisting.”

     

                Lena closed her eyes, swallowing thickly as her stomach swooped. “Can’t we just have breakfast first?”

     

                “You can’t keep avoiding the conversation,” Kara said with thin amusement, reaching up to press her fingertips to Lena’s cheek.

     

                Rolling away from her touch, Lena sat up and ran a hand through her hair as she swung her legs off the edge of the bed and hunched her shoulders. Kara’s hand reached across the mattress for her, urging her to come back into her embrace, but Lena didn’t see, head bowed as she rubbed at her forehead.

     

                “I’m not avoiding it; I’d just prefer not to have it right now.”

     

                “Lena-”

     

                “Kara.”

     

                “I’m not reenlisting!” Kara softly exclaimed.

     

                Lena stiffened and whirled around, eyebrows rising in surprise as her mouth fell open and she found herself speechless for a second. Quietly laughing at the look on her face, Kara shrugged and grinned goofily at her, although there was a subdued quality to it. A prickle of guilt, if Lena wasn’t mistaken.

     

                “I- you … you’re not reenlisting? Ever?” she asked, head cocked to the side with confusion crumpling her face. 

     

                “Never ever.”

     

                Lena felt her chest loosen and her breath return, slow and steady, as Kara pushed herself up and kissed the tip of her nose. Letting out a breathless laugh, Lena collided with her and pinned her on the mattress, peppering kisses all over Kara’s face as she squirmed beneath her, laughing. 

     

                “Thank you, thank you, thank you,” Lena murmured between kisses, her eyes stinging with tears that she could scarcely withhold.

     

                A thump sounded on the wall, the muffled sound of Alex’s disgruntled voice drifting through the walls, and the two of them pressed their lips together to hide their laughter, mouths quirking up at the corners as their foreheads touched and they shook from the effort. Lena’s heart could have burst from her chest at how happy she was to share such silly little moments with Kara.

     

                A minute later, the door shuddered with a frustrated kick and Alex opened it, squinting and irritable as her hair stuck out at odd angles. She rubbed at her bleary eyes and let out a scathing sigh.

     

                “Do you two have to be so cheerful at six o’clock in the morning.”

     

                “Uh, yeah,” Lena beamed at her, “because she’s not reenlisting.”

     

                Alertness dragged across Alex’s face as she slowly came out of lingering sleep, brown eyes owlishly round as her lips parted. The look of relief and elation was a mirror to Lena’s only minutes before and she tipped her head back, letting out a sigh. 

     

                “Thank God,” Alex mumbled.

     

                Rolling out of bed, Kara climbed to her feet, stretching as she smiled widely, backlit by the early glow of sunlight. As she approached Alex, her sister punched her squarely in the arm, eliciting a complaint as Kara gave her a wounded look, rubbing at the sore spot.

     

                “Ow? What was that for?”

     

                “For even considering it. Idiot,” Alex grumbled. 

     

                A choked laugh fell from Kara’s mouth and she ribbed her sister as she squeezed past her, leaving Lena to roll out of bed and fix the sheets as she smiled to herself. She felt happier than she could ever remember, perhaps even more so than last night. That lingering malodorous worry at what Kara would choose suddenly came loose. She’d go back for another five months and that would be it. They just had to make it through another five months apart, get her safely through the rest of her deployment, and then Lena would never have to let her go again.

     

                Making her way downstairs, she was greeted at the bottom with a steaming cup of coffee and a lingering kiss, smiling into it before Kara tugged insistently on her hand. They pulled on their coats and shoved their feet into shoes before Kara snagged a blanket and pulled her towards the back door. They sat side by side on the back porch love seat, sipping their coffee with the blanket spread across their laps.

     

                “I’ve missed this,” Kara sighed, eyes closed as she smiled, her head tilted upwards as the bracing sea air caressed her face. “I’ve missed the ocean, and the cold; it’s always so hot and dry there.”

     

                Lena’s lips twitched faintly and she listened to the waves just over the cresting dunes and let it soothe her, that ceaseless ebb and flow, the crash of the breaking waves, the grating sigh of its retreat as it left shells and smooth glass behind, little gifts on the shore. She was pensive and at peace, watching as the sky took its time to lighten as the sun rose from behind them, still partially obscured by the distant mountains and trees to the east.

     

                “What is it?” Kara asked suddenly, an expectant look on her face.

     

                Eyes creasing as she let out a quiet laugh, Lena tipped her head to the side and leaned it on Kara’s shoulder as she exhaled, deflating. “I’ve missed you being able to tell when I’m thinking too hard. I just- why aren’t you going back? Is it because of me? Because I asked?” 

     

                “Of course it is,” Kara murmured, smoothing a hand over Lena’s hair.

     

                “Then don’t,” Lena said around the lump of reluctance in her throat. “Don’t do it for me.”

     

                “Let me finish,” Kara softly pressed, laughing into her hair and placing a delicate kiss there. “Yes, I did it for you, and for Alex and my mom. But I also did it for myself. I think … I knew I wasn’t going to go back after this tour, I was just scared. About what I’ll do after - it’s been my life for so long that I don’t know what I’d do if no one told me to do it. But I knew I was coming home to see you, so I just- I needed to see you to realise exactly how much I have to lose. I don’t know how I’m going to bring myself to leave again for another few months, let alone over and over again for a couple more years. I … I don’t want to be the one that causes you pain.”

     

                “You’ve taken away more than you’ve caused,” Lena said, her voice wavering and small.

     

                Kara cradled the underside of her jaw and urged her to look up, a tender look softening her tanned face as she wrinkled her nose, a sweet smile curling her lips. “Even a little is too much for me. I just want to make you happy.”

     

                “You do . More than you could ever know. I just- I want you to be happy too, and I want you to be sure-”

     

                “The only thing I’ve ever been more sure about is that I love you.”

     

                “I’m glad you’re sure of that one,” Lena lightly teased, kissing her shoulder. “Although, you might’ve told me you were staying yesterday and saved me the extra day of worry.”

     

                “I tried!” Kara exclaimed, a look of indignation on her face as she let out a guffaw of laughter, “you told me not to!”

     

                Laughing, Lena groaned softly, tugging the blanket up higher as she burrowed up against Kara’s warmth. “I thought you were leaving again!”

     

                “No! But you told me not to tell you, and good news or not, I didn't want to make you listen.”

     

                “Alright, alright. I’m sorry for being evasive.”

     

                They heard the muffled shout of Alex calling them inside for breakfast, and Kara withdrew her arm from around Lena’s shoulder and gathered up the blanket. Whistling for Athena, who bounded over, sandy and damp, they walked back inside, shrugging off coats as the warmth slammed into them. They walked into the kitchen to find Kelly yawning widely as she nursed her own cup of coffee.

     

                “Glad to see you made the right choice,” Kelly said with a relieved smile.

     

                Kara gave her a crooked smile as she nodded, sinking down onto an empty chair while Lena went to help Alex, who was wielding a spatula with frightening efficiency as she cooked up a storm, everything sizzling and slightly smoking and clattering. Helping plate up fried eggs, bacon and French toast, Lena deposited them before Kara and Kelly, her touch trailing along the former’s shoulders as she relished the ability to do so. It felt like she’d never left, but Lena had to reassure herself that she was still there.

     

                “I’ve been thinking about this for so long, I think I might cry,” Kara announced as she drizzled syrup over her heaped plate.

     

                They ate fast, with Kara getting a second serving once she was finished, and then Alex and Kelly volunteered to go grocery shopping with Eliza, bidding them to stay home as they all filed out to the car and drove off. Finishing putting the last few plates away, Lena glanced over at Kara, who was wiping suds off her hands, and narrowed her eyes in a shrewd look.

     

                “Your sister isn’t very subtle.”

     

                Glancing over at her, Kara’s face split with a grin as she shrugged indifferently, “yeah, I wouldn’t say she’s known for it.”

     

                “Well, I , for one, am grateful,” Lena said, nudging a cupboard door shut with her foot and making a bee-line for Kara.

     

                She grabbed her by the waist, pulling her close, and kissed her greedily. Toying with the waistband of the sweatpants Lena wore, Kara hummed against her lips, pulling back as she glanced down and gave her an appraising look, appreciative and pleased.

     

                “You’ve been stealing my clothes?”

     

                “I missed you,” Lena simply replied.

     

                Kara distracted her with a kiss after that and they lifted her easily, corded muscles shifting in her arms as she wrapped them around Lena and whisked her upstairs - albeit clumsily and in lurching bursts of motion as they laughed against each other’s lips, tripping up steps and clinging to the walls. She kissed the scar on Lena’s stomach when her shirt came off, her lips lightly brushing the raised line.

     

                “I memorised every inch of you before I left,” Kara murmured, pressing another kiss to her stomach before glancing up with a flicker of annoyance in her eyes, “and went over it a thousand times while I was over there, so this is annoying.”

     

                “Annoying?” Lena snorted, “it’s so small, you can barely even notice it.”

     

                “I noticed it,” Kara pointedly replied. “Did it hurt?”

     

                Wrinkling her nose, Lena pushed aside the collar of Kara’s t-shirt and pressed a kiss to the hollow of her neck. “A little.”

     

                “You’re so full of shit,” Kara breathlessly laughed against Lena’s cheek as she pushed her down.

     

                They were both too impatient to stretch it out, teasing and luxuriating in it - that could wait - and it was enough that they had a handful of minutes to themselves, their desperation bubbling to the surface and leaving them blissfully exhausted afterwards. The room was cold but they were warm against each other, breaths evening out and sweat drying on skin, and after a few minutes of heavy-lidded content, Lena pushed herself up slightly, tracing a finger over Kara’s collarbone.

     

                “Bath?”

     

                Groaning, Kara gave her a grateful look, “I’ve been dreaming of one.”

     

                It was a small bathtub, and she squeezed in behind Kara, letting her lean back against her as she massaged soothing circles into her neck and shoulders. Bubbles frothed in piles around them and in the warmth of the steam, Lena could have fallen asleep, as content as she was with the heaviness of Kara pressing against her. She didn’t linger though; she climbed out of the tub and wrapped a towel around herself as she let Kara stretch out, basking in the feeling of a hot bath as Lena sank onto the bath mat and watched her.

     

                Raising her head off the rim of the bath, Kara gave her a slow smile, blonde eyebrows rising as her flushed cheeks dimpled and she brushed a damp strand of hair off her brow. “Hey, there’s somewhere I want to take you later.”

     

                “Mm,” Lena curiously hummed, leaning over to kiss Kara’s hand, gripping the side of the bath.

     

                “It’s an hour down south. It’s the perfect time of year to go there.”

     

                 “Well now I’m intrigued,” Lena said, climbing to her feet and stooping down to kiss her on the shoulder. “What are we going to see?”

     

                “You’ll have to wait and find out,” Kara told her with a smug smile, trailing her fingers through the thinning bubbles.

     

                Curiosity made Lena ask her half a dozen times but Kara wouldn’t budge and they soon found themselves on the sofa, watching Pride & Prejudice as they lazily kissed, a blanket drawn up over them as they laughed, both of them struggling to fit on the narrow cushions. Their teeth knocked and Lena accidentally elbowed Kara, but they couldn’t stop smiling. It felt like they had all the time in the world.

     

                Everyone returned home when they were still relatively early on in the movie and they paused it to help cram groceries into cupboards and the fridge, while Kara opened packets and sneaked in a few snacks in the process. She was wearing a faded Blondie t-shirt and cuffed jeans, leaning against the counters as she wolfed down a blueberry muffin and smiled whenever she caught Lena’s eye. 

     

                No one did much that day, although there was talk of going to the diner in town tomorrow as they ate leftovers and birthday cake for lunch, the day warming minutely beyond the windows as they filled their idle hours with the occasional comment as Lena completed the crossword and Kara and Kelly talked about mutual military friends.

     

                As the afternoon wore on, Kara informed them they’d be out for dinner, urging Lena to get ready as she grinned excitedly, a corduroy jacket thrown over her t-shirt as she took Eliza’s car keys and waited for Lena to put on her shoes. It was still bright outside, but dusk wasn’t too far away and Lena’s curiosity spiked as she sank into the passenger seat and buckled herself in, excitement kindling in her stomach.

     

                They followed the highway south, Kara singing along to the static-filled radio as she drummed her fingers on the steering wheel, while Lena leaned against the window and watched her, thinking that she would’ve stayed in that seat forever, listening to Kara sing as they drove aimlessly around the country, just the two of them. They’d picked up lattes on the way and the heater softly blew out warm air and Lena was comfortable .

     

                It was another twenty minutes of driving, turning down various roads that grew steadily narrower and quieter, until they were coasting along a road littered with leaves a dozen shades of autumn, damp and skittering in the brisk wind. The pines and conifers had given way to a riot of trees that exploded in colour - red maples and golden aspens and more crowded in besides in a spectacular display of maroons and fiery oranges and purplish browns - as they threaded up through the foothills of mountains. Where it wasn’t giving way to autumn, moss and lichen still blanketed the rocky terrain and Lena felt they had escaped elsewhere.

     

                “This is it,” Kara said, turning to look at her.

     

                It wasn’t quite sunset yet, but as they drove down the long road as it slowly sloped westwards, the sinking sun bathed everything golden, the trees forming a tangled canopy that shaded the dim road while the forest looked like it had been set on fire. Lena’s lips curved with a smile as she watched leaves whirl around them, turning to look at Kara.

     

                “It’s beautiful.”

     

                “It’s one of my favourite places in the world ,” Kara beamed, “but only at this time of year. I thought I was going to have to wait until next year to bring you.”

     

                Staring at her as she slumped against the car door, Lena realised she had never been more in love with Kara than in that moment. It should have been impossible that she kept getting struck by that realisation, but she wanted to capture the moment, bottle it and keep it with her at all times.

     

                “Where’s your camera? We should get some photos of this.”

     

                She straightened up in her seat and turned, rummaging around in the back as she found the camera in Kara’s backpack. Turning it in her hands, Lena smiled as she lifted it to her eyes and snapped a photo of Kara, who startled slightly and glanced over at her.

     

                “You’re supposed to be appreciating the view!”

     

                “I am!”

     

                Snorting, Kara’s cheek dimpled as she glanced sideways at Lena, “make sure you get one of yourself.”

     

                Lena laughed and leaned across the centre console, grinning widely as she held the camera out at arm’s length, trying to fit them both in as she pushed the button and blinked back the black spots as it chugged out a square. She made sure to take photos through the windshield too, catching starbursts of sunlight as the colours faded and the shadows lengthened. 

     

                They drove until the trees ended, the road dipping down and winding through the foothills as the dark pines crowded back in and the ocean was a seething mass reflecting the golden glimmer of waning sunlight spreading out in the near distance. Night came on fast, as it did on the coast, with nothing obscuring the view as the sun sank so low on the horizon that they couldn’t look directly at it as it drifted from sight.

     

                A seaside town greeted them with a smattering of lights against the encroaching darkness and Kara glanced sideways at her, taking a switch-back around a rocky rise. “This town has the best fish and chips - you have to try it.”

     

                She parked up along a short street lining the docks, clapboard shacks of shops and bars and restaurants greeting them as they climbed out of the car, pulling on coats and reaching instinctively for each other’s hands. Water lapped at the shore and music spilled out of a restaurant, but they slipped into one that was a little shabbier than the rest, peeling paint and rusted hinges and a fine layer of salt riming the windows.

     

                It was warm and smelled of beer and seafood inside though, and at a small booth, they ordered fish and oysters and calamari, Lena buying Kara beer under the insistence that she’d drive home - she wasn’t operating on a limited amount of time where she could indulge herself - and a Coke for herself, the cold sweetness of it making her teeth ache as she rinsed away the vinegary taste on her tongue.

     

                Afterwards, she sat behind the wheel and took a quicker route back towards Midvale, night leaving everything shrouded in darkness and shadow as they raced down winding tree-lined streets, occasionally driving along cliff-side roads as the ocean roared dully below them. It was peaceful with the radio crooning and Kara along with it, and before they went home Kara instructed her to take a turn-off and led them to a secret patch of woods right on the edge of the water. They were too high up for the headlight to illuminate anything but the darkness ahead, revealing nothing, and Lena cut the engine and the lights.

     

                It was a squeeze in the back seat of the car but they made do and afterwards they lay awkwardly, half-dressed as Kara rested her head on Lena’s chest while Lena ran her fingers through her hair. It was cramped and uncomfortable, but neither of them had a single complaint as they dwelled in silence. 

     

                “You know, I’ve never had car sex before,” Kara eventually laughed, pushing herself up slightly to look at Lena. “That one was a first for me.”

     

                Lena laughed quietly and brushed her knuckles across Kara’s cheek, a bewildered look clouding her green eyes as she shook her head. “I just can’t believe you’re here.”

     

                It felt surreal and she wasn’t sure she’d get used to it until she was leaving again. Two weeks felt like an eternity when they’d spent so long apart, but it would pass by quickly. Pushing the intruding thoughts aside before they could ruin her blissful glow, Lena kissed Kara and then pushed herself up, finishing getting dressed and climbing through to the driver’s seat.

     

                She drove the rest of the way home undisturbed, save for Kara’s fleeting kisses to the back of her hand or the squeeze of her knee, and they arrived home in time to sit through another movie with everyone. Lena felt a prickle of guilt at monopolising Kara’s time and willingly shared her, sipping wine beside Kelly as Kara showed Alex the photos they’d taken. 

     

                It was a later night than the one before, the four of them staying up late as Eliza went to bed on account of having work the next morning, and they drank wine and talked quietly over hands of poker, only half paying attention to the game - or else they might have noticed Lena was counting cards - past midnight. Collapsing into bed beside Kara later on, Lena pressed up against her back and kissed the side of her neck, feeling Kara’s hand cup the back of her thigh.

     

                “I love you,” Lena whispered into her hair.

     

                “I love you too.”

     

                A simple enough declaration that made them both sleep better, twin heart beats and breaths, wrapped up in the touch of each other as they slumbered, one at peace and the other restless and malcontent as bad dreams plagued her sleep.

     

                Lena was pulled from sleep before sunrise by a startled shout, hoarse and short.
