Groggily pushing herself up, a listless sigh fell from her lips as she glanced at Kara, who was sitting upright, head in her hands as her chest rose and fell with quick, panicked breaths. Reaching out, Lena hesitantly touched her knee and Kara’s warm hand engulfed hers as she gave it a reassuring squeeze.

     

                “I’m fine,” Kara mumbled before Lena could even ask.

     

                “Kara-”

     

                “Go back to sleep, baby,” Kara murmured.

     

                She stood in one fluid motion and crossed the room in long strides, slipping out without enough word as Lena was left looking at the closed door helplessly. Clutching the blankets in a white-knuckled grip for a minute, Lena shook her head to clear away the last vestiges of sleep and stumbled out of bed, the floor frigid beneath her bare soles as she crept downstairs, rubbing at her eyes.

     

                Kara was already gone by the time she made it downstairs, Athena’s leash gone from the table inside the front door along with Kara’s sneakers and her coat. Slipping her feet into the first pair of shoes she found, she dragged on a puffy coat that she thought might have been Eliza’s and opened the front door. Pushing the screen open, she found herself staring at the night obscured by a mist that had rolled in off the coat, laced with salt and bitterly cold as her breath plumed before her. She tried to squint through the veil but everything was obscured by it as the tendrils swirled and muffled the sounds of the still early morning.

     

                Sighing defeatedly, Lena rubbed at her forehead and deliberated for a moment before sinking down onto the front step. The concrete was damp and the cold seeped into her as she hugged her arms to herself, shivering and stiffening as she waited for Kara to come back. It was a matter of stubborn pride that she waited outside in the cold instead of in the warmth of the kitchen, one that she was slowly coming to regret as time dragged on for nearly an hour, long enough for dawn to break and the mist to thin, before Kara materialised.

     

                Athena reached Lena first, tongue lolling and tail wagging as she barrelled up the steps and started licking her cheeks, pungent damp fur assaulting her as she tried to calm her down. She was well trained that it didn’t take more than a gentle gesture for her to obediently sit, tail rhythmically thwacking against a bush as she waited patiently, Lena stroking the short bristles of her muzzle.

     

                “Oh!” Kara softly exclaimed as Lena’s form became apparent to her. Her shoulders drooped wearily and she frowned as she reached up, brushing damp hair out of her flushed face. “What’re you doing out here?”

     

                “I was w-waiting for you,” Lena stammered through clenched teeth as she tried to stop them from chattering.

     

                It made her jaw ache and didn’t dissuade the shiver that wracked her, her cheeks rosy from the cold. Kara dropped to a crouch before her, picking up Lena’s hands in her own and griping at the cold of them as she cradled them in her own warm ones and softly breathed on them, rubbing some warmth into her pink fingertips.

     

                “You’re freezing. You should’ve waited inside,” Kara frowned.

     

                “Where did you go?” Lena asked, ignoring her concern as she eyed the sweat-soaked collar of Kara’s shirt beneath the unzipped front of her coat.

     

                “Just for a jog, to clear my head,” Kara murmured, shrugging half-heartedly.

     

                They were both silent for a moment and Lena stared down at their hands, watching as Kara gently rubbed the warmth back into them, shockingly tanned against Lena’s pallid fingers. She let out a pent up breath, searing as it was forced up her throat, and wilted helplessly on the step.

     

                “Kara … I just- tell me how I can help you. Please.”

     

                Giving her a thin smile, Kara tweaked her chin as her sad eyes creased with love, “you can’t. But I’m fine. I promise.”

     

                “This is the second day in a row-”

     

                “It’s always like this when I get home,” Kara admitted. “My mind is just … struggling to catch up with everything that happened over there. I don’t really get time to process it, I’m too tired to process it, so it’s just- being home, having nothing to do … well, I’m not too tired to dream now. It’s the same every time; you just- you never knew me when I first got back last time. I’d already had a week to process it.”

     

                Lena blanched as she listened to Kara talk, felt a lump forming in her throat as that familiar bitterness at finding herself helpless well up in her chest. She didn’t know what to do ; she didn’t know how to help, and Lena hated to not have the answers to a problem.

     

                “Kara,” she whispered, her voice cracking and wheedling as her face crumpled.

     

                “It’s okay,” Kara murmured, a smile softening her expression as she cupped the back of Lena’s neck. “Just … give me a couple of days.”

     

                Letting out a choked breath, Lena gave her an aching look. “Have you thought about- about seeing someone? I mean, surely Kelly can find someone who can help-”

     

                “Lena, I’m fine . If I need a shrink, I promise you I’ll ask Kelly to find me one. Really. I just- it’s not that bad.”

     

                “Can you just not … dismiss it so easily?” Lena asked, lips tightening as she felt the tension brimming in her shoulders. “They’re not dreams - they’re memories. Bad ones. I just think you should at least consider it.”

     

                With a soft sigh, avoiding her worried stare, Kara cupped Lena’s cold cheeks in her hands and kissed her forehead. “You’re probably right,” she admitted. “I’ll think about it while I’m away, but … I don’t know. I just don’t think I’m there yet.”

     

                “And that’s okay, but I want you to take care of yourself, and if you need help … well, there’s nothing wrong with that. And I can help you too.”

     

                Kara met her eyes, her own softening as she smiled sweetly, “all I need right now is to get you inside before you freeze. And a nice cup of coffee.” Pausing, she wrinkled her nose. “And maybe a shower.”

     

                Shaking her head as her face pinched with amusement, Lena stiffly unfolded herself, climbing to her feet. “Okay, I get it; I’ll let it go for now.”

     

                “Thank you,” Kara whispered, hesitating as she brushed a thumb over Lena’s chapped lips. “But really, I think your lips are turning blue. I can help you warm them up if you’d like.”

     

                Lena rolled her eyes and nudged her before she pressed a lingering kiss to Kara’s lips and they pulled open the screen door and pushed her way inside. Shrugging off coats and kicking off shoes, Athena tracking damp poor prints down the passage as Lena hissed for her top stop and Kara laughed, the sounds seeming loud in the silence of the house.

     

                “I’m going to shower,” Kara whispered, “I’ll be quick.”

     

                Moving down the hallway, Lena slipped past the dog and made it to her bed first, snatching up the blanket and whispering her forward before she roughly dried her off and then rubbed her behind her pricked ears. Making quiet kissing noises and urging her down onto the rumpled blanket, Lena pushed herself to her feet and stepped through to the kitchen, switching on the light and clapping a hand to her mouth as a yelp escaped her.

     

                “Jesus, you frightened me,” Lena breathlessly laughed, pressing a hand to her chest as Eliza looked up.

     

                “Sorry, honey. You’re both up early.”

     

                Lena hummed, rubbing at her tired eyes. “Mm, too early.”

     

                “Coffee’s in the pot,” Eliza said, jerking her chin towards it. 

     

                Drifting over to it, Lena poured herself a cup and felt herself flagging, concern draining her, irregardless of a good night’s sleep. She sank heavily onto a seat and shivered, the cold of the outdoors still clinging to her skin.

     

                “I’m sorry,” Eliza softly said, regret welling up in her eyes as the lines of her face deepened. “I should have warned you.”

     

                A ripple of pain crossed Lena’s face as she leached the warmth from the cup in her hands, lips pressing together as she deliberated for a moment, slowly choosing her words.

     

                “No,” Lena softly objected, “no, I think … she would be embarrassed to know it was acknowledged.”

     

                Eliza grimly nodded, conceding to her point, “you’re right. The first few times … she hated for us to see her like that. Alex and I had no idea, of course, so we’d go running in, and would just- you’re right, she was embarrassed. I think … I should have helped her more, but in the end … I stopped going in.”

     

                An unfair flicker of anger passed through Lena, quickly smothered, and she nodded as she grimly sat with the knowledge that she would have to suffer the same fate to soothe Kara’s pride. It wasn’t a comforting thought, but it was the harsh reality of it, and Lena’s stomach sank as she felt irritation flare up at Kara’s reluctance to acknowledge that anything was wrong. She treated everything as a mild indifference, something to be shrugged off and masked with a winning smile. It no longer fooled Lena.

     

                She appeared in the doorway minutes later, looking soft and pink from her shower and wearing clean pyjamas as she finished pulling a sweatshirt over her wet hair. Lena gave her a twitch of a smile and climbed to her feet, moving to pour Kara a cup of coffee.

     

                “Morning,” Kara yawned as she took a seat beside Eliza, drawing her knees up to her chest and leaning her head on her mother’s shoulder.

     

                Eliza murmured a reply and absentmindedly stroked Kara’s hair as she scrolled through a new article on her phone. Setting a brimming cup down before her, Lena raised her eyebrows with a prompting look.

     

                “Breakfast? Pancakes?”

     

                “You spoil me too much.”

     

                “Is it spoiling when it’s one of three meals I can make?” Lena mused aloud with a scoff of laughter as she poked around in the cupboards, somewhat more familiar with the place after her week as a patient parked on Eliza’s couch.

     

                Kara watched with fascination as Lena moved around with ease, this new, comfortable version of her making her face light up as she watched from her seat, sipping her coffee, her inner delight hidden from Lena, who had her back to her. In short order, she had a stack of blueberry pancakes sitting before Kara and watched with an expectant look on her face as Kara took a bite and hummed appreciatively.

     

                Eliza left for work shortly after and it was a few hours yet before Alex and Kelly emerged, giving Lena time to monopolise the rest of the hot water for a shower before she spent some time answering emails while Kara watched baseball. 

     

                Once everyone was up and ready, they walked into town, following the shoreline as they went to get their pie from the diner. It was windy but it didn’t bother Lena as she laced her fingers with Kara and laughed as Alex and Kelly took it in turns throwing a tennis ball as far as they could and watched Athena kick up sand as she raced to fetch it. It felt like they could have been back in Midvale on that first trip, if not for the cold weather.

     

                By the time they reached the town, they were grateful for the cheap coffee and even more so for the pie as they huddled in what Lena termed their booth, deliberating over which flavour to go for. Kara opted for chocolate pecan once Lena said she’d get a slice of apple for them to share, and they lingered for almost two hours, getting refills as they hid from the wind. 

     

                Making the walk back home, they decided on a bonfire that night and Lena and Kara spent an extra hour outdoors, collecting driftwood and throwing the tennis ball as they raced up and down the beach, leaving criss-crossing paths of footprints, evidence of their presence. It wasn’t permanent, of course, but it made Lena’s heart swell, that proof of their being there, and when they stomped up the sand dunes with their arms laden with wood and their cheeks rosy, it felt nice and normal.

     

                Later on, the four of them sat on folding camp chairs on the sandy strip between the dunes and the ocean with a bonfire crackling merrily in the middle of the circle. They were bundled up in sweaters and coats and blankets, holding sausages and marshmallows over the flickering blue flames as they made hotdogs and s’mores, Lena eliciting a round of groaning complaints at the fact that she’d never tried the latter before.

     

                Kelly fed Athena sausages as she cuddled up as close to Alex as their camp chairs would allow, laughing at some shared joke, while Kara laughed along, snapping a photo of them, and Lena couldn’t help but wish the night would last forever. It seemed a recurring thought over the last couple of days, and would no doubt be at the forefront of her mind in days to come, but she grasped it so tightly as she already mourned the loss of Kara again. She wasn’t even sure she’d have it in her to let her go again, but this glimpse of the life they’d have, their future together once she returned, was a cold comfort to her. It almost felt too good to be true, like a dream, but when Kara came back, maybe they would have it.

    Chapter 38

                Halloween was days later, at the end of their time in Midvale, with just a couple of days left, and Lena opened her eyes to sunlight streaming in through the curtains, faintly yellow as it struggled against the turning weather. It fell across Kara’s sleeping form beside her, limning her gold as she breathed evenly, and Lena blinked in surprise as she pushed herself up, careful to not jostle the mattress too much as she looked at her. It was the first time in five days that Kara hadn’t woken them up from one of her bad dreams, whether by hoarse shout or sudden jerkiness, and Lena felt the knot in her chest loosen. It wasn’t much, but it was something.

     

                She was breathing slowly, her face smooth and youthful, and Lena was reluctant to wake her as she listened to the muffled voices and movements downstairs, signaling that everyone else was already up. It wasn’t surprising, considering the sun was already up, and she basked in the opportunity to languish in bed beside Kara while she could.

     

                It wasn’t long before Kara stirred though, her eyelids fluttering and then parting to reveal distant blue eyes, which creased at the corners as she seemed to remember herself, where she was. Giving her a sleep smile as she fumbled on the end table for her glasses, Kara hummed, shifting across the bed.

     

                “Morning,” she mumbled, blinking as her vision adjusted and she leaned over to kiss Lena.

     

                “You didn’t have any nightmares last night,” Lena said with a pleased look as she cupped Kara’s face and kissed her again, slowly.

     

                “Mm, I didn’t. I guess things are settling down again,” Kara said as she trailed kisses along Lena’s jaw and down her neck.

     

                “But … can you still think about what I said the other day?”

     

                “I will.”

     

                She wrinkled her nose and obligingly kissed, making her squirm as she hit a ticklish spot. Laughing as she struggled beneath Kara’s weight pinning her, she let out a yelp as Kara’s wandering hands found her ribs. A snort of breathless laughter made Lena’s words choked as she struggled to get them out, kicking her feet as she squeezed her eyes shut.

     

                “Stop, it tickles!”

     

                In a knee-jerk reaction, she accidentally kneed Kara in the stomach, cutting off her laughter with a sharp exhale as she found herself winded and breathless. Wincing, Lena pushed herself up, reaching for Kara with an apology in her green eyes.

     

                “Sorry! I didn’t mean to do that. Are you okay?”

     

                “Fine,” Kara faintly gasped, clutching her stomach, “just winded.”

     

                Giving her a sheepish smile as she spread her hands helplessly, Lena let out a yelp of laughter as Kara gave her a wicked smile and lunged for her. Scrambling to get away, Lena’s foot got caught in the bed sheets, restricting her from climbing out of bed, and momentum and gravity propelled her forward before she could shove her hands out and catch herself. 

     

                Pain lanced through her head and her vision went black for a moment as she was half in bed and half off, the blankets still ensnaring her legs. Kara’s hands were on her shoulders, the laughter dying on her lips, and as Lena struggled up and raised a hand to her head, she realised why. Blood stained her fingertips and she blinked at it, realising she’d caught her head on the edge of the end table.

     

                “Ow. Shit. Do you have any tissues?”

     

                “Shit, are you okay?” Kara asked, scrambling over the sheets and climbing out of bed to kneel on the floor at Lena’s bedside. She gently tried to pry Lena’s head off her head. “Let me see.”

     

                “It’s fine,” Lena said, but even as she let Kara pull her hand away, blood welled up and trickled down the side of her face with nothing to stifle the flow.

     

                Kara bared her teeth as she parted Lena’s dark hair around it and drew in a hissing breath between her teeth. “It looks deep; you might need stitches. I’ll go and see if my mom’s left for work yet.”

     

                Suppressing a sigh, Lena covered it with her hand again, feeling the blood slowly seep down her face in stripes, a few spots soaking into the fabric of her thin cashmere sweater, and her mouth thinned as she shoved her feet into slippers and let Kara usher her from the room. Her hands were warm against Lena’s back, hovering nervously as she walked downstairs, as if she expected her to pass out on the way down. 

     

                “Mom,” Kara loudly called out, halfway down and tense with dismay. “Can you get the first aid kit?”

     

                Eliza’s head popped out of the hallway, a furrowed look of concern creasing her face, which quickly alighted to shock at the sight of Lena’s bloodstained face, and she softly swore. Drifting towards them, Eliza reached out, beckoning Lena towards her as they reached the bottom, and Lena softly sighed.

     

                “It’s fine, I’m sure it’ll stop in a minute,” she reasoned.

     

                Eliza tilted her head down to get a better look and then clapped her on the shoulder, “go and sit.”

     

                Grumbling as she shuffled into the kitchen, Lena sank down onto a chair and gave the two stunned faces looking at her a wide smile, pain giving her a headache. Alex moved over a seat, reaching over to tut as she tilted Lena’s head to the side to take a look.

     

                “What hell have you been doing up there? Do I want to know?”

     

                “I fell out of bed. Kind of.”

     

                “Jesus.”

     

                “She didn’t fall out of bed ,” Kara sighed, apologetic and pink-cheeked as she raked a hand through her hair, agitated. “I tickled her and she whacked her head on the bedside table.”

     

                Rolling her eyes, Lena pulled her hand away and felt the hot trickle of blood resume, wiping the back of her hand across her face as she tried to stem it. “By falling. It’s fine; it’s nothing.”

     

                “I’m surprised you’re not crying,” Alex commented.

     

                Mouth turning down at the corners, Lena stole a piece of toast from her plate and narrowed her eyes in a cool smile. “I don’t cry that often, thank you.”

     

                “Breakfast. Yes. Good idea,” Kara muttered, turning to busy herself with scrounging up more toast and making some tea.

     

                Eliza returned a moment later, dumping a vivid red bag emblazoned with a cross on the kitchen table as she jerked the zip undone. “You girls might want to take your breakfast into the living room,” she warned everyone as she started unpacking the bag, strewing gauze and antiseptic wipes across the table.

     

                Nobody moved as Kara put bread down in the toaster and then leaned against the fridge, arms folded and a cloudy expression on her face, while Alex and Kelly seemed unperturbed as they continued to eat their breakfast, shifting to the other end of the table to give Eliza space to work. Washing her hands at the sink, Eliza pulled on gloves and deftly parted Lena’s hair, searching beneath the blood for the source and clicking her tongue.

     

                “Mhm, you definitely need stitches.”

     

                Lena sighed but didn’t protest, watching as Eliza tore open a package and pulled out a clean needle, quickly filling it from a vial of local anesthetic. Dabbing the wound clean, she carefully eased the needle into one end, Lena stiffening at the stinging sensation as Eliza gave her shoulder an encouraging squeeze. She did the other side then, spreading it around as Lena tried to mask her wince, murmuring a quiet thanks as Kara set a cup of tea down in front of her with a shaky hand.

     

                A plate of buttered toast cut into triangles was quick to follow, and Lena took a bite as she warily eyed the hooked needle Eliza unpackaged. Urging Lena to keep still, she was gentle as she eased the hooked needle through the edges of the wound, pulling the skin back together with slow, neat stitches, snipping the knotted ends until they lined up, four in a row. Once she was done, Eliza wiped it clean and then dabbed an antibacterial salve on it.

     

                “All done,” she gently said, her voice light as she smiled down at Lena. “They can come out in a week; just try and be careful in the future, okay?” 

     

                “I will. Thank you,” Lena said with a crooked smile.

     

                Her face softened as Eliza patted her cheek and then turned to clean away the bloody gauze and empty packaging, neatly packing away the paraphernalia she hadn’t used and zipping it all away in the first aid kit. Kara drifted to Lena’s side, hovering nervously as her fingertips brushed along the nape of her neck, worrying at the edge of her collar.

     

                “Painkillers are in the medicine cabinet,” Eliza instructed, “they’re not strong ones like last time. Now, I have to run. Take it easy today.”

     

                She doled out kisses on cheeks and the top of heads, leaving Lena blinking in mild surprise, and then was off to work, while Lena palmed off the rest of her toast to Kara to finish off and fed the crusts to Athena. Wiping crumbs on her pyjama pants, Lena cleared her throat.

     

                “I’m going to go and, you know, wipe the blood off,” she said with a droll smile.

     

                “Why ruin a perfectly good Halloween costume?” Alex asked.

     

                “Very funny,” Lena snarkily replied, moving towards the door as she exaggeratedly rolled her eyes.

     

                Making her way up to the bathroom, she looked at her reflection in the mirror, slightly paler than usual, but, aside from the blood, perfectly fine. The stitches were hidden by her dark hair and she gently prodded at them, wincing at the tenderness, as she waited for the water to heat up. Quickly showering, rinsing the blood from her hair and taking care as she shampooed the rest, she wrapped herself in a towel and scrubbed her teeth before the sink, pausing as a knock sounded on the door.

     

                “It’s me. Can I come in?”

     

                Yanking the door open, Lena let Kara squeeze past her and watched as she picked up her own toothbrush. Standing shoulder to shoulder, they brushed their teeth and stared at each other’s reflection, Lena smiling as Kara wrinkled her nose, bumping her waist as Lena shouldered her in turn. As Kara pulled her toothbrush out and stuck out her tongue, Lena scoffed with laughter and rinsed her mouth out, setting her toothbrush back into the holder and turning to face her.

     

                “What’s the plan for today?”

     

                Wiping her mouth on a towel, Kara hummed and brushed Lena’s wet hair out of her face. “Well, pumpkins are a necessity, as is candy.”

     

                “Candy?”

     

                “It’s Halloween! Kids will want candy when they knock.”

     

                “Fine. Candy. Pumpkins. What else?”

     

                “Halloween movies,” Kara grinned, setting her glasses down on the edge of the sink and squinting as she pulled off her shirt.

     

                Lena tugged her closer by the waistband of her sweatpants, humming as she pushed up slightly to kiss her, their lips soft and the taste of mint lingering. “Mhm, sounds good.”

     

                “First, I need to shower, so you need to cut that out,” Kara laughed, kissing behind her ear. “Go and get dressed and take some painkillers. You don’t have to be stubborn all the time.”

     

                Rolling her eyes, Lena fished two Advil out of the medicine cabinet and swallowed them dry before she slipped out of the bathroom in her towel and crossed the hallway into Kara’s room. Digging out a sweater and jeans, she dressed and then made the bed and threw the curtains open, cool air seeping in through the window as she cracked it. Making her way downstairs, Lena informed the other two women of their plan and switched to the news as they debated on whether or not to join them.

     

                In the end, the four of them walked into town, making a stop for hot chocolate first, which they sipped in the wilting park, Lena blowing on the curl of steam escaping through the hole in the lid as she allowed Kara to push her on a swing. Athena chased Alex through the sparse trees and the winding paths while a gaggle of children climbed over the equipment in rain boots and parkas, their mothers watching half-heartedly from benches. Kara took photos in between pushing Lena; of the plants, the trees, the playground, the dog, them . 

     

                “You know, I’ve never been to a playground before,” Lena mused aloud.

     

                “Never?” Kelly echoed, her voice coloured with surprise as she raised her eyebrows.

     

                Shrugging, Lena’s lips twisted with a smile, “my mother encouraged academic pursuits. You don’t get into college at thirteen if you’re busy on the playground.”

     

                “Did you at least enjoy it?” Kelly curiously asked.

     

                Deliberating, Lena narrowed her eyes slightly as a pucker formed between her eyebrows. “I mean, I didn’t know any different. But I do enjoy learning, so … I’m kind of glad that I was given that chance to make the most of it, you know? Sure, it’s … kind of fucked things up a bit - I mean, I definitely wouldn’t say I’m normal - but … you know, it’s- it’s not bad.”

     

                Kelly gave her a pitying look, sinking onto the empty swing beside her as they watched Kara crouch before Athena and snap a photo moments before the dog barrelled into her. “Normal is relative to your own experiences,” Kelly said, “and the people around you.”

     

                “Yeah, well, you guys make me feel more normal, you know, considering that I’m not.”

     

                Chuckling, Kelly climbed to her feet and held a hand out for Lena, dark brown eyes sparkling as she pulled her to her feet and then threw an arm around her shoulders. “We have more in common than you think. I’m glad she met you.”

     

                “Mm, me too.”

     

                When it started raining, they walked towards the closest supermarket, heads ducked against the salty drizzle as it snaked down the back of their necks and turned their hands and cheeks red. Walking into the airy store to the air conditioned smell of cheap bleach, bread and stale fridges, Lena looked around with interest as Kara fetched a cart.

     

                “And for the second time today … another first,” Lena mumbled, trailing Kara through the second set of doors. “Never been into a proper supermarket before.”

     

                “Ever?” Kara sceptically asked. 

     

                “Jess orders it for me and then it gets delivered and my housekeeper puts it away,” Lena explained with a shrug, “no need for it. I have been to 7/11 and bodegas, so it’s close.”

     

                “No, it’s not,” Alex snorted. 

     

                “Come on weirdo, climb on the cart,” Kara said, motioning to the end of it.

     

                “What?” Lena asked, frowning at Kara.

     

                With a sigh, Kara gave Lena an exasperated look. “On the end of the cart. Stand on it. I’m going to push you around; it’s more fun that way.”

     

                Glancing around at the other shoppers and the staff restocking shelves or checking out groceries, Lena apprehensively gripped the cold metal of the cart and dropped her voice. “Are we allowed?”

     

                “Yes, it’s fine,” Kara encouraged her, ushering her onto the end, and once Lena had balanced, perplexed and amused, on the end of the cart, she started pushing her down an aisle. “First things first, donuts.”

     

                “That wasn’t on the list.”

     

                “It’s … a type of candy,” Kara slowly said with an unconvincing smile. “It’s got sugar in it. It’s sweet.”

     

                Humming, Lena narrowed her eyes, “and are they for the kids?”

     

                “I’m technically someone’s child.”

     

                Snorting, Lena shook her head and allowed herself to be wheeled past loaves of bread and buns and fresh bagels before they reached the donuts. She picked up a dozen of mixed types and put it into the bottom of the empty cart before setting off again. They lost Alex and Kelly periodically, before they’d materialise at the cart and dump in their choices, while Lena and Kara spent most of their time in the candy aisle, going a little overboard on account of it being Halloween as well as compensating for Kara’s severe lack of sweet things. Chocolate didn’t mail very well, and it was the overwhelming majority of what they bought by the time they made it to the check out.

     

                Lena put her card against the machine as she watched the girls sort everything into bags, deliberating over weight and the evenness of them, before they all hefted their portion and streamed out into the cold. The pumpkins weren’t very big but were heavy as they made the long walk home, opting for the long road instead of the beach, their burden too heavy to slog through sand, and the cold made them shiver until they warmed enough, passing beneath dripping branches and over gleaming wet sidewalks.

     

                “Okay, before we carve … pumpkin spice lattes,” Kara said as soon as they were inside, unpacking candy at the kitchen table.

     

                “I’ll make it,” Kelly quickly volunteered, “after last year, I don’t trust either of you.”

     

                “What happened last year?” Lena asked, brow creasing with amused confusion. She loved hearing stories about times before she’d met them all; it made her feel as if she’d known them a lot longer than she had.

     

                With a scoff of laughter, Kelly smiled, moving a pumpkin towards the end of the table. “Someone insisted on making it from scratch - you know, fresh pumpkin, fresh syrup, all of that - but ended up leaving the syrup on the heat to reduce and setting it on fire.”

     

                “It wasn’t on fire,” Alex sighed, “it was smoking.”

     

                “That’s a precursor to fire.”

     

                “And you have the cheek to make fun of me?” Lena laughed as Alex gave her a dour look, chastening and unimpressed.

     

                Still, no one complained as Kelly went about making their lattes, while Lena helped sift through the candy for the kids and what was theirs, dumping it into the large bowl that Kara scrounged up and moving it to the table in the hallway. Clearing the table of their own snacks for later on that night and pulling apart that morning’s newspaper to cover the wooden top before they each set their little pumpkin in front of them and used an arrays of markers and knives to mark out faces and hollow them out.

     

                Lena finished first, her one nothing more than two small, round eyes bored through the pumpkin skin and a thin wobbly line she’d sawed through with the knife. When Kara leaned over to look at hers, she choked on a snort of laughter and Lena scowled, pulling her pumpkin towards herself and cradling it protectively.

     

                “That’s it?”

     

                “What’s wrong with it?” Lena defensively replied, bristling.

     

                “Where’s the face?” Kara exclaimed.

     

                Spluttering, Lena wordlessly pointed out the eyes and the line of the mouth as Kara threw her head back and let out a cackle, while Alex and Kelly asked to see it, already laughing along with Kara’s glee. Pouting, Lena turned it around and shrugged before a sheepish smile crept onto her face.

     

                “I don’t have an artistic bone in my body!”

     

                “I mean … yeah, but … what is that?” Alex asked, aghast.

     

                Scoffing, Lena raised her eyebrows and nodded to her, “let’s see yours then.”

     

                Turning hers around, Alex displayed the half-finished pumpkin, a classic style with its triangular eyes and zigzagging mouth, the edges neat and precise as she took her time. Rolling her eyes, Lena sighed. 

     

                “Okay, fine, yeah, yours is better, but I bet you’ve been doing this for years. I’ve never carved a pumpkin before, and I don’t think building machines is the same level of dexterity as using a bread knife to cut a mouth into vegetables. That’s all I’m saying.”

     

                “But surely your house would have been done up for Halloween, I mean, you practically grew up in the Haunted Mansion pre-haunting.”

     

                Frowning, Lena cocked her head to the side, confusion flashing in her eyes, “Kara, I’ve never once celebrated Halloween. Surely that’s not a surprise; look at my mom, look at the estate I grew up on - no neighbours - and then the fact that I was at a Catholic boarding school .”

     

                “You’ve never been trick-or-treating?” Kelly asked.

     

                “You mean, like … dressing up and knocking on doors? No, of course not. The most I’ve celebrated was approving an office dress-up day last year.”

     

                “What did you go as?”

     

                Arching an eyebrow, she gestured to herself, “a CEO.”

     

                “Oh man,” Alex groaned, “you make it so easy to make fun of you. Kara, go and find an old sheet.”

     

                She was already half out of her seat and vanished upstairs into the laundry closet, while Lena listened to the sounds of towels and sheets thumping onto the floor in piles as she sipped her pumpkin spice latte, silently admitting that it was pretty good, and waited expectantly. Kara’s footsteps thundered heavily downstairs and she was beaming as she walked into the kitchen.

     

                “Stand up for me,” she instructed Lena, who narrowed her eyes faintly but obeyed as she set her cup down.

     

                Kara tossed the sheet over her head and Lena stepped back as she frowned beneath it, the old sheet smelling of dried paint and turpentine and dust as sunlight filtered through the cotton and gave it a yellow tint. Lifting it with her hands, Lena opened and closed her mouth for a moment.

     

                “Kara, what-”

     

                She could hear her rooting around in the cutlery drawer, kitchen utensils clattering around before the drawer rattled shut and Kara’s shadow blotted out some of the sunlight. “Stay still,” Kara sternly ordered, “well, we’re going trick or treating tonight now, obviously. But seeing as it’s a bit last minute, you have to be a ghost. Now, keep still while I cut some eyes for you.”

     

                Lena made a choked sound of surprise at the back of her throat as Kara gently probed her face and plucked the sheet away. The scissors were blunted and it took a minute to work them through the bunched cotton, leaving the edges of the holes frayed and irregular.

     

                “Won’t Eliza care that you ruined a sheet?”

     

                “This is an old one used for painting. It’s fine.”

     

                “Alright then. Um … so are you really going to make me go out like this?” Lena asked as Kara finished and she dragged the sheet off, the static making wisps of hair stand on end.

     

                “Just to the neighbours, it’s fine.”

     

                Suppressing a sigh, Lena’s mouth thinned and she resigned herself to the fact that she was about to be twenty-five, dressed as a ghost for the evening. First, they finished their pumpkins though and made grilled cheese sandwiches for lunch before being left to their own devices. Lena played scrabble with Kelly, while Alex and Kara whispered to themselves in the living room, heads ducked low together in secrecy as Lena cast them furtive glances in between rounds.

     

                Once school was out, kids started periodically knocking on their door, Kara eagerly doling out too much candy as Lena insisted on waiting to go out in her sheet until it was at the very least dark outside. While she waited, she helped Kelly make a pumpkin soup from the scraps of their hollowed out lanterns, the four of them evenly placed outside with lit candles glowing through faces of varying skill, and, as the sun started sinking, they sipped scotch and ate soup and waited until Kara made Lena put on the sheet.

     

                All of them were set on accompanying her, dressed normally in coats and jeans, and Kara snapped a photo of her looking forlorn, even without being able to see her expression beneath the sheet, chuckling before she ushered her outside. Lena peered at the square and groaned at the sight of her.

     

                “I look ridiculous.”

     

                “It’s the spirit of it,” Kara placatingly replied, wrapping an arm around her shoulders as Lena tried to combat the overwhelming surplus of fabric as it attempted to drown her in cotton.

     

                They walked down the driveway and Kara determinedly set off for a specific house as everyone followed her lead. “I’ll take you to Mrs Li’s house; I was friends with her son in high school so she likes me.”

     

                Lena hung back as Kara confidently walked up the path and knocked on the front door of a neat house a street away. The lights were still on and a few kids were still making their way from house to house, and after a minute, there was the shuffling sound of footsteps and the door was opened to reveal a smiling middle-aged woman.

     

                “Mrs Li, hi!” Kara beamed.

     

                “Kara? It’s lovely to see you. Your mother told me you were back. And is that Alex too?”

     

                “It’s good to see you too! I, uh, I was hoping you could help me out with something - this is my girlfriend, Lena.”

     

                She gestured to Lena, who half-heartedly raised a hand covered by the sheet, and let out a quiet chuckle. “She’s never celebrated Halloween before, and I know we’re way too old , but I was wondering if you could help us out and let her give trick or treating a go?”

     

                With a quiet laugh as her face creased with gentle amusement and a little confusion, Mrs Li nodded, her smile warm. “Sure, Kara. I’ll close the door and you can do it again.”

     

                “Thank you!” Kara sang, her smile so wide it must have been hurting her cheeks.

     

                The door shut and Lena grumbled softly but was prodded forward by Alex, who was chuckling as she enjoyed herself too much, and raised a hand to knock. It opened immediately and Lena’s smile beneath the sheet was sheepish and vaguely embarrassed.

     

                “Um, trick or treat?” Lena slowly said, her voice hitching with uncertainty.

     

                “Hang on, can I just- let me get a photo of this,” Kara called out from behind her.

     

                Holding the bowl of candy, Mrs Li smiled as Lena turned and stood next to her, the flash blinding them both before she shook her head. “You still have that old thing?”

     

                Patting the camera affectionately, Kara smiled brightly, “sure do. It’s been through the ringer, but it’s still kicking. Anyway, we’ll leave you alone now. Thanks, Mrs Li.”

     

                “Here, take some candy before you go!” she urged them, shaking the bowl.

     

                Lena revealed a hand and plucked a little packet of Jolly Ranchers from the bowl and quietly thanked her before stepping aside, letting the other three take something. Lingering on the sidewalk in her sheet, Lena took in the shadowed outlines of parents chaperoning excited kids, taking in the Power Rangers and wizards and superheroes as they carried buckets brimming with candy.

     

                “You have a good night!” Mrs Li called after them, shaking her head fondly as she eased the door shut.

     

                “Alright, we’ll put you out of your misery,” Kelly laughed, “we’ve got enough candy at home, let’s go.”

     

                Mercifully dragging the sheet off, Lena laughed as she reached for Kara’s hand, pressing up against her as they walked back home. The moon was high and the stars speckled the sky in between clouds and Lena felt a pang of sadness as their time in Midvale started coming to a close. They still had another week in National City, a merciful stretch of days in the dusty city and their old favourite haunts before she lost Kara for another five months, and that was enough to dull the edges of the sadness.

     

                Back inside, they stripped off coats and Alex pried the bottle caps off four sweet apple ciders while Kara switched on a horror film they’d settled on and Lena stowed away the sheet. With bowls of popcorn and bags of candy tossed back and forth, they watched Nightmare On Elm Street and answered the door for the last few stragglers of older kids hoping for the last of everyone’s candy. 

     

                The movie was laughably bad but Lena enjoyed it, the cider making her mind blur once they were a few in and the sugar from too much candy making her teeth ache, and afterwards they put on Hocus Pocus at Kara’s insistence, sitting through that one too before they sat up for a few more drinks and then went to bed. Her lack of sleep for the previous few night’s sleep was catching up with her and she found herself dozing off more than once, so comfortable and warm beside Kara, their knees drawn to their chests and bumping occasionally as they shifted beneath the blankets.

     

                Her head was aching from the bruising and the stinging stitches and she stopped in the bathroom for some painkillers, scooping water from the tap to wash them down before she brushed her teeth and went to change into her pyjamas. 

     

                The two of them climbed into bed and Lena snuggled up next to Kara, resting her head on her chest and listening to the steady beat of her heart as the alcohol and painkillers slowly dulled the edge of the pounding headache. Reaching up, Lena gently probed around the stitches and Kara kissed the top of her head.

     

                “I’m sorry.”

     

                “It could be worse,” Lena lightly murmured, a smile in her voice, “it could have been a gun.”

     

                With a snort of laughter as she bucked slightly beneath her with the force of it, Kara tightened her arms around Lena and squeezed. “Mm, there’s always that.”

     

                “I love you, you know that, right?” Lena mumbled, already feeling the tug of sleep at the corners of her consciousness.

     

                “I do,” Kara whispered, her voice oddly emotional in the dark. “And I love you too. I hope- I hope you know that.”

     

                “I do. Of course I do. Why? What’s up?”

     

                Kara let out a breathless laugh, her fingertips gliding along the notches of Lena’s spine as she cradled her close. “Nothing. I just wanted to make sure that you know.”

     

                They both fell silent then, listening to the trees rustle outside the window until they were finally lulled to sleep. It was just past midnight when the first firework screamed through the sky and exploded, phosphorescent streaks shooting through the black sky in a shower of red. Lena woke to the absence of Kara’s warmth at her back, the empty coldness of the space rousing her as the second firework reverberated through the night, sharp and illuminating beyond the curtains. Sitting up, Lena frowned at the silhouetted outline of Kara and reached out to lay a hand on her stiff arm.

     

                “Kara?”

     

                A clammy hand clapped over her mouth as Kara pressed a finger to her lips, her face a shapeless blur above Lena as she hunched over her, bristling with fear as her pulse jumped beneath Lena’s fingers encircling her wrist.

     

                “Shh, they’re behind you. If you move, they’ll know we’re here.”

     

                Mouth dry and skin prickling, Lena struggled to swallow as her eyes burned, tears springing unwittingly to them as she shook her head beneath Kara’s hand. Keeping a tight grip on Kara’s wrist, Lena raised her other hand to try and pry her hand off her mouth, her voice muffled as she tried to speak, drawing in a shallow breath as she managed to move it.

     

                “Fireworks,” she rasped, pale and afraid, “Kara, it’s fireworks.”

     

                The last one exploded, the curtains translucent for a moment as it briefly illuminated the sky to the whoops of young kids causing trouble on Halloween. She watched as a ripple of panic crossed Kara’s face, her features momentarily visible, if a little shadowed. Her eyes were dark and unseeing and her face tightened.

     

                Unsure of what to do, Lena let go of her wrist and slowly reached up to touch her face, delicately pressing her cool fingertips against Kara’s cheekbone as she gently tried to ease her down onto the pillows again. She was stiff and uncooperative, trembling as she breathed heavily, and as she pressed a hand to the back of her shirt to help guide her, Lena could feel that it was plastered to her skin with sweat.

     

                Once she was down on her side, Lena wrapped her arms around her tightly, wrapping her in the comfort of her arms, in the smell of her perfume and detergent and the warm solidity of her. And then she started humming, off-key and hesitantly, the sound getting stuck in her throat and petering off a few times as fear made it constrict. It was an old song, a nursery rhyme she thought, although she couldn’t remember hearing it. But someone, at some point in the empty years of her childhood, must have hummed it to her before, and she closed her eyes and carried on the scraps of the remembered tune as she felt Kara slowly but surely loosen, going slack as her breaths evened out. 

     

                It was a strange and sleepless night for Lena, the hours clumping together and then falling away in great chunks as she watched Kara through the burning tiredness building behind her eyes. She never woke, but she murmured occasionally, stiffening and sighing as her eyes rolled beneath closed eyelids, and it made Lena’s pulse spike each time as she waited for the terrifying proof that Kara was far from okay. She managed to close her eyes just as sunrise blanched the autumn sky, grief weighing heavily in her chest as Kara slept beside her, unaware.

    Chapter 39

                Lena woke first, sitting in bed, knees drawn to her chest as she sustained herself off too little sleep, raw-eyed and slumped but harbouring a kernel of fear in her chest. She’d gotten a mere handful of hours, the sky still lingering in the shadows of a slow dawn when she roused herself, sitting up and silently keeping watch as Kara slept. She looked peaceful, completely unaware of her girlfriend sitting beside her, worried and exhausted from a sleepless night.

     

                She didn’t so much as move until Kara woke up, a smile splitting her face as she spread her arms, stretching, and blearily blinked. Lena let out a pent up breath, a spasm of a conflicted smile running across her face as her heart twinged and her stomach tied itself further into knots. 

     

                “Morning,” Kara mumbled, rubbing at her face, indented with the seams of the pillow case.

     

                Lena was slow in replying, and perhaps it was all written on her face, but Kara pushed herself up, blinking owlishly as she pushed her tangled hair out of her face. “What’s wrong?”

     

                Lena choked on a laugh, pinching the bridge of her nose as she ducked her head down, forehead almost touching her drawn up knees. “You don’t remember,” Lena murmured, “how can you not remember?”

     

                “Remember what?” Kara asked, her voice slow and cautious and thick with sleep.

     

                “There were fireworks,” Lena hoarsely said, a pained tremor in her voice, “last night. You- I don’t even know if you were awake or … you just- you covered my mouth. You- …”

     

                “Did I hurt you?” Kara asked, shoving aside the blankets as she moved towards Lena, paling as her lips parted and horror washed over her.

     

                Taking Kara’s hand in her own, Lena smiled unevenly as she fiddled with her fingers, lightly tracing the threading veins and bumps of fine bones and lines, shaking her head. “No, you didn’t hurt me; you scared me.”

     

                “I’m sorry,” Kara whispered, cupping the back of Lena’s neck as she leaned her forehead against her temple. “I’m sorry; I must have been dreaming. I didn’t-”

     

                “It’s fine,” Lena stressed, “you don’t have to apologise, I just- I didn’t know how to wake you up. How to help you. You were just … stuck in your head. It scared me.”

     

                “It’s- I’m fine, it was just- it doesn’t happen often,” Kara unconvincingly reassured her, a desperate edge to the words. “The dreams, the nightmares … they’re usually just for the first week. You saw for yourself - I didn’t have one the other night. It was just the fireworks; they must have-”

     

                With a frustrated scoff, Lena rubbed at the sore spot above her eye, a headache from a lack of sleep already building. “I know what they did. I’m not a psychologist, but I’m also not an idiot, Kara.”

     

                “It’s not-”

     

                “Shall I get Kelly in here? See what she thinks?”

     

                Kara made a low sound of irritation at the back of her throat, her gentle face furrowing into a frown as she clenched her teeth and jutted her jaw forward stubbornly. “Just leave it alone,” she softly pleaded, an undercurrent of a warning in her words, “I’ll be gone in a week anyway; it won’t matter.”

     

                Lena couldn’t mask the flinch at the flippant way Kara brought up her leaving, as if it was some mild inconvenience, as if it was nothing. She didn’t want to be confronted with losing her, and it made her temper spike for Kara to dismiss it as nothing, as if leaving would fix it instead of exacerbating the problem. Scowling, Lena pulled back the blankets and climbed out of bed, pulling a sweater on over her t-shirt as two splotches of red touched her pale cheeks.

     

                “Well, if it won’t matter then …” Lena sarcastically replied, jerking down the hem of the sweater.

     

                Stalking towards the door, Lena heard Kara sigh behind her, “well … where are you going?”

     

                “Breakfast.”

     

                Vanishing downstairs alone, she banged around the kitchen with flushed cheeks until she had a scalding cup of over extracted coffee and was gulping it down with a scowl on her face as she ran a brush through Athena’s fur, grooming the patient dog as the house creaked deafeningly around her. Eliza was home before anyone else stirred, the key in the lock and the sound of her running shoes squeaking on the lip of the door as she stepped inside. Lena could feel the gust of cool air down the hallway and listened to the sound of her disappearing upstairs, the pipes groaning as she went into the bathroom to wash off the smell of the hospital.

     

                Alone, Lena finished grooming Athena and let her outside, watching from the back porch as the dog sniffed around in the cold garden for ten minutes before padding back up to her. Burying her fingers in the damp bristles of her fur, Lena sighed and turned right as the door opened to reveal Kara standing there. Bundled up in her sweatshirt, looking drawn with sadness, she moved over to Lena and wrapped her arms around her, chin propped on her shoulder as she hunched down slightly.

     

                “Don’t be mad, please,” Kara murmured.

     

                “Then don’t be stupid,” Lena retorted.

     

                “I’m not. I just- I don’t think there’s any point in doing anything now . I’ve got a week left and then I’ll just be right back in the middle of it all, so … anyway, maybe it’d just be … better if I waited until I was back.”

     

                Mouth twisting down sourly at the corners, Lena leaned her weight back against Kara and was silent for a moment. “Fine.”

     

                With a soft sigh, Kara nuzzled the side of her neck, “can we just … enjoy our last day here?”

     

                “Of course,” Lena murmured, regret and sadness creeping into her face as she looked down at Kara’s tanned hands, clasping her bony wrists as she held Lena in the circle of her arms. “What’s on the agenda?”

     

                “How about we go somewhere? Just the two of us.”

     

                “Okay.”

     

                “There’s a spot just a little while outside of town. I used to love hiking there in high school; it overlooks the sea.”

     

                Humming, Lena nodded as she looked out at the roiling water spread out before them. They’d yet to indulge themselves in enough alone time, or much time to do anything but let Kara dwell in the interrupted time with her family, and the thought of a hike up through the sloping cliffs clinging to the coastline and a day spent in the waning sunshine of autumn before the cold swept in was too good to pass up.

     

                “Sounds perfect.”

     

                They filled a thermos with coffee and dressed warmly, Kara wearing a puffer vest over her hooded sweatshirt while Lena opted for a scarf. Eating a quick breakfast and packing lunch, they borrowed Eliza’s car and Kara drove them through the early morning, silent and stoic and a little wan as the grey light leached the gold from her tan. Tired, Lena leaned against the door and dozed lightly, tuning out the Podcast they were listening to as the few miles slipped by quietly, a haze of fog shrouding the car as they wound through tree-lined coastal roads.

     

                Kara pulled off in the shadow of a cliff face, pines and firs crowding the damp earth as moss blanketed everything else, and Lena drank in the damp air as she climbed out of the car. Athena sniffed at a rotting log and bounded through the underbrush as Kara hauled her backpack from the car and then smiled faintly. Holding out her hand, she jerked her head off to a gap in the trees.

     

                “This way.”

     

                Boots crunching through the earth, Lena crossed over to her and took her hand, giving it a gentle squeeze before they set off into the trees. It was cold and damp, birds crying out in the stillness of the trees and fog gathering around their ankles as they hiked the slowly sloping ground up to the top of the cliffs. It didn’t take long, barely an hour to make it to the top and then out towards the edge with the sound of the ocean beckoning them. 

     

                The air was briny and fresh, Lena’s cheeks rosy from the brisk wind, and she felt a little less tense as Kara stopped at the edge of the cliff, shaking out a plaid blanket and sinking down onto it. Settling down beside her, Lena stretched her legs out before her and exhaled heavily as she looked out at the expanse of gunmetal blue waves stretching out below them, as far as she could see. There was a fishing trawler crawling by in the distance and she watched quietly as Kara unscrewed the thermos and filled the plastic cup with hot coffee.

     

                They took turns sipping the bitter coffee, warming their hands as the morning slowly warmed with the sun climbing higher in the sky. Slowly, the palpable uneasiness between them dissipated and their halting conversation became smoother, if still a little infrequent. Sprawled out, Lena read from a book of essays while Kara listened to the rest of the Podcast with her earphones in, the morning passing by swiftly as they made the most of the damp coastline and its deciduous forests. Tomorrow, they’d be back in National City, in the dry heat and busy city, cramming their days with things to do, not wanting to waste time relaxing when there was so much to do.

     

                As late morning slipped into early afternoon, they ate their packed lunch and got up to stretch their legs, wandering through the trees as Kara led her with unerring direction, pointing out the occasional squirrel or bird in the gloominess of the coastal forest. The sound of the ocean stayed with them as they walked, although it remained out of sight, far below the cliff’s edge, and Lena was struck with a pang of sorrow.

     

                “I’m going to miss this,” she called out, fingertips grazing the lichen covered bark of a tree as she ducked beneath a branch.

     

                Kara slowed and glanced back over her shoulder, a soft smile curling her lips as her eyebrows winged up in a gentle look of amusement. “We’ll come back next time.”

     

                Lena returned her smile but didn’t have it in her to say how it wasn’t just that little spot on the cliffside, or even the quiet town, but the feeling that came with it. It felt different to be somewhere removed from her normal life, where she could enjoy Kara completely, knowing that she was safe and that they were together. Going back to National City felt like the end was coming, and Lena wanted to preserve their time in Midvale and live in it for an eternity.

     

                Instead, they lingered a while longer and then folded their blanket and drank in the sight of the glimmering ocean before Kara whistled sharply for Athena and they made the hike back down to the car. It was still early when they got home, the long stretch of afternoon waiting for them as they listened to music on the back porch and drank cider while playing Uno with Alex and Kelly. 

     

                Later on that evening, they made their own pizzas, rolling out dough and chopping mushrooms and pepperoni and basil leaves, the house dim as the sunlight faded and a chill seeped through the clapboard house. It was almost cozy, drinking wine in the amber glow of the dim lights, pizza cooking in the oven and warm air blowing from the vents as a light drizzle started up, gracing them with wet weather before they returned to California’s warmer climate. After dinner, Lena went upstairs to pack her bag while Kara washed the dishes and made the most of her time left with Eliza. 

     

                There was already a tangible sadness in the air, the impending goodbye between mother and daughter casting a pall over their last night together, and by the time they went to bed, there was a certain grimness to everyone’s demeanours, knowing that there would be goodbyes in the morning. Still, Lena was too exhausted to dwell in her sadness for Kara after her relatively sleepless night before, and nestled up against Kara’s back, she fell asleep quickly. It wasn’t a peaceful sleep, even though she didn’t wake until past eight, her head foggy and eyes thick with sleep as she stretched her aching muscles and sprawled out in the empty bed.

     

                She could hear the clattering of breakfast being made in the kitchen and lay in bed as swathes of weak yellow sunlight filtered in through the curtains, the sound of muffled voices leaving her unwilling to intrude on the final slices of family life the Danvers would be afforded for months. Eventually, she dragged herself out though, at the light tapping on the door and the gentle, curious blue eyes peering through a crack in the door before it was pushed open wider.

     

                “Good morning,” Kara smiled, slipping inside and holding a steaming cup of coffee aloft.

     

                “Morning,” Lena murmured, pushing herself up. “Are you alright?”

     

                Shrugging noncommittally as she crossed over to the bed and sank down onto the edge of the mattress, trying not to spill the coffee as it jostled, Kara smiled thinly. “Sure. We’ve still got a whole week of fun back home, so …”

     

                “Yeah. You’ll miss her though.”

     

                “Yeah. I will.”

     

                “What time is it now?”

     

                “Eight-thirty. Still a while before we have to leave.”

     

                She extended the coffee and Lena took the cup from here, taking a sip and rubbing at her eyes as she hunched forward. “We could stay, you know.”

     

                Kara let out a quiet huff of laughter. “Yeah?”

     

                Looking up as she raked her dark hair out of her face, Lena’s eyes creased with a smile. “Mhm. I’ll buy us a house, we’ll get your name changed and fake your death so you don’t get court martialed. We could live in the woods and visit Eliza at night for dinner.”

     

                “Somehow, I feel like you could make that happen. What would my name be?”

     

                “Linda Lee. You’d start a career as a wildlife photographer. Dye your hair black, get bangs. Maybe adopt a Russian accent.”

     

                “You’ve given this a lot of thought.”

     

                “I’ve thought of a hundred ways to make you stay,” Lena murmured as a spasm crossed her face.

     

                Shifting closer, Kara reached out and cupped her face with a rough palm. “Don’t. We’ve still got time - don’t think about it yet.”

     

                Smiling thinly, Lena nodded and drank her coffee before throwing back the covers and climbing to her feet. They went about stripping the sheets and airing out the room, the salt breeze chasing away the warmth as it ballooned out the curtains and made Lena shiver from the cold. Their packed bags were placed near the door and Lena showered quickly and dressed before heading downstairs. It was quiet, Alex and Kelly absent from the kitchen and living room as Lena wandered through the house, finding Athena missing as well.

     

                “I’m going to sit on the porch with Eliza,” Kara murmured, her hand brushing along Lena’s back in a lingering warmth before she moved towards the back door.

     

                Leaving them to spend time together before they left, Lena made herself toast and smeared avocado over it before refilling her coffee cup and sitting at the kitchen table. She read the local newspaper as she slowly ate, the morning seeming to slip through her fingers, until lunch was almost upon her and she’d barely moved, save to fetch more coffee.

     

                The screen door squeaked open then, footsteps tramping inside and voices minging while the sound of a dog panting grew louder, until a damp German Shepherd was at her feet, reeking of brine and her fur in tufted, wet spikes. Lena smiled fondly and fed Athena the crusts of her long-cold toast as Kelly stepped inside, making for the coffee pot.

     

                “Sorry, she went after a seagull. Probably not ideal right before a flight.”

     

                Waving a hand dismissively, Lena snorted, “don’t worry about it; she’ll be cooped in my house from now on. She deserves a last good run for a while.”

     

                “You’re all packed?”

     

                “Mhm. You?”

     

                “Of course,” Kelly said with a small smile, filling a cup with coffee and dragging out a chair.

     

                “Right. Of course, Sergeant,” Lena saluted.

     

                Kelly kicked her foot and rolled her eyes, protesting when Alex walked in a minute later and stole her coffee, draining half of it and then kissing her girlfriend on the head. Kara lingered in the doorway, watching them all for a moment with a misty-eyed look of longing, soaking up the sight of everyone in one place for the last time in months as Eliza roughly dried Athena off with a towel and Lena smiled up at Alex and Kelly, amused by their antics as her coffee grew cold in hand. 

     

                The spell seemed to snap a few minutes later with the sudden urgency of their departure rolling around. The car would be there soon to take them to the airstrip and Alex was still only half-packed, Kara was still being plied with things Eliza gave her to take with her - preserved foods and extra sunscreen - while Athena was taking up space in the kitchen as she wound through legs, damp tail thumping against the table or counters as she blocked paths and sought affection.

     

                Shortly after, the sound of tyres crunching gravel announced the arrival of their driver, and it was enough to force a lump into Kara’s throat as her stomach swooped. Everyone was quick to fetch their bags and bring them outside, while Kara dragged her feet inside, prolonging the inevitable. Pity wrenched Lena’s heart and made her own throat constrict, each pass by Kara leading her to graze her shoulder with her fingers or gently squeeze her arm, and it was hard to say goodbye to Eliza, knowing that she would be saying goodbye to Kara soon.  

     

                For privacy, Lena waited in the car, but watched through the tinted windows as Eliza wrapped her youngest in a tight hug, clinging to her for a long minute, and Lena didn’t have to see their hidden faces to know they were both crying. Alex sat in the passenger seat, which left room for Kara to slide in beside Lena in the back, her lashes spiky with tears and her blue eyes bright and bloodshot as she tried to flippantly wipe her cheek. Lena squeezed her knee and kissed her shoulder as the driver put the car into gear and reversed down the sloping driveway.

     

                The flight back to National City felt like it dragged, the sun sinking low on the horizon until they descended through the clouds into a lavender sunset. The air was warmer as they disembarked and made their way into the waiting car, and Lena felt exhausted as she leaned back in her seat and closed her eyes, Kara’s hand in hers and the urge to sleep building behind her eyes. They dropped Alex and Kelly off first before they went home to the townhouse.

     

                It was dark when they pulled up outside, and Lena switched the lights on as she walked through the ground floor, the driver bringing their luggage as Athena bounded up the front steps and made straight for her food bowl. Lena smiled and went to feed her, scratching her at the base of her neck as she looked up at Kara.

     

                “Someone’s pleased to be home.”

     

                “Mm, me,” Kara murmured, stretching her arms out wide as her face crumpled. Her shoulders went slack as her hands fell to her sides and she walked over to Lena, cradling her waist as Lena lazily looped her arms around her neck. “Dinner?”

     

                “Let’s order in.”

     

                They ordered pizza and changed into pyjamas before nestling up in bed with Lena’s laptop playing some TV show Kara picked on Netflix, Kara groaning at how comfortable the mattress was as she burrowed under the blankets and ate her chicken supreme with slow relish. They finished the episode and Kara closed the laptop before turning onto her side to face Lena, a tired smile creasing her face as her eyelids slid closed.

     

                “It’s good to be home,” Kara whispered.

     

                “Does that mean you still want to move in?”

     

                It was said teasingly as she reached out and trailed her fingertips down Kara’s arm, but Lena was still somewhat nervous to voice that small doubt at the back of her mind. Still, Kara smiled and hummed as her arm draped over Lena’s waist and her fingers splayed across her back.

     

                “Yes. Why?”

     

                Lena swallowed thickly and closed her eyes as she basked in the feeling of Kara’s fingers running over the ridges of her spine through the cotton of her shirt. “I know what it’s like to be lost and lonely and sometimes I think … it’s too good to be true. I never really felt what it was like to have someone until I met you, and you asked me all these questions about what I liked and what I hated, and I don’t know. It just felt like you really wanted to know. And since then … I haven’t liked the idea of living alone, so …”

     

                Kara’s reply was slow to come, but Lena felt a wave of calmness wash over her, her vulnerabilities seeming a trifling thing when voiced aloud to someone so solid and present that she could never imagine her leaving. So casual was their affection as they dwelled in the moment of silence, so comfortable were their bodies and souls next to each other that there could be no rejection, no discomfort with being honest.

     

                “I don’t … I don’t think I knew I was lonely until I met you,” Kara slowly confessed. “At home, after my parents died and my life fell apart, I just wanted everything to be okay. I wanted to be exactly what Eliza needed, and exactly the type of sister Alex wanted, and at school, I wanted to be the perfect student, so I tried to be calm and responsible and steady and- and happy , and I think I was nineteen years old the first time it occurred to me that maybe that wasn’t how some people lived. That maybe I just was someone, beyond who I tried to be. Enlisting was probably the first moment I ever made a decision that my family didn’t approve of, a career choice that just … it was stupid , but I thought I wouldn’t feel so alone if I chose to do something where I was always travelling and surrounded by people.”

     

                She trailed off and swallowed audibly in the quietness of the room, and Lena stared at her with intense green eyes, taking in the way the golden lamplight fell across Kara’s face, how her lips parted as she drew in a faintly ragged breath. And then a smile twitched the corners of her mouth and her face softened as she exhaled slowly.

     

                “And then I met you and I haven’t liked the idea of being alone since then either. But I just- I can’t … I’m sorry.”

     

                She was crying now; she covered her mouth with a hand and tried to press her lips together to stifle the sound, but the sobs couldn’t be kept in. Panic knifed through Lena as she pushed herself up, eyes widening as her lips parted and she reached for Kara, gently pulling her arm to get her to come to her. Tears pricked her own eyes as she felt her throat painfully constrict as Kara turned away from her, curling in as she dug the heels of her palms into her eyes.

     

                “I’m sorry,” came her muffled words, “I just- I can’t do it anymore.”

     

                Lena’s outstretched hand flinched back as her face went slack with shock, her heart squeezing tightly in her chest as she struggled to draw in a shallow breath. The blood seemed to drain from her face and her stomach swooped as she grabbed a fistful of Kara’s shirt, her voice low and pleading as she blinked rapidly, the building urge to cry threatening to overwhelm her.

     

                “Don’t say that,” she whispered, anguish making her voice crack. “You don’t mean that.”

     

                “What- I- not you.”

     

                Shifting up, hands falling away from tearful blue eyes and blotchy cheeks, Kara stared at her with panicked confusion, reaching out to grab her hand, golden tan against porcelain as she wound their fingers together.

     

                “God, never you, Lena,” Kara fiercely whispered, touching their foreheads together as she let out a ragged sob. “You are … the only thing that makes me happy right now. I just- I’ve been holding it together for so long now and I’m just … confused. I can’t pretend to be happy anymore because it just feels like- I’m exhausted. I’m just so tired all the time.”

     

                “Hey, hey,” Lena murmured, wiping away Kara’s tears and brushing her hair out of her face, “it’s okay, you don’t have to pretend around me. Not ever. I’ve got you, okay? You don’t have to keep it together.”

     

                Sharply exhaling, Kara leaned her head on Lena’s shoulder, her shoulders shaking as Lena’s arms came up to wrap her arms around her, holding her close as tears spilled down her own cheeks. “I don’t want to do this to you. It’s not fair. I don’t want to go back.”

     

                “Sh, it’s okay. You have to; just for a little while, and then this will all be over.”

     

                “I don’t want to upset you. You don’t deserve this; I’m sorry for making you cry all the time, I just-”

     

                Lena clicked her tongue and frowned slightly as she kissed the side of Kara’s head, enveloping her in her arms as she rocked them slightly. “Look, we’ll be alright. Don’t worry about me; I can handle it. I just- I want to help you. Talk to me and I’ll listen, and I’ll take care of you, okay? I love you. I don’t say it out of habit, I say it to remind you that you’re the best thing that’s ever happened to me. Just … tell me what to do to help.”

     

                “Can you just … hold me. I want you to hold me.”

     

                Her voice was weary and hoarse and Kara pulled back to give her an uncertain look. Taking her face in her hands, Lena kissed her brow, her cheeks, the side of her mouth, firm yet gentle, before she shifted on the bed, bringing Kara with her. They clung to each other on the bed, emotionally drained as they soaked up each other’s presence, a tangle of legs and blanket, with Lena’s chest pressed against Kara’s back. Her palm was over Kara’s chest, and her hand on top, and Lena could feel the steady beat of her heart as they lay quietly for a long while.

     

                “Do you want to talk about it?” Lena eventually asked.

     

                “I don’t even know what to say,” Kara murmured, resigned and tired. “I just don’t want to leave you again. I don’t want to go; I don’t want to go back there. I never want to go back, I never want to leave the people I love, but this time … I have someone who I’m in love with. It hurts; it hurts more than I thought it would, being over there without you. I don’t want to do it again. I’ve been trying to stay positive, I’ve been trying to think about how it’ll all be over in a few months, but I’m so tired. Being home … it’s made it harder than ever.”

     

                “I’m sorry, I don’t know how to make it easier for you. I feel … useless . I don’t know what to tell you, but I understand some of it, and I know it’s hard. You don’t have to do it alone, my love.”

     

                “I know, but I just- I’m so used to being the happy one, the optimistic one. I’m afraid that if- if I’m not … then I won’t be myself. I don’t know what else to be, I don’t know what else people expect from me.”

     

                “You. Just be you. It’s okay to change, you don’t always have to be the same person. I love you for you. I’ve seen you after rough days, I’ve watched you cry through a computer screen and it’s killed me to not be there to hold you, but I never once loved you any less for being upset,” Lena told her. “You have people who love you no matter what. We can help you, you don’t have to keep things to yourself.”

     

                “I know,” Kara sighed. “I should’ve known that I could talk to you about it – and Alex. Everyone just has so much going on, you all have your own lives, and I feel like everything over there is so out of touch with things here. It’s two separate worlds.”

     

                “I won’t pretend to understand what it’s like, but I know that you mean the world to me and your family. Nothing you have to tell us is unimportant; I want to hear everything, the good and the bad,” Lena told her.

     

                “Okay.”

     

                Lena kissed her shoulder and squeezed her gently, an ache of worry in her chest as she blinked back tears, her heart a little bit broken from Kara’s sudden breakdown. “Just talk to me.”

     

                Humming deep at the back of her throat, Kara pressed her back up against her and raised their entwined hands to press a kiss to Lena’s knuckles. “Did you really think I was about to break up with you?”

     

                Cheeks turning faintly pink, Lena sighed softly, “yeah. Yeah, I did. Out of left-field, obviously, but … everyone’s always leaving so I just- but … it would be nice if you stayed.”

     

                “My sweet Lena,” Kara whispered, “I’ll never leave you. I promise.”

     

                They stayed curled up against each other like that until they drifted off to sleep, the lamp still on, empty pizza boxes at the foot of the bed and the curtains wide open. They woke up still cuddled close together, Lena’s arms still wrapped around Kara’s wiry body in the warmth of the bed. They had no commitments for the day and stayed in bed late, the quiet house shifting around them and the sound of traffic outside and the rustling magnolia trees a gentle backdrop to the morning.

     

                Eventually, Lena rose to make them breakfast, bacon frying in the pan and eggs poaching while they listened to Beirut, sunshine saturating the kitchen as they danced and laughed, memories of the night before chased away by the way they looked at each other with so much love that they could still feel it every time they looked away.

    Chapter 40

                Their week together in National City seemed to fly by.
