They tried to make the most of everything, visiting art galleries and baseball games, tiny restaurants with a few booths doused in red light where they drank margaritas, and the bowling alley where Alex almost bowled a perfect game and they all got way too drunk at Al’s afterwards.

     

                It all felt so normal that Lena couldn’t bring herself to count down the hours remaining, until there were only a handful of them left and reality hit her like a slap across the face. She’d almost forgotten, so wrapped up in her bubble with Kara as she left Sam to field business calls and spent her days listening to records and learning how to make apple pie as Kara told her painful stories, piece by piece. Until it was the day before she was set to go back.

     

                Lena woke last, the cool air and grey sky telling her it was near dawn, and she felt around in the empty bed for Kara, finding her side cold. The feeling of waking up without her almost left her breathless with the pain of it and she had to force herself to move on, smoothing out the sheets and opening the curtains as she tried not to dwell on the passing time.

     

                Making her way downstairs, absent of Athena’s presence, she put coffee on the stove to brew in the Moka pot and scooped out the insides of two avocados for breakfast as she waited for Kara to return. She’d gone for a jog most mornings since being back, returning sweaty and increasingly quieter, before perking up again and allowing herself to enjoy the remaineder of her leave. Lena knew it was the nightmares, but that was one topic Kara steered clear of as she shared stories of her time overseas.

     

                She was outside, drinking her coffee with a cardigan pulled around herself as she took in the scattered autumn leaves littering her little garden, pulling stray weeds from the herbs as a lone bird called from one of the towering trees. The sky was overcast and the morning held a chill to it but she lingered out there until claws scratched against the wooden decking and Athena pushed her wet nose into Lena’s hand.

     

                A smile creased her face and she turned to look at the door as she scratched the German Shepherd under her chin. Kara was leaning against the open door in a pair of black shorts and running shoes, her pale body cast grey by the predawn as she studied Lena closely, a peaceful look on her face. Crossing over to her, Lena cupped her chin and kissed her sweetly.

     

                “You shower; I’ll fix us breakfast.”

     

                She poured coffee for them both and pulled out a packet of salmon, waiting until the sound of the upstairs shower stopped running before she put the toast down. They ate at the kitchen counters and washed the dishes afterward before Kara hugged her from behind and kissed the side of her neck, enveloping Lena in her warmth.

     

                “What do you want to do today?” Lena asked.

     

                “Hm, well, I need to finish packing this morning, but tonight I was hoping you wouldn’t say no to this new exhibit in the city. It’s just a small one from this new photographer - I think you’ll like it though - and then maybe dinner with Alex and Kelly?”

     

                “Sounds perfect. Do you want me to make dinner reservations? Somewhere nice for our last …”

     

                Kara turned her around in her arms and reached up to brush a stray hair out of her face and kiss her quickly. “Sure. That’ll be nice.”

     

                Kissing her back, Lena smiled sadly into the kiss, her hands ghosting up Kara’s arms before she laced them behind her neck. “Anything you need from the store? I’ll do a quick run while you pack.”

     

                “Jolly Ranchers.”

     

                Snorting, Lena rolled her eyes, “anything practical?”

     

                “Hm, socks?”

     

                She went to shower then, dressing down in dark jeans and a thin black turtleneck before she drove around to half a dozen stores, following the mental list in her head. Returning home with an armful of bags, she found Kara up in the bedroom she’d left all of her boxed up things, not yet completely unpacked, and set everything down on the bed, taking stock of the scattered sweatpants and battered books and toiletries.

     

                “You almost done?”

     

                “I got distracted,” Kara murmured, raking a hand through her hair. “I was following up on my promise.”

     

                “Oh? Which one.”

     

                Smiling up at her as she took her hand, running a thumb across her knuckles, Kara grinned, “filling your photo album with more photos.”

     

                A burning pressure built up behind Lena’s eyes and she cleared her throat as she looked down, biting the inside of her lip. “It’s not fair.”

     

                “I know.”

     

                “I’m going to miss you.”

     

                “I’ll be back before you know it.”

     

                Lena’s lips twitched ruefully but she nodded and looked up, inhaling deeply to steady herself. “Here, let me help.”

     

                It was past lunch by the time Kara’s bag was finally packed, her uniform hanging up, ironed and ready for the morning, and they ate Big Belly Burger in front of the TV, fitting in a movie before they started getting ready to go out. Side by side in the bathroom, they did their hair and makeup, Kara taking uncharacteristic care as she waved her hair and blindly tried to draw on her eyeliner before Lena had to remind her to put her contacts in. 

     

                Dressed in a black long-sleeved dress, Lena applied a nude lipstick and clipped her hair up, before kissing Kara gently enough to not smudge their lipsticks and slipped on her heels as she sank onto the edge of the bed. Her personal phone started buzzing then and she sighed as she glanced down at Sam’s name on the screen.

     

                “Hi, Sam, I’m just heading out-”

     

                “Shit. Can you swing by the office on your way? There was a security breach. One of the vaults-”

     

                “What?”

     

                “I called the cops but they want to speak with you. I’ve got two officer who just showed up; I don’t know what the fuck I’m supposed to do. I mean-”

     

                Pinching the bridge of her nose, Lena exhaled roughly, “okay, it’s fine, I’ll- give me ten minutes. Okay?”

     

                Hanging up, Lena climbed to her feet and pulled down the hem of the ruched dress as her mouth thinned with irritation. Ducking into the bathroom to watch Kara clear away Lena’s makeup, she grimaced.

     

                “I’m so sorry, I just got a call from Sam and something’s going on at the office. Some security breach. The cops are there-”

     

                Eyes widening, Kara’s eyebrows rose, “the cops? Shit, okay, um … we can go there on the way.”

     

                “No, no, you said it starts at six, right? You go on ahead and I’ll meet you at the gallery, okay? You shouldn’t miss out on it for my work stuff.”

     

                “We can cancel-”

     

                Lena stubbornly shook her head, quickly gathering up her things, sliding a coat off its hanger and snatching up her purse and making sure she had her credit card. “No, we’re going to the exhibit. It’s the last one you’ll get to see for a while; we’re not missing it.”

     

                “Alright,” Kara conceded, beckoning her over. “Come here.”

     

                Slowing, Lena stopped rushing around and walked over to her, serious and a little stressed, and Kara smiled slowly as she pulled her closer, reaching up to smooth out the collar of her shirt dress before she cupped the underside of her jaw.

     

                “You look beautiful.”

     

                Shoulders dropping, Lena smiled and kissed her quickly. “So do you. I’ll see you in a bit.”

     

                “Call me when you leave the office.”

     

                “Okay, I love you.”

     

                “I love you too,” Kara called after her as she rushed out of the bedroom.

     

                Heels thundering downstairs, Lena snagged her carkeys and unlocked the Porsche, quickly driving through the city and parking in the underground garage before riding the elevator up to her office. She barged in with a flicker of annoyance in her eyes and was brusque as the officers introduced themselves.

     

                It was brief, a quick conversation about how one of the alarms had been tripped and with Lena bringing up the inventory and heading down to check nothing had been taken, nothing tampered with and none of the servers breached by hackers, the police gave her polite smiles and left. 

     

                Sighing as she stood in the lobby with Sam, the sky darkening outside and her employees leaving for the day, Lena pulled her phone out and called Kara. It was already twenty past five and she was frustrated to miss out on her dwindling time with Kara over a false alarm.

     

                “Hey! I’m all done here. It was nothing major, just one of the vaults was apparently broken into and they needed me to bring up the inventory and double-check that nothing was missing. I guess there was an error with the lock keypad because everything was still in there. Must’ve just shorted out and made it look like it had been opened.”

     

                “Oh, well that’s good. At least it’s nothing serious.”

     

                “Yeah, everything’s all good. I’m leaving now, so I’ll see you in a bit.”

     

                “I’ll see you soon.”

     

                The call went dead and Lena shoved her phone into her bag before glancing at Sam. “Thanks for calling me.”

     

                Wincing sheepishly, Sam rubbed the back of her neck, “sorry about the false alarm. I didn’t mean to spoil your evening-”

     

                Waving a hand dismissively, Lena shook her head. “No, no, those servers are worth millions. Don’t even worry about it.”

     

                “Well, you look great. Can I give you a ride to where you’re going?”

     

                Hesitating, Lena bit her lip and then relented. “That’d be great, thank you.”

     

                Following Sam down to her sleek Audi, Lena climbed into the passenger seat and brought up the address Kara had given her on maps and directed Sam through rush hour traffic. They pulled up in a loading bay and Lena thanked Sam as she climbed out, her CFO giving her a warm smile as she ducked her head to look at her through the open door.

     

                “Have a good night, boss.”

     

                “Thanks, Sam. You too.”

     

                Shutting the door, Lena tapped the roof and stepped back, watching the silver car pull away before she turned towards the row of stores. They’d had to stop a few doors down from the gallery and her phone started ringing as she made for the narrow windowfront spilling harsh white light out onto the sidewalk.

     

                “Hey, I just got here,” Lena said as she answered Kara’s call.

     

                “I’m running a bit late, sorry! I’m almost there, I promise.”

     

                “Late?” Lena laughed, “you were supposed to get here early!”

     

                “I know, I know, I got held up. The Uber cancelled on me and then the other one was late and- anyway, it’s fine, you go on in and I’ll see you in a minute.”

     

                “Do you want me to wait outside?”

     

                “No, no,” Kara urged her, “I’m two blocks out; don’t hang around in the cold for me.”

     

                “Okay, love you, see you in a bit.”

     

                Kara replied similarly and Lena walked over to the building she’d been instructed to go to. As she reached the door, she hesitated, looking in through the windows to find the narrow room empty, it's wooden floors and white walls holding no one else within its confines. For a second, she thought she had the wrong place, but a quick look at the brass numbers fixed to the wall beside the door and she found that they matched the address Kara had given her.

     

                Brow creasing with confusion, Lena tested the glass door and pulled it open before stepping inside. Her heels were loud in the emptiness of the bare room, and her eyes moved to the archway at the back, disappearing out back to some storeroom or office.

     

                “Hello?” she hesitantly called out.

     

                No response was forthcoming and her expression clouded before her attention snagged on something small stuck to the wall near her. Arms folded over her chest, Lena walked over to it and peered at the small square, her stomach dropping as surprise washed over her. It was her.

     

                It was the first photo Kara had ever taken of her. The neatly scrawled ‘The day we first met’ and date was written underneath it in Kara’s handwriting, just like it was in Lena’s photo album. Lena reached out and gently touched the photo, her frown deepening. Moving onto the next one, she saw that it was another one of her, and so was the next, and the next. All of the photos Kara had taken of them both were pinned to the walls; some taken out of Lena’s photo album and others that were completely new to her. Lena smiled as she realized Kara must’ve taken them out of the photo album earlier that morning when she said she was adding new ones.

     

                Lena’s breath hitched as she reached the last one stuck halfway along the opposite wall. This was where the photos ended, on a blank polaroid. There was no photo, it was just black, undeveloped film, but underneath it, written in Kara’s handwriting was ‘Proposal’ with today’s date written next to it. 

     

                Whirling around with a surprised expression, Lena saw Kara behind her, kneeling down on one knee as she offered a ring nestled in velvet up towards Lena. Her eyes were shining with tears as she smiled widely, hopefully, holding the little box tightly in her hand. The air rushed out of Lena’s lungs and she opened her mouth to say something, but was cut off by Kara.

     

                “Before you say anything , just let me explain,” Kara said with a small laugh. “It’s only been ten months, I know that, and you might think we’re rushing into things and that it’s too soon, and well, you might be right, but I love you Lena, and it doesn’t matter whether it’s been ten months or ten years. I love you. I think I knew I would fall in love with you the moment I first saw you in that café. I wasn’t in love with you then, but I saw you sitting there and you- well, you altered my entire world, and I knew that I could so easily fall in love with you. You smiled at me and that was all it took, my heart went wild and I knew that you were it for me. You changed my life with one smile.”

     

                Lena let out a choked laugh, wiping at her cheeks as she was surprised to find herself crying, her heart hammering in her chest as adrenaline swept through her, making her shake as she gripped her arms tightly to steady herself.

     

                “You, me, kids ... I could see it. I can see myself waking up beside you every day and picking out furniture and paint colours and all that boring stuff that people do together. I want to get married and have kids and grandkids and get really old with my wife. That’s what I want. And I don’t want to wait. No one knows how long they get, and I don’t want to wait ten years or until it's too late for me. Falling for you … it wasn’t falling at all, it was walking into a house and knowing I was home. I want to come home to my wife ; Lena Luthor, will you marry me?”

     

                She had a hand covering her mouth as she quietly cried, unable to make her mouth work as she shook, watching Kara kneel before her, crying as well and looking at her with adoring expectancy, offering up everything Lena had ever wanted in life. And it didn’t feel real, didn’t seem like something so good and right could ever happen to her, that she would ever be wanted. But wasn’t that the definition of home? Not where you were from, but where you were wanted. Kara was her home as much as she was hers and Lena couldn’t stop the surprised laugh that escaped her as she cupped Kara’s cheek in her hand and wiped away a tear.

     

                “Yes,” she tearfully whispered. 

     

                “Yeah?” Kara echoed, surprised as she raised her eyebrows.

     

                “Yes. Of course yes.”

     

                She was laughing as she held a trembling hand out for Kara to slip the diamond ring onto her wedding finger. Once it was securely on, Kara surged to her feet and swept Lena up into her arms, both of them coming together in a crushing kiss as they laughed and cried.

     

                Setting her back on her feet, Kara touched their foreheads together and let out another breathless laugh, elation making her blue eyes bright as she smiled widely, cheeks dimpling as she wiped away Lena’s tears. Drawing her in again, she kissed her slowly, both of them swaying for a moment as they marvelled at the bubble of happiness they existed in at that moment, as if time had stopped just for them.

     

                “I love you,” Lena whispered, her voice uneven as she wrapped her arms around Kara and stared at her with quiet awe. “I love you, I love you, I love you,” she repeatedly murmured, pressing quick kisses to Kara’s lips in between confessions.

     

                “I love you too - if it wasn’t already obvious.”

     

                Lena laughed again, wiping at her eyes as she shook her head, unable to stop smiling as her chest ached with warmth and love. They lingered to look at the photos together, Lena’s arm looped through Kara’s as she pressed up against her, new ring shining in the light, and once they were done they went to the Chinese restaurant Lena had booked them into.

     

                Stepping inside and checking their coats, they were led to a table where Alex and Kelly waited for them, bright smiles full of happiness and a little relief lighting up their faces as they stood. 

     

                “Congratulations,” Kelly quietly exclaimed, holding her arms open for Lena.

     

                She couldn’t stop smiling, a certain shyness coming over her as Kelly inspected the ring and squeezed her hand before turning to Kara, while Lena was pulled into a hug by Alex.

     

                “Did you cry?”

     

                Scoffing, Lena rolled her eyes, “of course!”

     

                Clapping her on the shoulder, Alex ushered her to her seat and the four of them soon found themselves with champagne, clinking glasses as they all clamoured with excitement, the conversation a mix of overlapping voices and laughter.

     

                “I see you were both in on it then.”

     

                “Obviously,” Alex said with a grin, “who do you think called in a favour with an ex-girlfriend cop to show up at your office. Your CFO was in on it too.”

     

                “Sam knew?” Lena incredulously asked.

     

                “And the assistant.”

     

                Groaning, Lena put her head in her hands as she shook with laughter, “oh, man, I was completely oblivious.”

     

                “Good,” Kara smiled, picking up her hand and kissing the back of it.

     

                They ordered several courses of dishes, taking their time as they enjoyed their night - the subdued sadness of Kara’s departure momentarily overshadowed by the celebration of their engagement - and they had far too much to drink, considering Kara would be flying across the world the next day.

     

                Plans had been made for breakfast tomorrow morning and Lena was a little dubious as to whether they’d make it as they finished off their last round of baijiu and little mung bean cakes before calling cabs to take them home. 

     

                Handing the driver a wad of bills, Lena climbed out outside the townhouse and walked up to the front door, light spilling out through the curtained windows as she unlocked the door to let them in. Kara stripped off her coat as soon as she crossed the threshold, dropping it onto the console and locking the door before she picked Lena up, eliciting a squeal from her as she caught her by surprise. 

     

                Laughing, Lena let Kara carry her to the bedroom and deposit her on the bed. She lay on her back as Kara took her shoes off for her and kissed her way up Lena’s thighs, before straddling Lena’s lap and leaning down to press a rough kiss to her lips.

     

                It was dark as they both lay wrapped up in each other’s arms, tracing patterns on each other’s bare skin. Lena lay with her head on Kara’s chest, running her fingers over Kara’s stomach, and Kara absentmindedly stroked Lena’s hair, smiling to herself as she lay with her eyes closed.

     

                “I love you,” Kara quietly whispered.

     

                “I love you too,” Lena replied, smiling at the ring that she could just make out in the dim light of the dark bedroom.

     

                “I don’t want to go tomorrow. I want to go to the top of an abandoned building and watch the sunrise with you. I don’t want to leave. You’re my home.”

     

                “You go, and I’ll stay; I’ll wait.”

    Chapter 41

                They woke far too early that morning, laying together in bed, still half asleep as they drifted in and out of consciousness to the rustling of the trees outside. Eventually, Lena’s alarm went off and she groaned, slightly hungover as she forced her eyes open, feeling feverishly warm as her head ached and the sour taste of alcohol coated her tongue.

     

                She felt Kara’s arm tighten around her as she hummed with annoyance, and Lena quietly laughed, dissolving into a yawn as she covered her mouth and then stilled with surprise, blinking owlishly at the ring she’d fallen asleep with on her finger. 

     

                “Oh, shit. I almost thought it was a dream.”

     

                Laughing against the back of her neck, Kara hummed with delight, a sleepy smile gracing her lips as she kissed the soft spot behind Lena’s ear. “We’re getting married,” she said with smug satisfaction.

     

                Rolling over so she was facing her, Lena squeezed Kara’s cheeks and kissed her firmly before laughing against the warmth of her lips, that little of bubble of joy fighting against the tide of sadness that beat against her. Kissing her once more, Lena let out a soft sigh.

     

                “I’m glad you think you’d unconsciously dream about marrying me though; at least it’s not just me.”

     

                “Sometimes I think you are something I dreamed up,” Lena softly admitted.

     

                With a soft laugh, Kara reached up to trail a fingertip down Lena’s brow and over the bridge of her nose, down to her lips before she traced their outline. “That almost sounds like silly fairytale stuff; careful.”

     

                Scoffing, Lena closed her eyes and nestled closer against Kara, allowing the moment to stretch on, wishing they could stay in that bed forever and let life bypass them. What she would’ve given to just exist exactly as they were for an eternity.

     

                “What time is it?” Kara eventually whispered.

     

                “Six-thirty.”

     

                “What time is breakfast?”

     

                “Eight.”

     

                Humming pensively, Kara pushed herself up onto her elbow, “then let me make the most of my time with my fiancée.”

     

                Laughing loudly as Kara kissed her where she was ticklish, Lena wriggled beneath her and resolved to enjoy her morning. It would be the last good one for a while and she didn’t want to spoil it by casting a pall over everything; she would cry later anyway, so why spend the whole day in tears?

     

                They stayed in bed as late as possible before showering together, a lump getting stuck in Lena’s throat at the casual intimacy of it as she ran her hands down the tanned expanse of Kara’s back, memorising every freckle and muscle and bone. Dressing, they drove to their café, meeting Alex and Kelly inside the cramped space and crowded around the table together.

     

                “This is where you met?” Alex dubiously asked.

     

                Grinning, Kara pointed to the table situated near the window. “Mhm, right there.”

     

                “She wouldn’t stop talking,” Lena laughed, “I had to give up on work entirely. Thankfully.”

     

                “Have you set a date yet?” Kelly asked, raising her eyebrows excitedly.

     

                “No,” Lena laughed, “I haven’t even processed it yet. Oh, God, I have to tell my mom.”

     

                Kara shifted at the mention of Lillian and climbed to her feet, pointing around at everyone, “breakfast is on me; the usual?”

     

                Lena watched her join the queue to order, her face softening with tenderness as she answered Kelly’s questions about the wedding with helpless non-answers. They hadn’t spoken about it, didn’t know when it would be or whether they wanted something big or small - Lena was hoping for small - a beach wedding or something more traditional. Then there had been the comment about kids, something that Lena had never even considered for herself, but felt so natural for Kara. Could she be a mom? 

     

                Kara returned to her seat a few minutes later, arm slung around the back of Lena’s chair as she rubbed her shoulder, talking animatedly in the way that Lena loved so much. They were soon sipping their coffees and Lena was sure to order Kara another one, her last good one for the next four months, and she settled on an omelette for breakfast, the thought of food making her feel queasy.

     

                Try as she might to channel Kara’s optimism, clinging to their mapped out future, Lena could feel her departure creeping closer with each minute that ticked by. It was like a harbinger hanging over them and she could feel that nervous tension creep into her, growing increasingly tense as she sipped her bitter coffee and tried her best to remain involved, possibly overdoing it slightly in her effort to act nonchalant.

     

                Eventually, they were done and the four of them made their way outside, finalising plans for what time they’d pick Alex up before heading out to drop Kara off. It gave them a little more than an hour and they drove home and grabbed Athena’s leash before going for a walk, passing through the market to the park. It was packed, with people buying sourdough bread and artisanal doughnuts and bunched of flowers and vintage Barbour waxed jackets. Along the way, they bought boba and half a dozen croissants, arm in arm as they soaked up their last day.

     

                When they returned home, resigned and grim, Kara went upstairs to change into her uniform and Lena gathered together some extra things for her to pack, carrying it all up to her as her stomach twisted with nervous anticipation of goodbye.

     

                “I have some extra chargers for you in case the other ones die on you. Do you have enough film to tide you over until the first package gets there?”

     

                Kara laughed, raising the photo album and placing it on the middle of their made bed, “I should be good. This is for tonight.”

     

                “And for you,” Lena said with forced brightness, holding up a letter and handing it off to Kara to pack.

     

                Taking it from her, Kara traced her name written in Lena’s handwriting, her throat bobbing as she swallowed, head ducked down as she nodded. She packed it carefully with the rest of her things and blinked rapidly as she looked up at Lena, eyes creasing at the corners as she kissed her quickly.

     

                “I’ll be ready in five.”

     

                Nodding, Lena left her alone, feeling the cracks already appear in her facade, the ache in her chest so painful that she had to stand in the kitchen, taking deep breaths as she leaned against the counter, head ducked and shoulders tense. At the sound of heavy boots on the stairs, she pushed herself up and tried to compose herself, sure that her anguish was written in the lines of her face, and it was all she could do not to burst into tears at the sight of Kara dressed in her fatigues, carrying her bulging bag as she stopped in the doorway of the hallway.

     

                Setting the bag down, she dropped to one knee as Athena padded over to her, tongue lolling and tail wagging. Ruffling the fur around her jaw, Kara smiled sweetly and pressed kissed all over the dog’s head before climbing to her feet and hoisting her bag up. Lena got her coat and put her shoes on before silently leaving the house, walking down the steps as a coldness took root inside her. While Kara loaded her bag into the trunk, Lena gripped the steering wheel tightly in a white-knuckled grip before Kara climbed in beside her and she drove them to Alex and Kelly’s apartment.

     

                They lingered a few minutes at the apartment so that Kara could say goodbye to Kelly, Lena barely making it past the doorway as she vehemently rejected the fact that Kara was leaving again. She didn’t want to watch her say goodbye to Kelly, knowing her turn was coming sooner that she wanted to acknowledge. It was perhaps even more unbearable this time, knowing the anxiety and fear she’d been riddled with for months would return, that she’d go back to sleepless nights and seeing Kara through a screen, knowing what she was missing out on.

     

                She was silent as she put the car into drive ten minutes later, pulling into traffic as the three of them were left with the knowledge that their time was reduced to however long it took them to drive out to the base. They’d stay with her until the very moment she boarded the bus that would drive everyone to their first plane, but that wasn’t enough for Lena and she had to fight for her composure as she sped down the freeway, merging with traffic as her stomach fluttered with that sickening anxiety she’d grown to loathe.

     

                Parking, they all climbed out of the car and Kara grabbed her bag from the trunk and deposited it beneath the bus, while Lena studiously stared at the ground, the sight of so many goodbyes happening unbearable as she hugged her arms to herself. They didn’t have much time, getting there a little late with traffic, and soldiers in fatigues were already on the bus as Kara sighed wistfully and pulled her sister into a hug. 

     

                Lena’s vision blurred with tears as she worked to swallow the lump lodged in her throat, listening to Alex’s fiercely whispered threats as Kara let out a strangled laugh. And then it was her turn, Kara’s boots appearing in her line of sight before she was pulled off-balance and into an unwilling hug. That was all it took for her resolve to break, sinking into Kara’s embrace as she shook with silent sobs.

     

                Kara kissed her hair and swayed her from side to side, looking up at the sky as she swallowed thickly, blinking back her own tears. Letting out a choked laugh, vaguely embarrassed, Lena raised her head and pressed her forehead against Kara’s temple, squeezing her tightly.

     

                “Two kids,” she whispered, “I think two is a good number.”

     

                “Yeah?” Kara asked with mild surprise, cupping Lena’s cheeks in her hands as she looked at her with raised eyebrows, her voice cracking.

     

                “Two little Danvers sisters. We can get a house with a big garden if you want to move out of the city. And a spring wedding; not next year, but maybe the year after, or the year after that. I don’t know, I guess … there’s still a lot for us to talk about, but the point is that I have a whole life with you planned out so you just- you have to come home, okay? You have to come home because we’re getting married. Please, just come home, I’m begging you to just stay safe. Okay? Promise me, please promise me that.”

     

                “I promise. I’ll drag myself back to you if I have to. I love you.”

     

                “I love you too,” Lena whispered, her lip trembling as she caressed the side of Kara’s face before leaning in and kissing her roughly.

     

                Pulling back, she rested her forehead against Kara’s and drew in a ragged breath, holding her close as their eyes met. She didn’t want to look away, didn’t want to let her go, but she kissed her one last time, lingering and desperate, before she loosened her grip on her and let go.

     

                “You have to go,” Lena told her.

     

                Alex stepped forward and clapped a hand on Lena’s shoulder, squeezing gently, and the three of them made for the bus. At the door, Kara turned around and pulled them both into a tight hug, the three of them in tears and holding up the dwindling queue, before she climbed on and they moved back, watching her shadowed figure move down the aisle.

     

                She took a seat beside a window and knelt on the worn cushion, putting her face up to the small sliding window as she gave them a tearful smile, her blue eyes creasing at the corners.

     

                “I love you both. Look after each other for me.”

     

                Lena didn’t trust herself to speak so she settled for a nod, Alex’s arm slung around her shoulder as she put on a brave face and heckled Kara, eliciting a laugh from her sister. As the engine rumbled to life, Kara sank down onto her seat and pressed a kiss to her fingertips before pressing her palm against the dusty window.

     

                Standing amidst the crowd of family and friends, they waved to her as the bus pulled off, waiting a minute until it was out of sight before they turned for the Porsche. Lena wiped at her eyes and climbed behind the wheel, no objection from Alex this time, and they allowed themselves their minute of grief, sniffing and rubbing at their eyes and clearing their throats, and then Lena started the car, hands shaking so much that she dropped the keys into her lap twice and choked on another sob before the engine purred to life. 

     

                They made a pitstop on the way home to pick up Kelly and then went back to Lena’s place. This time, she opened the front door to an excited German Shepherd wagging her tail and shuffling closer and closer to Lena, taking the edge off the wave of loneliness that swept through her, but it was still devastating to listen to the silence, the absence of Kara’s singing drifting through the floors or her heavy footsteps on the stairs.

     

                It was just past twelve but Lena felt so tired as she shed her coat, tossing it carelessly on the narrow bench set against one wall. She kicked her heels off next as Alex picked her coat up and put it on the hook and scooped the shoes up, pressing them into Lena’s hands with a pointed look.

     

                “Mess will only make you feel worse.”

     

                “I might go and lay down for a bit.”

     

                “Alright. Mind if I make myself something to eat?”

     

                Waving a hand dismissively as she made for the stairs, Lena softly sighed, “help yourself to whatever you want. Car keys are on the console if you need to go to the store for anything. Credit card’s in the purse; use it.”

     

                She vanished upstairs, shoulders slumped and feet dragging as she made for her bedroom, stopping in the doorway as she took in the photo album in the middle of the bed and fought back more tears. It could wait until later, for the night when she could cry herself to sleep. For now, she just wanted to curl up into a ball and shut her eyes, a headache pounding behind them from crying and too much to drink the night before. All happiness at the engagement seemed to have been sucked out of her in a matter of hours and she collapsed onto the bed, curled up on her side, and wallowed. 

     

                Undisturbed for a couple of hours, she was finally roused by a gentle tap on the door before it opened with a faint creak. Poking her head inside, Kelly stared at Lena’s curved back, unmoving, and opened the door wider.

     

                “I know you’re awake.”

     

                Lena didn’t answer, swallowing thickly as she closed her eyes and willed Kelly to leave. Instead, the opposite side of the bed jostled and she bit back a sigh, pushing herself up and shooting Kelly a disgruntled look over her shoulder.

     

                Smiling crookedly, Kelly raised a mug. “I brought you tea.”

     

                Heart aching fondly in her chest, Lena smiled faintly and shifted into a cross-legged position, reaching out for the mug of peppermint. “Thank you.”

     

                “Anything you want to talk about?”

     

                Shrugging as she stared down into the depths of her tea, Lena chewed on the inside of her lip as her brow creased with frustrated confusion. “I thought … it would be easier this time. But it’s not.”

     

                “It’s never easier. It’s just … familiar. ”

     

                She hummed pensively and took a sip of tea, the searing heat loosening the tightness in her chest. “I don’t want it to be familiar,” Lena admitted. “I don’t want her … back there. She’s- she’s not well, Kelly. You of all people must know that.”

     

                Reaching out to pat her knee, Kelly gave her a sympathetic look of understanding. “I know you’re scared, you’re worried, but … there are things that happen there that make it hard for us to talk about it, to even admit that we’re struggling. I’ve spoken to Kara about it before and she … look, she knows that once she’s back there’s going to be a big adjustment, and she knows that it’s not going to be easy. When the time comes … we’ll all be here to help; we won’t let her do it alone.”

     

                “I didn’t- I didn’t know it would be like … this.”

     

                “The reality of it isn’t as pretty as you think,” Kelly sighed, “but she’s not going back after this, so … it’ll all pass. It’ll be over soon; it won’t be familiar anymore.”

     

                Nodding, Lena sipped her tea as Kelly left her alone, and eventually she changed into her loungewear and made her way downstairs. The days were already growing shorter in early November, the skies a little greyer as they sapped away the golden California sunshine, and she found the couple poring over the screen of Kelly’s laptop as they bickered over what takeout to order for dinner.

     

                “I’m down for burritos,” Lena said, making for the pantry and ferreting out a bottle of whisky.

     

                She raised the bottle and arched an eyebrow as she drifted over to the cupboard with the glasses, snagging three and sloshing a healthy measure into each before carrying them over to the counter and setting them down.

     

                They gave Alex their orders as she clicked away on the computer, Lena in a sullen mood that made her order far too much out of the desire to enjoy something, even if it was only the pleasure of treating her friends to a good dinner. Choosing a movie, they sipped whisky on the sofas, refilling their glasses, and were soon eating their way through the spread of Mexican food crowding the coffee table. Lena picked at hers with no enthusiasm until it grew late enough to call it a night and she threw the scraps in the bin.

     

                Knowing what was waiting for her upstairs, she dragged her feet a bit, loading the dishwasher and putting on a load of laundry as she fiddled with the dials and read the back of the detergent bottles, puzzling through some chores in an effort to delay the exhausted crying jag she would soon find herself on.

     

                When she couldn’t put it off any longer, she called goodnight into the front living room and went upstairs to bed, quietly shutting the door behind her and taking the time to brush her teeth and complete her skincare routine before sitting on the edge of the bed. Staring at the unassuming photo album for a long minute, she let out a weary sigh and moved further up the bed, pulling the blankets over herself and picking it up.

     

                Flipping to the last page she’d seen, she started from there, making her way through the new additions with agonising slowness as she drank in the sight of the captured memories, fingertips tracing over Kara’s face as her tears soaked into the rumpled linen sheets.

     

                The first one was Lena’s shocked expression as she stared at the camera, with ‘Surprise! Kara’s home!’ written beneath it. Lena’s birthday occupied the first few pages, ones of them at the bonfire on the beach, at the supermarket, at the playground. Dozens of new photos from every moment they’d spent together over the past two weeks, so many that it felt impossible to have shared so much in only fourteen days. Lena let out a sob as she got to the blank one with ‘Proposal’ written beneath it, and next to that one was a digitally printed photo of Kara down on one knee, that must’ve come from a camera set on a timer that Lena had missed. The last photo was from today at breakfast, and Lena smiled as she traced the photo of Kara smiling at her, with her arm thrown around Lena’s shoulders.

     

                The photo album wasn’t full yet; there was still room for more photos, and Lena remembered Kara’s promise that she would fill them up. Closing the album, Lena picked up the letter and tore open the envelope, unfolding the pieces of paper and taking a deep breath that rattled around in her lungs before she choked on a sob.

     

                Careful not to smudge the ink with her tears, she read through it, drinking in each word, making note of Kara’s smudges from her own tears, and felt a pang of such longing in her chest that it hurt to breathe. It hurt so much to not have Kara here with her, but the little pieces she left behind in the photos and the letters meant the world to Lena. Four months stood between their reunion and she cursed how long it seemed as she clutched the letter to her chest and quietly cried, wiping tears off her cheeks as she thought about how unbearably lonely she was going to be.

     

                Setting the photo album and the letter on the bedside table, Lena switched the lamp off and pushed her face into her pillows to try and muffle the sound of her crying. No one disturbed her, although she was sure one of them paused outside her door and heard her through the thick wood, and eventually she cried herself to the point of exhaustion and let it sweep her away, until she knew no more.

    Chapter 42

    To my fiancée,

     

    How weird is that? We’re getting married! If there was anything that could motivate me to do everything within my power to make it back home, it’s the thought of spending the rest of my life with you. I would have fought to make it back to you anyway, but the future we’ll map out together has made the stakes even higher. Not even death would be able to hold me back at this point, I promise you that.

     

    I know you don’t want me to go, and I don’t want to go either, but I want to start by saying thank you. A big part of why I kept doing this job was the fear of having no direction, of having no future, no career or life - not even an apartment - for me to come back to in National City. Now, I’m not so scared of being lost, because now I have a home and a life and I have you. I know the next four months will be difficult - for both of us - but you’ve made it bearable for me. 

     

    I thought it would be easier this time though, but I think it’s going to be harder. Right now, I can hear you downstairs while I finish getting ready, and all I can think about is how much I love that sound. For the next few months, all I’ll think about is the sound of you making coffee or breakfast in the kitchen, your footsteps on the stairs, the smell of your perfume and the detergent they use at the dry cleaners, of that little, infuriating scar and the way your hands are always so cold in mine. I have hours left to appreciate it all - but trust me, I will.

     

    I’ve been thinking a lot lately about our time together and how weird it seems that we’ve only known each other for less than a year. Doesn’t that seem strange to you? And yet I know without a shadow of a doubt that you’re the one person I want to spend the rest of my life with. I thought about proposing a lot while I was away, planning it out, figuring out what I’d say, and of course, I couldn’t quite get the words out properly but I’ve never felt so certain about anything before. The entire time we were at my mom’s house I had to stop myself from popping the question about twenty times.

     

    I’m glad I did it before I went back though; it’ll make the next four months have more meaning. And just think about how fast the last four months went (I know they didn’t feel like it, but in hindsight, it feels so fast) and how much we have to look forward to once this is all behind us. I know it’s asking a lot, but please try not to worry about me - Kelly’s story might have made you worry more, but we have our own story to tell, so just wait for me to come home. I’ll be counting down the days until I’m back for good and then we can start the rest of forever. Just a little while longer. I love you more than you will ever know – more than there are stars in the sky or something cheesy like that that I know you’re rolling your eyes at right now. It’s true though.

     

    I love you, Lena Luthor.

     

    Yours always,

     

    Kara xxx

    Chapter 43

                Lena’s alarm went off early the next morning and she fumbled to switch it off before sitting up and rubbing a hand over her face. Stretching, she yawned widely, jaw clicking, and felt the bone-deep exhaustion of a deep sleep cut too short after a night of crying. The photo album was just out of her reach, on the nightstand, and she reached for it, idly flipping through the pages as her heart twinged before setting it back down and climbing out of bed.

     

                Smoothing out the sheets and throwing open the curtains, she changed into workout clothes and moved through the dark house, down to the basement where she moved through a Muay Thai workout by herself, earphones in with music blasting and pent up energy to burn off. It was almost an hour later when she made her way upstairs, wiping her sweaty forehead with a small towel as she sipped lemon water and tried to slow her breathing, and went upstairs to shower and get ready for work.

     

                Donning a black turtleneck and grey tapered pants, she swept her hair up and did her makeup, masking the dark circles beneath her eyes and applying a dark red lipstick, hoping it would help muster her usual confidence for her first day back in two weeks. After brushing her teeth and picking out a handbag and coat to match her outfit, she made her way down to the kitchen, feeding Athena and then fixing herself a little bowl of muesli and taking it outside to her small garden.

     

                Sipping green tea in the morning chill, she stared out at the shadowy trees, blurred in the blue tint of dusk, the rotting smell of autumn enveloping her as she brooded alone. Athena joined her after a while, laying at her feet and enjoying the peacefulness before footsteps in the kitchen disturbed them both.

     

                Glancing over her shoulder, Lena blankly took in Alex’s silhouette in the open doorway. “What time is it?” Alex grumbled, letting out a weary sigh as she stepped outside, barefoot and hugging her t-shirt to herself.

     

                “Six-thirty.”

     

                “Why are you awake this early? Why are you sitting outside this early?”

     

                Climbing to her feet, Lena snagged her bowl and cup and walked over to Alex. “I was eating breakfast before work.”

     

                Groaning, Alex gave her a pained look, “please don’t tell me you’re going into the office today.”

     

                “I’ve been away for two weeks; do you know how many potential millions that could have jeopardized for the company? So, yeah, I’m going to the office today. What else am I going to do?”

     

                “Take a day and process.”

     

                Lena squeezed past her, dumping her breakfast bowl in the sink and pouring the dregs of tea down the drain before she wiped her hands on a dishtowel. Setting it down on the counter with a sigh, her lips twisted for a moment as she hesitated.

     

                “I don’t need to process anything; I’m fine.”

     

                “Yeah, I’m sure that means something. Let me wake up the resident shrink and see what she has to say.”

     

                “Very funny,” Lena softly laughed, her eyebrows winging up with amusement. “Don’t worry, you can stay as long as you want to. Just don’t touch my scotch.”

     

                Rolling her eyes, Alex assured her she wouldn’t and said she was going back to bed. Still, she waited for Lena to leave first, trailing her to the door, watching as she pulled on a pair of black Louboutins and touched up her lipstick in the hallway mirror before saying goodbye.

     

                Parking in her usual spot, Lena rode the elevator up to her office and was greeted by Jess as soon as she stepped off, her assistant taking her bag and coat and falling into their easy routine as she handed Lena her tablet and carried a coffee and the morning’s paper into the office. A row of manila folders was neatly arranged on her desk, pale morning sunlight streaming in, and Lena sank down onto her chair behind her desk with the comforting weight of ordinary life settling over her.

     

                “What meetings do I have today?”

     

                Jess wasn’t forthcoming with an immediate reply and Lena looked up from the screen as she logged into her computer, and frowned slightly, finding her assistant’s attention trained onto the engagement ring sparkling in the sunlight. Self-consciously covering it with her other hand as a spot of colour seeped into her pale cheeks, Lena ducked her head, clearing her throat as she reached for the first folder.

     

                “Sorry, I just- you said yes,” Jess said with mild surprise. “Congratulations.”

     

                “You knew?” Lena exclaimed, her lips parting as she blinked, taken aback.

     

                “Oh … yes, I, uh, I helped Kara- well, she called Miss Arias and me to help with the cop thing, so …”

     

                “Sam knew?”

     

                “Speaking of Miss Arias, she’s your first meeting this morning. A two-hour recap of the last two weeks; she has the budgeting report and the minutes from the meeting with Nth Metal Corporation.”

     

                Nodding, Lena took a sip of her coffee, lips pursed a little sourly as she thought about being the only clueless person. After a few more minutes of listening to Jess fill her in on the plan for the day, certain documents that she needed to read over, another from the company lawyers that she needed to sign and a statement from the copy-writers and publicist about a minor malfunction with the software that had their operating system down for twenty minutes the night before.

     

                Alone in her office, Lena turned her chair around and drank her coffee as she observed the view, the sunrise reflecting off a thousand windows and the murky waters of the bay sparkling in the distance. And out there, a thousand miles away, was Kara. Her brow creased pensively as she thought of how it was possible for her life to resume its normalcy while Kara was on a plane, being taken to God knows where in the middle of the desert. It put her into a quiet and mildly perturbed mindset as she brooded in silence, waiting for the workday to start.

     

                At eight-thirty on the dot, Sam knocked on her office door and poked her head inside, smiling widely as she walked inside and shut the door behind her. Lena climbed to her feet and grabbed her tablet and the stylus before walking over to the sofa.

     

                “Morning. How’re you?”

     

                Ignoring her question, Sam set her notes and laptop down on the coffee table and reached out for Lena’s left hand, raising it as her smile widened at the diamond ring on her finger.

     

                “I knew you’d say yes. Congratulations!”

     

                Lena blinked as she found herself being wrapped in Sam’s embrace, her CFO’s gentle warmth surprising as Lena frowned slightly. A little embarrassed by the attention, she laughed nervously and flexed her hand.

     

                “Oh … yeah. I heard you were involved.”

     

                Sinking down onto the sofa, Sam gave her a knowing look. “Well, I figured anyone who could drag you away from the office for two weeks was worth lending a helping hand to. And I know it’s none of my business and maybe I’m overstepping, but I’ve never seen you so happy before. It’s nice; I’m happy for you.”

     

                Ducking her head as she bit back a smile, Lena nodded and tapped at the tablet screen with the pen. “Right, well … thanks. And for the record, you’re not overstepping - we’re … friends.”

     

                Pausing, Sam let out a quick laugh, “are we?”

     

                “Kind of,” Lena shrugged.

     

                “You hesitated.”

     

                Sighing, Lena shook her head and opened up a blank document. “Well, I don’t have many friends, but you kind of are so … that’s nice. Maybe we should get lunch?”

     

                “Lunch? Jesus, she really did a number on you.”

     

                “You’re my CFO; we get lunch together all the time.”

     

                “For business meetings.”

     

                Rolling her eyes, Lena looked up and sighed as she deflated in her seat. “Truthfully, I’m just- Kara went back yesterday so … I mean, her sister and her girlfriend have become like family but … it’ll be nice to have someone not so caught up in it all. The worrying, you know?”

     

                With a solemn look on her face, Sam opened her laptop, “sure, Lena, we can get lunch. Now, go on, I know you’ve got a thousand questions for me.”

     

                “The malfunction last night?” Lena started with.

     

                They worked through their two hours, efficient and fast with years of experience and shorthand between them, before Lena was dragged into meetings with Human Resources and three short, consecutive catch ups with department heads. Over the couple of years since she’d taken over L-Corp, she’d phased out the older men that had been part of her brother’s boy’s club and sought out better suited replacements, but still, she always felt just the slightest bit incompetent sitting before management, as if they viewed her as their daughter instead of their boss. It was one of the reasons why she’d leapt to instate Sam as CFO, being only five years younger than her, and Lena was prickly and impatient by the time she’d wrapped up her meetings and made her way back to her office.

     

                Sam came by five minutes later, tall and pretty and observant as she took in Lena’s bristling frame as she shifted things on her desk and silently stewed over the wasted time. “Ready to go?” Sam asked after a tense minute.

     

                Humming distractedly, Lena fetched her coat and bag and swept past Sam, jamming a thumb into the elevator button and riding it down in silence. They cut an imposing pair as they crossed the lobby, CEO and CFO together, the former looking haughty and unapproachable and small. Stepping outside, the brisk wind washed over Lena and she exhaled roughly.

     

                “What do you want to eat?”

     

                “There’s a nice place next door to that Starbucks on Vine.”

     

                “Sure.”

     

                Lena let Sam lead and soon found herself in the middle of an airy narrow space filled with plants as she ate her quinoa and sipped a kombucha. “Meetings weren’t any good?” Sam asked, taking a swig of her drink.

     

                Wrinkling her nose, Lena gestured with contempt. “You know how it is; I’m too young, they’ve been doing their job a lot longer than I have, do I really know how marketing works? All valid points, but it’s just the way they say it, and what can I say? Well I’m CEO and I own the company? That’s shit.”

     

                “But true.”

     

                Rolling her eyes, Lena sighed, “anyway, I don’t want to talk about work.”

     

                “Alright, well, what did your mom say about the engagement?”

     

                Stilling in her seat, Lena cleared her throat and fiddled with her fork as guilt knotted her stomach. “I … haven’t told her yet.”

     

                “No?” Sam asked with mild surprise. “Why not?”

     

                She didn’t know how to voice her thoughts without sounding silly, like a child complaining about not getting her own way. Yet, Lena knew it ran deeper than that, had irreparably affected the way she was able to get close to people, to trust them, and it was a long while before she could bring herself to reply. Sam knew some of the family issues, had been around long enough to witness Lena decline calls and make sniping remarks about Lillian, spending late nights at the office together when the young woman - barely even old enough to drink - should have been at college frat parties and studying for midterms. Put together, it all spoke for itself.

     

                “I … it’s just- things with Lillian aren’t … the easiest. I mean, it’s fine , but I know she’ll disapprove.”

     

                Stabbing sullenly at the small grains, she chewed without relish and then let out a breathless laugh. “You know, it’s actually been pretty good lately. With her, I mean. Ever since I was shot …”

     

                “Ah, nothing like some mother-daughter bonding over a nice gunshot to the abdomen.”

     

                “Ha ha. How’d you manage? After Ruby?”

     

                Sam’s mouth thinned and she shrugged. “I didn’t have a choice; she kicked me out, what could I do? She’s never even seen the poor kid, so … I think I would’ve liked it if she’d reached out. Maybe I would’ve cut her some slack, patched things up.”

     

                “Mm, that’s what I thought,” Lena murmured, drawing in a rattling breath and then exhaling sharply. “Oh, well, I guess I’ll call her tonight anyway and find out. Maybe I’m being too harsh, or maybe I just know her too well.”

     

                “Would it matter what she thought either way?”

     

                Brow furrowing with a troubled look, Lena hummed in agreement, “it would to me.”

     

                Pausing, Lena pressed her lips together and cocked her head to the side, a tight smile curling the corners. “It wouldn’t have before , but now it would.”

     

                Sam nodded and took a bite of her caprese salad before she laughed, covering her mouth with a hand. “You know, this is probably the longest personal conversation we’ve ever had.”

     

                “Yeah, I’m not sure I like it,” Lena said with a grudging smile, “can we talk about work again?”

     

                They finished their lunch together, conversation surprisingly easy as the knot inside Lena loosened a little, the mild triumph of something ordinary - even if technically with a work colleague - making her feel like things wouldn’t be so stagnant without Kara. She paid and they left after their hour of freedom, Lena not wanting to miss the next meeting she had booked in, and by the time they parted on the top floor of the building, Sam making for her own office as Lena walked to hers, she felt marginally lighter. Light enough to promise herself she’d call Lillian.

     

                Despite her workload, Lena decided to work through the evening from the comfort of her office, the influx of emails better managed in cashmere and with wine, and she left along with Jess, both of them riding the elevator down together while they quickly ran over the next day’s schedule. Parting ways in the parking garage, Lena drove him while listening to one of Kara’s favourite albums and walked in to find her house occupied by Alex and Kelly.

     

                “Hey, I’m home,” she called out, the front door slamming and keys jangling as she dropped them into the dish on the console. 

     

                The TV muted and Alex craned her neck over the back of the sofa, raising a hand in greeting, “Hey, I made stir fry for dinner.”

     

                “Nice.” Lena dropped her bag as she shrugged out of her overcoat. “Where’s Kelly?”

     

                “Making good use of your sauna.”

     

                “Right, well, I’ve got some work to finish off so just shout if you need something.”

     

                She walked upstairs to the sound of Alex cursing out her bad work ethic and smiled to herself as she undressed and put her things in the appropriate places. Changing into something more comfortable, she made her way upstairs to her office and paused to move a piece on the Go board, observing the strategy laid out in black and white for a brief second before moving on to her desk.

     

                Athena had followed her up and laid herself out in the shafts of waning afternoon sunlight striping across the wooden floorboards. With her dog for company, Lena methodically made her way through the hundreds of emails - inter-company memos, international correspondances, upcoming board meetings and shareholder meetings - deleting useless ones, reading over passive-aggressive emails with lurid interest in the office drama that she was so far removed from.

     

                She was still busy at work when her phone vibrated on her desk and she looked down to find her mom calling. It made it easier for Lena, cutting out the active decision to reach out to Lillian first, and she only hesitated briefly before picking up.

     

                “Hi, mom.”

     

                “Hi, how are you?”

     

                Mouth twisting ruefully, Lena leaned back in her chair. “I’m alright.”

     

                “Kara went back last night, didn’t she?”

     

                “Mm, yeah. Yeah, she did.”

     

                “Is there anything I can do?”

     

                Running a hand over her face, Lena blew all the air out of her lungs and ran a fingernail over the grain of the wooden desk as she pouted. “It’s fine. It’ll just take a while to get used to her being gone again, I guess.”

     

                They lapsed into silence for a moment, weighted and expectant and Lena straightened up as she cleared her throat, glancing down at the ring winking dimly in the blue dimness of the office. “I- uh, I have something to tell you, actually.”

     

                Lillian was silent, waiting for her to speak and Lena chewed on the words for a moment, building up the courage to tell her and quietly hoping that she was wrong. 

     

                “Kara and I- well … Kara proposed. And I said yes.”

     

                There was a slight pause on the other end of the line before Lillian murmured, “ah.”

     

                “Ah?” Lena echoed, her face crumpling.

     

                “So … she did it anyway.”

     

                “You knew?”

     

                Her tone brittle and a little amused, in a condescending manner, Lillian replied, “yes, she asked for my blessing.”

     

                Stilling, mouth opening and closing for a moment, Lena let out an incredulous laugh, gripping the phone tightly as she pinched the bridge of her nose and smiled. “And you didn’t give it, did you?”

     

                “I- Lena, you’re barely twenty-five! You barely even know each other; it hasn’t even been a year. I’ve met her all of twice. Kara might have expected me to approve, but you know me better than that.”

     

                Scoffing, Lena climbed to her feet, eyes stinging with tears as a lump formed in her throat. She felt like a petulant child, brought to the brink of tears over her mother’s opinion, over her lack of care for Lena’s feelings yet again. Pressing her lips into a thin line, she raked a hand through her hair and paced back and forth in silence for a moment, shoulders tense and static silence filling the line as they both waited for her inevitable anger.

     

                “And you couldn’t have just given it for me?” Lena breathlessly asked, desperation and unbridled anger clouding her words as her hand shook with the effort it took not to yell. “To make your only child happy for once in her life?”

     

                “Lena-”

     

                “It doesn’t matter if I marry her now or in ten years ; I love her and she is the only person that has ever loved me without me having to beg for it. You think that time matters, but it doesn’t, because if it did, you would know me well enough to know that I would never make a decision like this without thinking it through-”

     

                “You’re young,” Lillian softly replied, full of regret. “You’re still just a kid-”

     

                “I stopped being a kid the moment you stopped being my mom,” Lena snapped, her cheeks flushing red as heat curled through her.

     

                “Lena, you’re going to hurt yourself. I told you I would look out for you, even if you didn’t think I was, and this is one of those times. You’re making a mistake.”

     

                Wiping at her eyes, Lena sniffed and grit her teeth, chin dimpling. “The only mistake was thinking that maybe, just maybe , you’d be on my side for a change. But I guess that was just too much to ask, and … I won’t let you ruin my happiness - not again so …”

     

                “Please just think for a second,” Lillian urged her, impatience and frustration colouring her words. “You think you’ve thought it through, that you’re smart enough and grown up enough to see things clearly, but you and I both know that strong emotions always make you rash and cloud your thoughts. And that’s not to say that you don’t love her-”

     

                “Mom, honestly … I really don’t want to hear your opinions on my relationship. Especially when you haven’t even been around. But I guess this is just another thing you can add to the long list of ways I’ve disappointed you.”

     

                She let out a pitifully small and sad laugh, sniffing and clearing her throat. “I think I’m going to go, so … maybe just don’t call.”

     

                “Lena-”

     

                Hanging up, she tossed her phone onto one of the armchairs and laced her fingers behind her neck, tipping her head back and blowing the air out of her cheeks as she closed her eyes. She could hear her phone vibrating on the seat and ignored it, until the quiet sound of a foot scuffing on the steps startled her. Dropping her hands as she raised her head, Lena blinked rapidly and wiped at her face, taking in Alex’s silhouette just above the lip of the first step.

     

                “Dinner’s ready,” Alex warily told her.

     

                “I’ll be down in a sec,” Lena muttered, embarrassment washing over her as she moved over to her phone, declining the next incoming call and tucking it into her pocket.

     

                The steps creaked as Alex climbed up the rest of the steps, giving up any pretense that she hadn’t been eavesdropping as she sank onto the arm of the closest chair, taking in Lena’s still form as she trembled with conflicting emotions, bottling them up inside.

     

                “Want to talk about it?”

     

                “Not particularly,” Lena brittly replied before relenting and letting out a sigh. “I mean, she’s just so …”

     

                She gestured with her hands, as if imagining herself choking her mother, making a scathing sound at the back of her neck before laughing quietly. It lacked any humour and Alex watched silently, waiting for her to continue.

     

                “I mean, would it kill her to just … pretend to be happy? For my sake. Just once.”

     

                “I’m sure she is happy for you. But she’s worried too.”

     

                “Why would she be worried if she was happy?”

     

                “Because I am too,” Alex simply stated.

     

                Lena paused and blinked as she absorbed Alex’s words slowly, her mouth opening and closing as her face crumpled with confusion. “What?”

     

                “Well … your mom’s right,” Alex hedged, holding a hand up to stop Lena’s forthcoming objection. “You’re both young, you haven’t been dating long, almost half of that time has been with Kara overseas and … well, no offence, but this is the first serious relationship either of you have been in and, yeah, maybe we’re all a little worried about how fast it’s all moving. But that doesn’t mean we’re not happy for you.”

     

                Spluttering as she bristled at Alex’s words, only slightly devastating as they cut Lena, she crossed her arms over her chest. “I- well, it’s different with you.”

     

                “Yeah, no shit. But she’s not wrong, kid.”

     

                “You-”

     

                “I’m right,” Alex insisted, “you only hate that she’s right because she’s your mom. Be honest, you’ve rushed into things - deep down you know you have, because you’re scared. Maybe- maybe it’s what Kelly told you about what happened, or you just really fucking love my sister - I know you do - but we all know you’re scared and you just- your mom can see that, Lena. Look, she might’ve been a shit mom in the past, but I don’t think that’s why she’s saying this.”

     

                “Well, seeing as you know her so well,” Lena bitingly replied, making for the stairs.

     

                Alex followed her down, feet thundering on the floorboards. “Hey, I’m not the one you’re angry at; don’t burn all your bridges at once, kid.”

     

                Shoulders slumping, Lena came to a stop and she sighed heavily, rubbing at her forehead. “Sorry.”

     

                Prodding her shoulder, Alex got her moving again and they made their way down to the kitchen, where Kelly was reading the label of a wine bottle. Dinner steamed in the wok and Alex pushed Lena towards the cutlery drawer while she started dishing up.

     

                “Look, all I’m saying is that maybe you should just give her some time. You guys have been doing better, right? But this is going to be hard for her; she doesn’t even know Kara, she probably feels like an outsider in this while we’ve all become a little family together.”

     

                Mouth thinning as Kelly whispered a question to Alex, Lena listened to their quiet conversation as Alex explained the situation as she set the table. A part of her knew that Alex was right but disappointment drowned it out. “I just … really wanted her to be happy for me, to be supportive for a change,” she said in a small voice, head ducked down as she accepted the bowl Alex pushed into her hands.

     

                Wrapping an arm around her shoulders, Kelly steered her towards the table, holding her own bowl, and sat down before reaching for the Chardonnay. Filling their glasses, she was gentle and empathetic as she reasoned with Lena.

     

                “I think the issue here is that Lillian sees your fears and doubts and then voices them to you, which you don’t like. No one likes to be confronted or criticised for their decisions, even when the logical side of us can see the truth to it. We put up defences to protect ourselves - some of us push people away.”

     

                She gave Lena a small smile and covered her hand with her own, “if your instinct is to do that to protect yourself, there’s a good reason for it. I’m not judging you for it. But … I think that you wouldn’t know what to do if you weren’t being pushed by her, you wouldn’t grow as much if you didn’t work through the conflict.”

     

                Sitting with her words for a moment, Lena struggled to speak around the dry tightness in her throat. Fiddling with her fork as she chewed on her lip, she swallowed thickly. “I’m just- I’m sick of all the conflict,” Lena whispered, anguish twisting her face.

     

                “I’m just scared that you’re not going to be prepared for reality,” Kelly murmured as Alex dragged a chair out. “Your mom said that Kara might not come back, and, well, she’s right. She might not. That’ll be heartbreaking for you; trust me, I know what it’s like to have the person you love not come home, and it will tear you to pieces . And you’ll need your family around if- if that happens. When she comes home though ... that’s going to be a big adjustment for you both. There’s going to be a lot going on, and I’m not saying you can’t handle it, I’m just saying that your mom is being harsh because … she’s your mom and she knows that no one else is going to be honest with you about the bad parts.”

     

                Blinking back tears, Lena shovelled in a mouthful of food and chewed as she shifted in her seat. “You could’ve just been honest too.”

     

                “But we’re happy for you,” Alex fiercely whispered, sipping her wine. “I see the way she is with you, the way you are together, and I’m grateful … so, the rest of it is just … irrelevant. Until it’s not.”

    Chapter 44

                After a restless night of pacing, frustration, worry and misery competing inside her for which one would wear her out first, Lena spoke to Kara in the early hours of the morning, her office still dark, illuminated by the harsh light of her computer monitor as the floorboards stopped creaking and she felt the knot in her chest unwind. The day she’d had was written on her face, a slight tremor in her voice, raspy from exhaustion, and her smile barely a faint twitch, 

     

                Insisting that she’d slept, that she was okay and just a little disappointed with her mom, Lena tried to ease Kara’s worry, wishing she could reach through the screen and smooth away the crinkle between her eyebrows. As it was, she felt marginally better after speaking to Kara, despite the visceral hatred she felt for the fatigues, the beige wall of the tent she was in, the distant shouts and the way Kara’s lips already looked chapped from the heat.

     

                When she had to go, Lena felt weariness seep into her, right down to her bones, and went to get ready for work. It was a long day, irritating and unproductive with a new prototype of her nuclear battery malfunctioning, a client pulling out of negotiations and half a dozen sporadic calls from her mother that she had the pleasure of declining. 

     

                The rest of the week followed much the same pattern, insomnia plaguing Lena as she paced in the office in the attic, the weather growing greyer and cooler and work pissing her off. She wished she had the liberty of calling in sick, of vanishing until she felt better, but as rich as she was, it came with the responsibility of running the company. For all her complaints to Sam though, Lena would fight tooth and nail if anyone even considered trying to displace her from her position as CEO.

     

                Still, on Friday evening, after a long day of work, Lena needed a break and as she rummaged around in her handbag for her keys, standing in the elevator with Sam, she paused. “I need a drink. Do you need a drink? God , I can’t even remember the last time I got drunk.”

     

                “Well, Ruby is at a slumber party tonight so … sure.”

     

                “Hang on, let me make a call,” Lena said, fishing out her phone and calling Alex. “Hey, what’re you two doing?”

     

                “It’s crime shows and face masks night.”

     

                “Come out for a drink with me. I’m bringing a friend from work; Sam.”

     

                Snorting, Alex replied with scepticism, “are you feeling okay?”

     

                “It’s just … been a long week,” she softly admitted.

     

                “We’ll meet you at Al’s in thirty minutes.”

     

                Lips curling into a small smile, Lena’s shoulders dropped as the tension bled out of her. “You’re the best; see you there.”

     

                Spilling out of the elevator and into the evening, a brisk wind whipping their hair around their faces, Lena hailed them a cab and sank into the cracked leather seats, tobacco and pine heavy in the confines of the cab as the heater stuttered out gusts of warm air. They were dropped off outside the grimy front of the bar, a neon sign blinking in the twilight while muffled music was contained behind yellowed windows plastered with so many old posters that they couldn’t even see inside.

     

                “This is where we’re going?” Sam incredulously asked, her nose wrinkling faintly with distaste.

     

                Laughing, Lena touched her arm as she leaned in, “I felt the same the first time I came here. It’s a bit of a dive, but it’s alright when you’re inside. Maybe just … don’t touch anything. And the floors are a bit sticky. And don’t use the bathroom.”

     

                “I didn’t think you’d be caught dead in a place like this.”

     

                “It wasn’t by choice. Nothing here is top shelf.” 

     

                “That’s what you get for dating someone normal.”

     

                “Did you used to come to places like this in college?”

     

                Sam shrugged as she pushed the door open ahead of Lena, holding it as she breezed inside. “Sure. Except, you know, I had a kid. I used to work in a bar like this while I was studying. Barely making ends meet - until you came along.”

     

                Discomfort twisted Lena’s stomach as she let out a slight laugh, “well … I hope I’m paying you enough now.”

     

                “More than I know what to do with. And thank you, again, for the reference for the private school and Ruby’s tuition and everything-”

     

                Waving a hand dismissively, Lena frowned, “it was nothing. Well, maybe it was bribery; if I don’t look after you then you’ll leave and I’ll have to find a replacement. And I really can’t be bothered going through all that effort again.”

     

                Sam snorted and Lena led them over to an empty table, a wad of beer coasters wedged under a leg to stop it wobbling, and Lena wrinkled her nose at the circles of sticky glasses left on the scarred wooden top. 

     

                “What’ll you have?”

     

                “Same as you,” Sam replied, looking around the dim room.
