                “I’m sure you’re very busy,” Eliza conceded and Lena firmly nodded. “You’ll still be coming for Christmas though?”

     

                Smile brightening, Lena eagerly nodded, “looking forward to it.”

     

                “Good.”

     

                They finished up and Lena found herself sitting beside Eliza, staring blankly at the TV screen as The Holiday played, her phone clutched tightly in her hand as she willed it to ring. It didn’t though, and she fell asleep without meaning to, sinking down further against the cushions as her tiredness caught up with her.

     

                She woke, murmuring as she blearily struggled to open her eyelids, to find Eliza gently shaking her awake, a blanket pooling around her waist as she shifted upright. “What time is it?” she gravelly asked.

     

                “Eleven. Go to bed, sweetheart.”

     

                Humming in agreement, Lena plodded upstairs and fell into her unmade bed, reaching out for the empty side and sighing wistfully. She slept restlessly and woke a few times during the night before bundling back beneath the blankets, bleary-eyed and troubled, and waking as the sun started to rise. Showering quickly, she was wrapped in a towel and browsing the rack of skirts, pants and sweaters when she heard her phone start vibrating.

     

                Stiffening as she tried not to get her hopes up, Lena quickly crossed over to the nightstand and felt the breath rush out of her as she yanked her phone off the charging cable and sank down onto the edge of the bed. Her knees felt weak and her hands trembled as she answered the video call, a painful constricting feeling in her chest as she blinked back stinging tears.

     

                Kara’s face appeared on the screen, pixelated for a moment, as Lena exhaled roughly, the breath hitching as she wiped at her cheeks, tears spilling down them. “Jesus, Kara,” she breathlessly sobbed. “I-”

     

                “I’m sorry,” Kara winced, a spasm of agonised guilt crossing her face. “I’m sorry I haven’t called. There was this storm and the power was knocked out by some lightning, and I’ve been- well, I can’t say where I’ve been but I haven’t been at base so there was no way we were getting signal out here. God, I’m so sorry, I bet you’ve been worried sick.”

     

                Lena let out a choked laugh, “yeah. Yeah, something like that.”

     

                “I’m sorry,” Kara said, her frantic rambling softening as she gave Lena a yearning look through  the screen.

     

                “It’s fine. As long as you’re safe, it doesn’t matter. I just- I thought-”

     

                She couldn’t even finish the sentence, pressing her lips together to stifle a shuddering sob, before shaking her head. Holding her towel closed, she climbed to her feet. “Your mom’s here. I’ll go and get everyone.”

     

                “How’re you?”

     

                Snorting as she yanked open the bedroom door, Lena gave her a wry smile, “oh, I’ve been great. Best week of my life, I think.”

     

                “God, I’ve missed you,” Kara said with a quiet laugh. “I love you. It’s so good to see your face; if it wasn’t for all the photos I have of you, I probably would’ve forgotten just how beautiful you are.”

     

                “You’re so full of shit. Here.”

     

                Lena paused outside the bedroom Alex and Kelly always occupied and knocked loudly. There was a minute delay before Alex opened the door, scowling and ruffling her short hair as she shot Lena a grumpy look.

     

                Face relaxing into a smile, Lena held the phone out, “it’s Kara.”

     

                Eyes widening as all prior disgruntlement vanished, Alex grabbed the phone off Lena and smiled as her shoulders dropped, relief knifing through her. “Oh, you little shit. ”

     

                “Did you miss me?” Kara chuckled.

     

                As much as she wanted to stay and drink in the sight of Kara, re-memorise every inch of her and never look away again, Lena touched Alex’s arm and jerked her head. “I’ll get your mom.”

     

                Kelly was still asleep in bed and Alex followed Lena out at a slower pace. Thundering downstairs, knowing Eliza would already be awake, Lena was almost giddy with relief as she swung around the end of the stairs and walked through to the kitchen. The back door was shut but she could see Eliza sitting outside in her little garden, idling scratching Athena behind her ears as she sipped a cup of green tea.

     

                As the door let out a quiet squeak, she looked up, taking in the glow in Lena’s green eyes, the slumped shoulders and pink cheeks, the smile she couldn’t fight back, and Lena similarly watched Eliza shed the mantle of worry they’d all been wearing for days now as a slow smile spread across her face.

     

                “She called?”

     

                “She’s fine.”

    Chapter 49

                Two days before Christmas, Lena was zipping up a leather overnight bag and eyeing the other one nearby filled with gifts, wearing an olive turtleneck as rain speckled the window panes and she stubbornly refused to acknowledge the thick coat waiting to be donned as they descended into Midvale. Snow was a given in Oregon at this time of year, and while she enjoyed the cold weather, it felt bleaker than usual to be spending the holidays without Kara. 

     

                Still, the prospect of Christmas in a small town was a novelty for Lena, some made-up scenario in her head with a log fire and puffer vests and paper snowflake decorations while children sang carols in town. She attributed that amusing picture she painted to the abundance of Hallmark movies she’d been forced to watch over the past week. The reality was most likely going to be too much food, too much drink and the same pair of pyjamas for the entire week. It was a welcome change to her usual holidays.

     

                Quiet excitement constricted her chest as she found herself on a plane, doing a crossword as she ate a green apple and periodically stared out at the deep grey clouds. It was the most she’d had to look forward to in a while and Alex and Kelly’s good mood was almost infectious. Even as they descended through the snow, it wasn’t as grim as Lena had anticipated, the view obscured through the haze of flakes, but she could still make out the snow-capped trees.

     

                The drive through winding back roads was slow as ice made the asphalt dangerously slippery, almost shining black in the grey and white landscape, and the windows of the private car fogged up from the heat generated by four bodies and a dog. The radio kept cutting in and out with static and Christmas music and Lena stared thoughtfully out the window, feeling the familiar peace of Midvale settle over her as they approached the outer limits of the small snow-dipped town.

     

                It was as she’d imagined, decorations and lights in every window and wrapping around the roofs, piles of white snow and brown slush in the gutters. They passed by a man shovelling snow and people walking outdoors in puffy coats, hats and scarves obscuring most of their faces, and Lena smiled as they were driven up to the house.

     

                Stepping out of the car, she was slapped by the stinging cold as a ragged wind was pushed in off the coast, shivering after the stifling warmth of the car. The driveway was salted and she was wary as she gingerly walked up the sloping drive, shepherding Athena ahead of her as she worried over the dog’s paw pads. Eliza was home, smiling as she opened the door, the smell of cinnamon and baking apples drifting out of the door with the heat as she ushered them all inside.

     

                Coats were shed and bags carried upstairs, while Lena unloaded her gifts beneath the colourful Christmas tree and eyed the stockings along the mantlepiece and the decorative Santa figurines and homemade decorations. There were ones with Kara’s name written on it in large loopy writing and ones where the glitter had flaked away over the years and it struck a pang of warmth and longing in her chest. They’d spoken of kids; maybe she’d get to give it to them.

     

                Sitting in the living room, the shutters closed to the dark clouds and snow sweeping in from the grey sea, they nursed cups of peppermint hot chocolate and played a Christmas movie on the TV which they only half paid attention to while chatting. The excitement of being there was tangible and Lena found herself laughing and smiling, warm and comfortable with a blanket over her lap, for the first time in weeks.

     

                She made a run to the store with Eliza shortly after lunch, picking up a few last-minute things that they needed before the stores closed, including a pie for dessert on Christmas Day. Lena marvelled at the town as they drove around, completing their errands, quiet in the passenger seat as she held the box with the pie safely in her lap, the trunk and back seats growing fuller with each stop. It was peaceful, Eliza’s company undemanding and understanding, and Lena was grateful for it as she made herself useful.

     

                The snow had stopped by the time they got home and the four of them made trips to unload the car, trying to cram food into the full fridge while the heater made the house suffocatingly hot after the freezing cold outside. Afterwards, they made cookies together, taking it in turns to mix and roll and cut, whoever was in charge of sprinkling icing sugar over the ones fresh out of the oven sitting on the counter and eating their way through a couple.

     

                Lena enjoyed it as Eliza coached her on the correct measurements of the dry ingredients, the thickness to roll it out to, making them with as much care as possible, knowing that a large portion of them would be sealed in an airtight container and shipped over to Kara.

     

                As the day waned into night, the winter wonderland outside so beautiful and stark against the darkness, Lena bundled up in her layers and walked out to the backyard. The dunes had a fine dusting of snow and the tall rocks piercing the waves were snow-capped as grey waves crashed against them before rushing in over the golden sandy shore. It felt at odds with one another, the beach evoking thoughts of summer and warm air while her breath plumed before her and she left footprints in the fresh snow. The blue of twilight blurred everything and Lena smiled to herself, spreading her arms wide as she drank it all in, knowing Kara would have loved it. She loved it for her in her stead.

     

                They slept late after a few bottles of wine, and Eliza had to work all of Christmas Eve, leaving the three women to lounge hungover on the sofa through most of the morning, drinking copious amounts of coffee and nursing headaches with Tylenol. Lena only stirred after lunch to take Athena for a walk, Kelly joining her as they walked along the beach, the air freezing and briny, the sound seeming subdued by the stillness of winter. They didn’t go far, too cold to withstand the battering wind as their hands turned numb in their pockets.

     

                Eliza was home late and they all spent Christmas Eve on the sofa, Lena reading a book as Alex versed Kelly on the worn plastic chess set, the remnants of a half-eaten charcuterie board on the coffee table while the TV played some old Christmas movie in between commercials. They went to bed just before midnight, a sense of anticipation hanging in the air as they all went to their respective rooms, and Lena breathed in the faint lingering smell of Kara in the freshly laundered sheets, wishing she was filling the empty space beside her as she willed sleep to come.

     

                She woke first the next morning, pulling on fuzzy socks and a fleece and padding downstairs. Brewing coffee, she yawned widely and stared out the kitchen window, taking in the freshly fallen snow, before switching on the Christmas tree lights, the colourful little bulbs casting a rainbow of light over the dim living room. Lena didn’t even have time to finish pouring her cup of coffee before footsteps sounded on the stairs.

     

                “Merry Christmas,” Alex greeted her with a yawn, quickly melting into a rakish smile as she stole Lena’s coffee and got flipped off in return.

     

                Pouring herself another cup, and a third for Kelly who was surely on her way down, Lena took a sip and then added some sugar and cream to sweeten it up. “Now what?”

     

                “Gifts, duh,” Alex said, snagging the other come and kissing Kelly as she stepped out into the hallway.

     

                Lena poured another cup for Eliza as Alex vanished upstairs to fetch her and the four of them had just assembled in the living room when tires sounded outside. Face creasing with confusion, Lena watched as Alex peered through the window overlooking the driveway and glanced over at Lena.

     

                “Your mom’s here.”

     

                “She’s early,” Lena murmured, looking down at her phone screen to find it was just past eight.

     

                Climbing to her feet, Lena walked to the front door and pulled it open, a blast of freezing air assaulting her as she squinted her eyes against the onslaught. Shivering in the doorway, she watched as Lillian approached, snow dusting her shoulders and hair as she hunched her shoulders.

     

                She smiled as she walked up the steps and Lena gave her a wary look. “You’re early.”

     

                Looking taken aback, Lillian straightened up, a frown forming between her eyebrows. “Was there a timeframe on my invitation?”

     

                “No, but I thought you’d- well … that’s not how our Christmases used to go.”

     

                Reaching out, Lillian cupped her chin and gave her a wry smile, “would you prefer it if I worked all day and showed up after dinner to drink port?”

     

                Rolling her eyes, Lena stepped back, her mother’s hand falling as she followed her inside, and smiled crookedly. “We were just about to open gifts; did you want coffee first?”

     

                She went to fetch her mother a cup as Lillian shed her cashmere coat and greeted Eliza warmly. Handing off the mug as she walked back into the room, Lena sank down onto the floor and reached for her phone, videoing Kara and waiting for it to connect. It took a minute but her face came into view, lit by a lamp as shadows gathered in the corners, and Lena let out a snort of laughter at the Santa hat she was wearing.

     

                “Merry Christmas!”

     

                “Merry Christmas,” Lena smiled with adoration, angling the phone as everyone leaned in to greet her. “We were just about to do gifts.”

     

                “I’ve been saving mine all day. Do you know how hard that was?”

     

                “You go first then.”

     

                Kara shifted her phone, leaning it against something to reveal herself sitting cross-legged in her uniform, a pile of colourfully wrapped gifts next to her. She picked one at random and tore the paper open, revealing an expensive brand of body lotion from Kelly. Most of her gifts would be practical, Lena knew, with little room for useless luxuries overseas, but Kara was appreciative with each one she opened on her turn.

     

                Alex doled out the gifts beneath the tree as they took turns opening theirs too. Lena bought Kelly a Coach handbag, VIP tickets for her and Alex for an upcoming concert, an expensive leather jacket she’d seen Alex admiring on a shopping trip she’d dragged her on for the Christmas party and a spa package for Eliza. There were other little pieces she’d picked up for them too if it caught her attention. Some of the same had been sent to Kara too, along with the vintage Leica MP film camera she’d bought her, modest in Lena’s eyes but an exorbitant amount to Kara as she unwrapped it and her mouth fell open.

     

                Lena chuckled with enjoyment at the look on her face and looked rather smug with herself at Kara’s happiness. For her own gifts, she received a hand-knitted forest green sweater from Kara along with a new vinyl record, a variety of small potted herbs, a new planner and a mug with a science joke on it. There was also a letter she saved for later but she pulled the sweater on immediately,  breathing in the smell of Kara’s perfume that had been sprayed on it.

     

                Lillian surprised her by producing gifts for everyone too, gift vouchers and bottles of expensive wine, and Lena was similarly surprised as Alex hesitated and held out a wrapped gift to Lillian. She almost laughed as her mother warily unwrapped a beige sweater, courtesy of Kara to match everyone else’s, and Lillian graciously thanked her on the phone as she neatly folded it.

     

                Once they were all finished, Lena opening an envelope from her mother to reveal a generous donation to a few not-for-profit's that Lena supported as well as the deed to a wind farm along the coast of Canada, she gave everyone hugs and thanked them before gathering up her gifts. She left Kara to talk to her family for a moment and jerked her head at Lillian before slipping down the hallway.

     

                “I thought you’d be coming later so your gift is upstairs.”

     

                Lillian looked mildly surprised that she’d gotten her a gift but followed Lena upstairs silently. In Kara’s room, Lena set her armful down on the bed before turning to her bag, while Lillian looked around the room, intrigue drawing her over towards the trophies and framed photos of Kara’s childhood.

     

                “Here.”

     

                Turning, Lillian took the gift-wrapped box and walked over to the bed, sinking down and carefully opening it as Lena stood before her, arms folded over her chest and a serious look on her face. It was a House of Staunton chess set, the pieces handcrafted with rare woods, and Lena smiled wryly as she hugged her arms to her chest.

     

                “I didn’t know if you’d replaced the family set after you gave it to me for graduation.”

     

                “Thank you. It’s a beautiful set.”

     

                “I- well, I didn’t know what to get you,” Lena admitted, sitting beside Lillian and picking up an envelope. “You already have everything so I thought … maybe something money couldn’t get you. This is the actual gift.”

     

                Lillian took the envelope and opened it, staring down at the itinerary for the flight from National City to Metropolis from the private airstrip that Lena stored her private jet at.

     

                “I thought … maybe I could come and visit and we could play …”

     

                She fiddled self-consciously with her fingers and looked up at Lillian, a flicker of wariness in her green eyes as she watched understanding settle over her mother. Shoulders slumping slightly, Lillian smiled softly, her eyes tender as she reached for Lena’s hands, stilling her fiddling as she squeezed.

     

                “I’d like that a lot. Thank you.”

     

                Nodding, her heart nervously pounding in her chest, Lena smiled slightly and then climbed to her feet. Wiping her palms on her sweatpants, she nodded again.

     

                “Thanks for the gifts - for everyone’s.”

     

                “It was nothing.”

     

                “It was kind.”

     

                Standing, leaving the chess set on the bed as she balled up the gift wrap, Lillian arched an eyebrow. “I have been known to be so. I’m just … relearning how to be more open about it.”

     

                “Ah, another therapy thing?”

     

                “Apparently suppressing things isn’t good for you. You might try not doing that too.”

     

                Snorting, Lena’s eyebrows quickly rose and fell, “I’ve actually gotten a lot better at that, thanks.”

     

                “But you still don’t trust me enough to tell me things.”

     

                Lena laughed quietly. “You’re too busy to hear about the business meeting with the Russians that I offended because I didn’t take their offer. It’s fine, honestly. It’s boring and it’s not interesting and I don’t want to bother you with stupid things.”

     

                “I already told you - I want you to,” Lillian said. “It’s not stupid, or boring, or uninteresting to me. I wish you would talk to me more. I know we see more of each other now but we don’t get to talk about the small things. I’ve missed out on so much already, I want to know everything.”

     

                “Everything?” Lena asked, arching an eyebrow.

     

                “Yes! Everything. I want to know if you tried a new restaurant and thought it was terrible, or what new vegetables you planted in your garden. You’re going to be planning a wedding and I want you to be able to call and ask my opinion on what flowers you should have.”

     

                “Peonies,” Lena said after a moment. “I was thinking about peonies. And we haven’t set a date yet but we’re thinking of a summer wedding. Don’t worry, not this  summer.” 

     

                Lillian let out a breathless laugh and reached out to brush the hair out of Lena’s face, cupping her cheek as she gave her a small smile.

     

                “That sounds lovely.”

     

                Lena gave her a shy smile and then moved towards the door, “come on, I think we’re having breakfast now. If you didn’t already have caviar on your way here.”

     

                Sighing at her daughter’s joke, Lillian ignored it, “I’ll be down in a moment. I suppose I’d better change first.”

     

                “Change?”

     

                Lillian gestured to the sweater that Kara had made for her as her mouth thinned with bewildered amusement. “It would be rude not to, wouldn’t it?”

     

                Staring at her for a moment, caught off guard and not entirely sure how to feel about it, Lena nodded, swallowing thickly. “Thank you.”

     

                Rolling her eyes, Lillian gestured at her to leave and Lena smiled to herself as she shut the door behind her and made her way downstairs. Eliza handed the phone off to Lena as she reappeared in the living room, and she spoke to Kara for a bit longer, until she had to go, giving her a fleeting glimpse of Lillian in her new sweater - endlessly amusing - and then helped make breakfast.

     

                It was a lazy day and they cleaned up the kitchen, opened the eggnog early and watched Christmas movies until it was just past lunch and they all took it in turns helping get dinner sorted. Lena mercifully wasn’t paired up with her mother in an effort to ensure their meal didn’t end up burnt, and she listened to the sound of loud conversation as she trimmed the ends off the green beans while Eliza basted the roasting chicken and peeled carrots. 

     

                It got dark early and with the Christmas lights and their sweaters, the music playing in the background and the cosiness of it all, Lena found herself eyeing the scene and wondering if this was what holidays would be like for the rest of her like. Only with Kara too. It was a future she envisioned and the feeling made her warm as she lingered in the doorway, working a cork into a bottle of red wine with a gentle look of peace on her face.

     

                They all sat around the dining table for dinner, passing dishes back and forth as they loaded up their plates, pulling Christmas crackers and putting on the cheap party hats. Eating until she was so full she could barely move, Lena sipped her wine and felt the pleasant kind of tiredness from a long day, full of excitement, and thought of Kara too. It was a bitter thought to constantly turn to, wondering what her day had been like because she wasn’t there, but Lena knew that next year would be even better with her.

     

                After dinner, they all poured fresh glasses of wine, and Lena, Alex and Kelly got started on the dishes, quickly working through the mountain of pots and pans and knives. Lena couldn’t stop herself from glancing through the open doorway every so often, an almost suspicious look on her face as she dried a serving spoon and watched her mom laugh from the opposite end of the sofa to Eliza, as if they were friends.

     

                “This is weird, right?” she blurted out as she returned to the sink, handing the spoon to Kelly and taking a baking tray off Alex.

     

                “Our mom’s getting tipsy together at Christmas? Yeah, kind of.”

     

                “I thought it was weird at my birthday.”

     

                “What about your family?” Lena asked, glancing at Kelly. “Where are they?”

     

                Rolling her eyes, Kelly gave her a wry smile, “my Aunt Vi lives in Calvintown so she goes to stay with my mom in Metropolis. James and Lucy spend the holidays with them while I get to disappoint everyone by staying on the west coast. I prefer not to freeze my ass off on the few days I don’t have to work, but they get me at Easter so they don’t mind it so much.”

     

                “Fair enough.”

     

                Finishing up quickly, they got more wine and returned to the living room, where Alex declared it time for games. They were unevenly split up without Kara, but Lena joined Alex and Kelly’s team and they took it in turns through a dozen rounds of charades and then pictionary afterwards, calling out answers as they acted out or drew when the pieces of paper said. 

     

                It was getting late when Lillian finished off her glass of wine and set it down on the coffee table, meeting Lena’s eye and smiling slightly. “Well, I should get going. It’s late and check-out is early in the morning; will I see you before I go?”

     

                “Check-out?” Eliza echoed, “you’re not staying at the bed and breakfast, are you?”

     

                “Yes, I got a room for two nights. It was … well, not to be snobby, but it wasn’t The Ritz.”

     

                “You stayed somewhere that wasn’t five stars?” Lena said, aghast. She clapped as she tipped her head back and laughed at the mere idea of it.

     

                “You make me sound so stuck up.”

     

                “Well …”

     

                “It’s Christmas, Lillian. You should be with family; stay here, I insist.”

     

                Lena stiffened slightly at Eliza’s words, and she saw a flicker of surprise in Lillian’s eyes too, the strange truth to the words catching them both off guard. Of course it was obvious to anyone that Lena had been pulled into their little family, an uncontested part of it, as integral as Kelly was, and yet she hadn’t viewed her mother as an extension of that. She’d just been Lillian, coming along as a kind gesture towards Lena.

     

                “It might be a tight fit. Well, we’ve got a spare mattress we can drag out from under Kara’s bed. Lena …”

     

                “It’s fine. I’ll take the mattress,” she agreed with a small and a quick nod.

     

                Hesitating, Lillian nodded as well and slowly relaxed back onto the sofa. After that, they all had a tea or coffee with apple pie before calling it a night. Changing into her pyjamas and donning her sweater again, Lena brushed her teeth and made her way back to Kara’s room, where Eliza was shaking out an old quilt over the foam mattress, and fished out Kara’s letter. Lillian excused herself to wash up before bed and Lena sat on the edge of the bed, thumbing a corner of the letter as she looked up at Eliza. 

     

                “Thank you for today. For …” she gestured after her mom and Eliza smiled, rosy-cheeked, and walked around the mattress, cupping her cheek affectionately.

     

                “Of course, sweetie.”

     

                Saying goodnight, Lena was left alone for a brief minute to read her letter from Kara, and was smiling to herself as she slid the paper back into the envelope, eyes a little bright, when Lillian walked back in. Stowing the letter away, Lena cleared the bed of her things and then sank down onto the mattress.

     

                Lillian hesitated as she slowly shut the door and turned off the main light, leaving the lamp to cast a warm glow over the room. Slipping into bed, the springs groaning, Lillian let out a soft sigh and reached for the lamp switch.

     

                “Thank you for trying,” Lillian slowly said. “Today has been … I wish we could have had more of this when you were younger.”

     

                “Me too,” Lena said, propped up on her elbows with a morose look on her face.

     

                “You know, I don’t think I’ve ever said it, but … I like the person you’ve become. Through no input of my own, you’ve turned out into someone who’s exactly like the one I’d hoped you’d become. I’m proud of you, and I’m glad I get to see it.”

     

                “Yeah, me too.”

     

                Switching off the lamp, they were plunged into darkness, and Lena lay on her back for a moment before turning her head to the side, staring blankly to where her mother lay in bed. 

     

                “We’ll have more days like today in the future.”

     

                “Goodnight, Lena.”

     

                “Merry Christmas, mom.”

     

                It still took a while for her mind to quieten enough for her to sleep, the blankets rustling with each turn as she restlessly rolled over and then back, her eyes not even remotely heavy despite the weariness in her limbs. Eventually, she feel asleep though, lips parted and eyelashes fluttering as she dreamed.

     

                It was still dark when she bolted upright with a quiet exclamation of panic, heart pounding in her chest and a cold sweat covering her skin as she breathed raggedly. Hunching forward, her dark hair spilling around her face, Lena dug the heels of her palms into her eyes as she exhaled sharply, before the lamp switched on.

     

                “Lena?”

     

                “Go back to sleep; I’m fine.”

     

                She lay back down and pressed a hand to her chest, feeling the lump of her locket and the hammering of her heart as she closed her eyes. Blankets pulled up to her chin, she waited a moment, tense and anxious, before the lamp switched back off and the orange glow inside her eyelids faded back to black.

     

                The next time she woke it was to pale sunlight streaming in through a slit in the curtains, curled up into a small ball beneath the blankets as the winter chill seeped into the room. Her mother was already up, smoothing out the blankets, and Lena watched her throught slitted eyes before realising Lillian knew she was awake.

     

                “Morning,” Lena muttered, sitting up.

     

                “How long have you been having nightmares?”

     

                Sighing, Lena raked a hand through her hair and then irritably gathered it into a ponytail and tied it up. “We don’t have to talk about it; it’s fine.”

     

                She sat up and pulled warm socks on before climbing to her feet and stooping down to gather up the blanket. Holding the quilt out between her widespread arms, she made a small squawk of protest as Lillian yanked in down to expose her face, giving her a stern look.

     

                “Well, you should.”

     

                “It’s fine. I’ve had bad dreams for years; you know I don’t sleep much.”

     

                “How often?”

     

                Rolling her eyes, Lena sighed and gave her an exasperated look. “A couple times a week. It’s probably just work stress. You know, with all the New Year proposals.”

     

                “You mean Kara stress.”

     

                Scoffing even as her cheeks flushed, Lena folded the quilt in half and then rolled it up, setting it down onto the made bed. “Mom, drop it.”

     

                “Alright, fine. But you really should sleep more.”

     

                “Yeah, yeah, I’ll make it my New Year’s resolution. How about that?”

     

                “Funny, you almost sound convincing.”

    Chapter 50

    To Lena,

     

    Merry Christmas! It seems unfair that I’m not there to celebrate with you in full Danvers style - I bet you’ve never had a Christmas like ours - but I’ll try not to complain too much about it, even though it is my favourite holiday out of them all. There’s something about the holidays that makes me want to come home more than usual, the thought of everyone being together, of all the food and the gifts and the snow. I hope you’ll enjoy it all for me and build the biggest snowman you can. Did you ever make one as a child? I know you’ve never celebrated anything normally but that seems like such a prominent childhood memory for most people. Send me a photo if you make one.

     

    I hope you like your gifts. I had to get Alex to buy them because there’s only so much I can do from the middle of nowhere, but she promised she’d get everything I asked for so I hope you like them. Especially the sweater - that one took me the longest, but it’s a nice distraction to knit while trying to get a signal for the baseball or a call from you. Apologise to your mom for me as well - I bet she’s horrified by hers but I didn’t want her to feel left out. I hope that’s okay.

     

    Speaking of your mom, I’m not sure how - I’m guessing Eliza - but she called me the other night. It was out of the blue and I almost didn’t pick up because I didn’t recognise the number, but I answered and it took me a second to place her voice but when I realised I think I was just in shock that she’d called. I thought maybe something had happened to you again. Maybe she’s already told you this, or maybe it was a secret for her to save face, but she apologised to me. It felt kind of weird for her to do that, because I still proposed anyway and didn’t really factor in her opinion on it even when she told me it wasn’t such a great idea, but I appreciated it. I know you two have a lot going on, but she sounded genuine and said that you’re a lot happier now, even with me not being there. It was a little awkward and she asked me to stay safe - purely for your benefit, I know, but I like that she takes your feelings into consideration now. 

     

    When I’m home we’ll have to spend some time with her so I can get to know her better and she can get to know me more. I think it’s strange that she’s been absorbed into our little family and I’m not there to see it. I kind of feel outside it all but I’m glad she’ll be there for Christmas with you too. I hope it’s a good day, the best Christmas you can ever remember having, and I hope that you rest. I might be over here but I know you and the holidays are a time to relax and have fun and enjoy yourself. Promise me you’ll make the most of it all. I’ll be impatiently waiting to speak to you, to come home to you and to next Christmas when we celebrate it together.

     

    Love you always,

    Kara xxx

    Chapter 51

                New Year’s Eve swiftly followed Christmas and they were back in National City for it, Lena spending all day in the office as she worked through a pile of legal documents in the suffocating stillness of the vast room. No one sent her emails, no one called her phone or poked their head in to inform her of a client that had shown up for a meeting. It was quietly productive and felt like any other day, if not quieter. She went for a walk near lunchtime, buying a green smoothie and a quinoa salad, sitting in a nearby park in her coat as she watched people walk past. 

     

                The wind was cold and the park had wilted with the winter weather, only a few flowers in bloom and a few species of trees holding their leaves. It felt strange to Lena how much time had passed without her really taking stock of it, one minute enjoying a searingly hot summer’s day hiking with the woman she loved and the next sitting alone in a park in mid-winter waiting for her to come home. Her phone rang in her pocket, breaking her from her thoughts. 

     

                “Happy New Year! You’re calling late,” she said as Kara’s face lit up the screen. 

     

                Glancing at the time at the top of the phone, she frowned, realising it was early hours in the morning there. Kara’s soft sigh in response came out crackly through the poor connection, her face mostly in shadow with the darkness of night.

     

                “Just got back to camp. We were out chasing up a story on a local skirmish … well, I can’t go into too much detail. I thought I’d call before bed.”

     

                “You look tired.”

     

                “You mean I look like shit?” Kara laughed, running a hand over her dust-covered face. “I’m looking forward to hot baths again, I’ll tell you that.”

     

                Softly sighing, Lena gave her a small smile. “We’re halfway through it. I wish it was sooner.”

     

                “Maybe I should shoot myself in the foot so I can come home now.”

     

                “Or I could get shot again. Maybe a nice stabbing this time.”

     

                “Nope. No more hospital visits for you. I’ll have to make the sacrifice this time.”

     

                Lena quietly laughed, shaking her head as she gazed lovingly at Kara. “I miss you, you dork.”

     

                “I miss you too,” Kara said, giving her a sad smile. “ And for the record, I would totally shoot myself in the foot for you. Just so you know.”

     

                “I’m very honoured and slightly concerned. And you say I’m the reckless one with crazy ideas,” Lena said. “I’m almost worried about what you get up to over there that’s not part of your job.”

     

                “Please. I’m the one with all the common sense in this relationship,” Kara scoffed.

     

                “You?” Lena spluttered. “I think you mean I am. I’m a certified genius , Kara. I know everything; I do what I want.”

     

                Laughing, her eyes creasing at the corners, Kara wrinkled her nose. “Mm, well, you’ve stolen half of my clothes already by the look of things.”

     

                Plucking at the thin navy sweater beneath her coat, Lena straightened up slightly, giving her a lofty look. “Your clothes happen to be very comfortable.”

     

                “Sorry, for the lack of designers in my closet.”

     

                “The ones I haven’t worn yet still smell like you,” Lena quietly admitted, almost shyly.

     

                “I like seeing you in my clothes,” Kara murmured, an appraising look in her eyes as she gave Lena a once over. “As embarrassing as it sounds, when we first started dating I used to bring you clothes that matched your eyes.”

     

                Lena let out a burst of laughter, startling a nearby pigeon, “you know, I had a sneaking suspicion about that. There were too many green tones for it to be a coincidence.”

     

                “And here I thought I was being sneaky about it,” Kara sighed before her expression softened. “You really do have the most beautiful eyes though. And the rest of you. Call me shallow, but that’s why I picked your table that day.”

     

                “ Please , you’re the least shallow person I know. But I’m glad if you were being shallow just this once,” Lena smiled. “And I hope you don’t mind if I say that I was being extremely shallow too, because I said yes, and we both know I wasn’t the kind of person to say yes to strangers invading my space.”

     

                “Well, I’m glad I was the exception, ” Kara smiled brightly, her eyes crinkling at the corners as she gazed lovingly at Lena. “Can you imagine if you’d said no?”

     

                “No,” Lena said quietly. “No, I can’t.”

     

                “Good, I’d hate to think that I hadn’t made much of an impact on your life,” Kara said, giving Lena a knowing look.

     

                Lena rolled her eyes, giving Kara a wry smile before she looked down, picking at a rusting flake of paint on the bench. “It’s not like you’ve changed my entire life or anything, right?” 

     

                Kara laughed quietly and Lena looked up, slumping slightly on the bench and watched as Kara yawned widely, blinking rapidly and then widening her eyes, a little glazed and bloodshot as exhaustion weighed her down.

     

                “You should sleep.”

     

                “Five more minutes,” Kara bargained with a crooked grin.

     

                “You’re practically falling asleep. Come on, bed time.”

     

                “Fine. I love you.”

     

                Smiling, Lena smoothed a thumb over the phone screen. “I love you too. Sweet dreams.”

     

                Hanging up, Lena sipped the dregs of her green juice and then stood, dropping it into the nearest trash can and making the walk back to the office. She stayed until mid-afternoon before driving home and taking Athena for a quick walk around the block and then showered and stared at the sequined dress hanging from the back of her closet door in a transparent garment bag.

     

                She’d received tickets for the Gatsby themed party of an old college acquaintance who owned a string of nightclubs, bars and casinos in the south-west, and after casually mentioning it to Alex and Kelly they insisted on going. Lena invited Sam and Jess too and they all planned to meet there after seven, giving her plenty of time to get ready. A hired makeup artist and hairstylist that she infrequently used for events showed up and she was silent and patient as they worked, turning her into a flapper right out of the 1920’s. 

     

                Dark hair tightly curled and lips red, Lena slipped into the gold dress and heels, pulled a dark fur coat over it and adjusted the strings of pearls around her neck. Checking her teeth for lipstick in the mirror, she grabbed the feathered headband and her purse and locked the door behind her and climbed into the Uber idling on the curb. Making a stop to pick up Alex and Kelly, they were driven through packed streets until they stopped down the street from the nightclub glowing neon red against the night.

     

                “I can’t believe you got us tickets here. Practically anyone who’s anyone in National City will be at Roulette’s tonight.”

     

                “Mm, I’ll introduce you to its namesake,” Lena contemptuously replied, her mouth thin.

     

                “You don’t like her?”

     

                Shrugging, Lena glanced sideways at Alex, her rouged cheeks reddening further. “We dated for a few weeks when I was fresh out of college. It didn’t end well … obviously.”

     

                Alex let out a loud laugh, nudging Lena, “oh, and does Kara know about this?”

     

                Elbowing her back, Lena rolled her eyes, “yeah, I think she’s pretty aware of the fact that I have a string of failed dates behind me. Child genius with no friends doesn’t exactly make it easy to be around other people.”

     

                “So, spill then.”

     

                Scoffing, Lena made her way to the front door, bypassing the lengthy queue and giving her name at the door. They were admitted immediately, the sound of music almost deafening as they entered the dim hallway and were led through to the spacious room beyond. White strobe lights flashed and the whole place was bathed in red light and they were led to a private booth in the back, a curved velvet seat forming a half-moon around a round table. 

     

                A bottle of Veuve was chilling in ice and they were served glasses in coups, the vintage touch in honour of the Gatsby theme, and Lena sipped the champagne as she glanced around, bubbles making her tongue tingle as she took in suits and fedoras and sparkling dresses, at odds to the EDM music making the room almost shake. The smell of alcohol and perfume was overpowering and the amount of people in there made the cavernous space seem cramped. She could spot at least two NFL players, a handful of socialites and a competitor in the tech industry at a cursory glance.

     

                “Happy New Year,” Lena said, raising her glass and knocking back the champagne before pulling the bottle from the ice bucket and refilling hers.

     

                “You good?” Kelly asked, raising her eyebrows as she smiled slightly.

     

                Shrugging, Lena wrinkled her nose, “it’s a night for it.”

     

                “I swear to God, if you get beat up again …”

     

                She laughed loudly in response, catching sight of Sam and Jess and raising a hand in a wave as she shuffled along the bench. “I’ll try not to.”

     

                Glasses were poured for them too and they all clinked glasses again, the champagne going down easily as they shouted over the music, trying to hold a conversation, heads ducked close together. Lena started running a tab once the bottle emptied, whisky and gin glasses crowding their table as the night wore on and the music got better. Midnight was still a few hours away and she could see the net stretched across the high ceiling of the old warehouse, holding hundreds of silver, gold and black balloons waiting to be dropped along with the ball. 

     

                Lena wasn’t one to dance and she lingered in the booth, sipping a pink gin and fishing out a raspberry as she watched the other four women slip through the crowd. And then she caught sight of someone familiar, a man watching her from near the bar, and almost choked on the berry as she forced it down, quickly looking away and silently praying he didn’t approach.

     

                Of course, Lena always had bad luck and had used what little good luck she did have on meeting Kara, so it was only a minute later when a shadow cut across the red-lit table and she looked up, eyes creasing as she smiled thinly.

     

                “Jack Spheer.”

     

                “Lena Luthor. I haven’t seen you in a while.”

     

                His accent was as charming as ever and she felt herself deflate, climbing to her feet and giving him a quick peck on the cheek as he hugged her gently. “The gala, wasn’t it?”

     

                “Mm, and before that, London..The tech expo. You never answered my calls.”

     

                She winced and sank back down to her seat, “ah, well …”

     

                He took a seat across from her, nursing his own sweating glass as he smiled easily, his brown eyes softening as he hunched forward, elbows on the table. “The gala seemed like an inappropriate place to bring it up, what with the new girlfriend there.”

     

                “Fiancée,” Lena haltingly corrected him.

     

                Jack’s eyebrows rose in surprise as his eyes landed on the diamond, sparkling even in the red light. “Ah, well, congratulations. She’s a lucky girl.”

     

                “Lena?” she looked up and almost swore, finding herself staring up at Veronica Sinclair.

     

                Hair pulled back into a sleek twist, her red dress showing off that sprawling dragon tattoo and her eyes appraising and cool as Lena looked at her, Veronica smiled slowly. “Veronica, hi.”

     

                “Oh, Veronica, hello,” Jack said, climbing to his feet and greeting her.

     

                They’d all gone to college together and Lena had slept with both of them before ghosting them, a thought that made her cringe in hindsight. Remaining seated, Lena sipped her drink and willed the ground to open up and swallow her whole, made worse only a moment later when Andrea Rojas and Russell Rogers materialised at her table, as if it sported a neon sign with her name on it.

     

                There were greetings all around, and Lena found her table growing rather crowded, blocked in on both sides as she stared at the dancefloor and hoped that Alex could sense her desperate need to be rescued. 

     

                “Well, look at this! So many familiar faces in one place,” Andrea smiled. “And where’s your one tonight, Lena?”

     

                “Overseas,” Lena brittly replied.

     

                “That’s right, she’s in the military, isn’t she?”

     

                Veronica arched an eyebrow and gave Lena a sceptical look, snorting with laughter. “You’re dating someone? You’re dating a soldier?”

     

                Flushing at the scorn in her voice, Lena tipped her head back and drained the remainder of her gin. Andrea laughed lightly and Jack hushed them, giving Lena a kind smile. “Lena was just telling me they’re getting married.”

     

                “Married. Fuck me, how far the mighty have fallen. Heiresses, billionaires and businessmen no longer do it for you, Lee, huh?”

     

                Stilling in her seat, Lena forced herself to relax, each muscle unwinding slowly as she smiled and hummed distractedly. “Something like that.”

     

                Looking up, she found Alex approaching, the rest of her friends trailing after her, and Lena jerked her chin towards her. “This is her sister, Alex.”

     

                Introductions were made and seats vacated, but no one left and there was an undercurrent of tension that Lena seemed hyper-aware of as everyone else chatted and drank. Alex ordered a round of tequila, giving Lena a small nod before she knocked hers back. Lena followed suit at a slower pace and let the alcohol warm her stomach as the conversation washed over her.

     

                After a few minutes, she excused herself, climbing to her feet and practically climbing over Alex, Kelly, Sam and Jess and making for the bathroom. It was cooler in there, the tiles emanating a refreshing chill, and Lena splashed cold water on the back of her neck, watching as a news reporter and a local actress snorted cocaine off the back of their hands. She slipped back out after a moment and ordered herself another drink, carrying it back to their booth to find it frustratingly overcrowded with the addition of a new person.

     

                “Oh, Lena, this is William. He’s a reporter for CatCo,” Andrea introduced them.

     

                She shook his hand and gave him a wan smile as Veronica, sipped her cocktail through a straw, a gleam in her eyes as she ran her hand over William’s arm, leaning against the edge of the booth.

     

                “Lena was just telling us about how she’s getting married. Weren’t you, Lena? To a soldier.”

     

                There was a flicker of surprise in William’s dark eyes, a slight straightening to his demeanour that made Lena’s stomach lurch, and she shot Veronica a venomous look. William ignored it, a hungry look to his expression as he leaned in eagerly.

     

                “Really?”

     

                There was the sinking certainty knotting Lena’s stomach that told her her engagement announcement would be front page of the gossip rags tomorrow, and she swallowed as she clutched her drink tightly. Lips twitching, Lena narrowed her eyes slightly at Veronica and then tipped her drink back, cool gin sliding down her throat, before she reached past her and set it firmly down on the table.

     

                “We should go.”

     

                Veronica grabbed her hand in a steel grip, holding her in place as Lena tried to draw back. “Don’t be sour about it, Lee.”

     

                Jerking back roughly, Lena ran a hand over her face, blinking through the slight blurring of her mind from too much alcohol. “Stop it. Now . I know what you’re trying to do.”

     

                “Or what? Are you going to cause a scene? I heard mommy’s around to bail you out now.”

     

                Scoffing, a muscle twitched in Lena’s jaw as she looked away, “have a good night, Ronnie.”

     

                Raising a hand, Veronica snapped her fingers and a hulking bouncer materialised out of the shadows, stopping at Veronica’s side. Meeting Kelly’s eyes, Lena jerked her head and gave her a small smile before turning. Walking down the steps, she was shadowed by the bouncer as her friends followed, and gathered her coat near the front.

     

                As they filed the rest of the way down the dark hallway, Lena's eyes snagged on a fire alarm set into the wall, above an extinguisher. While not a malicious person, Lena could be petty when the occasion rose, and knowing that Veronica was about to have the news run gossip stories about her quiet relationship with Kara was enough for her to reach out and grab the lever, her fingers a little clumsy, before she yanked it down.

     

                Immediately, an alarm started blaring inside, and Lena looked up just in time to see an overhead sprinkler come alive, showering her in a spray of frigid water. Kelly was behind her and roughly pushed her forward, hissing in her ear, “what the fuck are you doing?”

     

                “Well, now no one’s having a good night,” Lena snapped back.

     

                Cursing softly, Kelly pushed her ahead, propelling them out into the street while a stream of customers rushed behind them. They all spilled out onto the sidewalk, the crush of bodies seeming endless, and Lena winced at the rashness of her gesture as she watched bedraggled and damp people flow out towards the end, followed by a pissed off Veronica, livid and soaked as she snapped at a bouncer. The sound of the alarm blared even standing in the street and Lena snorted as amusement curled through her, watching as the road was clogged with drunk customers and the distant sound of a siren neared them.

     

                “We should go,” she said, wiping at her water-speckled face and shivering in the cold air. 

     

                Flagging down the nearest cab, she put Sam and Jess into one and handed over some bills before waiting for the next one. Alex was palpably disgruntled and she grumbled quietly to herself as they waited for the next cab, watching as a fire truck and a police cruiser both turned up at the club, voices clamouring and people swearing, smoking, vomiting and all sorts outside as they waited to be allowed back inside. Lena imagined it was almost akin to a swimming pool inside, countless broken glasses, wet velvet seats and large puddles of water making it inhospitable for the rest of the night. She wondered at how much money she’d cost Veronia and let out a snort of laughter.

     

                Her humour was short lived though, because they’d just managed to flag down a cab for themselves when a cop called out, catching their attention as she walked towards them. Lena let out a derisive snort, rolling her eyes as her lips twisted wryly, catching Veronica’s eye.

     

                “You should’ve just left,” Veronica harshly replied.

     

                Lena laughed. “You’ve got to be kidding me.”

     

                “Ma’am-”

     

                “Officer-”

     

                “We have probable cause to believe you were involved in tonight’s events. Did you know pulling a fire alarm under false pretences is a felony?”

     

                Clenching her teeth, Lena huffed, “look, there’s been some sort of misunderstanding-”

     

                “There are eye witnesses.”

     

                Alex started climbing back out of the cab and Lena shot her a sharp look as the officer’s hand moved towards her belt, towards her handcuffs. “We can discuss this further at the precinct.”

     

                “Precinct?” Alex exclaimed, “you’re arresting her?”

     

                “As I said, it’s a felony in this state.”

     

                “I-”

     

                All earlier amusement vanishing, Lena swallowed and clenched her hands into fists, mortification and idiocy slamming into her as Veronica smugly smiled from where she hung back behind the officer.

     

                “Alex, get back in the cab,” Lena quietly ordered her, “go home - with Kelly.”

     

                “Lena,” Alex quietly protested, a furious look in her eyes even as she stepped back towards the open cab door, knowing Lena was right for telling her to go.

     

                Giving her a rueful smile, Lena let the officer grab her arm and winced as it was twisted behind her back. “Oh, come on , that’s hardly necessary,” Alex commented.

     

                Lena silently willed her to shut up, her eyes flashing a warning, and allowed herself to be towed towards the nearby cruiser, lights flashing red and blue, while Veronica watched on with satisfaction. Nearby, William Dey was standing with Andrea Rojas, watching intently, and Lena knew with gut-wrenching certainty once more that this too would make it to the news tomorrow morning.

     

                Her head was roughly jerked down and she was pushed into the back of the Police cruiser by the other woman and the door was slammed shut behind her. It was another five minutes before the officer and her partner climbed into the front of the car and the engine rumbled to life. Stewing in her anger and misfortune, Lena glowered at the sliver of face she could see in the rearview mirror and let the blurry warmth of alcohol numb her to the ride to their precinct, where she was marched inside and put into a holding cell.

     

                Rubbing her wrists from where they’d been cuffed, Lena pulled her heels off and sat on the bench, two drunk women slumped nearby, another crying as she gripped the bars. It was giving Lena a headache, and she rested her head against the wall and closed her eyes to the harsh fluorescents as she waited.

    Chapter 52

    Dear Kara,

     

    I’m trying to be patient, really, I am, but we’re only halfway through your deployment and I’ve never been good at not getting what I want and my patience is wearing thin. It feels like it was only last week that I last saw you but at the same time it feels like forever, and the thought of another two months sounds like hell and way too long before I get to hold you again. You know, sometimes I forget you’re not actually here, that maybe you’re calling me on your lunch break out on base and you’ll be home soon and we’ll have dinner with Alex and Kelly and you’ll rush in late and claim that empty fourth chair. 

     

    Sometimes I have to pinch myself to convince myself that you’re not just a dream because it feels so strange that you’re not there that I must have made you up. It’s silly to think that after all this time I’m still not used to being away from you when I was so good at being alone before; it’s even worse that it only took me a second to get used to having you around. I think that’s the worst part, that I was okay being alone and then everything went from zero to a hundred so fast that I couldn’t imagine being without you and then I had to be.

     

    I shouldn’t dwell on the bad things though because we’re almost halfway! I don’t think I’ve ever looked forward to something so much in my entire life. When you’re back, I’m going to make sure we celebrate everything that we missed. Christmas, New Year, your birthday, Valentine’s Day. We’ll have a full day celebrating everything together. You’ve turned me into someone who is trying to have a positive outlook on life - look! So many things to look forward to, and I can’t wait to do them all with you.

     

    I just got off the phone with you before sitting down to write this letter, and you asked if I could ever imagine not meeting you and I said no. That’s not the truth though because I can imagine it, or more specifically, I’ve already lived it. Without you I was alone and closed off and it’s strange how one person can change all of that for me. Maybe I always wanted a reason to not be like the way I am, and you were that reason I was waiting for. It’s times like these where I think about the butterfly effect and if there’s any scientific truth behind it, but I guess you were my butterfly. Sorry if that sounds kind of weird, but it’s true. You were the thing that triggered a series of events that altered my entire life.

     

    Sure, you could argue it was my brother. What he did made me CEO, which gave me the option to move HQ out to National City, where I met you, but I think if I hadn't met you, I would have just been alone in a different city. I strongly believe it was you and you alone, and maybe my mom would’ve reached out and I would’ve forgiven her anyway, and maybe I would’ve made an effort to know Sam as more than my CFO, but the truth is that things wouldn’t have worked out the way they have now. I would’ve pushed them away eventually. But you - you were what I needed and what I wanted, and I have never once wanted what we have to end. You’re perfect, Kara. You’re the one part of my life that I’ve never doubted, even when we’ve been through enough things that have made us doubt where things were headed. No matter what, I’m completely sure of us. I just want you to know that.

     

    I love you always.

     

    Lena xx

    Chapter 53

                Midnight came and went from the holdings of the cell, the New Year rolling around with little fanfare in the quiet precinct. A heater shuddered as it blew out warm air, even though Lena’s arms still prickled with goosebumps from the cold, and officers and detectives typed away at reports at clunky computers. A drunken man swore and cursed them out from a different holding cell and Lena felt her eyes grow heavy as she seemed to sink further down on the bench.

     

                No one spoke to her, no one questioned her or gave her a phone call or even a sip of water. She wanted her bed, her pyjamas, her dark room and Kara, growing restless and uncomfortable in the cell as the hours dragged on. Eventually, it got so late that it started verging on morning, dawn just a couple of hours off, and it was as she was yawning, rubbing at her itching eyes when footsteps stopped outside the cell door. 

     

                A key turned in the lock and Lena blinked owlishly at the officer opening it, sitting up as a spark of hope shot through her. The man gestured to her, a sullen look on his face. “Luthor.”

     

                Quickly climbing to her feet, Lena balanced on one leg as she shoved one heel on and then wobbled unsteadily as she got the next one on. Hugging her coat to herself, she followed after the man, and had just stepped out into the open office of desk and overnight shift workers when her stomach jolted at the sight of a tall woman standing near a noticeboard and the door leading to a short hallway out to reception. Lillian.

     

                “Mom-”

     

                “Thank you, Officer,” Lillian cut her off, taking a step forward.

     

                She was quiet with anger, yet it rolled off her in waves and Lena felt small and pathetically childish in her shadow as she walked over to her. The officer spoke to Lillian for a moment and then Lena’s things were returned to her, her cell phone showing a text and two missed calls - one from Alex and another from Kelly - and she shoved it into her pocket as she was allowed to leave with her mother.

     

                Neither of them spoke as they passed the reception area and pushed their way out into the cold pre-dawn morning, and Lena climbed into the front seat of the luxury rental and slammed the door shut behind her, slinking down in her seat as she buckled herself in and watched sideways as her mom similarly did so. The car engine was a quiet purr as it came to life, the radio quickly silenced by the irritable twist of Lillian’s fingers, and Lena swallowed, her mouth dry and the sour taste of tequila at the back of her throat.

     

                “Mom, I-”

     

                Her voice was a low rasp, coloured with guilt and shame. Lillian didn’t even look at her as she softly replied. “Don’t talk.”

     

                Clamping her mouth shut, Lena bit back a sigh and leaned her head back against the headrest, staring out the window as the dark city passed them by, still illuminated with Christmas lights and near-empty at the time of the morning. The drive back to Lena’s brownstone was quick, headlights cutting through the dark as Lillian made turn after turn, silent, yet brimming with pent up anger waiting to be unleashed. 

     

                Bringing the car to a stop behind Lena’s Porsche, Lillian yanked the handbrake up with a little more force than was necessary, unclipping her seatbelt and making a brisk exit from the car. Feeling mildly hungover and more than a little put-out at Veronica getting one over on her, Lena followed after her mother at a slower pace, not particularly eager for the incoming conversation. 

     

                Walking into the open kitchen and dining room, Lena kicked her heels off and draped her coat over the back of a chair, fishing out her phone and staring at Lillian with wariness. Shoulders slightly hunched, she swallowed, her mouth dry as she licked at her chapped lips, red lipstick faded and smudged. 

     

                “Go on then.”

     

                Lillian exhaled sharply, hanging her head as she closed her eyes and pressed two fingers to her forehead as if to massage a headache away. “Just … go to bed.”

     

                The resigned weariness in her voice was worse than her quiet anger and Lena considered a sharp retort with something witty, a catalyst to light the fuse on Lillian’s anger, but decided against it. Still, she hesitated a moment before turning away, brow creasing with confusion and sheepish guilt. 

     

                Plodding upstairs, Lena shed the shimmering dress and fell into bed without changing, her curls half-undone and her bones weary from a long night. She didn’t even close the curtains to the encroaching grey dawn but sleep still sought her out and she sank into it with gratitude, her mind spared the tormenting of turning over her silly mistake for hours.

     

                It was dark when Lena woke again, the short day slept away and the night ushered in without her aware of it. Dragging herself out of bed, she glanced down at her phone and saw it was past six o’clock and she had two missed calls off Kara to add to the list of other notifications. Biting back a curse, Lena tossed her phone onto the rumbled bed and walked into the bathroom.

     

                The shower was hot enough to make her skin sting, steam clouding the spacious shower as she scrubbed herself clean, feeling a little light-headed and clammy when she stepped out and wrapped herself in a towel. Dressing in comfortable loungewear, she brushed her teeth vigorously and wrapped her damp hair in a towel before making her way downstairs.

     

                Lillian was sitting at the kitchen table, typing away at a laptop in the dim light of the kitchen as she sipped a glass of red wine. The remnants of her dinner - takeout from a nearby ramen restaurant - was pushed to one side and Lena’s stomach rumbled at the lingering smell of soy sauce and pork. She didn’t look at her mother as she made a beeline for the fridge, fetching a bottle of coconut water and twisting off the cap, but she could feel Lillian’s eyes tracking her movements.

     

                Tipping her head back as she swallowed, Lena lowered the bottle and walked over to the stretch of counters separating the kitchen from the dining table. Setting the water down, she trailed her fingertip around the mouth of it and looked down, her stomach twisting uncomfortably.

     

                “I know you’re mad-”

     

                “Mad?” Lillian echoed, aghast, her chair roughly scraping across the herringbone floor as she jerked to her feet, her face slack with disbelief. “Mad? Do you know what it’s like to get a phone call in the early hours of the morning, saying you’re in trouble? Do you have any idea what that feels like? Not to mention I had to fly here commercial on New Year’s Day. ”

     

                “I’m sorry, I didn’t think-”

     

                “No, you didn’t. That much is blatantly clear.”

     

                Flushing as she pulled the towel from her hair and ducked her head, toying with the bottle cap as she gritted her teeth, Lena softly exhaled. “You don’t know the full story.”

     

                “Oh, well, please enlighten me as to what could make you do something so stupid that you get arrested on felony charges. You could go to prison, you realise that, don’t you? You’re looking at thousands in property damage - tens of thousands - not to mention the waste of resources your silly little stunt caused.”

     

                “I’m not going to prison,” Lena scoffed, rolling her eyes, “and I’ll pay the damn fees.”

     

                Lillian let out a scoffing laugh, her eyebrows shooting up. “That’s not the point, Lena. You can’t just do whatever you want and then buy your way out of it. Actions need to have consequences.”

     

                “I know that. I made a mistake, okay? I was drunk, they were purposely antagonising me.”

     

                “What could have been so bad-”

     

                “I don’t want my personal life in the news,” Lena hotly replied, gesturing wildly as she frowned, “there was a reporter, and she knew - you don’t know her - either of them.”

     

                “Veronica Sinclair? I know you dated - briefly. And Andrea Rojas; your business partner out of college until she stole the funding from you.”

     

                Paling, Lena’s mouth fell open, the breath snatched from her lungs. Lillian gave her a wry smile, her eyes flashing with grim amusement. “Yes, I knew. I’ve kept tabs on you, looked out for you more times than you know. I just didn’t tell you because … well, if you were in trouble, I wanted you to come to me yourself.”

     

                Stiffening, Lena looked down, tapping a finger on the counter as her heartbeat fluttered in her throat. Her voice was a little hoarse as she replied. “Well, then you know the kind of people they are. Stupid, petty sabotage because of bad blood between us all.”

     

                “And you still shouldn’t have behaved so stupidly,” Lillian sharply continued, her momentary softness dissipating. “You don’t think clearly when you’re hurt. You have too much pride; you let your emotions cloud your judgement and make rash decisions. How are you supposed to be trusted to run a billion-dollar business if you can’t think clearly about trivial things?”

     

                “Well, I’m glad it’s trivial to you,” Lena snapped.

     

                “Grow up, Lena. People are going to try and hurt you but that’s not an excuse for your own actions. You’re the CEO of the biggest tech company in the world; you can’t afford to let it bother you. There are repercussions if you do. As it is, stock prices have dropped since this morning.”

     

                Lena straightened up, rankled by her mother’s words, “and? The market fluctuates.”

     

                Huffing, Lillian gripped her laptop and roughly pulled it around, opening up an article on a gossip site. “It doesn’t fluctuate when word of the CEO getting arrested leaks. It tanks.”

     

                Stomach sinking, Lena slowly rounded the counters, abandoning her water, and moved over to the table, hunching over the screen as she quickly scanned the headline and article, complete with a blurry photo of her in handcuffs. Biting back a curse, she stepped back and ran a hand through her hair.

     

                “It’s fine, it’ll blow over.”

     

                “It will,” Lillian curtly agreed, giving her a regretful look as she paused, “but you’re being stood down in the meantime.”

     

                Lena felt as if the air had been knocked from her lungs, disbelief slapping her across the face as she stilled. “What? You can’t do that - it’s my company.”

     

                “Of which I’m a boardmember and shareholder of. And it’s in everyone’s best interests for you to take a break and let this blow over,” Lillian reasoned, her voice low and stern. “I’m not doing this to spite you, I’m doing this so you understand that there are consequences that money can’t fix.”

     

                Speechless as her eyes stung with tears and wounded betrayal cut through her guilt and embarrassment, Lena swallowed thickly, rooted to the spot. Lillian let out a long sigh and turned the laptop back around, sinking down to her chair and reaching for her glass of wine.

     

                “Two weeks. Take that time to rest and refocus - you work too much as it is. We’ll reevaluate after that.”

     

                Anger suddenly washed over her and Lena clamped her lips together, blinking as she lingered a moment longer and then turned around and walked back upstairs. It was a testament to her self-control that she resisted the urge to slam the bedroom door shut for the small pleasure of annoying her mother as she had as a teenager. Instead, she closed it slowly, taking care to ease it into the frame, before she turned around and loosed a rough breath, digging the palms of her hands into her eyes.

     

                Walking over to the bed, Lena sank down on it and ran a hand over her face before reaching for her phone. Kara would already be at work for the day, which meant Lena would have to wait until the morning to speak to her, already feeling ashamed at having to explain everything to her, and she opened the texts from Alex and Kelly, inquiring whether she was okay. She called Alex and waited for the call to connect.

     

                “Hey.”

     

                “Hey.”

     

                “What’s going on? Are you okay?”

     

                Closing her eyes, Lena pinched the bridge of her nose and shook her head slightly. “It’s- well … I’m home. The rest is …”

     

                “Yeah. What the hell were you thinking?”

     

                “I clearly wasn’t.”

     

                “No shit. What did your mom say? Sorry, I called her, I didn’t know what to do. I figured you had family lawyers for this sort of shit.”

     

                Mouth opening and closing, Lena pulled the phone back and then pressed it back to her ear. “You called my mom?”

     

                “I- yeah, you were in handcuffs.”

     

                “That doesn’t mean you call my mom, Alex.”

     

                “Yeah, it kind of fucking does.”

     

                Anger bloomed anew in her chest and Lena gripped the rumpled bed sheets as she squeezed her eyes shut, gritting her teeth. “You- why would you do that?”

     

                “They arrested you, what else was I supposed to do? I wasn’t going to get you out of prison, was I?”

     

                “Not call my fucking mom.”

     

                Alex scoffed on the other end of the phone. “Look, I know you’re mad, but don’t blame me for you pulling that lever and ruining everyone’s New Year, okay? I was just trying to help.”

     

                “Well, thank you so much for your help. Really.”

     

                Hanging up the phone, Lena tossed it aside and made a low sound of frustration at the back of her throat before she pulled the blankets back over herself and turned her back to the door. She was too keyed up to sleep and her stomach rumbled with hunger, but she didn’t want to go downstairs and didn’t have anyone else to talk to, so she stayed in bed and, eventually, fell back asleep.

     

                Waking early the next morning, she bundled up in gym clothes and laced up her running shoes and went for a three-mile jog with Athena, a haze of fog obscuring the city as she let her lungs burn from the cold. Returning back home covered in a cold sweat, she went downstairs and continued punishing her body as she whaled on the boxing bag for the next hour, until her wrapped knuckles were bruised and stinging from the repeated impact.

     

                Lillian was up by the time she materialised in the kitchen, freshly showered and sullen as she poured herself a cup of coffee and filled a bowl with granola and yoghurt. Setting the bowl down a little heavy-handedly, Lena dropped onto a chair and took a gulp of black coffee, her mother not looking up from the laptop screen as she typed away and sipped ginger tea.

     

                “Good morning. You look well-rested.”

     

                When Lena didn’t reply, Lillian looked at her over the top of the screen and softly sighed. Her fingers tapped at the keys for a moment as Lena spooned her breakfast into her mouth, silent as resentment rolled off her in waves.

     

                “There’s no point being angry at me,” Lillian continued, raising her mug to her lips and then setting it back down. “And if you think you’re smarter than me and can work around this, you should know that security has been told to escort you from the premises if you try to go to the office. And if you’re planning on working from home,” she reached for something on the chair beside her and set Lena’s work laptop down on the table, “this is company property that’s being confiscated.”

     

                Cheeks flaming at being outsmarted - because, yes, she was feeling a little smug as she hatched a work-around for her mother’s orders - Lena let her spoon clang against the edge of her bowl and placed her palms on the table. “And who is replacing me?”

     

                “Samantha Arias. She’s already briefed on everything - it’ll be a smoother transition. I assume you have no issue with that.”

     

                Lena’s shoulders went slack with relief. Sam, she could work with. Sam would keep things sailing on ahead as planned, the company safe in her hands, and Lena nodded before picking her spoon up again. Finishing her breakfast as quickly as possible, Lena was drinking her coffee when Lillian looked at her again, grim wariness in her pale blue eyes as she stopped typing.

     

                “There’s nothing about you or Kara in the news so far,” she hedged. “You might think I’m being harsh, but this will die down. I’ll have my lawyers-”

     

                “I have my own lawyers,” Lena cut her off, climbing to her feet.

     

                “Then call them.”

     

                Nodding, she let out a quiet scoff of laughter and carried her bowl and mug to the sink, dumping them there and stalking upstairs. She pulled her phone out and fiddled with it for a moment before calling Kara. There was no answer and she sighed, tossing it onto the bed and then making it, pulling sheets taut and fluffing the pillows. She was almost done when it started ringing, lunging for it and answering Kara’s call.

     

                “Hey,” Lena breathlessly greeted her, an uneven smile on her mouth.

     

                “Hey,” Kara echoed, disappointment and weariness letting Lena know that she knew . “Happy New Year. Sorry it’s a little late; it’s hard to make calls to people in jail.”

     

                Flushing, Lena spluttered, “I wasn’t in jail. I was- I was just at the precinct.”
