                “What the hell, Lena. Really, what the hell was going through your head. Because I keep thinking about it but you would never pull something that stupid - you’re too smart for that.”

     

                “Please, spare me the lecture,” Lena drawled, pinching the bridge of her nose, “I’ve already had it from my mom, your sister and been grounded from work for two weeks.”

     

                She couldn’t stop herself from sounding sour and petulant, and paused, exhaling roughly as she scrubbed a hand over her face. “Sorry, I just- I’m not in the mood.”

     

                “Neither am I,” Kara snapped, blue eyes blazing, suntanned cheeks turning rosy as she gave Lena a disgruntled look. “I’m all the way out here and my biggest worry is that you’re there doing something stupid . Again!”

     

                Lena had the decency to look chastened, picking at a loose linen thread as her hand holding the phone dropped. She was silent for a moment before peeking at the screen, Kara waiting patiently. Exhaling, Lena rubbed at her forehead and dropped her hand.

     

                “I’m sorry. I didn’t mean to make you worry.”

     

                “I know. I just- God, Lena. What happened?”

     

                Choking on a laugh, Lena gestured vaguely, “you’ve clearly already spoken to Alex.”

     

                “I want to hear it from you.”

     

                Chewing on her lip, Lena was quiet for a long minute. “You know I’ve never been good at relationships. Well, Veronica Sinclair was one of them … she got … mad. I guess she never let it go. Andrea was a good friend of mine too - I told you before that we went into business together, but it didn’t work out. She stole the funding right out from under me and funelled it into her family’s tech company to stop it from going under. Clearly it worked because Obsidian is doing great in VR. But … well, there was a reporter she knew there; I’m sure it was planned. Dropping little bits of information about you. I’ve always been private, always tried to keep my personal life out of the business. I guess they’re still holding onto their grudges.”

     

                “And you too.”

     

                Lips thinning, Lena reluctantly nodded. “I just- I want to protect us from it all. I may not be an A-lister in the typical sense, but people write stories about me and I don’t want you to be one. I like my quiet life.”

     

                “I know, baby, but you can’t control everything. You can’t get yourself in trouble over it.”

     

                With a churlish twist of her lips, Lena sighed and ran a hand through her hair. “It’s too late for that. I have two things in my life that make me happy - you and work - and now I have neither. I guess my mother’s lesson will make its point.”

     

                “Two more months. Give me two more months and I’ll be back, okay? Stay out of trouble until then.”

     

                “I can’t make any promises,” Lena said, a spark of amusement in her eyes as she pressed her fingertips to her lips, knees to her chest as she hunched forward. “But, I’ll try. I’ll do some, ah, self-reflecting over my absence.”

     

                “You’d better self-relfect fast, because I won’t be very happy if I’m coming home to you in a prison cell.”

     

                “Don’t worry, I’ll be waiting impatiently at the airport with a bouquet of flowers.”

    Chapter 54

                Two weeks dragged by without work or Kara, and ordinarily Lena would have been fine with dinner or drinks or brunch with Alex and Kelly to fill that hole of socialising, but she was stubbornly holding onto the wounded betrayal of Alex calling her mom and ignored them both. Lillian left the following day, a brittle warning for her daughter and an exasperatedly amused look in parting before she caught a flight back home, and Lena briefly considered seeing if she could flaunt her mom’s orders but thought better of it as the mortifying image of security bodily removing her from L-Corp came to mind.

     

                Instead, Lena resolved to wait out the two weeks and let them see she had every intention of being serious about her work. Every day, she woke up and completed a workout before briefly speaking to Kara and then spent at least an hour on the phone with Sam, the CFO filling her in on as much information as possible while Lena coached her from her end. They still made a good team, even if Lena had been frozen out of the meetings, and Lena felt a small sense of satisfaction at the slight victory. It was short-lived though, because two weeks was a long time to be removed from her office and the inner-workings of the business.

     

                She had lunch with Sam on Thursday and was glum and unconvincing at trying to bribe her to bring a laptop connected to the L-Corp server to Lena’s house. Sam was sheepish but no pushover and Lena admired her more for that before brushing aside the topic of work and trying to evoke some sense of normalcy from their lunch. 

     

                Boredom started to settle in, holed up in her house with nothing to do. She tried her hand at cooking, scrambled eggs turning rubbery, muffins raw in the middle while starting to blacken on top, tended to her garden and read a dozen books outside in the cold, drinking coffee bundled up beneath a blanket as Athena lolled at her feet. Lena wasn’t used to taking time off work to spend time with herself and it was unsettling to be in the house with no one around and nowhere to go.

     

                Of course, there was nothing stopping her from buying a ticket to Bali and spending two weeks in the sunshine, pool-side with a cocktail in hand, but Lena had never been one for relaxing holidays. She had never been one to relax at all, her mind needing stimulation, needing to be kept busy, and she felt like she was going insane with nothing to do. In the end, Lena fetched a dusty prototype for one of their upcoming nuclear batteries - an older model that they’d quickly upgraded - and disassembled it in the attic offece, piecing it back together and trying to work out any other improvements as she cross-referenced hard copies of current blueprints.

     

                That took up most of a day and she left Sam a long voicemail with her findings before ordering takeout for dinner and watching Pride & Prejudice for the fifth time that week. Her phone rang halfway through the movie and she set down her wine glass and stared at Kelly’s name on the screen before softly sighing and answering it. She wasn’t as pissed off with Kelly but they came as a package deal and Lena had missed her in the days she’d been left alone.

     

                “Hi.”

     

                “Oh. You finally decided to pick up.”

     

                Wincing slightly, Lena slunk down on the sofa, pouting as she reached for the remote and paused the movie. “I’ve been busy.”

     

                “You’re sulking.”

     

                Lena didn’t deign to reply and Kelly softly sighed.

     

                “How’ve you been? You’ve had us worried.”

     

                A stab of guilt cut through her and Lena’s lips twitched ruefully, “I’m alright. You?”

     

                “She feels bad.”

     

                “Yeah, I know. I just- I needed a minute to be dramatic about it all.”

     

                “Can we have dinner tomorrow? I’ll cook.”

     

                Picking at one of the pilled balls of the knit blanket, Lena hesitated and then swallowed thickly as a swell of loneliness washed over her and her eyes prickled. “Sure.”

     

                “Good,” Kelly said with relief, “okay. Well, you probably have a lot going on …”

     

                “I don’t,” Lena admitted. “I … it’s awful.”

     

                Kelly let out a breathless laugh, “get some fancy wine out; I’ll come and pick you up in five.”

     

                A part of her wanted to argue, but she swallowed and nodded to herself, agreeing with Kelly’s orders before she hung up. Slipping on a pair of boots, Lena filled a tote bag with a few bottles of wine for variety and refilled Athena’s food bowl before she waited on the stoop and watched Kelly’s Volvo pull up. 

     

                Slipping into the passenger seat, Lena buckled herself in and exhaled sharply, turning to look at her. “Jesus,” Kelly said, putting the car into drive, “when was the last time you slept?”

     

                “Last night,” Lena replied, nettled.

     

                “You might consider more.”

     

                Humming dismissively, Lena reached for the dial and turned the radio up, a pop song filling the car as she sank into the seat, staring out the window at the streetlights and headlights. Kelly was content to pass the drive in silence and pulled up outside her apartment building twenty minutes later, killing the engine and climbing out. Grabbing her bag of wine, Lena followed suit and stepped into the bright lobby before riding the elevator up.

     

                Kelly unlocked the door and Lena followed her inside, the wall of warmth hitting her as she took in the homely glow of the place. It was comfortable and messy in a lived-in way, Alex’s boots by the sofa, Kelly’s psychology books spread across the coffee table. It struck a pang of longing in Lena and she let out a breath, shoulders sloping as she blinked slowly.

     

                Setting her bag of wine down on the kitchen counters, Lena started removing her coat as Alex materialised from down the hallway. She slowed at the sight of Lena, and Lena gave her a rueful smile, folding her coat and setting it on the bar stool before folding her arms over her chest.

     

                “I’m sorry,” she said, firm and precise.

     

                Alex let out a quick laugh and crossed over to her, wrapping Lena in a tight hug and rocking them from side to side for a moment. “I didn’t mean to get you in trouble; I was worried about you.”

     

                Breathlessly laughing as she raked a hand through her hair, Lena arched an eyebrow, “you can see why that usually doesn’t end well for me.”

     

                Giving her a droll look, Alex squeezed her arm and fetched clean wine glasses. Lena didn’t mention she’d already had a glass and a half and readily accepted the Riesling Alex handed off to her before moving over to the sofa.

     

                “What did your lawyers say?” Kelly asked, moving a pile of folded laundry off the sofa.

     

                Sighing, Lena rolled her eyes. “We’re going to settle outside of court. No charges, but I’ll pay for damages and lost revenue. Also the local Fire Department will be having a generously donated refurbished lounge at their station under the guise of a bribe to not charge me for wasting their time.”

     

                “Well … that’s good.”

     

                “Yep. I also have to apologise to Veronica; I’d almost rather do the jail time.”

     

                Wrinkling her nose, Alex set her glass down and handed one off to Kelly. “When are you back at work?”

     

                Snorting, Lena smiled thinly, “been digging up gossip from your sister?”

     

                “She’s been very evasive.”

     

                “I don’t know. My mom said two weeks, so I hope on Monday, but I haven’t spoken to her.”

     

                “Burning all your bridges again?” Alex asked, raising her eyebrows as she smiled knowingly.

     

                Lena flipped her off and took a sip of wine and they fell back into their usual rhythm of banter. The knot in Lena’s chest slowly unwound as the night progressed, that lonely hole filling itself back in as she relaxed, a rosy flush to her cheeks and a brightness to her eyes as her laughs came easier and she caught up on what her sulking had missed out on. There was also a gentle undercurrent of gratitude at how easily her snub was forgiven, how easily she was pulled back into their circle, exactly like she was family.

     

                They stayed up too late, considering Alex and Kelly both had work the next morning, and Lena ended up sleeping in their guest room, the warm flush of wine and her body’s exhaustion making for a relatively peaceful sleep. She woke once in the early hours of the morning, a cold sweat prickling her skin as she shook off a nightmare and shivered in the chill of the room, and finally rose with the sound of the coffee machine grinding in the kitchen.

     

                Sipping a cup as it chased away her tiredness, she watched the two women rush back and forth, getting ready for work, while Lena sat on the sofa with nowhere to be. Alex left first, kissing Kelly goodbye and telling Lena to be back by six for dinner before she went out the door, and Lena tidied up as Kelly hurriedly ironed a clean shirt and kept up a running torrent of curses as she glanced at the clock.

     

                “Are you ready? I’ll drop you off on the way,” she said, throwing Lena a quick glance as she tucked her shirt in and reached for her running shoes.

     

                “I’ll catch a cab if you’re running late.”

     

                “No, no, there’s something I want to talk to you about. Just get your things. Quick.”

     

                Lena finished putting a plate in the dishwasher and obediently grabbed her coat and slipped her shoes on. She was at the door when Kelly rushed towards her, shooing her out and locking up behind them, and Lena looked at her with amusement as she took in her friend’s unusually harried look.

     

                In the car, Kelly threw them into drive and pulled into traffic, jerking her chin towards Lena. “Open the glovebox.”

     

                Obeying, Lena jerked the door down and fished out a small black box. Holding it in her palm, she turned to Kelly without opening it, already knowing what would be inside, eyebrows rising as a grin spread across her face.

     

                “Seriously.”

     

                “Mhm. I don’t know when but I saw it the other day and knew it was the perfect ring so I impulsively bought it, and now it’s just sitting in my car because she’d probably find it snooping around, and now I’m anxious that my car’s going to get broken into and someone’s going to steal it, so I need you to take it and hide it.”

     

                “Okay. Can I see it?”

     

                Kelly nodded quickly, an almost alarmed look on her face as she glanced over at Lena, watching her open the ring box and study the diamond ring inside. “It’s beautiful. She’ll love it.”

     

                Seeming to deflate at Lena’s reassurance, Kelly eagerly nodded in agreement. “Now, I just need to find the right time. But this whole … thing is stressing me out. I mean, this is the second time I’m going to be engaged, and, well, you know how it went last time … and I just- I want it to be perfect because, I mean, unless I’m the unluckiest person in the world-”

     

                “She’s going to say yes,” Lena interrupted, resting a hand on Kelly’s arm. 

     

                “Right. Of course she will. It’ll be fine.”

     

                “Exactly.”

     

                Kelly seemed to relax as Lena offered suggestions - even so far as to offer up her private jet so they could slip away to some tropical paradise for an over-the-top proposal - and by the time they pulled up outside the brownstone, she seemed visibly more composed. Clutching her hand tightly around the box, Lena gave her a pleased smile.

     

                “I’ll keep it safe until the right moment.”

     

                “You’re the best,” Kelly said, grabbing her face in her hands and jerking Lena’s head forward so she could kiss her forehead. “Now, I need to go or I’m going to miss my first client.”

     

                “I’ll see you later.”

     

                “Mhm.”

     

                Climbing out, Lena went inside and made it a priority to hide the ring inside the small safe in her closet, right beside copies of NDA’s and other confidential documents, a registered pistol and some of her more expensive pieces of jewelry. Locking it shut, she dusted off her hands and felt a glow of happiness in her chest for her friends, before making her way upstairs to her office and sitting down behind her computer.

     

                Calling Kara, she waited patiently for it to connect, wondering if perhaps she was still eating dinner or enjoying a round of cards with her friends, and if that’s why she hadn’t called yet. It took a long minute for her to answer but Lena quickly figured out a reason for the delay as her mouth fell open at the sight of Kara’s bruised face.

     

                “What the fuck .”

     

                “Okay, so I know it looks bad,” Kara said with a strained laugh, thumbing the split lip as she wrinkled her nose, wincing with pain.

     

                Both eyes were black with bruises behind her glasses, giving her a rather similar appearance to a raccoon, and Lena couldn’t even speak as she sat there with her mouth hanging open. A small sound of surprise managed to vocalise itself at the back of her throat and Lena shook her head.

     

                “What the hell happened?” Lena gasped, touching her fingers to the screen. “Are you okay?”

     

                “I got punched. Clearly.”

     

                “No shit,” Lena spluttered, “how?”

     

                “Two guys got into a fight so I tried to break it up and kind of got in the middle. My nose isn’t broken though so that’s good.”

     

                Lena burst out laughing at her optimism, staring at Kara with unabashed shock as she struggled to comprehend her blithe attitude. “Good? That’s your idea of good?”

     

                “It could’ve been worse; my nose could’ve been broken. Then I would’ve been upset; I don’t think a crooked nose would suit me.”

     

                Scoffing, Lena shook her head, “and will they be punished for it?”

     

                Kara eagerly nodded, “oh, sure. Maybe a demotion as well as some hard labour around camp.”

     

                “If I could get my hands on them …”

     

                “It’s just some black eyes,” Kara rolled her eyes.

     

                “They hurt you,” Lena argued, her expression darkening with displeasure. 

     

                “Now, imagine if that was a bullet wound …”

     

                “Very funny,” Lena said, letting out a quiet huff before giving her an agonised look. 

     

                She wanted to cup Kara’s face in her hands, smooth her thumbs over her bruises and kiss them better, but she was too far away and it filled Lena with an all too familiar frustration to be stuck so far away, helpless. Running a hand over her face, she grimaced.

     

                “I just- I hate to see you like this,” she confessed, her throat closing up.

     

                “You better not start tearing up on me,” Kara softly laughed, trying to lighten the mood.

     

                “Me? Crying? Not likely,” Lena hoarsely replied, giving her a wry smile. “You’re okay though, right?”

     

                “Yeah, I’m fine. Not the first time I’ve been roughed up a bit. Now, tell me about your day.”

     

                Giving her a slow, grudging smile, Lena cocked her head to the side, eyes narrowing with faint amusement. “I think I’d rather hear about yours - it sounds awfully exciting.”

     

                She stayed on the phone with Kara for most of the evening, talking right up until it was time for Kara to go to bed, saying hi to her friends that popped in and telling her about her night and how she was going to Alex’s for dinner that night. It lessened the loneliness in Lena’s chest, but she couldn’t help but wish they were talking about their days on opposite sides of the dinner table or as they washed the dishes while listening to old records. So much of the early days of their relationship felt missing from what they had now, and it seemed wrong to think that they were closer now, more comfortable and confident, and now thousands of miles separated them. 

     

                When Lena had to say goodnight at ten o’clock in the morning, it only drove that reality home harder, and she was left sitting behind her desk for a while afterwards, lost in her own thoughts as she absentmindedly bit her thumbnail. The sound of her phone vibrating on the desk roused her a while later and Lena looked down to see her mother’s name on the screen. Part of her was tempted to decline it, but it seemed to be a day for phone calls and she let out a withering sight before picking it up, thumb hovering over the screen before she answered it and pressed it to her ear.

     

                “Hello.”

     

                “Hi, am I interrupting something.”

     

                “Mm, yes, because I’m so busy,” Lena drily retorted. “I’m busy dusting off my bookshelves and reorganising my vinyl collection - you know, top priorities for a CEO.”

     

                Lillian’s reply was laced with amusement, “I see you haven’t lost your attitude since we last spoke. Although, I think I should be grateful you even answered. I thought you’d still be ignoring me.”

     

                “I was tempted.”

     

                Her mother laughed affectionately, “of course you were. It would’ve been more surprising if you weren’t.”

     

                Lena didn’t reply, pursing her lips as she idly tapped a finger on her desk. Lillian sighed after a moment, turning serious. “I’d like to talk to you.”

     

                “We’re talking now.”

     

                “In person,” Lillian stressed, exasperatedly. “How would you like to come and visit? You did say that’s what the chess set was for.”

     

                “When?”

     

                “This weekend.”

     

                “Will I be at work on Monday?”

     

                “If you come and visit, we’ll talk about it then.”

     

                Brooding in silence for a moment as she considered it, Lena opened her mouth to speak when Lillian cut her off. “You can invite Alex and Kelly, too. I’m sure they’d be interested in seeing where you grew up. Or getting away for the weekend, at the very least.”

     

                “I- fine. I’ll ask them.”

     

                “See if Eliza would like to come too; it’ll be nice to repay her kindness and host her here.”

     

                “Fine.”

     

                “I’ll see you Friday.”

    Chapter 55

                Friday evening Lena found herself restlessly pacing the length of the private jet as she cracked her knuckles and waited in anticipation of the landing. She wasn’t sure why she was so nervous to take her new family to the sprawling mansion she’d grown up in, only that it was a different world to the life Lena had cultivated for herself in National City. A modest brownstone in a wealthier area and an expensive sports car weren’t exactly out of reach for doctors or lawyers, and while they knew Lena was a CEO of a tech giant, seeing the extravagant display of wealth on the Luthor estate was another thing entirely.

     

                Not to mention that her mother would be there and Lena was still trying to work out how to feel comfortable in the place she’d been made to feel the exact opposite for the vast majority of her life. Even Alex’s offer of Diazepam wasn’t enticing as Lena left the other three women to relax after a day of work - Eliza sleeping off a sixteen hour shift on a made up bed in the corner - and tried to guess at what her mother would say. Surely she wasn’t going to keep Lena away from the company she’d worked hard to rebuild and rebrand over the past three years.

     

                She didn’t keep still until it was time for them to descend into Metropolis, snow providing low visibility and the anticipation of the frigid January weather an altogether disgruntling prospect as Lena buckled herself in and eyed the thick winter coat dispassionately. It was a stomach-lurching moment of unease for her and her fear of flying as the wheels touched down and she feared the tires wouldn’t have enough traction to stop, before they eventually came to a gentle standstill on the private airstrip. 

     

                A car had been arranged to meet them there and Lena dragged on her warm coat and descended the steps before making her way into the back of the car. The heater smoothly blew out warm air and she watched snow fall beyond the window, the darkness of midnight giving the illuminated airstrip a ghostly grey quality to it. Their luggage was quickly loaded and Lena hesitated as the driver pulled away, glancing at Alex with a certain shyness to her wary look.

     

                “Hey, um, the house is a lot to take in, so can you just … I don’t know. Don’t comment on it.”

     

                Giving her a bewildered look, Alex laughed, “what do you mean?”

     

                “I mean what I said. Just don’t be a dick about it.”

     

                Snorting, Alex rolled her eyes, “you’re so cranky. I think you need to sleep more.”

     

                “I don’t need to sleep more,” Lena tightly replied, tense and brimming with nervous energy as she stared out the window, watching the freeway fly past. 

     

                They weren’t heading into the city, they were heading away from it, a few miles out in the acres of land that was removed from the suburbs and any semblance of normal life, and it made Lena more tense as the anticipation of coming home grew with each mile. It was late so no one said much as they drove, the movements of the car lulling them all into a stupor, and Lena picked at invisible lint on her coat as she shifted restlessly, eager for it to be over.

     

                Eventually, the car pulled up outside the gates and they were buzzed through, starting the long drive up to the house. The trees that overarched the long driveway were bare of leaves this early on in the year, and the headlights illuminated skeletal branches as Lena’s agitation grew. It was one thing to come here alone, but it was another thing to introduce her new family to her childhood, a sort of meshing of two worlds that Lena wasn’t sure would mix well - like oil and water. She’d been intent on keeping it separate to her normal life in National City that they’d only had a glimpse into the sort of upbringing she’d had via stories and snippets here and there. Boarding school and money were about all they’d needed to know, all Lena had willing divulged.

     

                There was a palpable tension to the quietness of the car as gravel crunched beneath the tires and they made their way towards the house, before headlights eventually highlighted a narrow portion of the huge, sprawling house. Squinting, Alex leaned through the partitioned area, trying to see it clearly, and let out a low, appreciative whistle before she turned to look at Lena.

     

                “I mean … Kara said , but …”

     

                “You’re like … rich rich,” Kelly said with quiet awe, looking mildly alarmed by the revelation. “You should consider a prenup.”

     

                Out of all the things to say, that was the most unexpected and elicited a choked laugh from Lena. It was another minute before they pulled up outside and the engine was cut, the driver climbing out to open Lena’s door. Athena burst out ahead of her, bounding straight for a patch of snow off to the side, the driveway and steps immaculately cleared of all but the latest glazing of snow. Lena followed the dog out, thanking the driver and then making for the wide steps leading up to the door.

     

                A large rectangle of light spilled out of the open door and Lena quickened her pace, hands buried in her pockets and a wry sense of amusement at how she’d never been so excited to get inside that infernal house. Lillian was waiting on the threshold, rubbing her arms as she waited with an impatient edge to her expression. Lena wanted to laugh and watched her mother straighten up, a slight softened to her sharp face as Lena stepped into the square of light spilling onto the stone.

     

                “Hi, mom,” Lena murmured, stopping in her tracks as Lillian gently grabbed her chin and tilted her head from side to side while observing.

     

                Humming disapprovingly, Lillian’s mouth thinned before she pulled Lena into a brief hug. Lena was a moment slow in returning it before stilling in Lillian’s arms as her mother sighed in her hair,  “you haven’t been sleeping.”

     

                “I’m fine. It’s just been a long day.”

     

                Giving her an unconvinced look, Lillian shooed her inside and greeted everyone else in turn while the driver brought their bags. Shedding her coat, Lena hung it on the stand inside the door and looked around the foyer as she kicked off her shoes and shivered in the chill of the cavernous space. The house never seemed to be warm everywhere at the same time, too big for the vents to warm the bigger rooms, and Lena quickly made her way towards a small kitchenette off a sitting room, small enough to be stiflingly hot as she shivered and set water on to boil.

     

                It was smaller than the open kitchen overlooking the gardens, a row of counters and cupboards with a stocked liquor cabinet, a coffee machine and a kettle for easy access from the adjoining living room. Lena grabbed mugs from the cupboards and fished out a few teabags, opening the door to the living room and shooing everyone into it as they filed into the small kitchen and soon found it cramped. The room beyond was far more spacious that the renovated servants parlour and Lena carried cups through to everyone as they sat on leather sofas or wingback armchairs, looking around at old oil paintings, gilt mirrors and antique furniture with open interest.

     

                “How was the flight?”

     

                “We had a bit of turbulence,” Lena said, taking a seat beside Kelly and leaning on the arm as she cradled her mug.

     

                “This is a beautiful house, Lillian. How long has it been in the family?”

     

                “Lionel’s great-great-grandfather bought it. He was an oil tycoon - a big shareholder in the Standard Oil Company - before Lionel’s father sold it all off and started Luthor Corp.”

     

                Sipping her tea, Lena stayed quiet as she listened to the conversation, her thoughts on how the men had run the family conglomerate, a tedious topic she’d argued with Lillian through most of her late teen years. Lena had prevailed against her mother’s doubts when rebranding it though, but now didn’t seem like a good moment to smugly bring it up and rub it in, so Lena drank her tea and waited for bed. It was already past midnight; it wouldn’t be much longer.

     

                Eventually, tea finished and exhaustion taking over from their flights, despite the time difference, they fetched their bags from the foyer and Lillian informed Lena which rooms had been made up for them. She walked upstairs, shoulders tense and eyes itching with tiredness, and showed Eliza to her room first, wishing her goodnight before she took Alex and Kelly down the hallway and into another bedroom. They were too tired for a proper tour and Lena said goodnight before making her way up to her room.

     

                Depositing her overnight bag at the foot of her bed, she changed into pyjamas and sank onto the mattress, running her hands over her face before realising she wouldn’t be able to sleep. Still, she gave it her best effort, amassing all of an hour altogether as she tossed and turned in the too-big bed, the canopy overhead feeling suffocating and eliciting more bad dreams than usual as Lena’s subconscious spiralled further into her fears, past her worry for Kara and right down to her childhood.

     

                She woke just past four and finally gave up, pulling on a fluffy robe and slippers before padding downstairs and making tea in the light of her torch, reluctant to turn the lights on as she dwelled in her thoughts. Sitting at the kitchen table, she sipped her tea and answered emails on her phone, coldness seeping in through the glass doors at her back as a light snow dusted the acres of land surrounding the monolithic house.

     

                Lillian found her there an hour later, startling slightly at the sight of her daughter sitting there, unaware of her presence, absorbed entirely by something on her phone as she curled up on the seat. Lena didn’t register her appearance until Lillian stopped at the table and dragged a chair out, frightening her so badly that Lena dropped her phone and uncurled her legs, slippered feet touching the cold stone floor as she braced herself to leap to her feet. Heart hammering in her chest, Lena exhaled and ran a hand through her hair.

     

                “Oh. Good morning.”

     

                “You’re up early.”

     

                “Not really.”

     

                “It’s three in the morning in National City.”

     

                Lena rolled her eyes and then did climb to her feet, snagging her cup off the table and walking over to the stretch of counters. “Then I’m up late. Coffee.”

     

                “You’re so stubborn . A splash of cream please.”

     

                “You’re the one that instilled it in me.”

     

                Lillian didn’t reply and Lena glanced over at her to find her staring blankly off in space, running a thumb over her lips as she contemplated something. Shaking her head, Lena set a second cup between the steel monstrosity and watched as fresh espresso poured through the filters and then added another shot to hers while adding cream to her mom’s. Carrying them over to the table, Lena took a sip and closed her eyes, exhaling softly. 

     

                “So … L-Corp,” Lena ventured.

     

                Giving her a reproving look, Lillian narrowed her eyes slightly and cupped her coffee mug between her palms. “All in good time.”

     

                “I’m not going to get on my jet and leave the moment you say I’ve been reinstated.”

     

                “Knowing you, you would.”

     

                With a rakish smile, Lena sipped her coffee. “Are you working today?”

     

                “No, Lena. Some of us don’t work weekends - or most of the week, for that matter. What’s the point in being in charge if you don’t allow yourself to enjoy your free time?”

     

                “To create new things? Change the world?”

     

                “You have an idealised view of things. Has the past two weeks truly been that awful?”

     

                Lena almost choked on her splutter, “yes! I’ve been bored stiff.”

     

                Mouth thinning, Lillian set her cup down. “That’s disappointing.”

     

                “Mom, my fiancée is half a world away; what did you think I was going to do if I wasn’t working? Fly to Afghanistan to spend two weeks with her?”

     

                “I thought it might give you more perspective.”

     

                “It did; I won’t do anything to be stood down again. Point proven.”

     

                “That was only partially the point.”

     

                With a strained smile, Lena raised her eyebrows a fraction, “I’m fine , mom. Look, I’ll take more time off. Work regular hours and all of that. Especially when Kara’s back.”

     

                Wrinkling her nose slightly, Lillian hummed dubiously, “I wish you wouldn’t let a girl be the source of you having a life.”

     

                Rolling her eyes, Lena let out a scoffing laugh. “She’s not just a girl.”

     

                “I know, I know, but you should be able to enjoy your life on your own merit. You shouldn’t be waiting for her to come home so you can go out and do things-”

     

                “I do plenty. I’m always with Alex and Kelly. It’s nice. I enjoy my life now - I really, really do.”

     

                “Alright. Well … we’ll talk properly later.”

     

                Biting back an impatient sigh, Lena nodded and swallowed the rest of her coffee before fetching another cup for herself under Lillian’s disapproving gaze. She felt dry-eyed and a little jittery, too strung out on caffeine and not enough sleep as she dragged herself through the days, and Lena stifled a yawn as she reclaimed her seat and picked up her phone again. It was too early to talk to Kara yet and she ended up picking up her coffee and softly whistling to wake Athena from the basket placed near the hallway entrance.

     

                Giving her mom a quick smile, Lena opened the back door and stepped outside, the sharpness of the cold taking her breath away as she stood on the patio and watched Athena trot out into the cold. Taking a seat on an iron lattice work chair, the metal so cold it seemed to brand the back of Lena’s thighs through the robe and pants, she sipped her coffee and watched her dog leave a trail of pawprints in the fresh snow, exhaling a cloud of white as she  cupped her coffee between cold fingers. Her nose and cheeks turned numb and red as she watched the dawn eventually creep in, the dark sky streaked with deep indigo before lightening to grey.

     

                When it became unbearable, she walked back inside and roused Alex and Kelly shortly afterwards, banging on their closed bedroom door as she offered them a tour. They were grouchy and slow but once she made them coffee downstairs they perked up a little as she took them into the foyer. 

     

                “This is the foyer,” she proclaimed. “You were just in the kitchen. That closed door has a living room; that closed door has another living room-”

     

                “This isn’t a tour. Come on, we’re not going to snoop; show us around.”

     

                Rolling her eyes, Lena walked over to the nearest door and opened it, gesturing around the opulently decorated space, dark woods and shades of deep emerald and crimson and cream giving it an elegantly and wealthily dated ambience as they breathed in furniture polish, leather and just a hint of dust that seemed embedded in the gleamingly clean room.

     

                The sheer size of the house meant it took a while to make it through the downstairs rooms - parlour rooms, sunrooms, a room devoted to the untouched grand piano, another with billiards and more yet still for libraries and offices and mudrooms and closets. She could see the awe written on Alex and Kelly’s faces with each new door that yielded some old world snippet of the generational wealth funneled into the home, the antique vases and heavy drapes, the Persian rugs and marble statues.

     

                What was worse was the dawning realisation that almost each and every room on the ground floor housed photos. When she’d last visited, there had been empty patches on the walls, empty photo frames on end tables and consoles and mantle pieces where family photos and ones of her and Lex had been removed in turn. Only, now they’d been refilled. There were so many of Lena that she was alarmed to see half of them, wondering where Lillian had kept them all this time. Did she have a box of old photos that she’d never let see the light of day? Were there albums Lena had never been made privy to? It made her throat close up, especially when she saw a couple in the foyer, on display for any guests to see, of them recently. And Lena knew some of them could only have come from Kara; one of the three of them at the L-Corp gala, another of Lena sitting beside her at her birthday, one of Lena and Lillian sitting in close proximity - not even together but close enough for it to warrant being developed and framed in her mother’s home.

     

                Walking upstairs, Lena started showing them the next floor, trailing behind as she let them open doors and explore, poking their heads inside while Lena informed them what was inside. It wasn’t until Alex reached for the door handle of an all-too-familiar room that Lena’s stomach jolted and she opened her mouth to protest. It was too late to stop Alex from easing the door open on creaking hinges though and Lena found herself standing in the doorway, mouth dry, staring at a empty room as Alex and Kelly ventured inside.

     

                She let out a soft exclamation of surprise, staring at the place where the bed had stood, the mess of papers and abandoned shoes and books and carafes of liquor, the nightstands and his favourite armchair, as disorderly as it had been last time she’d visited, only to find it all gone. It looked like her mother had taken her advice to heart and finally emptied the room of his personal items, along with everything else. 

     

                “What’s this room?” Alex asked, looking over her shoulder and raising her eyebrows expectedly.

     

                “This … was my brother’s room,” Lena replied, somewhat hoarsely as she struggled to stamp down the mixture of emotions within her. “I guess my mom finally cleared it out.”

     

                Kelly blanched, looking apologetic as she quickly moved back over to the door, “sorry, we didn’t mean to-”

     

                “It’s fine. There’s nothing in here now, anyway.”

     

                She shut the door behind them and continued the tour, this time in the lead, before making her way up to her room last. It could’ve been just like any of the other unused bedrooms, save for Lena’s bag and her rumpled bed sheets, and Alex hovered in the doorway, uneasy.

     

                “This is your room?”

     

                “It was.”

     

                “It’s a bit … bare.”

     

                “Yeah, I cleared it out when I left; my mom put the rest in storage,” Lena said, staring at the empty bookshelves as she crossed her arms and leaned against one of the posters holding up the canopy of the bed. “Anyway … that’s the house.”

     

                “It’s … a lot.”

     

                “Yeah.”

     

                “It’s kind of creepy,” Kelly admitted with a short laugh.

     

                Lena snorted, arching an eyebrow, “try growing up here. Shockingly, it always felt too small for all the bad shit that went on here. Never enough places to hide. I was glad to leave for college a few years ahead of schedule; it got me out of this place.”

     

                “Do you ever miss it?” Kelly softly asked.

     

                Grimacing, Lena shrugged nonchalantly, patting the wooden post, “maybe in some way, but … things are better now. A lot better, and that’s the only reason I can stomach coming back here. There was … a lot that went on. I don’t talk about it much.”

     

                “We know,” Alex murmured, “but thanks for bringing us.”

     

                Waving a hand dismissively, Lena gave them an easy smile and pushed off the bed, moving towards the door. “Honestly, I think my mom likes having people in it again. It’s too big for one person all alone in here. If she didn’t know how much I hate it here, I’m sure she’d try and convince me to move back in with her.”

     

                “For everyone’s sake, it’s probably for the best that you don’t,” Alex laughed, clapping a hand on Lena’s shoulder and then following after her.

     

                Back downstairs, they found Eliza drinking coffee with Lillian while the chef set about making breakfast for them all. It wasn’t long before Lena was digging into an omlette with chives and mushrooms in it, sipping freshly squeezed orange juice and trying to mask her tiredness as she clamped her jaw shut and refused to let the yawns make themselves known.

     

                After they finished eating, Lillian took Eliza to her office to go and read over some medical proposal for new Cadmus technology that Lillian had been explaining to her at breakfast, and Alex excused herself to go and shower first, slipping upstairs while Lena was left alone with Kelly. Looping her arm through Lena’s as they walked towards Lena’s favourite sitting room - the small one nestled behind an old servant’s stairwell with green lamp shades that cast an emerald quality over the space - Kelly gave her a nervously excited grin, eyebrows rising.

     

                “So, you brought it?”

     

                “It’s in my bag upstairs,” Lena nodded, squeezing her arm encouragingly. “Any idea on how?”

     

                “I was thinking I’d just take her out for dinner tonight and do it then.”

     

                “In a crowded restaurant? That won’t do; do you want me to arrange for somewhere to close for you?”

     

                Kelly scoffed, rolling her eyes and opened the door, “no, she’d know immediately.”

     

                “What about my boat? I’ll come too and stay below deck. I’ll even poach my mom’s chef for you.”

     

                “I- that sounds nice, but-”

     

                “But what?” Lena asked, lugging a log from the basket near the empty grate and kneeling before it as she began the arduous task of trying to set it alight, which wasn’t nearly as easy as it seemed. 

     

                Sighing as she sat down, Kelly propped her elbows on her thighs and leaned forward, cup cradled between her palms. “But I couldn’t let you do something like that. I mean, that’s … a lot. That’s something I could never even consider doing-”

     

                “Well, you can let me do it, and, even better, you can consider it kindness repaid for putting up with me while Kara’s gone. I know I’ve been … prickly and stubborn. Probably a pain in the ass for most of it, but what I lack in personality I make up for in money, so … let me do this for you both. It’s what family does.”

     

                “Oh, the family card, huh?” Kelly laughed.

     

                Lena joined in as she watched the small fire start to spread and then climbed to her feet, flopping down onto a sagging velvet loveseat and switching on the emerald lamp, smiling softly at the comforting glow. 

     

                “If I have to use it, I will. It’s my manipulative businesswoman side; it works quite well, actually.”

     

                “It’s tempting,” Kelly hedged.

     

                Rolling her eyes, Lena waved her phone in a goading manner as a smile split her face. “One phone call. I’ll have it arranged in no time.”

     

                After five more minutes of debating, Kelly allowed Lena to make the call, looking a little nervous and ashy as the reality of her proposal started to settle in, and Lena found herself perking up at the chance to plan something. She’d been feeling like a spare part with nothing to do, but making sure Kelly’s secret proposal went off without a hitch was something for her to do, and something she did with eagerness. Even in mid-winter, it would be perfect.

     

                Neither of them mentioned it until lunchtime, all five of them eating fresh salads and sandwiches and little petit fours as if they were at a high tea, when Lena casually brought it up as she poured kombucha from the bottle into a glass.

     

                “So, I thought that maybe we could go out on my boat tonight,” she casually suggested, raising her eyebrows at Alex.

     

                “Lena, it’s been snowing,” Lillian tutted.

     

                “And? It’ll be fun; I’ll just go with Alex and Kelly. They should do something fun while they’re here, right? We’ll just anchor it in the bay and have dinner. Can I borrow your chef?”

     

                Mouth thinning, Lillian exhaled softly and waved a hand dismissively, “fine, if you want to freeze out on the water, so be it. Make sure you wear a coat.”

     

                Rolling her eyes, Lena picked up her glass, “yes, I’ll wear a coat. So … Alex? You in?”

     

                She was trying to fight back a smile as she straightened up, a spark in her brown eyes that surprised Lena. “Yeah. Yeah, absolutely. That sounds- that’s perfect . Right, Kelly? We should … do that, right?”

     

                “Yeah, it could be fun,” Kelly agreed, more subdued as she patted Alex’s knee and nodded indifferently.

     

                Lena paused slightly before picking up a small cake and taking a bite. Her suspicions about Alex’s behaviour were proven a short while afterwards when she enlisted Lena’s help to find the games room so she could play a game of pool. Once they were inside, Alex firmly shut the door and whirled around, grabbing Lena by the shoulders and giving her a manic look.

     

                “Oh, I could kiss you!” Alex quietly exclaimed, her hands moving up to Lena’s cheeksas she squeezed her head and then did just so, planting a firm kiss to her cheek.

     

                “Um, what?”

     

                “I’m proposing tonight,” Alex explained, spreading her hands as she raised her eyebrows expectedly.

     

                Lena’s stomach lurched and she swallowed a near-hysterical laugh as her mind took a moment to process what Alex had just told her. Realising she hadn’t said anything, Lena managed to make her mouth open and close wordlessly for a moment before she let out a choked sound.

     

                “Oh, shit.”

     

                “I know, right?” Alex grinned, grabbing a cue and picking up the chalk to roll it over the tip. “I was going to just do it as some lowkey thing but when you brought up the boat … I mean, that’s perfect, huh?”

     

                Feeling a little sick, Lena forced a smile to her face and nodded eagerly, “mhm. Couldn’t have planned it better myself. Um … anything else you need for it?”

     

                Giving her a bright smile, sexcited but a little nervous, Alex shook her head and inhaled deeply, drawing herself up to her full height. “No, this has just- I mean, I’ve been waiting for the right time, and this is it. I can feel it.”

     

                “I’m happy for you.”

     

                Alex lined up the triangle of balls on the table and sent the white smashing into them, claiming stripes for herself as she pocketed one. Lena was agitated and distracted throughout the duration of the game, letting Alex thrash her before she pretended to be annoyed by it and they drifted back out to the living room.

     

                 “It’s … two o’clock now,” Lena said, glancing down at the time on her phone screen. “We should probably start getting ready, right? I mean, if we’re having dinner at six, we’ll need to be on the boat before that and we have to drive to the harbour.”

     

                “Oh, yeah,” Kelly said, glancing at her watch, “I, uh, I need to get- yeah, I’m going to take another shower.”

     

                “I should probably iron my clothes,” Alex said, glancing sideways from Lena before she turned around and exited the living room.

     

                Lillian put down the manila folder in her hands and raised her eyebrows at Lena, “what’s wrong with them?”

     

                A breathless laugh escaped Lena as she quickly crossed over to the sofa opposite her mother and sat down beside Eliza, looking mildly panicked as she stressfully ran a hand through her hair.

     

                “You need to help me. Alex is planning on proposing tonight.”

     

                Eliza smiled slightly, “oh, tonight is it? She did tell me she bought a ring a few weeks ago.”

     

                Turning to her, Lena looked at her with distraught in her green eyes, “Kelly’s proposing tonight! I arranged the boat and flowers and champagne and everything for her and now Alex is hijacking it.”

     

                “Oh. Oh, oh no.”

     

                “Well, at least they’ll both say yes,” Lillian reasonably replied, “depending on who manages to ask first.”

     

                Humming in agreement as she ran a hand over her face, Lena nodded and then glanced down at her phone as a call came through. It was Kara, calling late again, an increasingly regular occurrence as she was dragged out all over the place, reporting on skirmishes and patrols and a few casualties. Lena wondered what it had been this time that had kept her up until the early hours of the morning, hunched over a computer as she typed up an article by the soft glow of a lamp inside a tent.

     

                Holding it up, Lena smiled, “Kara. Do you want to speak to her, Eliza?”

     

                “I’ll just say hello.”

     

                Lena answered it and spent five minutes downstairs, fitting herself and Eliza into the camera frame before she slipped upstairs to her bedroom. Stretching out on her bed, Lena smiled softly, the canopy shading her face from the slanting sunlight seeping in through the wide windows, and she took in the circles beneath Kara’s eyes. 

     

                “You look tired.”

     

                “So do you.”

     

                “Long flight,” Lena dismissively excused, “how was your day?”

     

                Kara let out a weary sigh, “long, boring, slow. I guess that’s what you want to hear, right? I just finished writing up a report so I’m done for the day.”

     

                “It’s two in the morning . What’s got you up so late?”

     

                Sighing, Kara ran a hand through her loose hair, looking younger and softer as it curled slightly around her face. “Work’s just been … a little chaotic recently. Nothing to worry yourself about; it’s not me who has to deal with it all. I just have to follow up with the aftermath so it’s just- it’s a lot.”

     

                “You know you don’t have to stay there. If you- if you tell them how you’re feeling, they’ll discharge you. You know that.”

     

                “It’s two months. I want to finish my service the right way; it’s not that much longer.”

     

                “It still feels like forever,” Lena said with a short laugh, her lips turning down slightly at the corners as she fiddled with the sheets. “How can six weeks feel so long?”

     

                “You’ll never have to let me go again. I’m counting down the seconds.”

     

                With a quiet scoff of laughter, Lena gave her a wry look, “I bet you’ll wish you were gone again within five minutes of being bombarded with attention.”

     

                “Never. We have a wedding to plan.”

     

                Smiling, her eyes gently creasing at the corners, Lena hummed, “mhm. You know, it’s funny, when Kelly saw the house, she said I should get a prenup before we get married.”

     

                “Oh, well, obviously you’d need one. Not that I’m a greedy fortune hunter who’s planning on divorcing you, but, I mean, yeah, logically.”

     

                “No, that’s not what I was going to say. I mean, it was a joke when she said it, and yeah, for legal reasons I will have to protect the business on that front, but … from a personal standpoint, I want to share everything with you. You know, a joint bank account, some shares in your name, stuff like that.”

     

                “I- well, that’s a bit unfair, though.”

     

                “What do you mean?”

     

                Kara let out a soft sigh and gave her a strained smile, eyes tender with adoration, “you have so much money. More money than ninety-nine percent of the world will never be able to even dream of - including me - and that’s kind of the point. I can’t put that kind of money into our relationship. My savings would be … pocket change in your bank account.”

     

                “Kara, I don’t care about the money. I just was you. I don’t care about us coming into this on equal financial terms, but I do want our marriage to be equal. I don’t want mine and yours; I want ours. And sure, I’ll sign a prenup so in ten years if you get sick of me you won’t make off with my fortune, but until then … whatever is mine is yours too. If we buy a new house, I want your name on the deed, I want you on the insurance for our cars, okay?”

     

                “I want us to share things too, but … I meant more like the bills and grocery shopping. I just- I have nothing to give you. Nothing . I don’t even own a car; I’d be riddled with student loans if I didn’t enlist.”

     

                “I know what you’re trying to say, and it might be uncomfortable for you, but … this isn’t about being fair. There’s no one in the world who could come to me on equal terms and make me love them more than I love you, okay? It’s easy for me to say that because I have money, but I know you don’t love me for mine. I don’t think it’s unfair for me to want to take care of you, to make sure you never have to worry about whether or not you can afford something you want because you have to pay for bills while I … I’ve never had to question whether I could or not. This changes nothing, because if you want it, I’d just buy it for you anyway.”

     

                Kara snorted with laughter, a wariness in her blue eyes as she chewed on her bottom lip. “Fine. We’ll talk about it more when I’m back, but I won’t be going overboard with expensive things. You can’t turn me into a posh girl.”

     

                With a loud laugh, Lena grinned, “I wouldn’t dream of it. We’ll have to upgrade the Tesla for you though.”

     

                “No expensive things! The Tesla is already too much.”

     

                Rolling her eyes, Lena chuckled, “fine, but I do have more in storage so I’ll let you pick which one you want. Do you want the Aston Martin? Or are you more of a Bugatti person? I prefer a Rolls-Royce for my chauffeur car but I can swap it out if you want to take it.”

     

                “I really can’t tell if you’re joking about how many cars you own,” Kara said with a withering sigh, “I’m a bit concerned. How many warehouses of extravagant things do you have?”

     

                “Too many to count. But hey, at least my boat here is getting put to use.”

     

                “Did Alex ask you for it?”

     

                “You knew? Of course you knew. No, Alex didn’t ask, but you know who did ask? Kelly.”

     

                “I- what? Kelly’s proposing? She can’t - Alex is proposing.”

     

                “Yeah, I found that out like an hour ago, after I’d already helped plan this spontaneous boat trip for Kelly to do it. Now, I don’t know which one of them is going to do it first but someone’s proposing, which I guess is all that matters.”

     

                They spoke about the proposal for a few more minutes, both of them quietly happy and thinking about their own wedding too, before the conversation slipped onto other topics. Lena divulging her opinion on her mother’s evasiveness about letting her go back to work, while Kara told her a funny story about Winn and Mike, and then Lena started reading out a proposal she’d been editing for the Tokyo expo she was going to next week.

     

                It was somewhere in between the pages of her speech, while editing and taking Kara’s advice into consideration to pass onto her publicist, that Lena drifted off to sleep. In between one sentence and the next, her eyes found themselves incapable of reopening as she slowly trailed off into silence, her laptop balanced on her lap and the phone leaning against the screen. Kara watched her for a few minutes, smiling softly as her eyes drank in the sight, before she hung up.

     

                Lena was woken two hours later by a knock on her bedroom door, startling as her eyes flew open and she pushed herself up onto her elbows. Dry-eyed and muddled, she frowned as Lillian stepped into her room, flattening her messy hair as she processed the situation before her.

     

                “Oh, shit,” Lena hissed a moment later, hurriedly scrambling for her phone as she remembered she’d been talking to Kara.

     

                The screen lit up to reveal a text message off her and Lena’s stomach sank with guilt and disappointment as she read it.

     

    [Kara]: you fell asleep and i didn’t want to wake you. don’t be upset, you really needed it. I love you xxx

     

                “Is everything okay?”

     

                Lena glanced up at her mom and pressed her lips into a flat line as she shut her laptop screen and rubbed a hand over her face. Sighing, she closed her eyes and shook her head. “No, I- I just … fell asleep. Didn’t get to say bye.”

     

                “Oh. Well … dinner is ready.”

     

                “Dinner? I’m eating on the boat.”

     

                “They left an hour ago. Alex came to check on you and said you were asleep; probably the best excuse for them to go alone, really.”

     

                Swallowing as frustration welled up inside her, Lena let out a sharp sigh and gestured off-handedly. “Fine.”

     

                Studying her from the doorway for a moment, Lillian opened her mouth and then closed it before hesitating. “Come and eat; Eliza showed me how to make casserole. Seeing as you poached my chef.”

     

                Nodding, Lena shuffled across the wide bed and climbed to her feet, feeling loose-limbed and still tired. She followed after Lillian at a slower pace and walked into the kitchen a few minutes later, rubbing at her eyes and hugging her arms to herself as the heater tried its hardest to dispel the lingering chill as she stared out at the blackness beyond the windows. 

     

                The smell of beef and the thick gravy it rested in made her stomach rumble and Lena fought back a yawn as she grabbed cutlery and set the table for three. Eliza gave her a small smile as her blue eyes tracked her across the room, serving up mashed potatoes and casserole while Lillian’s voice drifted out of the spacious pantry as she browsed the wine rack and offered up suggestions before materialising with a bottle of red wine she picked herself anyway.

     

                Lena found herself at the head of the table, Lillian and Eliza sitting across from each other, and she stared down at her dinner and gave Eliza a faint smile. “Thank you, Eliza; it looks good.”

     

                Raising the bottle of wine, Lillian watched Lena closely as she filled three glasses - Lena’s to a lesser extent - and set it down. Dinner was a mostly quiet affair with Lena offering very little to the medical conversation, despite latching onto familiar terms she’d grown up hearing from her mother as she followed along. Afterwards, she insisted on cleaning up, the two older women vanishing to Lillian’s favourite living room as soft music quickly sounded from a distance, and Lena took her time, washing dishes, wiping them dry and then putting them away in turn.

     

                Afterwards, she finished her wine and refilled it again before joining them. They were sitting opposite each other on sofas and Lena took a seat beside her mother, setting down her glass of wine and sinking back against the cushions.

     

                “How about a game of chess?” Lillian suggested after a moment.

     

                “Right now?”

     

                “You wanted to talk, didn’t you?”

     

                Eyes sliding over to Eliza, Lena bristled slightly, jerking her chin forward. “Okay.”

     

                The brand new chess set she’d bought her mother was on the coffee table, the pieces poised to begin a new game, and Lena climbed to her feet and sat on the floor, Eliza just behind her left shoulder. Her side was white, and she gave Lillian a wary look, the vague notion that she was being tested settling over her in an uncomfortable way.

     

                “Your move,” Lillian motioned.

     

                They got through the first few moves of the Sicilian Defence opening, opting for the Sveshnikov variation - her mother’s favourite - before Lena spoke, her voice low and smooth as she kept her gaze lowered to the checkerboard.

     

                “So … what is it you wanted to say?”

     

                “I have my reservations about reinstating you.”

     

                Scoffing, Lena’s lips quirked into a bitter smile as she reached forward and retaliated against her mother’s move. “Of course you do. What are they then?”

     

                Eliza’s hand gently dropping onto her shoulder startled her slightly, and she glanced up to look at her in surprise, before her cheeks warmed at the concern she saw on her face and looked back down. “We’re worried about you.”

     

                “Ah, so it’s an intervention, is it?” she muttered, raising her eyebrows.

     

                Lillian completed the opening and straightened up, giving her daughter an appraising look. “Must you treat everything like a joke?”

     

                Snorting, Lena ran her tongue over her cheeks as she eyed the board, picking her next move carefully before she reached for a pawn. “If I don’t treat it like a joke, I’m going to get pissed off.”

     

                She took one of Lillian’s pawns and then gave her a tight smile as she set the piece off to the side. Lillian looked at her with cool impassivity, her eyes unreadable as she scrutinised her daughter, making Lena want to squirm. Eliza behind her had a calming effect on Lena though, keeping her seated to the floor and trying her hardest not to let her annoyance make her impulsive or sharp. She had to admit, her mother roping in Eliza’s help had been a smart tactic.

     

                “There’s no need to get pissed off; I’m supposed to worry about you. It comes with the job of being a mother.”

     

                “Yeah, well, thanks, but I’m fine.”

     

                “Oh please. No one would believe that for a second. You’re wearing yourself out; you never sleep, you have terrible bags under your eyes, you spend too much time at the office - obviously I’m not talking about the past two weeks.”

     

                Lena quickly shut her mouth and rolled her eyes. She waited for Lillian to make a move and then assessed the board, reaching for her rook and shifting it forward. 

     

                “If I hadn’t gotten the board to agree to stand you down, you would’ve still been at the office morning, noon and night every day for the past fourteen days. And don’t even try to tell me I’m wrong. Just because I’m not in National City, do you think I don’t know what you’re doing? Do you know how many hours you’ve clocked per week over the past three months? On average.”

     

                “Well, obviously it’s going to be higher; Kara’s not here.”

     

                “One hundred and three hours. You’re clocking three times the amount of hours as your full-time employees.”

     

                “I’m CEO; I should-”

     

                “Be working hard, yes, but over a hundred hours. Jesus Christ. It’s a wonder you’re getting any sleep at all.”

     

                Frowning as she stared at the board as if it was the most fascinating thing she’d ever seen, Lena listened to her mom’s soft exclamation of horror and found herself unable to form a smart retort to the truths Lillian shoved in her face. Raking a hand through her hair in an antsy manner, Lena swallowed, her mouth dry.

     

                “I’m just- I’m worried about Kara. That’s all.”

     

                “We know you are,” Eliza murmured, reaching out to grip Lena’s shoulders and squeeze gently, “we all are too - you’re just … not handling it the same way we are.”

     

                “The reckless behaviour, the late nights, all the work you’re doing,” Lillian listed disapprovingly, lunging forward as Lena reached for her wine and snatching it from her as her expression darkened. “Drinking.”

     

                Lena let out a mewling sound of protest, reaching for her glass with a forlorn look on her face. “Oh, come on. This is a joke. I do sleep, mom, I just- I have bad dreams. What do you want me to do about that?”

     

                “When was the last time you had more than six hours of sleep?”

     

                Mouth opening, Lena hesitated, doubt crossing her face as she slowly closed her mouth, nothing coming out. The truth was she couldn’t remember. She either restlessly slept for a few hours, or woke up from a bad dream and gave up on sleep entirely. 

     

                Lillian reached into the pocket of her pants and fished out a little orange bottle, firmly setting it down before Lena and twisting it so she could read the label and then slid a piece of paper across to her with Eliza’s name on the prescription. Snorting, Lena ran a hand over her face, muttering beneath her breath.

     

                “Sleeping pills? Really?”

     

                “This is my condition. You can return to work - on reduced hours - and you’ll take the pills and sleep. No more recklessness, no more drinking, no more isolating yourself.”

     

                “Oh, God,” Lena choked out, a half-smile curling her lips as she shook her head. “You’re unbelievable.”

     

                Scrambling to her feet, two high spots of colour in her pale cheeks, Lena swallowed thickly, a muscle twitching in her jaw. Eliza reached out to gently take her hand and Lena quickly pulled herself free before turning and stalking out of the room, her anger manifesting in icy silence.

     

                Making her way up to her room, she paced back and forth for half an hour, stewing in her anger, her frustration, her loneliness that made her eyes smart, until her emotions burned themselves out to nothing but resigned smouldering ashes. Sharply exhaling, Lena dug the heels of her palms into her eyes and swallowed before crossing over to her bedroom door and yanking it open.

     

                She stalked back downstairs, brimming with tension, and walked back into the room, taking her seat on the floor and moving a piece forward on the board, the string of moves still clear in her mind. Avoiding Lillian’s gaze, she plucked the orange bottle from the coffee table, shook out two pills and swallowed them dry, a flicker of resentment at the fact that she couldn’t mix them with alcohol making itself known.

     

                “I have a prescription for Ambien already,” she admitted after a moment. “I just don’t like to rely on them.”

     

                “Oh.”

     

                “It’s your move.”

     

                Eliza pulled Lena’s dark hair back and absentmindedly played with it as Lena leaned back against the sofa, knees drawn up to her chest. She could feel the two women having some sort of silent conversation and after Lillian leaned forward and shifted her knight forward and right, she gently cleared her throat.

     

                “You can return to work on Monday.”

     

                A sigh of a breath escaped Lena and she closed her eyes briefly. “Thank you.”

     

                Lillian looked equally relieved and she nodded, dropping the subject as she waited for Lena to make her move and then swiftly counteracted it. Lena won the first two and then Lillian won the next, Eliza making tea for them and then versing Lena, while Lillian rubbed Athena behind her ears and watched on. The pills started taking affect, making Lena’s mind a little foggy as she tried to concentrate on the game, and while she ached for bed, she wanted to wait up until Alex and Kelly returned. 

     

                They weren’t late, the sound of the front door opening and closing just past nine, and Lena looked up, an eager look on her face as she stared at the door, waiting. Her face split into a smile as Alex and Kelly appeared in the doorway, rosy-cheeked and glowing as they brimmed with excitement. Pushing herself to her feet, Lena let out a quick laugh.

     

                “So, who managed to ask first?” 

     

                “Me,” Alex beamed.

     

                Lena snorted and shook her head, cheeks dimpling, and beckoned her in for a hug, holding her tightly, “thanks for upstaging my proposal plan.”

     

                “Don’t worry, I said no,” Kelly stage whispered, smiling as Lena pulled back and then wrapped her in a hug in turn.

     

                “Technically, you didn’t reply. And neither did I. But we’re engaged!”

     

                Lena let Eliza wrap them both in a hug, babbling with excitement, and then she reached for Kelly’s hand, eyeing her ring and complimenting Alex’s choice. Lillian congratulated them and fetched a bottle of champagne, giving Lena a glass with a mere mouthful in it while her daughter gave her a disgruntled look.

     

                Filling the sofas, they toasted the newly engaged couple and settled in to listen to them both tell the story, their giddiness amusing and infectious as they breathlessly interrupted each other, sitting side by side, hands on knees and backs and entwined as they shared secret glances, bright-eyed and in love. It reminded Lena of Kara, of how giddy they’d been and that excitement of knowing you were going to spend forever with your person. She was still thinking about it later that night, the thought warming her, as she finally succumbed to the sleeping pills and slept almost soundly for the next ten hours.

    Chapter 56

                Valentine’s Day rolled around a couple of weeks later, finding Lena at her office, where she belonged, freshly returned from her three-day business trip to Tokyo with Sam and Jess. The three of them had eaten at some of the most expensive restaurants in the city, spent a long night at the tech expo, where Lena gave her presentation while a translator echoed her to the packed auditorium, and were treated to a night out where Lena moodily nursed club sodas while the other two tried sake and a variety of cocktails.

     

                Even though she was limited to the amount she could drink, had cut her hours of work almost in half, and had a somewhat normal sleeping pattern now, Lena found herself agitated. It was good to be back at the helm of L-Corp, and she was on her best behaviour, watching as stock prices made a small increase and revenue boosted after the expo, relishing the small victories of being back in charge. Still, there was that lingering unease that only got worse the closer it came to Kara coming home, her whole body tense and poised for something to go wrong. Would an all-out war arise that would keep her over there on orders, would she back out of her promise to not re-enlist, her fears and desire to not rely on Lena for money forcing her into signing on for another tour so she could go back to college, or something far worse that Lena didn’t want to entertain.

     

                A dozen red roses were delivered via courier at nine o’clock, along with four red velvet cupcakes topped with hearts and a card in a red envelope, and Lena had found it endlessly amusing and only slightly embarrassing as Jess carried it in, looking equally as amused as she tried to hide it. Lena was still making her way through her carrot and apple juice, taking a moment to do the crossword in the paper, and set it aside to open the card, her eyes quickly scanning the cheesy message inside before she opened the box of cupcakes, smiling as she plucked one from it.

     

                Reaching for her phone, she called Kara and waited for it to connect, a smile toying on her lips as she watched her face fill the screen. “Two weeks!” Kara shouted the moment she appeared on screen, still slightly pixelated. “It’s officially two weeks!”

     

                Lena burst out laughing and raised her eyebrows, “Happy Valentine’s Day to you too.”

     

                “Right! And that! Happy Valentine’s Day. Did you get my gifts.”

     

                “Jess just put it on my desk. I love it, thank you.”

     

                “I haven’t opened mine yet so … just hang on … here.”

     

                She watched Kara lean off her low cot and get the small box Lena had sent with a few trifling gifts. Tearing off the tape, Kara pulled out the card first and beamed as she opened it, eyes quickly scanning the words before she looked down at the three polaroids that slid out.

     

                “I- oh, fucking hell. Lena,” Kara hissed, her cheeks flaming as she quickly pressed the photos to her chest, glancing around to make sure no one else was around before she spluttered. “Jesus.”

     

                “I borrowed one of your cameras. I hope you don’t mind,” she said, a slow smile spreading across her face.

     

                “I mean … no , of course I don’t mind. A little warning would be nice though.”

     

                Chuckling, Lena leaned back in her chair and took a bite of her cupcake, ignoring the fact that it was far too early for that much sugar as she lingered in a brief moment of happiness with her fiancee. 

     

                “Well, then I wouldn’t have gotten that reaction. That photo is worth a small fortune though - just for the record - so if you lose it or leak it, I’ll kill you.”

     

                “You think I’m letting anyone find this?”

     

                “Good. That’s not your gift though. Keep looking.”

     

                Digging through heart shaped candies and the letter for later on, Kara fished out an envelope tied with a red ribbon and opened it up, pulling out a folded piece of paper which she hunched over as she read.

     

                “Lena-”

     

                Cutting her off as a half-smile graced the corners of her mouth, Lena’s eyes creased at the corners. “When you get back, I’m taking you to Napa Valley for as long as you want and you’re going to drink wine and eat good food and try a different massage and facial every day at the spa. We’re not even going to think about anything else the entire time we’re there; it’ll just be me and you.”

     

                “It sounds … perfect,” Kara managed to thickly reply. 

     

                “I love you,” Lena whispered, a spasm of pain in her chest. “I’ve become such an impatient person lately; I feel like I might … explode if you’re not back soon.”

     

                “Two weeks. And then I’ll make sure you never have to worry again. I mean … I’m just- I’m sorry. You don’t know how sorry I am to put you through all of this.”

     

                The breath was expelled from Lena’s lungs in a soft huff as her eyes smarted and she smiled crookedly. “Hey, don’t blame yourself for this. I knew what I was getting myself into, and there’s nothing in the world you could have given me to make me back out.”

     

                “It’s just … been so hard. It’s so hard, for both of us, and it isn’t fair.”

     

                “Well, make it through the next two weeks and you can make it up to me by marrying me.”

     

                “I’d have to be six feet under for you to stop me from doing that.”

     

                Stiffening as the cold feeling of dread coiled in her stomach, Lena wrinkled her nose as her brows drew together. “Nope. Not a good joke.”

     

                “Sorry,” Kara sheepishly apologised. “Two weeks though. Two more weeks and I’m going to make you so sick of me that you’d wish I’d stayed over here.”
