They must have assumed she’d died originally, but here she was and they’d have endless questions for her. It was a consolation that Mike had come with her to corroborate things, and the thought of him made her prick up slightly with panic.

     

                “Mike, the other guy-“

     

                “He’s recovering well.”

     

                She felt a stab of relief and nodded, falling silent for the remainder of the checkup as Grace gently sat her up or peeled back bandages. Kara was too afraid to look, keeping her eyes closed as the hospital gown was hitched up, the blankets pulled down, cool air on her skin that she couldn’t bring herself to look at. What sort of damage had been sustained? She’d been in so much pain but she hadn’t known the full extent of her injuries, and it frightened her that they might have been worse than anticipated.

     

                “You’re healing nicely. We’ve had you in a course of antibiotics and an IV for hydration. You’re probably starving, but it’ll take a few days to get you back onto normal solids. All in all, you’re lucky to be alive, Sergeant.”

     

                Kara’s lips twitched ruefully and she knotted her fingers in the scratchy sheets as she dipped her chin in a slight nod of acknowledgement. Grace stared at her for a long moment, a flicker of pity in her dark eyes, before she set the clipboard back to the end of the bed.

     

                “I’ll send them in.”

     

                Hank Henshaw, her Commanding Officer, walked in first and Kara straightened up, stiffening as she sharply saluted from her bed. She couldn’t have made herself stand up even if she’d tried. Behind him followed Colonel Lauren Haley, and Kara blanched although her salute didn’t waver beyond the tremor of weakness in her hand. 

     

                Her eyes strayed to Henshaw’s face and she saw a flicker of relief in his dark eyes, his stern composure slacking a little. He met her salute, as did Colonel Haley.

     

                “State your rank, soldier,” he ordered her.

     

                Swallowing, her throat constricting and dry, she blinked back tears at the rush of comfort a familiar face brought. “Sergeant Kara Danvers. 7th Infantry Division. 296th Brigade Support Battalion. A Company.”

     

                “Major Henshaw, Sergeant Danvers, at ease,” Haley said, and Kara’s hand limply fell to her lap as Henshaw’s posture relaxed into rest. “Major Henshaw, you can confirm her identity?”

     

                “Yes, Colonel.”

     

                “Your DNA tests haven’t been returned yet, Sergeant,” Haley said, her tone cool and unassuming. It made Kara feel as if she was being interrogated, and she assumed they would do that, but hopefully not without some explanation first. “You can understand our … confusion, I hope. Your entire platoon goes missing and you show up with the British two weeks later.”

     

                Clearing her throat as she leaned back against the thin mattress, Kara wiped her brow. “I- yes, ma’am. I don’t understand most of it myself.”

     

                “Start from the beginning,” Hank softly urged her, not unkind as he searched her haunted face, dragging a chair over to the bed and gesturing for Haley to sit before he fetched his own.

     

                “We were sent out to collect intel on a skirmish the British had with a town in the Sangin Province. I don’t- I don’t remember the name. I don’t know if it had one. I- I’m a Public Affairs Specialist-“

     

                “I know your MOS, Sergeant. We’re also aware of your mission; what we don’t know is what happened after you left the town. We can skip to that.”

     

                Swallowing thickly, Kara looked down at her lap. “Private DuBois … mislaid his rifle. We were a few hours into the return trip already. Lieutenant Tran made us turn back to recover it. It put us out about five hours by the time we recovered our ground. Lieutenant Tran told us to stop at a town we passed through on the way; he didn’t want us driving through the night. Comms were down … I don’t think they got them back up to relay it all. And then …”

     

                She trailed off for a minute, drawing in a shaky breath as she twisted the sheets in her lap, one hand heavily bandaged and a tremor in her voice.

     

                “I’d gone to get a drink from my pack in one of the houses. It was set back from the road, falling apart but enough cover to sleep in. The first airstrike hit while I was in there. It’s- it’s the only reason I survived. The building collapsed on me. I don’t really know what happened … I think I was unconscious for a few minutes. It was too dark to see but I- I was bleeding. Another one hit just after it.”

     

                Cutting off, she ran a hand over her face, squeezing her eyes shut, and then let out a choked breath. They didn’t push her but she knew they wanted the whole story out of her and wouldn’t let her rest until it was out.

     

                “I called out. I heard a shout. It was Mike- Specialist Mike Matthews. He was with DuBois. Everyone else … they were just … gone. All of them. I knew we weren’t safe so I told Mike to get clear. He took DuBois. I went back for the packs - I knew we- we wouldn’t get far without them. I met them outside of the town and … we walked. I don’t know how far we went but we walked until it was light. There was a cave; DuBois was already dead by then. We had to- to leave him there. We were both hurt; we tried to patch ourselves up. I’m not sure how long we stayed there - a couple of days I think. In the end, I knew we had to go … go somewhere. We couldn’t go back - no one knew to look for us there and the rebels ... I thought … if we could get back to that town, maybe the British could help. We walked until we reached a town - I don’t think it was the same one - I’m not sure what happened after that. I don’t remember much of the walk either.”

     

                Her two superiors exchanged a look, a grimness to it and a flicker of unmistakable guilt, before Hank cleared his throat and shifted forward.

     

                “Kara,” he said with surprising tenderness - this, the man who’d shouted himself hoarse at her on more that one occasion when she’d fucked up immeasursbly in his presence - the lines of his face deepening. “There were no rebels.”

     

                She blinked in surprise at his words, her mouth opening before he swiftly cut her off with the explanation.

     

                “The British spotted activity out in an abandoned town. They did recon; saw a fire, thermal vision confirming the numbers. They checked in with us - we had no one out there; we thought your platoon was almost back to base - and they called in a strike.”

     

                Feeling like the breath had been knocked from her lungs, she sank into the mattress, his words rattling around in her mind as a strange, tingling numbness spread over her. Friendly fire. All but two of the platoon had been obliterated - or nearly so - in friendly fire. The next breath got stuck in her throat, making her choke as tears stung her eyes.

     

                “You-“

     

                “The British were sure it was rebels. I’m so deeply sorry that we- I understand that you lost many good friends. First Lieutenant Alphonso Tran … he was-“

     

                “How?” she cut him off, too aghast to even stop herself from the insubordination.

     

                He let it go, under the circumstances, and looked weary of the mere idea that they’d called down the deaths of more than a dozen of their own. Letting out a soft sigh, he shrugged helplessly.

     

                “We didn’t know until the next morning. The British found military grade vehicles, your tags … we assumed all of you- we didn’t have any reason to think we had to look … forgive me. We … failed you. If we’d known, you wouldn’t have- but, as it is, from what we know from the British, locals came and found them - they were still stationed at that town; it took a man more than a day to walk there to inform them - and they came to get you. From there, they took you to their base and notified us, identifying you as American, and we airlifted you to Germany for treatment. You’ve been out for a couple of days - it’s been almost seventeen since you went missing in action.”

     

                “My family …”

     

                His mouth thinned and he gave her a solemn look, “I informed your mother myself. They … held a funeral for you with all military rights; I was present for that as well. Everyone thought … well, we’ve notified them and they’ll be here shortly to see for themselves. We were vague - we had to identify and confirm it with you first.”

     

                She nodded, her eyelids closing as she breathed slowly. It was difficult to comprehend that the worst night of Kara’s life had been nothing more than an accident. That people had come the next day, people who could have saved them, maybe even saved DuBois if they hadn’t carried him for miles through the desert, bearing him away out of fear of being killed if they’d stayed. They’d made a hard, long trip at a snail’s pace, for almost a week, for it to have been meaningless. But they couldn’t have known any of that and they’d put themselves through hell to survive.

     

                Tears leaked out of the corners of her eyes and Kara gritted her teeth, a sob hitching in her throat. A part of her was embarrassed to be crying in front of senior officials but she was on too many drugs and too exhausted to stop herself, the relief, the anger, the pain, the guilt and grief all too much for one thin body to contain after enduring so much. The next sob was louder and ragged, the feeling that her chest might cave in so physically painful that for a brief moment she thought she might have a heart attack.

     

                “You’ll be compensated, of course,” Colonel Haley pressed on, “and awarded for your service. I’m sure there’s a medal …”

     

                She trailed off at Kara’s hollow bark of laughter, the sound caustic and rough. There was a momentary lapse of silence before Hank climbed to his feet.

     

                “We hope you recover quickly and can go home soon. We’ll be in touch once you’re back on home soil. Once again … we’re deeply sorry.”

     

                It was all Kara could do to close her eyes and nod at his words, finding them empty no matter how genuine. What good were words when they’d sanctioned an airstrike on their own people? If there had been any room for hatred at that moment, Kara was sure she would’ve felt it, white-hot and blinding. Instead, she was hooked up on morphine and was just as likely to fall asleep, and she managed a weak salute, almost mocking, echoed by her superiors, before they both left.

     

                Her whole body went slack the moment they left the room and Kara promptly burst into tears. It was somehow better and worse that it had been her own countrymen who’d done it, but it didn’t make it easier. She cried until she was further exhausted, until it verged on the edge of a breakdown, and only then did Doctor Parker return with a sedative.

     

                It whisked her away quickly, and as her thoughts unravelled like cotton thread, unspooling into shapeless thoughts and dreams, her heart ached for Lena. All she wanted was to see her again, to be held and comforted. Only then would she be able to find even a sliver of peace in the horror of her reality.

    Chapter 70

                As exhausted as she was, Lena was up at the crack of dawn - German time - dressed and showered and anxiously pacing back and forth the room she was sharing with her mom. It was the nicest hotel within close proximity, Lillian sacrificing luxury and comfort for her daughter’s sanity, but even still her mom was taking her sweet time getting ready, carefully applying the makeup she’d bought the day before to her drawn face as Lena brimmed with impatience. They’d arrived at the hotel Lillian had texted her to find designer clothes and necessities for all of them - including Kara - waiting in their appropriate rooms.

     

                “You should go down for breakfast.”

     

                “I’m not hungry.”

     

                “They’re not going to let us in this early anyway; the sun’s not even up yet.”

     

                Sighing, Lena pulled on the new trench coat, tearing off the tag, and grabbed her purse before she stepped out into the narrow hallway. Knocking on Alex and Kelly’s door, she waited for them to let her in and hovered just inside the door.

     

                “Breakfast?”

     

                Alex arched an eyebrow, disbelieving, but nodded as they finished getting ready. She pulled on a thin quilted coat and eyed herself in the mirror, “you know, this is probably the nicest coat I’ve ever owned.”

     

                “I’m glad this trip is turning out so well for you,” Lena said as she rolled her eyes.

     

                Giving her a wide grin, mood buoyed by the fact that the world had righted itself, Alex raked a hand through her hair and grabbed the key card, shoving it into her back pocket. Kelly was spraying herself with perfume, humming in appreciation as she eyed the label before she walked towards them and the trio made their way downstairs. 

     

                It was a continental breakfast buffet and Lena put a croissant on a plate and poured herself orange juice and coffee before taking a seat. Buttering the croissant, she took a bite, thinking of Kara. Was she awake now? Was she wondering where they were? Had she eaten and gotten enough sleep?

     

                Draining her cheap coffee, grateful for the buzz of caffeine, she sipped the sharp orange juice and her mom and Eliza joined them at the table with their own breakfasts. It was seven o’clock when they finally caught two cabs back to the base, repeating the process of being granted access and passing through security before they were allowed into the hospital. Eagerness seized Lena, her heart soaring in her chest as it pounded loudly, a prickle of excitement running through her, the same relief as yesterday swelling inside her as she walked down the hallway - this time without the nervous dread.

     

                Opening the door, Lena stepped inside and felt everything inside her unwind, relief washing over her, even though she’d known Kara was safe. She was still there, in the bed, turning to face the door as she smiled thinly. She was propped up a little more on the pillows now, a small TV in the high corner of the room playing some German daytime TV show on the grainy screen, and breakfast lay abandoned on the wheeled tray over her lap.

     

                Rushing over to the bed, Lena grabbed her face in her hands, as gentle as if cradling a fragile flower in her palms, and leaned down to kiss her. Kara’s lips were chapped and peeling from sunburn, rough against her own, but it was perhaps the sweetest kiss of Lena’s life. She’d been too afraid to kiss her yesterday, barely keeping it together and hardly daring to touch her, but her mind and body had time to adjust to the news and all she could think of now was kissing Kara. It was a deeply intimate moment, their noses brushing and foreheads touching afterwards, while Alex lingered in the doorway, holding everyone else at bay.

     

                “Good morning,” Lena whispered, bright-eyed and coy, if still slightly drawn with worry as her eyes anxiously roamed across Kara’s face.

     

                “Good morning,” Kara murmured, her eyelids shuttering as she smiled faintly, one hand searching for Lena before she knotted her fingers in the fabric of her coat sleeve.

     

                “How’re you feeling today?”

     

                Lena dragged a chair over to the bed and sat down, a tender look on her face as she smiled softly at Kara.

     

                “I’m fine.”

     

                Her eyes slowly traversed the rest of the room, smiles for all of them as they all crowded in, encircling the bed and asking her the same, repeated questions, all of them still somewhat in shock at her being there. 

     

                “I’ll speak to the doctor,” Eliza said after they’d all settled in, “see when we can get you home.”

     

                Climbing to her feet, she vanished out into the hall with Lillian swift to follow after her, quieter and more subdued in Kara’s presence, as if she still wasn’t quite sure what to make of her. Yet, there was still that palpable air of gratitude in the silent way she set down a bag of necessities for her while the others fussed over Kara, the way she’d forked out the tens of thousands to send her plane to fetch Eliza and reunite her with her daughter, just relieved that Kara was alive to drag Lena out of the fog of grief.

                

                “Did they give you anything for the pain?” Lena asked.

     

                Shrugging nonchalantly, Kara smiled, more of a grimace, as her eyes closed, “yes, but it’s not so bad anyway. There’s nothing really wrong with me.”

     

                Lena wanted to object to that; they’d spoken to the doctor yesterday after they’d been told visiting hours were over, hearing the horrors of the infected wound where rusted metal had impaled her, the blood loss and fevers, the scabbed over deep cuts and dehydration and malnourishment, the fractures and all sorts. There would have been bad bruising too, faded and gone now after weeks gone by, and the rest was following in its wake, the IV pumping fluids into her, the carefully controlled diet already adding on pounds and the antibiotics battling the fever and the cleaned out wounds. They’d put her into a medically induced coma upon arrival to treat her, just for a few days, before waking her the day before, verifying her identity, but Lena could only imagine the state she’d been in to warrant that.

     

                Still, over the following days, they watched her improve swiftly. The next day she was sitting up in bed, the day after she was on less medication and was up to a round of cards with Alex, while Lena watched on silently and intently. All of them had stopped being there at once as the shock and elation and relief finally mellowed into normalcy - except for Lena, who refused to leave her side. Eliza would come in the morning, Alex and Kelly in the afternoon, and Lillian came for quick visits with good food and coffee and enquiries as to whether Kara needed anything, but Lena was there from the minute she was allowed until she was forcibly removed.

     

                It was five days later, while Kara slept and Lena dozed in the chair beside the bed, midday sunshine streaming in as the monitors beeped and the room was silent, that she was torn from her peaceful slumber by a hoarse shout. Bolting upright, instantly alert, Lena looked at Kara and scrambled to her feet as she paled at the sight of her thrashing around on the bed, face twisted with anguish. Reaching out to pin her, she stopped at the sound of her mother’s voice.

     

                “Don’t touch her.”

     

                At the wary caution in Lillian’s low voice, Lena snatached her hand back and looked back over her shoulder, eyes wide and lost. Lillian beckoned her to her side and Lena reluctantly obeyed, brimming with panic as her heart jolted in her chest and her mouth went dry. Stepping around her, Lillian moved to the bedside and rifled through the bag of toiletries she’d brought in, pulling out a tub of body lotion, sweetly perfumed, and unscrewed the lid.

     

                “Kara? Can you hear me?” Lillian cordially asked, assuming the role of a doctor as she waved the lotion before her nose. “It’s Lillian. You’re safe; you’re having a bad dream.”

     

                Glancing over her shoulder, she jerked her chin at Lena, “turn the TV on - not too loud.”

     

                Fingers trembling as she picked up the remote, Lena turned it on, German flooding through the tinny speakers of the boxy TV. It was a children’s show, the tones high pitched and incomprehensible to Lena as her heart leapt into her throat and she rubbed her clammy palms together, shoulders tense and an anxious look in her eyes. 

     

                “Speak to her,” Lillian brusquely ordered.

     

                “Hey, it’s me,” Lena softly said, moving back over to the bed as Kara’s thrashing already started to ease to restlessness, her lips moving soundlessly as sweat beaded her forehead. “You’re safe; you’re home. Wake up - you’re not there anymore. You’re home with me.”

     

                She reached out with a shaking hand to touch a finger to the back of her hand, jumping slightly as Kara’s eyes flew open and she let out a hoarse shout, sitting up. No one spoke for a moment as Kara hunched forward, chest heaving as she panted, eyes closed and face turned away from Lena. She muffled a sob and wiped her sweaty face on the shoulder of the pyjamas Lillian had bought her, and Lena sank to a crouch beside the bed to get a look at her face as Kara purposely avoided looking at her. 

     

                “Hey,” Lena repeated, her voice wavering slightly.

     

                Clearing her throat, she pressed her lips into a flat line and covered Kara’s hand with her own. A weary sigh slipped from Kara’s lips as she squeezed her eyes shut, lines radiating from the corners, and then looked at her, unfocused without her glasses.

     

                “I thought I’d dreamt you,” Kara whispered, her forehead pinching as she gave Lena a bewildered look.

     

                “I’ll give you a minute,” Lillian murmured, screwing the lid back onto the lotion and turning off the TV, exhaling as she set the remote down on the nightstand.

     

                Lena swallowed and reached for Kara’s glasses, gently easing them onto her face. Blinking, Kara looked at her for a long moment and Lena gave her a thin smile. “I’m real; I’m right here.”

     

                “Right. It was just a nightmare.”

     

                “A memory,” Lena gently corrected, a grave look of concern on her face as she reached up to brush damp hair out of Kara’s face.

     

                Kara hummed in disconcerting agreement, rubbing at her forehead before she eased herself back on the pillows. Lena poured her a glass of tepid water from the plastic jug and handed it to her, Kara silently taking a sip as the cup shook in her hand. Lena didn’t comment on it but she noticed.

     

                “You should sleep some more. Do you need more pain meds? I can get my mom to talk to the doctor; it’ll help you sleep better.”

     

                “I … don’t want to sleep. I can’t … I just- I see it all over again.”

     

                “Okay,” Lena murmured, “that’s okay. Just rest then; focus on getting better and then we can get you home.”

     

                Kara let out a pent up breath, her shoulders caving as she slumped on the bed. Pinching the bridge of her nose, she swallowed audibly. “I just- I need you to help me. I don’t know … I’ve been so- so alone . I can’t do this without you; please don’t leave me alone.”

     

                Lena felt the air rush from her lungs, winded by her words, and climbed to her feet quickly before she nudged Kara over and climbed onto the bed with her. Wrapping her arms around her, Lena pulled her in close - as close as they’d been since she’d been found - feeling how thin and frail she was as she cradled Kara against her side.

     

                “Shh, it’s okay. I’m here; I’ll never leave you alone. I’m not leaving your side ever again. Do you hear me?”

     

                “I just … need you.”

     

                “I’m not going anywhere. I’ve been waiting for you for months.”

     

                Kara huffed a laugh and wiped her nose, “I’ve been dreaming about home for months - about you. You waited.”

     

                “I would’ve waited forever.”

     

                Kissing the side of her head, Lena sank back against the pillows and held her as they sat in comfortable silence, the weight of Kara’s pain bearing down on them both, but Lena would bear it willingly if it meant she could help, could alleviate some of it for Kara. She would do anything for her, even just for this moment, a moment she’d never thought she’d get again. After what Lena had been put through while Kara was gone, helping the love of her life through her trauma seemed to pale in comparison, despite the severity of it.

     

                The door opened a minute later and Lillian walked back in, coffee and cheap cafeteria sandwiches in her hands as she furtively eyed them and set everything down. “Lena said you like chicken, Kara. I wasn’t sure whether you preferred it with avocado or salad so I got both to be on the safe side, but if you don’t-”

     

                “Thank you, Lillian,” Kara politely cut her off, offering up a genuine smile.

     

                Nodding, Lillian withdrew slightly and hesitated. “How’re you feeling?”

     

                “I … don’t know,” Kara admitted, looking surprised at herself at the honesty, although Lena had never known her to be much of a list anyway. “I just- I’m relieved … everything else is …”

     

                “You just need to give yourself time now.”

     

                Kara nodded and Lena felt a rush of gratitude. Towards Kara for somehow finding her way back to them - she was still blurry on the details offered up by the soldier who’d briefed them, but didn’t want to press Kara - and to her mother as well. They’d all been through hell for weeks, and those feelings weren’t easily dismissed, her body still suffering from the effects of her grief, even though her mind had caught up now. 

     

                Lillian had been the strong point for Lena during that time and as she eyed her mother, she knew there would be no coming back from that now; their relationship had been irrevocably changed once more by grief and pain. Only this time, for the better, and it was a strange dichotomy that something so awful could have produced something good as well. But that was Kara - whether in life or death, she had been committed to leaving a lasting impression on Lena’s life. It was a solace now to know she hadn’t lost her at all, but she’d forgiven her mother entirely.

     

                Still, it was a lot, and Lena murmured she needed to use the bathroom as she climbed to her feet, pressing a kiss to Kara’s brow and slipping into the en-suite. Sitting down on the closed toilet lid, she ran a hand over her face and hunched forward. In her pocket was the worn and crumpled final letter she’d received, transferred from pocket to pocket and always carried with her, and Lena drew it out with a shaking hand. It was creased and worn and folded in half, faint streaks of mud staining it and the limp feeling of too much handling. The first time she’d read it seemed like a lifetime ago, but it had barely been a week. Just a week since she’d buried an empty box, cried her heart out at the edge of an empty hole and felt her heart break that little bit more beyond repair.

     

                Only now, it was cobbled back together and patched up with nothing more than relief and love, struggling along as she tried to process it all. How did you go from one extreme to the other and just pretend it was all okay? Kara wasn’t the only one having bad dreams, and although Lena had been trying to wean herself off sleeping pills since that first week of oblivion, she’d had to take them so that she’d sleep through most of the night at the hotel, knowing she needed her strength for Kara. Her mother had been silent the times Lena had woken her with a startling cry as she tore herself from sleep; now seemed to be the moment Lillian seized.

     

                “Lena?” Her mom’s voice drifted through the thin wood as she lightly tapped on the door. “Are you alright?”

     

                Withholding a sigh, Lena looked up at the door, looking so drained and helpless that even her elation and happiness dimmed slightly in comparison. 

     

                “Can I come in?”

     

                Climbing to her feet, Lena yanked open the unlocked door - the first mistake she’d made by thinking her mother wouldn’t notice her hiding in there - and looked up at her mom’s towering figure.

     

                “I’m just thinking.”

     

                Lillian looked down at the letter clutched tightly in her hand and then back up at her face, her pale eyes scrutinising. Pushing her way inside, Lillian gently shut the door and gave her a troubled look.

     

                “Are you okay?”

     

                “I just-“ Lena cut off, her eyes stinging with tears as she looked down, embarrassed, although she’d cried more times in front of her mom in the past month than she had her whole life, and gestured towards the closed door in a helpless wave. “I don’t know what to do, mom.”

     

                “Oh, honey, it’s okay. This is a big shock - a good one, of course - and it’ll be an even bigger adjustment. But … Kara will be okay.”

     

                “Will she though? What if- I mean … if-“

     

                “You’re scared. That’s okay - it’s okay to be scared, but she needs you now more than ever. And you need her too, that much is clear to me now, but she needs you. She needs your help and love and patience and kindness. I’m sorry that you’ll have to go through this, but I know now how much you love her. I know that now. There’s no one else and there’s no mistake; you won’t be happy without her. She dragged herself through hell to make it back to you and I will never be able to thank her enough for that. For giving you back your happiness and for bringing you back to me. That girl … God, that girl loves you. I know I’ve- I’ve said things in the past … I’ve voiced my concerns and my doubts but I- I was so wrong . You see, I want you to be happy more than anything, so if I could’ve picked for you … I would’ve picked her too. So you’re going to be strong for both of you and you’re going to get through it and get married . You’re going to live the life that you deserve and you’re going to be happy, Lena. I want that for you and she’s going to give it to you.”

     

                Lena let out a long, slow breath, quietly stunned by her mom’s tirade as she shoved the letter into her pocket and felt the knot inside her loosen slightly. It wasn’t that she didn’t think she could handle being around for it all, only that she wasn’t sure how to help Kara, but her mother’s words bolstered her anyway. Nodding to herself, Lena squared her shoulders and stepped forward, wrapping Lillian in a surprising hug before she pulled back.

     

                “Good,” Lillian curtly nodded, satisfied that Lena wasn’t backing down from the fight now.

     

                She turned to leave and Lena hesitated for a moment, her expression clouding as she found herself briefly tongue-tied, unable to make her voice work. “Mom?”

     

                Glancing back over her shoulder, Lillian raised her eyebrows expectantly and Lena swallowed, shrugging slightly, a helpless manner as her lips twitched with a small smile. “I love you.”

     

                There was a flicker of surprise on Lillian’s face, the fact that Lena was saying it unprompted for the first time in perhaps twenty years , of her own volition, not lost on either of them. Her mother’s sharp and stern face softened minutely, a barely perceptible reaction that Lena was able to pick up on for knowing her expressions so well, having studied them for disappointment and dissatisfaction for years, and yet now it was slacking with the surprise and quiet joy at three words that she’d always found so hard to say, to Lillian most of all. Giving her a thin, wavering smile, her pale eyes bright but not quite teary, her mom nodded and slipped out of the bathroom without a word. Lena suspected she was having just as much a hard time speaking then too.

     

                Stepping out of the bathroom, Lena inhaled deeply and gave Kara a bright smile as she took a seat on the chair beside the bed. Pulling the worn letter out of her pocket, she studied it for a moment and then looked up at Kara, showing it to her.

     

                “What have you got there?”

     

                Snorting, Lena gave her a rueful look, eyes narrowing slightly, “you know damn well what this is, Kara Danvers.”

     

                “I never meant for you to read it. I guess you can ignore it now.”

     

                “Ignore it?” Lena spluttered, turning the worn envelope over in her hands as she smiled crookedly, “you want me to ignore the fact that you told me to move on and find someone else if you died? You sorely overestimated me if you thought that was something I could do.”

     

                “Well, I mean … I would have wanted you to. I mean- no, I wouldn’t have wanted you to be miserable forever. But I’m home! So we can just forget anything I said and pretend I just came home normally.”

     

                “Everything?” Lillian laughed, cutting in with a sudden reminder that she was still there, on the edges of the conversation. “I imagine you’d still like me to uphold your wishes.”

     

                “You got a letter?” Lena spluttered, aghast at the idea.

     

                Bristling slightly, Lillian drew herself up imperiously, “I did.”

     

                “What did it say?”

     

                “That is between Kara and myself - although I think you’d be pleased as well, if you knew what was in it.”

     

                “Tell me,” Lena demanded, a faint whine in her voice as she tried to convince Lillian, who just looked amused as she silently ignored her.

     

                “I can always reenlist and go missing in action again and leave you to figure it out yourself,” Kara joked, giving Lena a grin before she rolled her eyes at the stony silence she received in response. “Or … I guess I can just mope around here and never make another joke again.”

     

                Sighing, Lena pinched the bridge of her nose as she closed her eyes, “we just got you back; we don’t even know what happened , and I’m not saying you have to tell me right now but … this isn’t a laughing matter.”

     

                “You think I don’t know that?” Kara harshly snapped, her eyes brightening with frustration.

     

                Lillian silently rose to her feet and made towards the door, murmuring something about finding a doctor, before she stepped outside of the uncomfortable tension in the room. Kara winced in bed and turned her head aside, looking towards the slatted blinds covering the window as Lena stared at her, irate and silent as she stewed in the pain of losing Kara.

     

                “I’m sorry. I don’t want to think about it, so I just need to … I need to act like it’s fine.”

     

                “But it’s not. You clearly went through a lot, and it’s not fine.”

     

                “I don’t need your pity. I don’t deserve it.”

     

                “Kara-”

     

                “I watched them die , Lena. There were fifteen of us … and three of us made it out.”

     

                “Three? I thought-”

     

                Kara let out a small, choked laugh, turning her head to stare up at the panels of the ceiling, “yeah. Three. Only two of us made it home; he’s still- he’s out there. I don’t even know where we were. We had to- we left his … body.”

     

                “There’s nothing you could’ve done.”

     

                A hitching sob got caught in her throat and she clapped a hand to her mouth, closing her eyes as she frowned. A moment later she lowered it and her mouth turned down at the corners before she spoke.

     

                “I couldn’t save him. It was … hell . I’m scared to- to close my eyes. I can hear the … screams, the- the bombs. I shouldn’t be here; I don’t deserve to be here when they’re all-”

     

                “Hey,” Lena gently cut her off, a firm edge to her voice as panic set in, “don’t say that. Don’t you ever say you don’t deserve to be here. You … you did what you could to survive - you saved that other guy. Someone else has their son home because of you. Just … tell me what you need and I’ll give it to you.”

     

                “Stop it. You don’t know-”

     

                “No, I don’t, but I know that you’re here and you’re alive and I’m not going anywhere. So you do whatever you have to and I’ll look after you, okay?”

     

                She gave Kara a searching look, piercing and expectant, and Kara eventually met her eyes, chin wobbling as she nodded. Relief swept through Lena and the tension bled out of her where she sat, reaching out to take Kara’s hand and press a kiss to the back of it. Her eyes creased slightly at the corners, an aching look of love, and she pressed it to her cheek, staring at Kara with badly concealed worry.

     

                “I love you.”

     

                “I know you do,” Kara said with a spent sigh, sagging against the pillows. “I love you too.”

    Chapter 71

                They kept Kara in hospital for a week, and by that point she was on her way to recovery. She’d suffered another infection a few days before, from too many open wounds exposed to dirt and bacteria, but after another round of antibiotics she’d recovered well. Her burns had healed to shiny new skin, her scabs were starting to fall off to reveal pinkish skin beneath, and her stitches had been removed, leaving behind puckered beginnings of scars that would fade to white with time. 

     

                Her broken bones would take weeks yet, if not months, but she’d put on a healthy amount of weight, no longer looking quite so hollowed out and frail, and the IV had hydrated her thoroughly. After another day of observation, Kara was discharged.

     

                Lena had some reservations about it after sitting through a few more days of nightmares, of thrashing and screaming, but even she had to concede to Kelly’s point that a familiar home might be helpful. To be in her bedroom might prove to reassure her unconscious mind that she was home and safe while asleep. Perhaps the nightmares wouldn’t be quite so bad if that was the case.

     

                They decided on Midvale for the time being, the quietness of the sea and a small town a better place to convalesce than a bustling city. Lillian made plans to stay in National City for the meantime, offering Sam a hand running the company while she took care of Athena for Lena and readied the house for when they came back. Lena almost wished her mom was coming with her but never would have said - it always felt easier to be bluntly honest with her mom than anyone else in the family, like she could’ve said anything and Lillian wouldn’t have held it against her, understanding her anger, her frustration, and dismissing it. 

     

                The truth was Lena was angry. The last week had been the best and worst of her life, gratitude for every moment she got to spend with Kara the main feeling, yet overshadowing darker ones - all her worry, her grief, her fear, her anger. How could she not be angry, knowing the truth behind Kara’s suffering? They’d been briefed by Major Henshaw and Colonel Haley, discreetly informed of the major oversight that had allowed a dozen of their own to be killed. And now Lena had to sit and watch her fiancée shy away from her touch, wake from awful nightmares, wrapped up in thoughts of pain and suffering. 

     

                For her part, she spent most of her time at Kara’s bedside - as much as she could - reading poems to her, flipping through magazines, filling her in on funny anecdotes and old stories Kara had already heard but she repeated for her now, just for something to talk about. Kara mostly stared at her in silence, watching her as she listened to her talk, and Lena was left with the vague notion that Kara wasn’t there at all - not mentally, at least - and she didn’t know how to bring her back.

     

                The day they left, it was raining in Germany. Lena had never appreciated the dreary weather so much before, grateful for something in such sharp contrast to the relatively arid climate of Afghanistan, hoping that it would provide some comfort to Kara, and serve as a reminder that she was far from danger. Turning away from the window at the sound of the bathroom door opening, Lena gave Kara a small smile as she watched her awkwardly hobble out, her flowing pants hiding most of the cast on her foot.

     

                “Ready?” Lena asked, reaching for the handles of the overnight bag full of things for Kara.

     

                Giving her a faint smile, Kara nodded, looking more like herself in a plaid blue shirt, her hair in a ponytail and her scratched glasses on her fuller face. Still, one foot was in a cast and she was stiff with her movements and quite aloof as Lena picked up her bag and moved to help her. Kara ignored her hand - or more unlikely, didn’t see it - and lowered herself onto the wheelchair Doctor Parker held steady for her.

     

                “Let’s go home,” Kara said with weary resignation, slumping in the chair as she pressed her lips into a thin line.

     

                They were escorted to the airport in military vehicles with soldiers to escort them and were passed through security quickly, everything readied for them as quickly as possible on military orders - something money couldn’t bypass for them. In short order, their luggage was stowed and they were seated in the plush interior of the jet, food and drinks laid out and the engine whirring as the aircraft was readied for takeoff. 

     

                The flight back felt shorter, and Lena watched Kara the entire time, sitting across from the made up bed where her fiancée slept. Kara woke on occasion, a quiet, startled cry tearing her from sleep or the sharp intake of breath heralding her rough exit into consciousness and Lena had to force herself to stay seated as she watched Kara chest quickly rise and fall before she calmed down and slept some more. Everyone else watched her too, although they were more furtive about it and made an effort to read or watch a movie on a tablet, picking at the selection of food. Lena was immobile though, rigid and intense as she watched Kara closely, the fear that if she took her eyes off her she’d vanish not quite gone yet.

     

                When the plane touched down at the private airstrip in the middle of the forest, it almost seemed to her that it was just another trip to visit Eliza. Although, the last one had been the stuff of Lena’s nightmares and even she dreaded the return, although she tried not to dwell on memories of the funeral as she fluttered around Kara, helping her down the stairs and into the luxury minivan she’d hired for space. Sitting beside Kara in the back, their arms pressed against each other - the longest period of contact they’d had since reuniting - Lena couldn’t help but feel that dread grow, like there was still worse yet to come. Realistically, she knew there was nothing worse than what they’d already endured, but things were far from normal and it was discomforting.

     

                At the sight of Eliza’s house though, Kara let out a soft, pent up breath, the tension bleeding out of her shoulders as her blue eyes brightened with a sheen of tears. Lena reached for her hand and squeezed it gently, Kara returning the gesture with wiry fingers. As they came to a stop outside, everyone else filed our first and Lena helped Kara out, Alex hovering outside to help bear her weight as they helped her down from inside the van, and then they made an awkward trio as they helped Kara hobble up to the front door and into the house.

     

                The hallway was only wide enough for two so Lena let Alex tow her sister through to the back living room and into a sofa. Holding their bags in hand, Lena hesitated before carrying them upstairs and depositing them in Kara’s childhood bedroom. 

     

                Making her way back down, she found Eliza making tea in the kitchen and stepped inside to help, silent and shaking as she stirred honey into three cups. Eliza laid a hand on her arm for a brief moment and Lena looked up to meet her gentle blue eyes, lips twitching with a wry smile as she shrugged half-heartedly in silent reply. Nodding, Eliza didn’t say anything, just picked up three cups and carried them through, leaving the other two to Lena.

     

                They switched the TV on and Lena saw Alex’s hesitation before she put The Great British Bake Off on, perhaps the safest option she could think of, and the five of them sat before the TV nursing their tea while they watched two episodes in silence. No one spoke and Lena watched Kara, taking in her unfocused eyes, the lack of attention as she tuned out the show, clearly lost in her own thoughts. Eventually, Kara turned to meet her eyes and softly sighed, a faint crease forming between her eyebrows.

     

                “What is it?”

     

                “What?” Lena asked, eyebrows rising innocently as she shifted back on the sofa, legs curled beneath her.

     

                Closing her eyes, Kara’s lips twitched as she rolled her shoulders restlessly against the cushion behind her head. “You keep looking at me.”

     

                Flushing faintly as she fleetingly met the eyes of everyone else in the room before fixing her gaze on the TV screen, rubbing at her jaw. “Am I not allowed to?”

     

                “You don’t have to keep watch,” Kara murmured, her voice still somewhat scratchy. She curled up on her side, staring at the TV again as she continued. “I’m not going to vanish into thin air.”

     

                Lena let out a choked laugh and gave Kara’s leg a reassuring pat as one side of her mouth hitched up into a smile. “Maybe I just like looking at you.”

     

                “Lena … watch the damn show. You might need to know this, for when I make you make them for me.”

     

                “If you wanted macarons, I’d fly to France and get them for you. It’d be a lot easier than …” she waved a hand at the TV screen, “whatever this is.”

     

                Kara let out a soft laugh, the sound sweet and easing Lena’s knotted anxiety. The fact that Kara had been missing for almost three weeks and still had enough energy to mock Lena’s baking and cooking skills was a relief, and Lena felt bolstered by it, taking it as a sign that they’d move past this, if not overcome it. They lapsed into silence for a moment longer, the sky darkening beyond the windows as the sound of the sea was cut through with the sound of flustered bakers on screen, and then Kara’s stomach rumbled.

     

                “Hungry?” Lena asked, her face creasing as it softened with a smile. 

     

                She was already making to climb to her feet, eager to take care of Kara, struck with the bizarrity of their circumstances, that Kara was home and wouldn’t be leaving again. Amidst it all, that homecoming had gotten lost, and Lena hadn’t taken the time to appreciate having her there, safe and able to shower her with affection and whatever she wanted. Although, it seemed like affection was on the back burner for the time being, giving Kara the necessary space to process while she tried not to focus on the ache of longing in her chest; she was alive, that was more than enough.

     

                “Do you want me to make you something? Maybe not macarons …”

     

                Kara scoffed at her weak joke and Lena smiled slightly, arching an eyebrow. Giving her a small smile, Kara shrugged nonchalantly, her suntanned cheeks dimpling sheepishly. “I could really go for some Chinese food. Can we get it for dinner?”

     

                She looked around the room as if anyone was going to deny her anything for the next few months at least , although Eliza hummed dubiously for a moment. “Are you sure you’ll be able to keep it down? It might be too rich after bland hospital food.”

     

                “I’ve been thinking about it for months .”

     

                “Alright then. I’ll order it now.”

     

                Alex climbed to her feet, “don’t worry, we’ll go and get it. We’ve been cooped up in a hospital for the past week; I think I need some fresh air. Wouldn’t hurt for you two to do the same as well.”

     

                The latter was directed at Kara and Lena, who rolled her eyes but knew that Alex was right. Perhaps in the morning they could sit outside in the bracing sea air - Kara wouldn’t be able to walk far with her cast, and not yet strong enough to wield her crutches effectively for a walk along the beach. 

     

                “The usual?”

     

                “Double order of dumplings. Oh, and can you see if they have those little egg rolls as well, please.”

     

                Lena fetched her credit card and slipped it to Alex, asking her to order extras for leftovers tomorrow - if it made Kara eat, she would’ve ordered enough for the whole week - and then made fresh cups of tea for them. Eliza excused herself for a work phone call as Lena walked back in and reclaimed her seat beside Kara, looking at her as she set her cup down on the coffee table. Kara didn’t so much as flinch at her movements.

     

                “Hey,” Lena murmured, waiting patiently for Kara to look at her and frowning when she didn’t even blink in acknowledgement. “Hey, come back.”

     

                She squeezed Kara’s let gently and watched her jump, blinking rapidly as she turned to look at Lena. “What?” 

     

                “You weren’t watching.”

     

                “It’s not that interesting.”

     

                “Oh … well, we can watch some else.”

     

                Leaning forward, Lena reached for the remote and gave her an expectant look. “What do you want to watch?”

     

                “I don’t care. Whatever you want.”

     

                “You pick,” Lena urged her, a warm smile on her lips, if a little forced, as she tried to keep her composure enough to not be overbearing and show her concern. 

     

                Truthfully, Lena hated to see Kara like this, so uninterested in everything, spending all of her time just laying there with a glazed over look in her eyes as Lena talked but she didn’t take in any of the words. It was like she couldn’t concentrate on anything, just kept replaying that night - that week - over and over in her mind, although she didn’t reveal that to Lena. Even when she was awake and her eyes were wide open, Kara relived it all - the blinding brightness of the explosions, the searing heat, the taste of blood and the suffocating weight of brick and metal and wood pinning her down. It was enough to leave her paralysed with the fear the memories brough, playing over and over again, like she was still there. It was as if she wasn’t really present in her body at all, a part of her still stuck in Afghanistan, and Kara didn’t think that part of her would ever come back. 

     

                “I don’t want to watch anything,” Kara admitted after a moment, her voice barely above a whisper.

     

                “Do you want to sleep for a little bit? Or listen to some music? I could read to you, if you’d like.”

     

                “No.”

     

                “What do you want to do then?”

     

                “I- nothing.”

     

                Her eyes were fixed on some point on the far ceiling, a defensive hunch to her curled up position, and Lena studied her for a long minute before she pressed her thumb down on the remote and turned the TV off. The room was plunged into silence but it was like it didn’t even register to Kara, as if Lena wasn’t even there. But if Kara didn’t want to do anything, then Lena would do nothing with her.

     

                Eliza walked back in a minute later and sat back down, not even questioning why the TV was switched off as she reached for a medical journal and thanked Lena for the tea, settling in quietly after sharing an understanding and somewhat sympathetic look with Lena. There was nothing any of them could do to help Kara, except support her and make her feel safe, loved, understood as she navigated her trauma in her own way. She was confused, hurting, guilty and angry, and although none of them knew the true story of what had happened, they were content to let her bide her time and process it until she was ready to tell them. In the meantime, they’d slowly help her transition back to the real world as smoothly and safely as possible. Trying to keep her grounded was proving harder than Lena had anticipated though.

     

                A lump rose in her throat and she forced it down with a gulp of hot tea before sinking into her own thoughts. No one spoke much until Alex and Kelly returned a while later with Chinese food and a chocolate pecan pie they’d bought from the diner while they were out as a surprise for Kara. Lena was grateful when she saw the spark in Kara’s eyes, the hungry edge to her lean face that had been missing since she’d been back, that old enjoyment for good food seemingly vanished. It was the most emotion she’d shown, after the initial tears, and Lena felt a flicker of relief at something familiar being instilled back in her.

     

                They ate dinner on the sofa, the coffee table spread with takeout boxes as a perfume of soy and ginger hung over them, but Lena barely touched hers even though she made a show of it. The whole time she watched Kara, her appetite making an appearance as she wolfed down dumplings and sweet and sour pork, egg rolls and wonton soup and fried rice. It felt good to see her enjoy something ordinary, unclouded by the pall her disappearance had cast over them all. It could have been any night at home, like many they’d had before she’d been deployed - albeit, mostly in National City - and that was enough to sate Lena. Once they’d finished, she took a thin slice of pie in an effort of solidarity, but, again, barely managed a mouthful as she toyed with it and watched Kara polish of a marginally bigger slice.

     

                After dinner, they watched TV again for a while longer, Alex putting on some old favourite of Kara’s that she deemed safe. It was an old musical, something that would have elicited a burst of singing for each song, loudly echoed lines a split-second before the actors themselves said them, but Kara was silent throughout it all. They hadn’t even finished the movie before Eliza suggested Kara get an early night’s sleep, the flight and homecoming wearing her out and her mother worried she would overexert herself.

     

                Eliza kissed Kara on the top of her head, lovingly stroking her blonde hair down with a sense of satisfaction, as if all was right in the world now. As Lena climbed to her feet and helped pull Kara up, Eliza squeezed her arm and Lena gave her a fleeting smile before she hurried to help bear half of Kara’s weight. It was an awkward trip upstairs, Lena trying to alleviate as much of Kara’s weight from her bad foot as possible, even though the staircase was too narrow for them to go side by side, and she finally gave up and allowed Kara to do it herself as she sensed her growing annoyance.

     

                Feeling a little flustered and helpless as she walked behind her, hands nervously waiting to reach out and grab her if she fell, Lena slowly followed her upstairs. It took a few minutes but they eventually found themselves in Kara’s bedroom - or rather, Lena stood in the hallway for a moment as Kara stood on the threshold, rooted to the spot.

     

                “Hey? You okay?”

     

                Shaking herself out of it, Kara hobbled inside and let out a weary sigh, “yeah. It just … it feels weird. Never thought I’d see this place again, sleep in this bed again.”

     

                She said it nonchalantly but there was a waver in her voice and her shoulders hiked up towards her ears, her taut back to Lena as she stopped in the middle of her childhood bedroom. Walking over to her, Lena laid a hand on her shoulder and kissed the heathered cotton of her t-shirt before resting her head against the nape of Kara’s neck for a brief moment.

     

                Fetching pyjamas for them both from the clothes Lillian had supplied them with, she helped Kara out of her clothes, eyes snagging on the patches covering wounds, covering stitches, the pinkness of new skin and the puckering of scars. Swallowing, Lena was quick, trying not to look, trying to avoid looking at the bandages binding Kara’s chest or the ridges of her spine, careful with the cast on her leg and the bandages on her hand. Pulling back the sheets, she helped Kara into bed and then quickly changed into her own pyjamas, avoiding looking down at the changes to her own body; while Kara’s recovery in hospital had helped her gain a few pounds, Lena’s general lack of appetite had left her even more wasted, a month of grief and emptiness and then worried hovering taking its toll on her.

     

                Gently climbing into bed beside Kara, feeling odd at the sensation, as if it should have felt wrong to slide between the pilled sheets, worn from use, the heavy comforter with its faded floral pattern covering them both for the first time in months. Turning to look at Kara, Lena took in the slightly drawn look of pain on her face and swallowed thickly.

     

                “Are you okay?”

     

                “Fine. Just … the pills haven’t kicked in yet.”

     

                “Oh.”

     

                Neither of them spoke for a moment and Lena hated the awkwardness of the silence, as if they’d forgotten how to be around each other. Lena ached to reach out across the few inches separating them in the double bed, craving Kara’s touch, but she didn’t though. She didn’t want to risk Kara pulling away from her, that sting of rejection an old wound for Lena that had never healed over, so, instead, she switched off the lamp and lay there with her eyes closed, listening to the quiet sound of Kara’s breathing. 

     

                She opened her eyes again at the jostling of the mattress and a small smile curled her lips as Kara pressed up beside her and threw an arm across Lena’s waist. Nestling in closer, content and that knot of unease loosening in her chest, Lena wrapped an arm around her and cradled her against her chest, pressing a kiss to the top of her head. She could have cried, her eyes stinging with the beginning of tears and she exhaled slowly, shakily, with relief.

     

                “I love you,” Kara murmured a moment later.

     

                “I love you too.”

     

                The simple act of hearing words exchanged a hundred times made Lena’s body go slack, the warmth in her chest a comfort as she held onto Kara and let sleep bear her away. Exhaustion knocked her out swiftly and she slept peacefully for the first time in a long while, no nightmares plaguing her until she was wrenched from her sleep by a muffled scream. It was still dark and she was disoriented for a moment, blinking owlishly as sleep clung to the edges of her mind like cobwebs. Kara had fistfuls of Lena’s shirt in her fists, her face pressed against the fabric as she let out a hoarse shout, her whole body rigid.

     

                Freezing for a second, helpless, Lena opened and closed her mouth, her tongue dry and useless as she tried to make a sound. The first time she’d witnessed this in the hospital, Lillian had told her to put some space between herself and Kara but she found herself pinned beneath her. Heart pounding in her chest as her skin prickled with alarm, a cold sweat sliding down her back at the thought of Kara thrashing around on top of her without being able to contain her, Lena slowly tried to wriggle out from underneath her. Letting out a choked breath as she managed to get her legs out and most of her upper body, except where Kara had buried her face in her shoulder, Lena cautiously pressed a hand to Kara’s taut back and lifted her up with her, slowly flipping them over and lowering Kara down onto her back.

     

                Her eyes adjusted to the darkness of the room, everything grey and shadowed, but she could see Kara’s face, screwed up and wet with tears. Straddling her, Lena slowly wrapped her fingers around Kara’s wrists and tried to prise her hands off her shirt as she spoke calmly, soothing, as if faced with a wild animal. There was a wildness to Kara’s struggling beneath her and Lena’s forehead pinched with worry, feeling out of her depth.

     

                “Hey, hey, it’s me. Kara, it’s Lena. You’re safe.”

     

                “No!” Kara yelled, and Lena winced at the loudness of the ragged shout.

     

                Hushing her as she tried to wrestle her hands off her, Lena struggled from the exertion as Kara starting violently writhing and thrashing beneath her, kicking her legs out as she fought against the heavy blankets, her arms hitting Lena’s ribs and waist and shoulders as she struggled. Grunting with the effort it took to try and tear herself free while making sure Kara didn’t hurt herself in her already injured state, Lena panted as she managed to loosen Kara’s grip on her and sit up, grappling to pin her arms as she stayed straddling her lap.

     

                “Kara, it’s okay. You’re not there; you’re home. You’re having a bad dream, okay? Wake up.”

     

                Her efforts to calm her unconscious mind were in vain and Lena softly cursed as Kara flailed around and struck the nightstand with her arm, the wooden furniture scraping against the floorboards with a low groan before the lamp teetered at the unexpected movement and pitched itself over the edge. The crash was loud in the silence of the night, and if Kara’s shouts hadn’t woken everyone yet, she was sure the sound of the lamp breaking did.

     

                The sound seemed to startle Kara into still silence for a moment and Lena let her guard down as she exhaled heavily, pulling back only for Kara to wrench herself from sleep with a sudden shout and a defensive attack. As she bolted upright, chest heaving and arms lashing out, she struck Lena’s cheek in a heavy-handed blow, the air rushing from her fiancée’s lungs as she grunted at the sudden, blossoming pain spreading across the left side of her face. 

     

                The effort flung Lena back and she felt out of bed with a further loud thud, elbows cracking against the floorboards first, painfully hard, before she landed on her ass, feet still somewhat tangled in the sheets. Pressing a hand to her numb and hot cheek, Lena stayed on the floor for a moment, trying to regain her composure as her eyes smarted with tears, before the door creaked open.

     

                There was a stillness to the room before Eliza switched the light on, looking pale and worn in the doorway, clutching at the front of a bathrobe as she squinted against the sudden light. Sitting upright in bed, chest rising and falling rapidly, Kara blinked away her confusion, eyebrows knit together, and peered through her bad vision to take in the sight of her mom in the doorway before her eyes glanced next to her for Lena and then further, finding her hazy form sprawled on the floor.

     

                Cheeks flaming with embarrassment, Lena slowly picked herself up off the floor, a headache already throbbing at her temples, and she couldn’t face Eliza as she turned slightly towards the door. “It’s fine, Eliza. I’ve got it. Go back to bed.”

     

                Hesitating, she nodded with a dark flicker of concern in her eyes and then shut the door, leaving the light on while Lena reached down to pick up the lamp. Moving over to the cluttered desk, Lena set it down there, far away from arm’s reach, and then walked towards the lightswitch beside the door.

     

                “I … I hit you.”

     

                Turning to look at Kara, still somewhat pink-cheeked, and took in the dawning look of horror on Kara’s face as she reached up to press her fingers to her parted lips, eyes swimming with tears. A tender smile softened Lena’s tired face and she reached for the switch.

     

                “It’s okay. Go back to sleep.”

     

                Plunging them back into darkness, Lena moved back over to the bed and climbed in beside Kara, reaching for her and letting out a small sound of protest when Kara shied away from her touch. 

     

                “I hit you,” Kara echoed, the horror in her voice making Lena’s stomach jolt as she hurried to reassure her.

     

                “It’s okay, I’m fine. That- it wasn’t you, you were just- you were dreaming. I’m sorry if I-”

     

                “Don’t,” Kara harshly interrupted, “don’t you dare apologise. I hurt you, I-”

     

                Inching closer as her face was torn with a pleading look, invisible in the dark, Lena reached out for Kara and pulled her closer. “Kara, please. Look, I’m fine, really. It was- it was a glancing blow. Let’s just sleep now, okay?”

     

                Kara let out a breathless sob which quickly turned into tears, until she was wracked with sobs, going willingly into Lena’s arms and soaking the front of her t-shirt with her tears as she murmured garbled apologies, over and over again, until she wore herself out. Tugging the blankets back over them, Lena murmured her own soothing words back and rubbed her back, until, eventually, the tears stopped and her sniffles subsided into the silence of early morning, a grey pre-dawn light already seeping in through the windows and birds twittering over the sound of crashing waves.

     

                Sleep seemed obsolete by that point but neither of them moved for another half an hour, until Kara sat up, her back to Lena as she hunched over and ignored the gentle questions. After a few minutes of being paid no notice, Lena threw back the covers and climbed out of bed, hesitating for a moment as if expecting some sort of reaction. Biting back a sigh, she knelt on the bed and leaned across the space to kiss Kara’s shoulder.

     

                “I’ll go and see if anyone’s awake to help you downstairs.”

     

                Kara didn’t even so much as look at her and Lena winced slightly, the left side of her face aching with a dull pain before she shook her head and slipped out of the room. She was quick going downstairs and found Alex sitting at the table alone, eating a bowl of Special K and reading a news article on her phone. 

     

                “What was going on in your room last night?”

     

                “Nothing,” Lena replied, short and bristling as she turned her right cheek to Alex, hiding the bruise she knew marred her pale skin. Closing her eyes, she ran a hand over her face and shook her head slightly, as if to clear her frustration. “Sorry. Uh, can you just- can you help her get downstairs?”

     

                Spooning the last bite of cereal into her mouth, Alex wraily nodded and climbed to her feet, carrying her bowl to the sink and dumping out the milk. Lena braced herself against the sink and listened to the sound of Alex’s footsteps disappearing upstairs before they returned again a few minutes later, followed by a slow and uneven set, one footstep louder than the other on account of the bulky cast.

     

                “How about you sit on the porch? It’s a clear day; the sea might do you some good. Been a while since you’ve seen that, right?”

     

                If Kara offered any reply, it didn’t fall on Lena’s ears, but all the same, Alex helped her out to the back porch and set her down on a shaded seat, the morning still damp, although the slight fog had already been swept out by the breeze. Slipping back inside, Alex came back for her coffee and Lena busied herself with making two fresh cups before she went outside to sit beside Kara, handing one off to her.

     

                “Are you warm enough?” she asked, reaching out for Kara’s good hand and feeling her cool fingers.

     

                No reply was forthcoming and her mouth thinned, but she didn’t press the matter as she took a sip of coffee, bitter and dark and hot as it slid down her throat. It was a long minute before Kara inhaled sharply and looked stoically out at the bluish waters, foaming as the waves rushed up the shore and greeted the thin band of golden sand beneath the swell of the sand dunes on their doorstep.

     

                “You should go home,” Kara hoarsely told her.

     

                “You don’t want to stay here?” Lena asked with mild surprise, her eyebrows rising gently. “I thought we’d stay at least a couple of weeks.”

     

                “I do. But … you should leave.”

     

                Letting out a sharp laugh, Lena looked at her with disbelief, her stomach curdling as her eyebrows drew together, the mere idea of leaving bringing a sour taste to the back of Lena’s throat.

     

                “I’m not leaving you.”

     

                “You should go … where I can’t hurt you.”

     

                Kara’s voice cracked faintly and she looked oddly sallow beneath her tanned skin, a muscle jumping in her jaw as she clenched her teeth and closed her eyes to avoid looking at Lena. Reaching out for her good hand, Lena threaded their fingers together and squeezed tightly, almost painfully tight. 

     

                “Look at me,” she firmly ordered her, setting her coffee cup down with her other hand and reaching up to cup Kara’s chin, forcing her to look at her. Kara stubbornly refused to open her eyes though and Lena exhaled sharply. “Kara, look at me,” she repeated, her voice softening, a gentle plea.

     

                Slowly, she opened her eyes, slightly unfocused without her scratched glasses, and furiously blue as they cut through Lena. She looked angry and upset, resentful even, but Lena didn’t care, staring back at her with adoration and love and sympathy. Lena watched as her eyes landed on the bluish-purple shadow of the bruise, almost black at the corner of Lena’s slightly swollen eye, and she let out a ragged sob, clapping a hand over her mouth.

     

                “It’s okay,” Lena murmured, cradling Kara’s face between her hands and giving her a strained smile as she thumbed away a tear.

     

                “No,” Kara objected, shaking her head as she closed her eyes. “I did this to you. Me. I did.”

     

                “It’s fine; it doesn’t even hurt,” Lena lied. “Honestly, you’ve seen me beaten to a pulp by a man twice as strong as me. This … it’s nothing. You were dreaming - you were asleep.”

     

                “But I did this to you, not some drunken … asshole,” Kara furiously whispered, her eyes full of tears and hatred, burning blue. Lena hated that she knew the hatred in her eyes was for herself and she wished she knew how she could take the blame away from her.

     

                “You didn’t mean to. Just like you didn’t mean to tickle me when I fell out of bed and needed stitches. It’s okay if you accidentally hurt me; I’m not going to run away because you had a bad dream and didn’t know what you were doing. What I’m not okay with is you trying to push me away; that hurts a hell of a lot more than a dumb bruise. Let me help you. Please.”

     

                “I’m sorry,” Kara whispered after a moment, looking down with such forlorn guilt on her face that Lena couldn’t stop herself from cupping her face and kissing her, trying to push all of her love for Kara into it.

     

                “I forgive you,” she said to appease her, although she didn’t think there was anything needing forgiving. “I love you.”

     

                “I love you too.”

     

                “Now, let’s get you some breakfast. What’ll it be? My famous pancakes?”

     

                Kara let out a croak of laughter, wiping at her face and picking up her coffee. “Sure.”

     

                Kissing the top of her head, Lena helped her to her feet and picked up her own coffee, considerably cooler but still warm as she chugged it down, and followed Kara inside. Monopolising the kitchen, she made pancakes for them both, and Kelly too, who materialised minutes later, her eyes widening a fraction at the bruise on Lena’s cheek, but made no comment.

     

                After nervously hanging around Kara, pouring syrup for her and refilling her coffee, cutting her food into bite-size pieces, Lena finally sat down with her own breakfast and Alex helped escort her sister back upstairs. Chewing her food with little enthusiasm, Lena barely even glanced at Eliza as she walked in, still feeling a little vulnerable at being caught so helpless earlier that morning. She was aware of her moving around the kitchen as Lena picked at her food and Kelly read a magazine that she’d swiped from the counter.

     

                When Eliza stopped beside her chair and sank down to a crouch, Lena looked at her, resigned and defeated. Giving her a small, crooked smile, Eliza reached out to gently turn Lena’s head, peering at the bruise.

     

                “How’re you doing?” she murmured, probing at Lena’s cheek with gentle, practical fingers, eliciting a sharp hiss and a wince as Lena’s lips curled back at the blossoming pain. “She got you good, huh?”

     

                “It’s not so bad,” Lena murmured, nose wrinkling slightly at the lingering soreness. "I'm fine."

     

                Clicking her tongue and giving her a dubious look, Eliza pressed an ice pack to her cheek and Lena brought her hand up to hold it in place. It numbed her instantly, the cold almost burning, and she hoped it would take away some of the discolouration. If she didn’t look so unsightly, maybe Kara would forget about it more easily.

     

                “Of course you are,” Eliza said as she pushed herself to her feet and squeezed Lena’s shoulder, “physically. But … it’s hard seeing her like this.”

     

                “It was harder thinking she was dead,” Lena callously replied with a shrug. “Nothing will ever be harder than that. I just- I don’t know how to help her. Kelly … she needs professional help, but I- it’s too soon. So what are we supposed to do?”

     

                Letting out a soft sigh, Kelly gave her a grave look, setting down the magazine and leaning back in her seat. “Right now, she just needs to feel supported. She’ll tell you what she wants, but otherwise … she’s going to be uninterested in everything, irritable at everyone, depressed, grieving. Her mood’s going to be erratic for a while; try not to take it too personally. But, otherwise, she’ll tell you when she wants something, if she wants to do something, so … let her reach out to you, okay?”

     

                Wiping at her damp eyes, Lena’s chin dimpled as she pouted slightly, looking down at her mostly full plate. “But … I’m scared that if I leave it up to her … she’ll pull away and I’ll never get her back.”

     

                It took a great deal of effort to stop herself from crying as her voice shook slightly, voicing her concerns to the two women before her. Kelly gave her a pained smile, understanding in her dark eyes as she reached across the table, touching the back of her hand.

     

                “I know. I work with a lot of veterans with PTSD; it’s not nice and it’s not easy. She just needs to figure things out in her head first, and even if she pulls away, she can’t do it without you.”

     

                Nodding as she drew in a deep breath and then blew all of the air out of her lungs, Lena pushed her plate away from her and pressed the ice pack against her cheek more firmly. “Right. Thank you.”

     

                “Make sure you look after yourself too,” Eliza gently reminded her, “you haven’t been sleeping again. There are four of us here; you don’t have to look after her by yourself.”

     

                Nodding again, Lena climbed to her feet and scraped her food into the bin before returning the ice pack to the freezer and getting started on the dishes. Eliza interceded and sent her upstairs, and Lena didn’t argue as she followed the sound of water pounding into the tub.

     

                Running a hand through her hair as she mounted the steps, she touched her fingers to her reddened cheek, feeling the coldness of it, the numbed pain of the bruising and swelling, and walked into the bathroom to find Kara sitting on the toilet seat while Alex tested the temperature of the water, bubbles frothing in the steam. Slipping away to the bedroom to fetch clean pyjamas for Kara, Lena returned a moment later, putting the clothes down out of reach of the water.

     

                “Alright, I’ll leave you to it,” Alex said, her eyes snagging on Lena’s red cheek as she wiped her hand on a hand towel and squeezed past her. 

     

                Shutting the door, Lena turned and moved over to Kara, sinking down to a crouch before her as she smiled up. “Right, let’s get you out of these.”

     

                It had been easier in hospital with the gown, and Eliza had been more efficient at helping her daughter while Lena helplessly hovered, but she still managed to get her clothes off with minimal wincing and twinges, before helping remove the bandages and get Kara into the bath with her plastered leg remaining out of it as it hung over the side.

     

                Lena was careful and methodical as she gently scrubbed her skin and washed her hair, and once she was done she bit back a sigh and gave Kara an exasperated look. “Hang on, I forgot to get towels.”

     

                She was only gone for a minute, but when she walked back in with clean towels in her arms, she froze at the sight of Kara standing before the sink, water and suds sliding down her bare skin as she held a pair of scissors in her hands and a chunk of mousy hair lay in the sink. Letting out a small sound of surprise, Lena hurriedly shook out a towel and moved to ease the scissors from Kara’s hand before wrapping the towel around her. Dropping to her knees with the other towel, abandoning the scissors, Lena dried off Kara’s bad leg thoroughly, trying to stop the plaster cast from getting damp, and then climbed to her feet with the scissors in hand once more.

     

                Standing behind her, she cleared her throat as she pulled Kara’s hair back. “How short did you want it?”

     

                “To what I just cut off.”

     

                Nodding as she pressed her lips into a thin line, Lena grabbed a hairbrush and eased it through Kara’s tangled hair before she took the scissors and cut it as evenly as she could. Even then, she was no hairdresser and it was far from a salon job, choppy and a little crooked in places, barely brushing her shoulders as it curled slightly, damp.
