Running her fingers through it, checking to make sure it was relatively symmetrical, Lena wrapped her arms around her and leaned her chin on her shoulders, smiling slightly at their reflection in the partially fogged over mirror.

     

                “What?” Kara asked as she met Lena’s eyes in the mirror.

     

                “I like it,” Lena whispered against the side of her neck, eyes creasing at the corners.

     

                Turning in her embrace, Kara smiled slightly and reached out to cup the back of Lena’s neck in her good hand, pulling her closer and kissing her roughly. Stomach jolting, Lena smiled into the kiss and pressed her gently against the sink, bracing her waist as she kissed her back for a moment.

     

                “I’ve missed you,” Kara whispered with a wispy sigh, leaning her forehead against Lena’s.

     

                Lena brushed her nose against Kara’s and let out a quiet, shuddering laugh. “I’ve missed you too.”

     

                She helped her dress after than and then showered quickly and dressed in the bedroom before helping Kara downstairs. The shorter hair looked strange, edgier and blunt, but she heeded Kelly’s advice - Kara would let her know what she wanted. If that was a butchered haircut, Lena was all too willing to oblige. Still, she could see the spasm of shock on three faces as she helped Kara through to the living room.

     

                “Your hair,” Eliza softly exclaimed.

     

                “It looks good,” Kelly encouragingly said with a smile, glancing at Alex and elbowing her until she got a similar response out of her.

     

                “We’re going to go and sit outside for a bit,” Kara quietly told them, ignoring the comments with a vague air of embarrassment as she ducked her head.

     

                Lena helped fetch her crutches and Kara managed to use them with some difficulty, unbalanced and too weak to manage smooth motions, but she managed to get herself outside and lean the crutches against the clapboard wall. Sitting down, Kara exhaled at the feeling of the cool sea air on her skin, briny and fresh. Lena draped a blanket over her lap.

     

                “Do you want tea? Coffee?”

     

                “Tea would be good.”

     

                Darting back inside to quickly make a round of tea, Kelly and Eliza accepting the offer too, Lena set cups down before them and then slipped back outside with cups for her and Kara and took a seat beside her. Setting one down safely on the arm of the bench, she kissed Kara’s cheek and sat back, cradling her own in her hand. Looking down at Kara’s hands, she saw her fiddling with something.

     

                “What’ve you got there?”

     

                Thumbing a ragged edge of the Polaroid she held, Kara hesitated before holding it out to Lena. It was dusty and creased, Lena’s face somewhat worn off it from days of smoothing her thumb over it, and Kara shrugged slightly, lips twisting wryly.

     

                “I looked at that photo every day. Sometimes … it was the only thing keeping me going. Especially- especially at the end. We were … in a cave. I thought we- well, I didn’t think I’d see you again. I just- I stared at the photo, waiting for it to be over. I wanted your face to be the last … sorry. I- I don’t think I want to talk about it anymore.”

     

                “That’s okay,” Lena patiently replied, her voice warm and soothing. “You don’t have to say anything you don’t want to.”

     

                Nodding, Kara held it out with emphasis and Lena took the photo from her. It was an old one, one of the ones from when they’d first met, and she smiled sadly - fondly - down at it as she smoothed her thumb over where Kara had done it a thousand times before.

     

                Glancing at her, face clouded with troubled thoughts and wariness, Kara jerked her head at it. “You should put it in the photo album with the others.”

     

                “There are still a few pages left to fill.”

     

                “And now we have all the time in the world for it.”

    Chapter 72

                Their first week at Eliza’s passed by quickly, with Alex and Kelly returning to National City after a few days for work - their shifts had been sporadic at best over the past month, with unpaid leave allowances for bereavement, and then to go to Germany - because they didn’t have Lena’s luxury of taking as much time off as they wanted. Lena arranged for her jet to drop them off and Lillian picked them up from the airport, sending Athena back on the jet with the private air hostess so she could head back to Metropolis for a few days to check in with her own business.

     

                The arrival of the excitable German Sherpherd seemed to awaken Kara though, some sort of light going on inside her as she was slobbered over and hounded for scratches under Athena’s chin and was brought tennis ball after tennis ball to throw from the back porch when she sat outside. Lena hadn’t even thought that a dog would be able to bring back some life to her, but she would watch from the doorway as Kara let out hoarse laughs, unusual when they’d been so common before, and cooed in a high-pitched voice, eyes creasing at the corners behind the new glasses Lena had ordered from her optometrists, as close to her old frames as she could find. 

     

                Still, even into the second week there, resting and recuperating as her bones slowly knit themselves back together and she indulged in as much food as she wanted to, a healthier glow to her fuller face and a more serene expression on her face, Kara was still uncharacetristically morose. Most nights she woke screaming and Lena would try and put as much distance between them as she could while simultaneously trying to calm her down, trying to stop her thrashing. It was more so out of concern for Kara’s feelings if she hit Lena again, rather than her own physical wellbeing if she was hit again. Most nights, Lena slept only a few hours, staying up after the nightmares to hold Kara as she cried herself back to sleep, whispering nonsense to her until the sun came up - old snatches of poetry, of essays, remembered monologues of TED Talk speeches she’d given, dialogue from plays or novels, lists of what she loved about Kara or what they were going to do. She got little sleep in those two weeks, but none of that mattered. 

     

                Eliza was back in work as well, her long hours leaving the two of them alone at home for the most part. Lena thought she would have craved being home alone with Kara after so long apart, but instead it just felt impossibly lonely, something she just couldn’t comprehend. Kara was the one person who’d always managed to make her feel anything but alone, and yet there was an insurmountable void between there that their shared ordeal had put between them, both of them on opposite sides of the experience.

     

                After she’d tidied up the kitchen that morning, she went to find Kara. She was wearing navy blue corduroy shorts, left in the closet from some previous stay, a faded tourist t-shirt from an old trip to Colorado Springs, and there was sand on her bare right foot from where she’d ventured off the porch on crutches. Leaning against the railing, looking golden with her tan and dressed for summer, she could have been ready for the beach, squinting out at the blue waves, her freckled nose wrinkled slightly, and Lena studied her for a moment, committing it to memory.

     

                “What do you want to do today?” she disturbed her eventually. “We could go somewhere. The diner maybe. The bookstore - there were a few new releases I think you’ll like. That new Sally Rooney book seems good.”

     

                “I don’t mind,” Kara replied, brushing her short hair out of her face as she tipped her face towards the sunlight filtering beneath the roof of the porch.

     

                It was a warm day, April already in the throes of spring, with flowers and bees and birds. Lena was hoping Kara would be well enough for a hike in another month, so they could go to that meadow they’d frequented, filling the place with Kara’s laughter once more. 

     

                “Well, what do you feel like doing?” Lena patiently asked, walking over to her and pulling her hair back, kissing the shoulder of her t-shirt. “We can do whatever you like.”

     

                Kara let out a rough sigh, leaning down to itch beneath the lip of the cast as she watched Athena run around the garden. “I don’t want to do anything,” Kara snapped, giving up on trying to reach the itch as she stretched her leg out and scowled at the horizon.

     

                “Alright,” Lena murmured, giving up easily, knowing better than to try and force her to do something she didn’t want to.

     

                Heeding Kelly’s advice, Lena resolved to sit on the porch steps and keep her silent company while she waited for Kara to decide. She knew she didn’t mean to snap and tried not to let the sting of it hurt her, instead choosing to focus on the sweet smell of the flowers in the garden, the dampness of the sand dunes and the sea and forest. It was a beautiful time of year to be in Midvale - it was everything else that was ugly about being there. Lena was trying to keep it together as best as she could, taking every bit of effort she had, but she still felt like she was failing at helping Kara.

     

                Brooding over her shortcomings as a fiancée, Lena kept coming back to the old argument of finding a therapist for Kara, someone good that Kelly would know, who could treat her without the unethical relationship her sister-in-law had with her. Still, Kelly’s help had been sound so far, if not exactly given as a professional to a client, and Lena spoke to her almost every day, hunting for something new to try and help. Once they were back in National City though, she’d get some real help, proper therapy sessions for Kara; Kelly would know a dozen therapists working with PTSD patients. 

     

                Lena’s thoughts were interrupted by the buzzing of her phone in her pocket and she glanced sideways and up at Kara before answering. It was her mom, calling once more to check in, and Lena felt that flicker of relief. It had been good to have someone to talk to who wasn’t personally involved in Kara’s life so that she didn’t have to keep her thoughts to herself. Meeting Kara’s gaze, she climbed to her feet and walked down the steps, further out into the back garden, to the beginnings of the sand dunes as seagrass brushed her legs.

     

                “Hi, mom.”

     

                “Hi, how’re you?”

     

                “I’m fine.”

     

                “And Kara?”

     

                Mouth thinning, Lena grimaced, “the same as ever. Sometimes she laughs, or asks if we can do something. Other times … well, it’s … it’s like she’s not even there.”

     

                “It’ll get easier. With time, it’ll-”

     

                “I know,” Lena brusquely cut her off, raking a hand through her hair, “I just- I want it better now.”

     

                She knew it was unfair to complain; thirteen people would never see their family again, yet she’d been lucky enough to get Kara back. Still, Lena just wanted Kara’s suffering to end. It was selfish and callous, but she didn’t care about those other people, and they were beyond help now - Kara wasn’t.

     

                “I know you do - of course you do. You just have to remember that we’re talking potential years to process this level of trauma. You don’t know what she’s been through, but you need to make sure you’re ready to deal with this.”

     

                “I am,” Lena defensively replied, her tone a little haughty as if her mother was doubting her commitment. “Of course I am; I couldn’t leave her even if I wanted to. Sometimes … I think I need her more than she needs me.”

     

                As Lillian started to reply, there was a loud bang as a car backfired a few houses down and Lena glared in the direction as she plugged her ear and pressed the phone closer to her other ear. “Sorry, what were you saying? A car-”

     

                She trailed off from explaining to her momas a loud shout cut her off from behind. “No!”

     

                Lena whirled around at the sound of Kara’s shout, finding her hunched over the wooden railing of the back porch, stiff and pale and unmoving. Lillian was still talking as the phone slipped through Lena’s fingers and she swore, running across the garden and thundering up the steps. She was hesitant to touch Kara, staring at her with wide, fearful eyes, while Athena excitedly brushed up against them both, wondering what the fuss was, trying to play as her tail thumped against the chair leg.

     

                “Kara?” Lena called out to her, her voice panicked as she took in the glazed and unfocused look on Kara’s face, her lips moving soundlessly, lost in some far away moment, somewhere else. It didn’t take a genius to figure out where her mind had gone.

     

                It was the car, Lena realised. The car backfiring with a loud popping noise, not quite the same as an explosion, but loud and startling enough to trigger the memory of that moment, triggering a flashback that sucked Kara right in. She didn’t seem to be aware that she wasn’t actually there as she gripped the wooden fence in a white-knuckled grasp, her face strained with fear and pain and horror in every line.

     

                “Mike, go!” Kara shouted, talking to a man that wasn’t even there. “Take him- take him and go. I’ll be right behind you. I’ll meet you- go!”

     

                Lena lowered her voice to a gentle murmur as she reached out, gently cradling Kara’s shoulders in her hands as she spoke. “Kara, you’re okay, you’re not there. You’re home. It’s Lena. Can you hear that? The sound of the ocean - you can smell it too. And look, feel. Can you feel that? It’s Athena, our dog. She wasn’t there with you; she’s here, at home, with you. I’m here too. We’re all home at your mom’s house. We’re all back together again. Can you hear me? Come back to me, my love. Please.”

     

                There was a tremor in Lena’s voice, small and weak, and she had to fight the urge to cry as she tried to guide Kara back. Her chest was heaving as she breathed heavily and Lena was worried it wouldn’t be enough, that panic still evident in her vlue eyes. But eventually, after a long minute, Kara’s eyes seemed to focus on her, confusion blooming on her face as the stiffness of her posture loosened minutely. She let out a breathless sob, clapping a hand to her mouth as her knees gave out and she slowly sank to the wooden decking, Lena reaching out to help guide her down without hurting herself.

     

                “Oh, God. I thought-”

     

                Sinking down to her knees beside her, Lena wrapped her arms around her shoulders, “it’s okay, you’re safe.”

     

                “It’s like … I was there . I was-”

     

                Cutting off, she couldn’t even finish her train of thought, her breaths coming so rapidly, so shallow and fast as she clutched a hand to her chest, that she couldn’t speak as she stared at Lena with wide eyes. She was shaking, a sheen of sweat on her face as she dragged in a lungful of air between trembling lips. Lena recognised it for a panic attack, although she’d never witnessed oen before, and she tried not to panic as she fumbled through her mind for a solution.

     

                “Okay, baby, take a deep breath for me and count to ten, okay? Can you do that for me? Breathe with me, okay?”

     

                Inhaling deeply as shetried to guide her, Lena started to count aloud, reaching out for Kara’s hand clutching at the front of her t-shirt and guiding it to her own chest. Lena held her palm against her chest, feeling her heartbeat - not quite steady, but not as fast as Kara’s - and exhaled slowly.

     

                “You’re not there; it’s just a memory. This place is safe - you’re safe. Can you lift your arms above your head for me?”

     

                Lena reached for his limp wrists and gently raised them above Kara’s head and then back down again, slowly. “Good. You try it this time. Just keep breathing. In and out. Copy me, okay? One, two, three … good.”

     

                Kara slowly started bringing her arms above her head and then back down while she breathed along with Lena’s counting. It took a few minutes before the panic attack started to subside, but soon her breathing had slowed and she wasn’t shaking quite as violently. Lena brushed damp hair back out of Kara’s flushed face and looked at her with concern.

     

                “I felt- I felt like I was … choking, like I was going to be sick,” Kara rasped, her voice hoarse from her ragged breathing. “Like I was going to d-”

     

                “You were having a panic attack. The car …”

     

                “The car,” Kara breathlessly murmured, closing her eyes and shuddering. “Can we go inside, please?”

     

                “Of course.”

     

                Lena pressed a kiss to her palm before climbing to her feel and helping haul Kara up, fetching her crutches for her and watching her make her way back inside. The sudden thought of her abandoned phonecall hit her and Lena called after Kara that she’d be a second before she ran back to find her phone in the sandy lawn, hoping her mom would be able to help.

     

                “Hello?” she breathlessly said as she put the phone to her ear, lingering outside so Kara wouldn’t overhear the conversation.

     

                Lillian hadn’t hung up, waiting to find out what had happened, and her voice came through sharp with concern. “What happened? Is everything okay?”

     

                “She- a panic attack. Some car backfired-”

     

                “I heard it. Is she okay? How often-”

     

                “First time. I- what should I do? Should I call Eliza?”

     

                “No. If it’s passed then leave it until Eliza comes home - I doubt Kara will want to be fussed over. And that goes for you as well. Just … keep her mind occupied, try and keep her grounded. Cater to her senses - strong flavours, strong scents, sounds and touches that won’t remind her of there. And make sure she breathes.”

     

                Making a mental note of the advice, Lena swallowed thickly, throat bobbing as she nodded. “Got it. Thanks, mom.”

     

                “Look after yourself too. I love you.”

     

                “Yeah,” Lena sighed, “I love you too.”

     

                Jogging back to the steps after hanging up, Lena quickly made her way into the living room and sank down before Kara, who avoided her gaze. Lips twitching with displeasure, Lena touched her knee and looked up at her with wide green eyes, full of worry.

     

                “I’ll be back in a second, okay?”

     

                Kara didn’t reply but Lena rose to her feet anyway and was quick to dash upstairs, gathering a pillow and a blanket, fishing out a dusty box from the closet while she was at it and carrying it all downstairs. She turned the radio on to a pop station in the kitchen, filling the ground level of the house with the staticky sound of synth, bass and snare drums, making mint tea and cutting up an orange into wedges.

     

                Carrying it into the living room, Lena set the plate down before Kara on the coffee table and pressed the hot cup into her palm, holding it there for a second. “Does that feel hot enough to you?”

     

                “It’s boiling.”

     

                “Okay, good,” Lena said, kneeling beside the coffee table and taking the lid off the box she’d brought down. “Smell it; it’s mint tea. Good, right?”

     

                Kara frowned but obeyed, sniffing the tea and shrugging indifferently while Lena unpacked a cardboard chess board and plastic pieces before turning on the TV and picking one of the anime movies Kara had made her watch at some point - the one with the big rabbit-like creature that Kara thought was cute and she’d forgotten the name of - and Lena put on the dubbed version to play in the background.

     

                “Take a sip,” Lena ordered Kara as she set the chess pieces on their squares. “Eat your orange too.”

     

                “Okay, what are you doing?”

     

                Lena didn’t look up as she set a pawn down, but she jutted her chin forward in a stubborn manner as she picked up a black knight and set it down. “What do you mean?”

     

                “Mint tea. Oranges. Ghibli movies. Chess. What are you doing?”

     

                “I’m trying to keep you grounded,” Lena meekly murmured, her cheeks reddening faintly.

     

                “What?”

     

                “My mom said that after panic attacks you need to keep your mind off things. Keep you grounded to your reality by focusing on your senses; strong smells, strong tastes, comforting sounds, hot temperatures. That way … you’ll know you’re here, and not there.”

     

                “Oh.”

     

                “Sorry, I just- I’m trying to distract you.”

     

                Kara opened and closed her mouth before taking a gulp of tea and picking up a wedge of orange and taking a bite out of it. Her gaze alternated between the movie and and Lena setting up the chessboard and she breathed deeply, slowly, evenly. There was a faint smile of amusement at the corners of her mouth and Lena was reassured by that, but was worried about what would happen if she lapsed into another panic attack. She didn’t want Kara to dwell on unsafe thoughts and quickly took over, explaining chess to her as if it was her first time playing, as if she was a child.

     

                She went easy on Kara and they played in silence for a moment, Kara not quite bad for someone who wasn’t a champion player - she’d definitely played a little before, or at least knew the rules and was strategic enough to plan ahead - and after draining her tea, Kara leaned across the space between them and kissed Lena gently.

     

                “You’re distracting enough, by the way,” she whispered before checking Lena with a crooked smile.

     

                Letting out a quiet snort of laughter, Lena shook her head and undid Kara’s efforts. Still she backed herself into a corner on purpose, letting Kara win, although by the unimpressed look she received, it seemed that she hadn’t been as inconspicuous as she’d hoped, and laughed as she reset the board with a shrug.

     

                The rest of the day was spent playing chess, Lena explaining certain moves to Kara, and watching movies. Pride and Prejudice came next, the sly look Kara shared with her reminding Lena of that first date to the movies, making her feel warm, her stomach fluttering with butterflies. Eliza came home in the evening with pizza and joined them in the living room mid-Disney movie, and Lena was pleased to see that Kara almost seemed liek her old self again, smiling and singing along as she made Lena laugh, eyes lighting up with joy even if she pretended she hated it, while Kara looked a little smug as she grinned.

     

                When it was time for bed, she let Kara make her own way upstairs while she tidied up, folding the blanket and stacking the pillow on top, feeling drained from the day. Eliza was clearing away the empty pizza boxes and studied Lena as they cleaned up in silence, before she broke it.

     

                “How was today?”

     

                “She, uh, she had a panic attack. A car backfired, she had a flashback, and then … I was on the phone to my mom; she said not to call you. Sorry if it was the wrong call, I just- I didn’t know what else to do.”

     

                “No, that’s fine, sweetheart. Your mom’s probably right - I would’ve been worried sick all day and fussed over her too much, which is the last think she wants. I wouldn’t be able to help myself; mother’s instinct. But she got through it though? She seems okay; were you okay?”

     

                Rubbing at her forehead, feeling unsettled as closed her eyes and exhaled through her nose, Lena swallowed. “I … tried. Tried to bring her out of it by talking to her - that seemed to work fine until the panic attack. That’s, uh, that’s what the movies and chess was for. My mom told me to keep her grounded.”

     

                “Smart woman, your mother,” Eliza smiled, cupping Lena’s cheek. “But are you okay?”

     

                “I’m fine,” Lena dismissively replied, a thin smile crossing her face for a brief moment. “I mean … it frightened me, but more so for her. I wasn’t sure what to do for a second. I thought … well, she was gone for a minute. I wasn’t sure if I’d be able to snap her out of it.”

     

                Gripping her shoulders, Eliza gave her an earnest look, “you’re both going to be okay. Okay? You’ll work through it.”

     

                “I know. I just thought … nevermind. I just hate feeling helpless, you know? Ever since I was a little girl I always had to answer or solution to everything and now …”

     

                “You’re still little; you’re twenty-five. You’re not helpless, you’re just young, and this is beyond what you should be dealing with. Both of you. No one your age should ever have had to bury the person they loved, grieve for them, be stuck with helping them heal through things like this. You’re not helpless, Lena - none of us are - and just by being here, you’re helping her. You’re stronger than you think. I think it would be a lot worse if you didn’t love each other so much, because this kind of thing … well it can ruin people, but the two of you wouldn’t be able to leave each other even if you tried. Maybe that’s not such a good thing, but at least you know you’ll come out of this together.”

     

                “I know,” Lena whispered.

     

                “Go on, now, you go to bed. You look exhausted; I’ll finish tidying up.”

     

                Nodding as Eliza pat her shoulder, Lena hoisted the blanket and pillow, balancing the chess box on top, and carried it up to the linen closet upstairs, returning it all back to their rightful places before she went to brush her teeth and made her way to their bedroom. She smiled as Kara met her eyes and quickly changed into pyjamas before flipping the light switch and crawling into bed beside Kara. Tonight, she just wanted to hold her, for her to know that she was safe and that Lena wouldn’t let anything bad happen to her.

     

                “Come here,” Lena whispered, tugging her closer until her head was on Lena’s chest.

     

                “I shouldn’t. If you get stuck under me again- what if I hurt you?”

     

                “Sh, you won’t. Just sleep, okay? I’m right here; nothing bad will happen. I’ve got you.”

     

                She kissed her in the dark, her lips warm and soft after weeks of chapped kisses, and the tension bled out of Lena as she breathed in the familiar smell of Kara’s perfume, a comforting smell, and held her in her arms, the feeling so natural that everything felt okay - just for that moment.

     

                “I love you,” Lena whispered into her hair, squeezing her just that little bit tighter.

     

                “I love you too.”

    Chapter 73

                They were into their third week at Eliza’s, and a whole month since they’d been notified of Kara’s reappearance, and yet, every day, Lena still felt like it wasn’t real. In the middle of the night, she’d wake up from a bad dream of Kara being gone again, only to find her fast asleep, curled up at her side, her head on Lena’s chest and fingers clinging to her shirt. Only then would she be able to sleep, for however briefly until the nightmares that plagued Kara inevitably woke her from the screaming and thrashing. Some mornings, if Eliza was home, she’d come in and sent Lena into Alex’s room to sleep and stay with Kara, holding her through the long hours until dawn crept in. Lena was grateful for those stolen hours of sleep, running on very little for the most part - it was was starting to catch up with her.

     

                Still, Kara had decided she wanted to return to National City now, despite Lena suggesting they stay a little bit longer, where Kara seemed more at ease. She was worried that the loud city noises and busy crowds might be too much for Kara to bear, thinking the empty beaches and sea air would be preferable, but Kara had insisted. So, of course, Lena relented and paid to arrange everything, packing their bags in the morning and enjoying one last breakfast with Eliza, until she was called away to the hospital. They weren’t leaving until the afternoon, which left an empty morning for them, sitting on the back porch as Kara tossed a tennis ball for Athena. Lena thought back to when she’d first adopted her to help combat her loneliness - now, it looked like she wasn’t the only one benefiting from that decision.

     

                Once she’d tired of the game, Kara rolled the sandy neon green ball between her palms, a clouded look of wariness on her face as her mouth turned down at the corners before she looked at Lena. “Hey, I- I need you to take me somewhere before we go.”

     

                “Oh, sure, okay. Anywhere.”

     

                Kara let out a short laugh, her mouth hitching into an uneven smile as her eyes creased at the corners, “I promise you, you won’t want to take me. I … I want to see it. My grave.”

     

                “Your- Kara. That is not a good idea,” Lena protested.

     

                “I told you,” Kara said with amusement before she turned solemn. “I think it’s be … good. For both of us. I might give us some closure, help but this whole … thing behind us. I don’t know, I just- I need to do this.”

     

                “You need to?”

     

                “Yes, I need to.”

     

                With a withering sigh and an eyeroll, Lena climbed to her feet and stooped down to give Kara a kiss. “I’ll get your shoe.”

     

                Kara insisted on them walking there, rather quick with her crutches these days, while Athena padded along on a leash. The weather was warming up considerably, less damp days of late, with summer not too far away, and they both soaked upthe sunshine as they made their way towards the cemetery. Kara had her old camera in hand, returned with the rest of her belongings, and she snapped a few photos along the way, a part of Lena relieved that she could still find the beauty in things around her, despite the horrors of war she’d witnessed firsthand. She was still Lena’s Kara.

     

                They made a detour on the way to buy flowers for Jeremiah’s grave, but it still didn’t take long for them to reach the acres of land studded with headstones and the little church nestled amidst the trees. They were silent as they made their way through the eerily quiet morning, Kara following the familiar path to the grave of the adoptive father she’d barely known. Lena followed with more reservations, dread pooling in her stomach as memories of that day, of the harrowing experience of burying an empty box in Kara’s stead, flooded back. It almost seemed like a distant dream - a nightmare - and Lena hadn’t been back since. Perhaps Kara was right and it would bring her some closure too, even if it was only the beginning of Kara’s healing. 

     

                They came upon her headstoen a moment later, grass already growing over the mound of earth where the whole had been dug for the empty casket. The fresh flowers placed on her grace had long since shrivelled up and been removed by a caretaker, no more to take their place not that Kara was back alive, but it was still an uneasy feeling to stand there, staring at the grave for a girl that wasn’t dead.

     

                “Oh,” Kara murmured.

     

                “Are you okay?” Lena hoarsely whispered, her throat feeling painfully tight at the memory of kneeling at the edge of the hole in the rain, reading the last letter from Kara. She slipped her hand into Kara’s and squeezed it tightly.

     

                “I- no, I don’t think so. I feel … strange. Not many people get to see their own grave, I guess.”

     

                “No. They don’t.”

     

                Kara raised her camera and snapped a photo of it while Lena’s brow creased with a perturbed frown, but she didn’t say anything. If she needed to take a photo of it, Lena would let her take a photo of it. Tucking it inside her pocket to let it develop, Kara stared at it for a long few minutes, while Lena took the flowers for Jeremiah and put them on his grave beside Kara’s.

     

                “I think … I’d like to leave now,” Kara slowly declared a moment later.

     

                Lena was quick to oblige and they were silent as they left the cemetery, a pensive look on Kara’s face as she swung herself down the street with her crutches, her previous enthusiasm for taking photos on the way there forgotten about. As regret for bringing her welled up inside Lena, she felt a flicker of panic and latched onto the first idea she had in hopes to bring Kara out of her thoughts.

     

                “Hey, how about some pie?”

     

                “Pie?” Kara echoed, her face lighting up a fraction as she smiled. “You know I’m always in the mood for pie.”

     

                Mirroring her smile, Lena angled towards the road into the centre of town and they made for the diner. It didn’t take long for them to reach it and Kara sank down onto a chair outside in the shade, Athena sitting dutifully at her side while Lena went inside to place their order.

     

                Rejoining Kara outside, Lena laced their fingers together and squeezed her hand, watching as Kara took in the view of people she’d known for half of her life walking about, some casting her curious looks, others absorbed in their errands as they slipped in and out of stores. Kara didn’t look at Lena, she just stared off into the distance, and the only acknowledgement she gave to Lena’s presence was a gentle squeeze of her hand. After the panic attack, Lena had tried to give Kara some space, but sometimes it hurt her to watch Kara ignore her, but she never complained.

     

                The waitress emerged a minute later, setting down two iced coffees and returning again with a tray bearing six different slices of pie. Kara let out a snort of laughter as they cluttered the small table, arching an eyebrow as she looked at Lena, roused by the smell of fresh pie.

     

                “You ordered all of them?”

     

                “I didn’t know what you were in the mood for. I figured I couldn’t go wrong with all of them.”

     

                “You spoil me too much.”

     

                “You deserve it.”

     

                They took turns trying all of the pies, drinking their iced coffees and chatting as if everything was normal, and each time Kara smiled Lena drank it in, treasuring it, wishing for the day when she never stopped smiling again. She watched as Kara scratched Athena behind her ears and fed her the crust of the pumpkin pie, making a quiet fuss over her before she looked up and caught Lena staring.

     

                “What?” she asked, perplexed as she smiled.

     

                “Nothing. I’ve just been thinking lately … you seem very relaxed around the dog. Like she makes you feel less … well, I think her being around helps, so I’ve been thinking that when we get home, I might register her as a service dog for you.”

     

                “A service dog?” Kara sceptically repeated.

     

                “Yes, for when you leave the house. You know, like one of those emotional support dogs. That way you’ll be able to legally take her in places with you - we can get her one of those little vests and register her online. I just thought that … well, if you find yourself getting anxious … maybe she’d help. I’ve heard it’s useful for military personnel when they … you know … go through things .”

     

                “Uh huh. And who did you hear that from?”

     

                “You know who I heard it from, otherwise you wouldn’t be asking me in that tone,” Lena countered, her eyes narrowing as she smiled wryly. “Of course I was going to enlist the family shrink’s help; we want to help you, and apparently dogs do that. I’ll even get you a new puppy - six new puppies if you want. As many as you want, if it helps.”

     

                “A hundred?” Kara goadingly asked, raising an eyebrow as she cut her fork through the slice of blueberry pie.

     

                Snorting, Lena rolled her eyes, “well that’s just unrealistic; where would we put them all?”

     

                “We’d buy a mansion, of course.”

     

                “Mm, grew up in one of those - they’re overrated.”

     

                Scoffing, Kara shook her head as she pressed her lips together, corners quirking up into a smile as she swallowed her mouthful. 

     

                “I’m still curious to see that place.

     

                “Ah, well, I’ll take you when you’re ready. It’s definitely big enough for a hundred puppies, you know, if you felt like it.”

     

                “But then who would look after our little girl?” Kara cooed over Athena, who climbed to her feet, excitedly wagging her tail as she put her head in Kara’s lap.

     

                Stroking her snout, Kara sobered up and looked up at Lena, “thank you. I think … you might be right.”

     

                Picking up her coffee, feeling a little more relaxed as Kara took her suggestion well, Lena leaned back in her chair and smiled crookedly. “When am I ever not?”

     

                Kara hummed in agreement and finished off the cherry pie while Lena nursed her coffee, content to sit and let her enjoy her food until they had to go. It was peaceful, sitting in the sunshine, the fresh air and bustling town around them, and it didn’t go unnoticed by Lena that it was the first time things had felt normal since Kara had returned.

     

                Eventually, they had to leave though, making the long walk back home as Kara started to flag, exerting herself on her crutches, even as she insisted she was fine. They beat the hired car to the house and had their bags stacked in the hallway when it pulled up, crunching gravel signalling its arrival, and Lena locked up and hid the spare key as Kara climbed into the car with Athena.

     

                The flight was short and Kara dozed through it all while Lena read on her phone and occasionally glanced up to check on her. She roused her ten minutes before landing, taking in Kara flushed cheeks and bleary eyes as she stretched, wincing as she became aware of her aches and pains, before they strapped in and touched down. It was a funny thing, but Lena found that she wasn’t afraid of flying anymore - what use was it being afraid of that when she’d already experienced her worst fear?

     

                Settling in for the drive through the city, Lena watched Kara as they wound through familiar streets, past her old haunts and favourite joints, the bodega they’d gone to in the middle of the night one time for a tub of Ben & Jerry’s, the Italian bistro that Kara thought served the best pasta, L-Corp, where it struck a pang of longing in Lena’s chest, being away for so long.

     

                When they pulled up outside the brownstone, Kara looked like she might cry, the air quietly forced from her lungs as she stared at the door through the windows. Helping her out of the car and fetching their bags, Lena gave her a small smile as they walked towards the steps.

     

                “Welcome home.”

     

                Kara smiled, reaching out to squeeze Lena’s arm, and reached for the door handle. Lillian had returned for a meeting with some boardmembers and Sam, keeping everything running smoothly while Lena was given the time to take care of her private life, so they walked straight inside, Athena padding ahead of them.

     

                “Mom?” Lena called out as she came in last and eased the door shut.

     

                “In the kitchen.”

     

                Lena dumped their bags at the foot of the stairs and grabbed Kara’s hand once she’d set her crutches down, frustratingly adamant she could maneuver around without them indoors, and helped her through to the open space. There was a slight loosening to her shoulders as Lena studied her closely, taking in the way Kara absorbed the familiar design, from the paintings to the brickwork, the table and the kitchen. 

     

                “Hi,” Lena greeted Lillian as she pulled out a chair and helped Kara down onto it. 

     

                Kara murmured her own greeting as Lillian gave her a small smile before surprise flashed across her face. “Oh! Kara, your hair …”

     

                Playing with the ends of it, Kara gave her a strained smile, “I needed a change.”

     

                “Well, it suits you. Can I get you something to drink?”

     

                “I’ll make,” Lena quickly interceded, shooing her mom over to the table. “Coffee? Tea? Water?”

     

                They weren’t particularly interested in the options so Lena grabbed three cans of LaCroix from the fridge, holding out the options of lemon or mango out to Kara and watching as she picked the mango one. Holding out the remaining two to her mom, Lena ended up with lemon and sank down onto a chair beside Kara, squeezing her leg before she opened her can and took a sip of seltzer.

     

                “You’re looking well,” Lillian commented, if a little awkwardly.

     

                “Oh, yeah, I’m fine, Lillian. I’ll be back on my feet soon; the foot should be all cleared in a week or so. How’re you? I know we didn’t really get to talk while I was in hospital; I think I was on too many pain meds. I wanted to thank you though.”

     

                Waving a hand dismissively as she let out an airy laugh, Lillian shook her head, “not at all. I was just glad to be of use for a change.”

     

                Snorting, Lena gave her a sceptical look, “you’re not planning on taking over my company, are you?”

     

                Clicking her tongue as her expression clouded, Lillian rolled her eyes. “You can have that back the moment you want to. It’s far too much work for my liking - CEO of Cadmus suits me just fine.”

     

                “Sam’s coping okay? I haven’t really spoken to anyone much.”

     

                “Understandably. She’s doing well, though. I’ll leave it in her capable hands from now on though; the jet’s all booked for this evening, so I’ll be on my way soon.” Lillian glanced down at the watch on her wrist before looking back up at Lena. “The fridge is fully stocked. I replaced some of your records too.”

     

                Face crumpled with confusion, Kara looked at Lena, “what happened to your records?”

     

                Wincing slightly, Lena gave her a sheepish smile as she shrugged. “I was … kind of angry. You know, when you- well … I couldn’t listen to music so I just- I … broke them?”

     

                “You broke your vinyl collection?”

     

                “Mm, and the TV,” Lillian drawled. “Replaced that too.”

     

                Sighing, Lena gave her mom a pointed look, “thank you. Send me the itemised receipt, why don’t you. Are you sure you won’t stay for dinner?”

     

                “No, I have a meeting in the morning; I’ll want to get a proper night's sleep. I’ve already ordered Chinese to be delivered at six for the four of you though - I assumed Alex and Kelly would be joining you.”

     

                Lillian left shortly after that, finishing her LaCroix and fetching her leather case. She’d ordered a car to come and pick her up, a sleek black Rolls Royce appearing outside on the dot, and she said goodbye to Kara before Lena walked her to the door.

     

                “Thanks for everything, mom,” Lena earnestly said, reaching out to hug her, still feeling somewhat odd about the act but not uncomfortable anymore. 

     

                Lillian kissed her cheek as she pressed a hand to her back, giving her a small squeeze. “Look after yourself, please. And call me.”

     

                “I will.”

     

                “And bring her to visit when she’s better.”

     

                Fighting the urge to roll her eyes, Lena nodded, “I know, we’ve already spoken about it.”

     

                “And give her that ring.”

     

                Lena let out a choked laugh of surprise and nodded, wrapping her arms around herself as she hovered in the doorway and watched Lillian make her way down to the car. She raised her hand in a wave as her mom wound down the window and waved before pulling away, and then Lena shut the door and disappeared back inside.

     

                Kara was sitting in the back living room, the one they’d rarely strayed into, and it felt deafeningly quiet in there as Lena sank down onto a sofa and put her feet up, turning her head to look at Kara. Eyes closed, she might have been asleep, chest rising and falling with even breaths, and Lena watched her for a moment longer before mirroring her pose. The house was warm and its old bones groaned in the heat, stretching and expanding while birds tweeted beyond the glazed windows.

     

                “What’re you thinking about?” Kara asked after a long while.

     

                Eyes opening as she blinked rapidly, turning her head to look at Kara, cheek sticking to the leather, Lena’s brow puckered slightly. “I was thinking about you.”

     

                “What about me?”

     

                Lena’s face softened with a smile, “just you - I’m always thinking about you. What are you thinking about?”

     

                With an impish grin, Kara wrinkled her nose, “dinner.”

     

                Letting out a loud laugh, Lena smiled as she sat up, checking the time on her phone. It was past five-thirty and she climbed to her feet, walking over to Kara and leaning down to kiss her. “It’ll be here soon. Shall we play some music?”

     

                “Did you break your Eagles record that you had?”

     

                “Baby, I broke them all,” Lena whispered with a clouded expression. “But maybe my mom replaced it.”

     

                Retreating to the front living room, switching the lights on and investigating her new TV - slightly bigger and a newer model - Lena rifled through the unorganised shelf of records, grimacing at the lack of a shelving system, and eventually pulled out one with a sound of triumph. Hotel California - an original 1976 copy. She carefully placed the record on the turntable and flooded the house with the sound of music.

     

                Kara wandered in after her and sat down on the sofa, a soft look of delight on her face as she closed her eyes and swayed slightly. There was a knock on the door a minute later and Lena went to answer it, Alex and Kelly standing at the top of the stoop and smiling brightly as she opened the door. She hugged them both and Alex immediately went to find her sister, while Kelly shed her jacket and hung it up, glancing expectedly at Lena.

     

                “How are you?”

     

                Lena knew she looked tired, pale, drawn. It wasn’t really anything new for her to be holed up inside without sleep, but usually there wasn’t the added stress of grief for a prolonged period of time to wear her down. Raking a hand through her hair as she blew the air out of her lungs, she smiled thinly.

     

                “Fine. She’s- well, not good , but … not bad. Just about as expected, I guess.”

     

                “I know how Kara is, dummy,” Kelly said, nudging her and then looping her arm through Lena’s, keeping her voice down as she dragged her out to the kitchen. “But how are you? You never talk about yourself.”

     

                “Well, I’ve never been one for that anyway. I’m okay, though.”

     

                “Yeah? You haven’t really left her side much.”

     

                Shrugging as she braced herself against the counters, Lena’s lips twisted ruefully. “I just- I didn’t think we would get anymore time together, but we do, so … everything else just seems silly when I remember that. She’s- she’s not in the best mood most of the time, and I know she doesn’t mean to snap, but I’m trying to make it easier without being too overbearing, you know? I just feel so … incredibly lucky.”

     

                “I get it,” Kelly murmured with a sad smile, “your wish came true - it’s not the same for all of us who lost someone over there. Just … take some time for yourself, okay? Tomorrow or next week, just … I don’t know, buy a new business, take a spa day, go shopping. Whatever it is you need to do to have some fun. Alex and I will keep an eyes on her.”

     

                Lena tried protesting as she fished out a bottle of white wine and opened it, Kelly fetching four glasses for her, and they quietly bickered over the benefits of her taking some time for herself, of getting some space for a few hours, while they poured drinks. It wasn’t like Lena was opposed to spending time alone - she’d had more than her fair share of that - but she wanted the fun things to be done with Kara, aiding in her healing process, things they could share together as they tried to work past this. 

     

                A knock on the front door signaled the arrival of their food a minute later and they laid the topic to rest as Kara limped in and Alex fetched the bulging bags, Lillian ordering far too much for them. Clustering around the kitchen table, they unpacked everything and took a glass of wine each, Alex making a wry comment about their being enough alcohol left in the house for that, brushed off by Lena, and they fell into easy banter and quick conversation, with Kara happily engaging in it.

     

                It felt so normal that Lena hoped to prolong the night for as long as possible, but Alex and Kelly didn’t stay later, leaving them to it with promises of dinner tomorrow night. Lena made two cups of tea once they’d gone and turned off the music, suggesting they watch a movie in bed so Kara could rest properly. 

     

                Carrying their tea up to the bedroom, Lena let Kara settle in while she quickly dashed upstairs and fetched her laptop from where it had been left to gather dust, and made her way back downstairs. They were both tired from their general lack of sleep and the trip back from Midvale and it was nice to lounge in bed, watching Dirty Dancing and drinking tea as they cuddled up beside each other beneath the blanket.

     

                They didn’t finish it, Kara’s eyelids growing heavy after a while, and Lena suggested an early night as she closed her laptop and set the dregs of her tea down on the nightstand beside it. Brushing her teeth and applying skin products to her face, she joined Kara in bed and watched her take the sleeping pills Eliza had prescribed her in the hopes that it would help. Lena had stopped taking hers in case it made her groggy when Kara needed her in the middle of the night, but she already slept better just for having her beside her, a warm reassurance.

     

                Trying not to jostle the mattress as she climbed into bed, Lena planted a kiss on Kara’s cheek and switched off the lights before she pressed herself up against Kara’s back. “Goodnight. I love you.”

     

                “I know,” Kara distractedly murmured.

     

                Lena could hear the warmth and tenderness in her voice but Kara didn’t say it back, silent for a long moment with the distinct impression that there was something on her mind, something she wanted to say before they slept. Patient, Lena waited a long minute before running her fingers down Kara’s arm as she pressed her face into her shoulder.

     

                “What’s wrong?”

     

                Letting out a soft sigh, it took Kara a few moments to reply, sounding embarrassed and uncertain when she did. “I was just- I was thinking about … well, we haven’t had sex since I’ve been home. You haven’t even tried- even asked , and I just- I thought … it’s- do you not want to?”

     

                Mouth opening and closing for a moment, her mouth dry and a wince of guilt crossing her face in the dark, Lena let out a resigned sigh. “No, I don’t,” she eventually admitted, her voice a slow whisper. “You’re right, but it’s just- you’re still healing. You’ve got casts and bandages and … I don’t think it’s a good idea. Not yet. Why? Do you-”

     

                “No, I don’t think so. I don’t know. I mean … yes, but also I can’t- I don’t think I’d be able to. It all feels a bit … numb.”

     

                “It’s okay,” Lena murmured, kissing Kara’s shoulder and brushing her hair out of her face. “We don’t have to rush anything;  you just focus on getting better. That’s all that’s important now.”

     

                She could feel Kara relax, as if she’d been dreading the conversation and was relieved by Lena’s response. It sent a stab of sadness through Lena, the thought discomforting, and she tightened her grip on Kara and kissed her shoulder again.

     

                “I love you,” she repeated, suddenly anxious that she hadn’t said it enough.

     

                “I love you too.”

    Chapter 74

                Two weeks later, Kara’s cast was finally removed from her leg. The weather had warmed in National City, muggy and oppressive, the magnolia tree outside scattering waxy flowers across the sidewalk and the sun a harsh light that greeted them earlier each day. Kara had made a small amount of progress, uninhibited by bandages or casts, although she still ached when she stretched her unused muscles, and they’d made an effort to go for a walk each morning at sunrise, with the intent of building up to sunrise jogs before the day grew too hot. They took Athena with them and being outside was good for them all, stopping at Starbucks for coffees on the way home, going to the park to see the riot of colourful flowers, passing down some of Kara’s favourite streets. 

     

                Of course, there was also the bad side to her recovery. Once when Alex had been over, she’d slammed a cupboard shut so loudly that Kara had stiffened in her seat, the blood draining from her face as she was dragged into a flashback, her ragged pleas and helpless blubbering as she sobbed over memories causing Lena to practically baby-proof the entire house, every door, cupboard, drawer and cabinet made to not slam in an effort to limit the things that could trigger her. The heat itself seemed to make Kara feel worse, sweating and crabby out the back, as if she was back in the desert heat, and while her nightmares were less frequent, the ones she did have were by no means calmer. 

     

                It was at least three times a week that Lena was woken by her thrashing and shouting, sometimes earning a knee to her stomach or an elbow to her ribs as she tried to calm Kara down. She kept it to herself if Kara was unaware of it, and it was a small win in Lena’s book - it wasn’t every night now, only most of them. It was a victory nonetheless, and they returned once more to the topic of therapy. Lena was insistent that it would help, with Kelly less pushy as she also tried to coax Kara into giving it a go, and in the end she relented and started visiting an old colleague of Kelly’s, who specialised in PTSD with army vet’s, enduring weekly sessions that she didn’t speak about with Lena. It was evident that she cried in her sessions though, red-eyed and embarrassed as she avoided Lena’s eyes when she came out afterwards.

     

                Lena still didn’t have much of a life for herself, despite her promises to Kelly to take a break, but she was obstinate and refused to admit that it was all taking a toll on her, no matter how much better it had gotten. She barely let Kara out of her sight, and definitely not out by herself, considering therapy for herself as a way to vent all of her pent up emotions, stamped down to the bottom of her heart to make room for the overwhelming relief and joy at having her fiancée home. It didn’t seem that she’d be able to fully process it unless she gave herself the room to do it, but with so much going on, Lena didn’t even have the time.

     

                Still, that hour that she sat in the comfortable reception area of Kara’s therapist office was like her own reprieve from her life, listing to a Podcast in one of the waiting chairs while she waited for Kara to emerge. Afterwards, they would get lunch, trying the tacos at a nearby Mexican food truck, bibimbap at a Korean restaurant or an assortment of pastries and desserts from a bakery to take home instead. She never pushed Kara to do anything she didn’t want to, but Lena had hoped she’d show more interest in doing things again, now that she was off her crutches, but the only real interest she had was in her photography. Lena was even more thankful she’d made the decision to turn one of the spare rooms into a little dark room and photography space for Kara, and she often shut herself in there, toying with her cameras or developing photos, although Lena didn’t see the outcomes.

     

                On a Friday night, after work, Alex and Kelly came over with board games and a stack of pizzas, and they all stayed up relatively late as they played Monopoly and drank beer, the windows open to let in the warm night and the hum of the city. There was a lot of laughter and it felt good , leaving Lena feeling lighter than she had in days, the responsibility of two people’s happiness and wellbeing and mental health momentarily shared between two other people, lightening her load - although she never would have called it a burden - and she lounged on the floor, sipping Corona from a bottle with a wedge of lemon as she laughed at Kara and Alex’s bickering over whether or not the latter was allowed out of jail yet.

     

                When they left, close to midnight as a cab idled outside the house, Kelly lagged behind with Lena as they made their way towards the door, the sister’s already ahead of them as Alex shrugged on a leather jacket.

     

                “You look tired.”

     

                “This is the latest I’ve stayed up in weeks,” Lena said with a weary smile, rubbing at her eyes.

     

                “Yeah, but, I mean … more than that. I’ve said before, you know, if you want to go out and do something for yourself, we’ll watch her.”

     

                Biting back a huff, Lena’s mouth thinned and she reached out to squeeze Kelly’s arm, “thank you, but I’m fine.”

     

                Stopping, Kelly pulled Lena to a stop as well, a worried look on her face as she frowned. “Lena, you are not fine. You’re burning yourself out; it’s not going to help either of you if you do that. Trust me-”

     

                “I know you mean well, but … this is my relationship; it doesn’t include four people. I love you and I wouldn’t have been able to get through … everything, but right now, I just- I need you to stop , okay? I’m trying to fix my own shit as best as I can, and I know this is your job, but stop psychoanalysing me. Seriously. I’m fine.”

     

                “Oh … well,” Kelly murmured, blinking in surprise as hurt flashed across her face. “Alright then.”

     

                Heaving a sigh as immediate remorse slammed into her, Lena reached out to grab the cuff of Kelly’s shirt, a pained look on her face. “Kelly-”

     

                “No, it’s fine.”

     

                “I’m sorry. I just- I need to do this by myself, because if I- if I can’t help her, then I can’t marry her, so just … leave it alone. Please.”

     

                Giving her a tight smile, Kelly nodded, her dark eyes bright even though she was gracious enough to forgive Lena for her rebuke. It was unwarranted and Lena felt her stomach lurch as her tongue tripped over itself, trying to form a better apology, voice her reasons in some way that didn’t hurt one of the only people she genuinely loved. 

     

                “I’m such an asshole. I didn’t mean- I’m sorry.”

     

                “Don’t sweat it,” Kelly murmured, pulling her into a quick hug and rubbing her back as tears stung Lena’s eyes. “This is just- this is what I mean. You need a break. Soon.”

     

                Swallowing as Kelly pulled back, her eyelids fluttering shut, Lena exhaled as she slumped. Kelly followed Alex outside and Kara stared at Lena, her expression unreadable but leaving no doubt that she’d heard Lena’s words - all of it. Raking a hand through her hair, brimming with frustration, Lena dug the heels of her palms into her eyes as she stood in the hallway, feeling the warm caress of the late night air.

     

                “Sorry, I, uh, I didn’t-”

     

                “Don’t worry about it. Let’s just … go to bed,” Kara murmured, shutting the front door.

     

                She passed by Lena and walked upstairs, while Lena went into the living room and gathered beer bottles for recycling and straightened pillows, tidying up. After she was done, she found herself still too wound up to sleep and slipped downstairs to the gym. Donning her boxing gloves, she punched the hanging boxing bag, the collision of her fist with the heavy bag feeling good as if swung away from her. 

     

                Punching until her arms were dead and she was covered in sweat, breathing heavily, Lena tore the velcro strips and pulled the gloves off before draining a bottle of water in the fridge and making her way upstairs to the bedroom. Fetching clean pyjamas, she showered quickly, the smell of Kara’s soap unwinding any lingering tension from her spent muscles, and she climbed into bed afterwards. Putting her back to Kara, she breathed slowly, sinking into the mattress, and closed her eyes. A moment later, she felt Kara’s arm wind around her waist and swallowed the lump that closed off her throat as she pressed back against her, feeling a little ashamed for her feelings.

     

                She slept a little easier with Kara’s warmth beside her, and there were no nightmares that night, both of them feeling well rested in the morning as they woke past sunrise. They were rather quiet as they made breakfast together, Kara scrambling eggs in a skillet while Lena buttered toast and poured orange juice into glasses. Feeling a little awkward after the night before, feeling the need to explain what Kara might have overheard but unsure of how to broach it, Lena glanced at her frequently, but each time she opened her mouth to speak, she quickly shut it again. She didn’t want Kara to think that she was complaining - she was just frustrated and tired, but that didn’t mean she resented looking after her. Not even for a second.

     

                They ate at the kitchen table and afterwards they cleaned up, Kara washing the dishes while Lena dried them off and put them away. Wiping her hands on the dish towel before handing it over to Kara, she smiled encouragingly, eyebrows rising.

     

                “Walk?”

     

                Wiping her hands and setting the towel down, Kara reached out and tugged Lena closer by the hem of her shirt, a wavering, playful smile on her lips as her eyebrows rose imperceptibly. “Actually … I was thinking we could go for a hike. Maybe take a picnic. You, me, Athena, our spot.”

     

                “Our spot?” Lena echoed, mildly surprised at her desire to do something. “Okay, sure. Let’s- you shower and I’ll pack some food.”

     

                As soon as Kara disappeared upstairs, Lena was a flurry of excited activity, snagging fruit out of the fridge, trail mix and chips out of the pantry, bottles of water and seltzer and hastily making sandwiches with what her mom had stocked the fridge with, and crammed it all into a tote bag. Fetching a blanket that would suffice for a picnic, she went upstairs and fetched her own clothes, opting for athleticwear and hoping it wouldn’t be too hot for it, before she took Kara’s place in the shower and watched her fiancée brush her teeth through the foggy glass of the shower door.

     

                Pink-cheeked from the hot water, Lena pulled her damp hair into a ponytail after dressing and slathered sunscreen on her pale face before washing her hands and lacing on a pair of running shoes. She jogged downstairs to find Kara waiting, hiking boots and cut off shorts paired with an old t-shirt with a hole in the neck and a plaid shirt knotted around her waist. She was holding Athena’s leash in her hand and had her old Polaroid camera hanging around her neck.

                

                “Ready?”

     

                Beaming as she nodded, Lena grabbed her keys and locked up behind them before unlocking the Porsche and stowing the bag and blanket in the trunk. With the windows rolled down and the radio on as it broadcasted Leslie Willis’s show, they drove out of the city and onto the highway, Lena heading towards the dusty foothills as they sped through traffic.

     

                The drive went by fast and soon enough she was pulling over at Kara’s direction, down a sliproad and parking on the side of the road, hoping no one came along and decided to steal her car. Athena jumped out as soon as Kara opened the back door, sniffing around while Lena fetched their food and blanket, and she bounded over at a whistle and the trio set off through the trees. Lena trusted Kara’s unfailing sense of direction as they walked, the dog forging ahead and then trotting back, tongue lolling and the occasional bark splitting the serenity of the woods as birds flitted through the canopy shading the way and the trees rustled in the breeze. Holding hands, they navigated their way around trunks and over roots, chatting easily and laughing as they breathed in the fresh air, the distance from the smoggy, packed city rejuvinating them both. Even when they fell silent, Kara hummed or whistled, and Lena inhaled deeply, feeling like she could breathe properly.

     

                The click of a camera, a quick flash and the subsequent chugging sound of film printing caught her attention and she whipped her head around to look at Kara, wary amusement clouding her face. Kara just gave her an easy grin and tucked the developing square into the pocket over the breast of her t-shirt.

     

                After a few minutes, Kara pulled it back out and stared down at it, a smile stretching across her face. “Perfect.”

     

                Lena latched onto her arm and craned her neck to peer over her shoulder at the photo of herself, staring ahead, oblivious. Snorting, Lena rolled her eyes and quickly whipped the strap of the camera over Kara’s head, backing away as she held it up to her eye. Before she could take a photo, she tripped over a log and let out a yelp as she keeled over backwards, landing on the leaf-strewn ground while Kara threw her head back, hands pressed to her chest and eyes screwed shut as she laughed loudly, unhindered by any dark memories, any lingering grief and guilt and pain. It was pure, unadulterated mirth and Lena grinned to herself as she raised the camera and snapped a photo of it, blinking back tears at the swell of love in her chest as she vowed to one day make Kara laugh like that again every day.

     

                Laughter subsiding into chuckles, Kara helped Lena to her feet and kissed her quickly, before Lena returned her camera to her and they ducked their heads together over the photo to take it in. Safely tucking it into her pocket with the other one, Kara steered them onwards, the sloping ground heading uphill as patches of sunlight and shade dappled the way.

     

                Eventually, they stepped out into the crescent of a meadow perched on the edge of the ravine, and as Lena looked around at the grass studded with wildflowers and the cerulean sky overhead, the sound of the slow moving river below them, she could have believed they’d never left that place and had dwelled there since the last time they’d come, so many months ago now. Spreading the blanket out and dropping her bag down onto it, she walked over to the edge of the sheer cliff and looked down at the water, smiling as arms snaked around her waist.

     

                “Don’t drop your camera in again.”

     

                “Why? Wouldn’t you go in and get it for me anymore? Was that all part of your plan to woo me, and now you have me you don’t have to try anymore?” Kara joked, her embrace tightening around Lena.

     

                Turning around in her arms, forcing her back a step to stay clear of the edge, Lena brushed Kara’s hair out of her face and hummed dubiously before reaching out to adjust her slightly wonky glasses and kiss the tip of her nose. “I’ll never stop trying.”

     

                Kara kissed her properly and Lena pushed back against her lips, cupping the back of her neck and smiling at the memories of coming here with Kara the first time, when they’d first started dating, the act of kissing her so new and nervous, but just as thrilling. Breaking Kara’s grip on her, Lena laced their fingers together and gave her hand an insistent tug.

     

                “I’ve got something for you.”

     

                She towed her back towards the blanket and felt around in the tote bag for the small velvet box. Barely able to contain her smug excitement, she presented the box to Kara with a flourish. “One Luthor family heirloom, as promised. Courtesy of my mom who you shockingly did manage to charm in the end.”

     

                Kara let out a snort of laughter and opened the box, staring down at the sapphire and the starburst of diamonds on the gold band. Removing it from the box, she hesitated and Lena took it from her, sliding it home, fitting surprisingly well considering she hadn’t had it altered from her mom’s ring size. Beaming with pride, Lena looked down at it as she cradled Kara’s hand in her own, taking in the glow of delight on her fiancée’s face as she peeked at her and then looked back down at the ring.

     

                “Let’s get married,” Kara suddenly declared.

     

                Choking on a laugh, Lena arched an eyebrow as she squeezed Kara’s hand for emphasis, “I believe we already are .”

     

                “Let’s get married now . Today. Next week. Now.”

     

                Spluttering as her eyes widened, Lena’s face crumpled with confusion. “What? Is this- is this about what I said last night? Because I didn’t mean it like that - I meant that I wanted you to get better so that things could be okay in the future, so we can have a happy life. I didn’t mean I wouldn’t marry you if you didn’t- if you didn’t get better. I don’t care if it takes five years, ten years or fifty years - I’m not going anywhere.”

     

                “I know. But … I want to marry you. That thought was the singular thing that got me through it, and I just- I don’t want to waste time. Let’s get married - before something else goes wrong.”

     

                A shadow of regret passed Lena’s face, “Kara-”

     

                “You don’t want to,” Kara said, pulling back slightly as she failed to keep the sting of hurt out of her voice.

     

                “Look, I don’t give a shit about how we get married. But we deserve a day of celebration, with our family and our friends and all the people who love us. I want to marry you more than anything in this world, but I don’t want it to be some rash decision; I want a special day, with the love of my life that I never thought I’d find, a thousand peonies and a white dress. We deserve a day like that after everything.”

     

                Sighing as she pitched forward, forehead resting against Lena’s, Kara grimaced. “You’re right.”

     

                “You’re still getting used to being home, but … if this time next year you decide you want to run off and elope, then we’ll do it. If you’re sure, I’ll- I’ll whisk you away to Tuscany and we’ll … eat big bowls of pasta and drink lots of wine and get married in secret. I love you. I love you more than anything else in the world, and if that’s what you want, I’ll give it to you, but … there’s a lot going on right now.”

     

                “Yeah,” Kara murmured, pulling back and cupping Lena’s chin before she kissed her fleetingly, “I love you too.”

     

                Kara eyed her ring for a minute in the sunlight, a softness to her face as her cheeks dimpled and her eyes creased at the corners and then she looked at Lena and let out a unabashed laugh, taking the sandwich offered to her and sprawling back on her elbows.

     

                Athena found a stick and they took turns tossing it for her, and Kara took photos of flowers and trees and of the dog, but mostly of Lena, who was content to sit and watch her. They stayed all afternoon, leaving late, when sunset wasn’t too far off and the days longer, stomachs rumbling for dinner and the thought of takeout on the way home aiding their trip back to the car, which was thankfully still waiting for them.

     

                Picking up shawarma on the way home, the night considerably cooler as Lena queued at the food trunk while Kara waited in the car as the early nightlife was loud in the busy street, and then they went home, eating out the back as they watched the last streaks of sunset overhead before a few stars managed to pierce the veil of light pollution. Lena was proud of Kara, of how she’d stayed out the entire day, no flashbacks or panic attacks, and any intrusive thoughts seeming to be dismissed beneath the expanse of sun as she’d laid on her back and tanned. It had been as perfect a day as she could have hoped for and she voiced her thoughts to Kara, who smiled crookedly.

     

                Feeling sticky from sunscreen and sweat, the heat of the day still clinging to her, Lena crumpled up the tin foil and grabbed Kara’s trash as she climbed to her feet. “I need a shower.”

     

                Kara hummed in agreement and as Lena made her way upstairs and started the hot water, stripping off her workout clothes and stepping under the showerhead, it was with a flicker of surprise that she watched Kara walk into the bathroom and strip off, joining her.

     

                “Oh, I-”

     

                Lena didn’t get another word out before Kara’s lips came down on hers, a spray of water blinding her momentarily as she was pushed up against the cold tiles, goosebumps breaking out on her skin as she was pushed out from under the water. A breathless laugh got caught in her throat as she gasped Kara’s name, fingers knotting in her hair and eyelids shuttering at the feeling of kisses trailing down her neck. 

     

                She could have stayed in that shower all night, craving the intimacy of the simple act of showering together, hands everywhere and kisses placed to bare skin, but at some point the water was shut off and they carelessly let their wet skin soak into the linen bedsheets, heedless of the discomfort it would bring, come bedtime. That was the last thing on their minds though, and Lena luxuriated in the relief and release sleeping with Kara brought, realising just how desperately she’d missed her touch. 

     

                It was late and she was exhausted when Kara collapsed on top of her, the weight of her comfortable and warm as Lena loosely encircled her waist and stared up at the ceiling. Kara’s fingers threaded through her tangled hair and her warm breath ghosted against Lena’s bare chest, slowing with each passing second as their heartbeats calmed. Lena felt the pleasant hum of contentedness in her heavy limbs and it wasn’t until hot tears fell onto her skin that she realised Kara was crying, and that feeling was banished as she startled, pushing herself up slightly as she cradled Kara to her chest.

     

                “Hey, what’s wrong? Did I- did it hurt you?”

     

                Kara let out a tearful laugh and swiped a thumb across her eye as she sniffed. “No, no, it didn’t hurt. I just- I love you so much. I’ve … missed this.”

     

                “Oh,” Lena softly exclaimed, settling back down. “Yeah. Me too.”

     

                Neither of them moved for the rest of the night, and Kara fell asleep in Lena’s arms, feeling safe and loved in her warm embrace. Lena similarly slept peacefully, and they didn’t stir until the sun peeked through the drawn curtains the next morning, well past dawn as they slowly woke, hands lazily trailing over soft skin, murmuring to each other and pressing kissed to palms and shoulders and cheeks as they stayed wrapped up in the lazy morning in bed for as long as possible.

    Chapter 75

                Lena returned to L-Corp a week later at Kara’s urging, normal life creeping back in and dragging her back to her office at the top of the skyscraper, her desk vacated of all of Sam’s things and a million emails and post-poned meetings for her to attend to as she navigated her way back into the business with slight difficulty. It was a jarring change of pace for her after months of absence now, but Lena was nothing if not efficient and intelligent, picking up the thread of things with Sam’s help as her CFO helped her transition back into her role as CEO, staking her claim in all of the new projects, proposals and conference meetings.

     

                She kept to strict work hours, not arriving at the office until the tardy employees had made their way up to their respective floors and not staying a minute past the time when everyone clocked out for the day. It was still exhausting though, but it provided some much needed routine and normalcy to Lena’s life, and gave her and Kara some space to themselves. As much as they loved each other and felt anxious being parted, it was a necessary part of ordinary life that Kara had to adjust to life back home without relying on Lena, and Lena had to resume her job as CEO and owner of L-Corp and take care of herself as well.

     

                It didn’t stop her from going home on her lunch breaks to spend it with Kara, or meeting her at a local salad bar of café with Sam, or Alex or Kelly, trying to incorporate other people into Kara’s daily life so that she’d feel more comfortable being out in public. It was a big adjustment for them both but it felt more normal and they had things to talk about when Lena got home from work at night, Kara taking over organising dinner, greeting her with the smell of sizzling steaks or homemade curry Kelly had helped her make. It began to feel like this was what their life together would be like, the sort of future Lena could envision for them - albeit, with a lot of time and assimilating.

     

                It was just past lunch when Lena called her mom, returning to the office and sitting behind her desk as wide swathes of sunlight filtered in through the windows, warming her back as she listened to her phone ring.
