Lillian answered on the third ring and they exchanged the necessary pleasantries before her mom cut to the chase.

     

                “How’s work?”

     

                “It’s okay; the same as ever, I guess.”

     

                “Yes, I know what the work is like, but how are you doing being back?”

     

                “Fine,” Lena said, rolling her eyes as she tapped her fountain pen on the desk. “I leave when everyone else leaves - you’d be impressed. I think … it’s good for us both to have some time away from each other to adjust back to normal life. Kara’s happy with it, at any rate.”

     

                “Are you?”

     

                Lena’s lips twitched and she swallowed a sigh, “sure. I mean, I spend most of my day worrying about her, but she’s getting better. She still acts like nothing happened, which is probably why she was so eager for me to come back to work. She acts as if she never left, didn’t almost … die. I don’t want to force her to confront it but … well, she’s going to therapy, which is more than I’d hoped for. And you thought I was stubborn.”

     

                “I can guarantee you the only reason she’s going is because you’re so stubborn.”

     

                “Mm, probably.”

     

                “She missed out on a lot of things while she was gone though - not just while she was missing - and she can’t pretend that chunk of her life didn’t happen. Didn’t you say she catches up on all the movies and TV shows she missed while she was away? Maybe you should try something like that to help her come to terms with the fact that she was gone.”

     

                “What, should I buy a copy of every newspaper and magazine that was printed while she was gone so she can catch up on the not-so-current affairs of our esteemed nation,” Lena sarcastically replied.

     

                “If that’s what it takes to remind her of everything that’s changed,” Lillian exasperatedly replied, “she’s not going to open up to you until she’s ready; a gentle reminder of what she missed out on, something engaging, can’t hurt.”

     

                “Mm, maybe you’re right,” Lena murmured as a plan started forming in her mind.

     

                The phone call turned to other topics after that, Lena asking Lillian for her opinion on a few of the projects that had progressed while she’d been away. Her mom had spent that past two weeks working with Lena via phone calls and video calls to bring her up to speed on what she’d been involved in with Sam to try and aid Lena in a smooth takeover, and Lena had to admit that she was impressed her mom had stuck to the projected timeframe and half-finished plans Lena had left beind. It was something she was grateful for. 

     

                They ended the phone call with hesitant promises that Lena would try and make it to Metropolis soon, and at the very least would call Lillian again in a couple of days, keeping in touch. It felt strangely comforting to know that her mom wanted to know the smaller details of Lena’s life and she knew that she would find the time to call, and if Lillian happened to call her, she’d answer it these days without hesitation. 

     

                Working through the afternoon and leaving a little earlier than usual, Lena made half a dozen stops on the way home at various stores around Downtown before driving home. She let herself in, laden with an armful of bags and caught the tail end of a conversation between Kara and Alex as she quietly eased the front door shut, trying not to eavesdrop but making little effort to not .

     

                “Well, I don’t know, maybe moving would be a good idea,” Kara hedged.

     

                “It’s a good promotion offer for me - management positions are hard to come by, and the pay rise would be nice. I just- Kelly isn’t sure . She has the practice here, and even though all of her family is over that side, I don’t know if she’d pack up and leave. I think she thinks I won’t pack up and leave you .”

     

                “It’s a good opportunity, Alex.”

     

                “You’re right, but I don’t think I could move to Metropolis right now.”

     

                Kara let out a strained laugh, “I could. I wish I could start over somewhere new. Tomorrow.”

     

                Lena felt a lump rise in her throat and she shut the front loud enough to announce her arrival, rustling the bags and kicking off her shoes as she let her keys clatter onto the console. “Hey, I’m home!”

     

                The conversation cut off and she slipped through to the kitchen, smiling at the sister’s as she set her bags down on the counter. Shrugging off her coat, Lena walked over to Kara and dropped a kiss on her head. 

     

                “Hi. Good day?”

     

                “Mhm. Boring and uninteresting. What’ve you been buying?”

                

                “It’s a secret. Coffee?”

     

                She picked up the mugs off the table and brewed a fresh pot on the stove for the three of them before joining them at the table. Kara murmured a thank you and took a sip before giving Lena a warm smile, eyebrows rising.

     

                “How was work?”

     

                “Busy. I spoke to my mom for a bit.”

     

                “Did she mention anything about a job? Last time I spoke to her she said she knew Cat Grant and could maybe hook me up.”

     

                Lena masked a choked sound of surprise, bristling at her mom’s interfering before she calmed herself down, “I- no, she didn’t mention anything about a job.”

     

                Small wonder at that as well, knowing that Lena wouldn’t react well to Kara being thrown into the deep end of normal life with a brand new job on top of the load of trauma she was still wading through. Making a mental note to call her mom, Lena let the conversation move on as she drank her coffee and offered her two cents when the occasion arose, but otherwise contentedly lingered on the edges of the conversation, thinking about what she’d overhead when she’d walked in. She wondered if either of them would bring it up, but as soon as she finished her coffee, Alex left.

     

                Once her sister had left, Kara disappeared upstairs to Lena’s office, which was fine by Lena as she set everything up, getting changed and answering the door when the delivery guy showed up. Double-checking that everything was in order, she made her way up to the office and paused at the sound of her mom’s voice on the phone before she emerged from the stairs and interrupted.

     

                “Hey.”

     

                “Oh, uh, hey, what’s up?”

     

                “Dinner’s ready. Are you almost done?”

     

                “Don’t be mad, Lena. You of all people should know how frustrating it is to sit at home all day.”

     

                Making a low sound at the back of her throat as she folded her arms over her chest and smiled faintly, amusement at the expectation that she’d be on the attack making her eyes brighten with mirth.

     

                “It would’ve been nice if I’d been involved in this conversation, but … well, Kara’s an adult. I’m not her mom; if she wants to get a new job, she can.”

     

                “I- Lillian, is it okay if we continue this tomorrow?” Kara politely asked, shutting her laptop and climbing to her feet as she picked up her phone.

     

                “Of course. I’ll email you the job descriptions for what they’re looking for. Enjoy your night.”

     

                “Thank you, you too.”

     

                “Bye, mom,” Lena called out, pointedly cordial before Lillian laughed and the line went dead.

     

                Kara let out a withering sigh, “so, you probably don’t think it’s a good idea, but- hey, is that the Christmas sweater I knitted you? It’s June , Lena.”

     

                “Never mind that,” Lena dismissively replied. “And no, I don’t, but … well, you are an adult. You don’t need my permission, but I wish you’d talk to me about it. I know people in the media industry too, you know.”

     

                Quietly laughing, Kara moved over to her and cupped her cheek in her hand, “it’s Cat Grant. I read her book so many times while I was in college.”

     

                Rolling her eyes, Lena pressed a kiss to Kara’s fingertips as she captured her hand. “Okay. Well, just … don’t rush into anything, okay? Now, let’s eat before my surprise is ruined.”

     

                “Surprise? What surprise?”

     

                “The thing about surprises is that they usually work best when you see for yourself.”

     

                “Funny.”

     

                Laughing, Lena walked downstairs ahead of Kara and stopped in the open kitchen and dining room, spreading her hands out wide as she smiled. “Tada.”

     

                She watched as Kara took in the birthday balloons and banners, the candles and red roses, the fully decorated artificial Christmas tree and felt autumn leaves scattered on the table. Athena was stretched out on the floor in a dog’s Santa costume with a party hat on and Kara didn’t know whether to laugh or look horrified. 

     

                “I told you we’d celebrate everything you missedwhen you got home. So, here’s an anniversary, birthday, Christmas, Thanksgiving, Valentine’s Day and New Year’s dinner. With the appropriate food for the most part - although, I did order some Chinese takeout too, but seeing as you technically missed Chinese New Year too, it does count.”

     

                Kara laughed then, her face crumpling with confused amusement at the bizarrity of it all and looked at Lena in wonder, as if she didn’t know where she’d found her. “It’s amazing, thank you.”

     

                “You like it?” Lena guardedly asked, hope written all over her face.

     

                Kara walked over to her and kissed her slowly, “I love it. I love you. Now, where do we begin?”

     

                “Well, first you need a party hat. And some New Year’s Eve party glasses. Do you want champagne? I splurged on the good stuff - I figured if we’d celebrated our anniversary together, I would’ve wanted to celebrate it well.”

     

                “Jesus, okay, um,” Kara slowly said as she donned the colourful party hat and put the plastic glasses on over her read ones. “Can I get my camera first?”

     

                Lena picked it up off the table and snapped a photo of Kara, laughing, “already got it. Now quick, before the food gets cold. Do you know how hard it was to find somewhere to make thanksgiving dinner takeout in June?”

     

                There was a variety of foods crammed onto the table, from turkey and cranberry sauce, to fresh oysters and chocolate dipped strawberries, birthday cake and dumplings. Lena played Christmas music through the TV and unscrewed the cap of the champagne - no loud corks - and poured it into two flutes.

     

                “Happy anniversary, birthday, Christmas, Thanksgiving, Valentine’s Day and New Year,” she said while Kara echoed her and clinked glasses. 

     

                Piling a plate with food, Kara eyed it all with exasperated amusement. They talked animatedly as they ate, laughing and taking photos, the flicker of the candles somehow making the ridiculousness of it all romantic, aided by the abundance of roses, although the cheap party hats and glasses made it humorous. 

     

                Once they’d eaten as much as they could stomach - sans the birthday cake saved for later - Lena changed the music and climbed to her feet, holding a hand out to Kara and pulling her from her seat. As Lena walked her into the open space and pulled her into her arms, one around the waist while the other adjusted its grip on Kara’s hand, Kara frowned, perplexed.

     

                “What’re you doing?”

                

                “I believe I once exposed myself as a ballroom dancing master at your mom’s house and you made me promise you we’d go dancing sometime. It might not be a fancy gala, but I always keep my promises.”

     

                She turned Kara in a circle before pulling her close and into step with the music. They were clumsy and uncoordinated though, not really dancing, and Kara kissed her with a hungry edge to it as they swayed. They ended up dancing through a few songs, and on a particularly slow one, Lena rested her head on Kara’s shoulder.

     

                “I’ve missed this,” Lena whispered.

     

                “I’ve missed you.”

     

                Lena smiled slightly, eyes half-lidded as she swayed them for a moment longer before pulling back and brushing Kara’s hair out of her face. It was already starting to grow out again, brushing past her shoulders, and Lena thought it suited her as she leaned in to kiss her and then stepped back.

     

                “Sit down; give me two seconds.”

     

                Kara obliged while Lena fetched the birthday cake from the fridge, the riot of colour and sprinkles a last-minute selection from a bakery she’d gone to on the way home, and she poked a few candles into it and lit them before walking over to Kara. Sinking down to a crouch before her as Kara groaned, already hiding her face in her hands, Lena sang happy birthday to her, off-key and plain bad , but Kara loved every second of it. Lena snagged her camera and took a photo as she blew the candles out, unable to hide her grin, her cheeks flushed pink and the ridiculous plastic glasses covering her bright eyes. 

     

                Lena cut two slices from the cake and carried them over to the table, sitting across from Kara as she slowly ate her piece, eyeing her across the table. The candles were definitely helping build tension because Lena ached to reach across the gap between them and pull Kara into a rough kiss - and not to sound vain, but she thought Kara was thinking the same thing. She ate the late bite slowly, savouring it as she tried to fight back the smile twitching at the corners of her lips as Kara narrowed her eyes slightly. 

     

                “I know what you’re doing,” Kara murmured in a sing-song voice, amusement colouring her words.

     

                Shrugging, Lena plastered an innocent look on her face and climbed to her feet with her plate in hand as she rounded the table to pick up Kara’s. “And what’s that?”

     

                She stopped as Kara’s fingers circled her wrist and the plates were removed from her hands, abandoned on the table. Climbing to her feet, standing so close to Lena that they were almost nose to nose, Kara grabbed her waist.

     

                “Dinner. Flowers. Candles. And let me check,” she murmured, leaning in to whisper in Lena’s ear as she tugged up the bottom of the sweater and pulled it over Lena’s head, a quiet huff of laughter falling from her lips as she looked down. “Mhm, lingerie. Classic seduction technique. Are you trying to seduce me?”

     

                “I wouldn’t call it seducing you; that makes it sound like you’re not interested. And I’m not trying; that makes it sound like I’m failing at it. I’m hoping neither of those statements are true.”

     

                Smiling, Kara leaned down to blow out the candles clustered on the table, beforethey accidentally burnt down the house while otherwise occupied, and in the dimness of the kitchen, Lena felt Kara’s arms wrap around her waist and lift her up. Letting out a squeal of laughter as she was hauled over Kara’s shoulder, she felt her stomach swoop with the old thrill of loving her.

     

                “Come on then,” Kara laughed, making for the staircase, “persuade me.”

     

                It didn’t take much effort and Lena felt that warm bubble of satisfaction in her chest, wrapped in the gratifying feeling of being with Kara, until she was so exhausted that she couldn’t bring herself to move from the bed. Kara was laying on Lena’s chest as the sweat cooled on her skin, while Lena trailed her fingers up and down her spine, an absentminded gesture, before she suddenly rolled off her and onto her stomach, face turned away.

     

                Lena was silent for a moment, shifting onto her side and continuing her featherlight tracing. “Are you okay?”

     

                She heard the long, rattling indrawn breath before Kara sharply exhaled, not turning around. “We left on time but one of the guys, DuBois, lost his rifle. We had to turn back. We lost about five hours on the return trip so Tran, the platoon leader, told us to stop in an abandoned town we’d passed through on the way there. The-”

     

                “Kara,” Lena cut her off, her voice just a little too loud in the sudden silence of the bedroom.

     

                “I- I want you to know. Things have been getting easier … it’s still hard, but I think … telling someone might help. Even just a little. I just- let me say it. Please.”

     

                “Okay.”

     

                Lena was careful to stay where she was, withdrawing her hand in case Kara didn’t want to be touched, and she lay there, staring at the shadowed outline of her and listened to her talk, hardly daring to breathe.

     

                “Comms were down; they didn’t manage to let anyone know we’d stopped for the night. We built up a fire, put our packs in one of the empty houses, and we- we were having dinner. It was already late but … everyone was laughing. I went to get a drink … it was so quiet, you’d think you could’ve heard for miles around, out there in the middle of nowhere. And then the first airstrike hit. I was inside - one of the walls hadn’t collapsed inwards yet so … it collapsed on me. Saved my life. It was … chaos. I couldn’t hear a thing, I was underneath all the brick and wood - the whole thing collapsed on top of me - and I tried- I tried to get up but another one hit.”

     

                She fell silent for a long few minutes, the audible sound of her swallowing making Lena’s throat turn dry with fear as well. 

     

                “When I got free I- I went out. It was so dark. I couldn’t see a thing but I- I called out. Mike … he answered. He was with DuBois. He was in bad shape - I could already see that; he’d lost a leg - so I told- I told Mike to get him clear. I knew we couldn’t stay there because … if they found us, we’d be dead. Like everyone- everyone else. But … we’d be dead with no supplies too so I went back … I went back to that house and dug out some packs and caught up with Mike. We- there was another aistrike when we were leaving. I knew we had to get clear so we just- we walked, as far as we could, until it was almost dawn and we found this little cave. Mike- he tried to- to look after DuBois, but he was already- already d-dead. We’d carried him all the way there but … he never stood a chance, so … we patched ourselves up and slept. I buried DuBois the next day; I piled rocks over him. Mike … he had a fever. I don’t know how many days we stayed in that cave, but … I just- I kept thinking that I was getting married. I had that photo . I had a fever too, couldn’t even move, but I knew- I’d made a promise to you so …”

     

                Trailing off, Kara drew in a long, shuddering breath, swallowing the sound of a sob, before she pressed on. “In the end, I just knew we had to go. If we stayed, we’d be dead for sure. But we couldn’t go back so I said we’d- we’d go back to that town where the British were stationed. I didn’t know the way but we just … walked. We had barely any food, barely any water … we walked for more than a week, sleeping wherever we could find shelter in the day, walking at night. We reached some random town - a different one - and I just- my legs gave out from under me. I wouldn’t have cared if they’d killed me; I couldn’t go any further. They sent someone to go and find the British soldiers at that town and … they looked after us. For all they knew, I’d terrorised their towns with everyone else, killed civilians, bombed them , but … they helped me. And when the soldiers came, they turned us over to them. The British realised we were American and handed us over. I don’t remember any of that; the next thing I knew was waking up in Germany.”

     

                She didn’t cry, but her voice would break occasionally, or her breath would hitch on a word, and Lena knew that she was breaking inside. Reaching out slowly, Lena found Kara’s hand under the blanket and gently touched it, and when she didn’t pull back, Lena covered it with her own. 

     

                “Before you landed there … they told me- they said … it was us. No one was supposed to be there. The British thought that we- we were rebels, because we should’ve almost been back at base. They called an airstrike down on us, and we gave it to them. Thirteen people. Dead, like that. All because of a- a mistake. How is that possible?”

     

                It was a few minutes before Kara rolled over and buried her face into the crook between Lena’s neck and shoulder. Swallowing the lump in her throat, Lena wrapped her arms around Kara. She wanted to cry, but Kara hadn’t cried, and even thought Lena’s heart broke for her, she wouldn’t fall apart when Kara was trying to keep it together.

     

                “I’m … so sorry,” Lena whispered, her voice shaking as she talked. She didn’t know what else to say - there were no words of comfort, nothing she could say to take away the pain or undo what she’d gone through.

     

                “Tell me,” Kara mumbled into Lena’s shoulder, and it took her a moment to realize that Kara wanted to hear her story.

     

                Floundering for a moment, scrabbling for memories of that day, the ones she’d tried so hard to blot out. “I- well … I got home from work that day. Alex’s car was outside but she- she didn’t answer when I called out. When I saw her sitting there at the table … I knew. I just knew. But I didn’t believe it - I felt like … I would’ve felt it. I didn’t want to believe it, but I just- I fell apart. Like that,” she snapped her fingers, eyes brimming with tears. “I fell to the floor; I couldn’t move. I just … screamed. Cried until I couldn’t. Kelly showed up, and then my mom did, but I just- I didn’t feel any of it. But my mom held me - and I let her, for the first time I can remember, and I- I hated it. Eliza came then and the whole thing was just … surreal. Somehow my mom was the only one holding us all together. I couldn’t do anything; I woke up and cried myself back to sleep again. I couldn’t … couldn’t eat, couldn’t move. Your mom started making funeral arrangements and we- we went to Midvale. It was almost harder at your mom’s house; I stayed in your room almost all day. I would’ve been content to never move again. The day of your- your funeral, Alex gave me the letter you left. I stayed behind after the service and read it. It was pouring down; I was freezing. I sat there for ages begging you to come back and then I went back to your mom’s house. I ended up getting into a fight with Alex - I wasn’t very pleasant to be around, or very nice to her - so I flew home. But … I couldn’t come back inside here. I slept in my car because I couldn’t bear the thought of being here without you. My mom found me, convinced me to come inside, and one day when she was out I just- I let my anger out. I broke things. Broke the vinyls, broke the TV, smashed every bottle of alcohol in here, drunk off my ass, until Kelly found me and talked me down. And then Alex came over and I said sorry, and the next day … they found you.”

     

                Lena fell silent, her words hanging heavily in the ensuing quietness of the room, and she startled slightly as she felt hot tears drip onto her shoulder, tearing her from the memories. Realising that Kara was crying, she shifted up the bed slightly, brushing her hair out of her face and then burying her face in it, kissing it softly as she listened to Kara’s garbled apology.

     

                “I’m so sorry. I- I put you through … hell. I never meant- I’m sorry.”

                

                “It wasn’t your fault,” Lena hoarsely replied, “don’t apologisse for it. You … you dragged yourself, bleeding and starving, through a desert while I- I fell to pieces and gave up on you. I should be apologising; if- if I’d know-”

     

                “I know. That’s why I had to- that’s why I fought.”

    Chapter 76

                Coming home from work early the following Wednesday, wearied from a lack of sleep the night before and too many meetings that day, Lena was happy to be home as she walked inside. Things had felt marginally better since speaking about their own experiences with Kara’s missing period, as if they understood each other better now, felt closer . Of course, that didn’t mean Lena expected everything to be fine all of a sudden, but it still gave her pause to find Kara sitting at the kitchen table, staring blankly at the wall while a pot of potatoes bubbled over on the stove, hissing.

     

                There was a blankness to her expression, that vacant look in her eyes, which Lena had come to associate with Kara’s more difficult days. Briskly walking over to the stove, Lena turned it off and then warily crossed over to Kara, gently calling her name. She jumped and quickly stood up, blinking herself out of a daze before she plastered a smile on her face. If Lena hadn’t just walked in and seen her elsewhere in her own mind, she might’ve assumed that she was fine.

     

                “Is … everything okay?”

     

                “Yeah, fine. I was just … thinking.”

     

                “Anything you need to talk about?” Lena asked, cupping her cheek, gently thumbing her cheekbone before kissing her.

     

                There was a flicker of something there, but it was gone before Lena could figure out what hidden thoughts and emotions were concealed in her blue eyes. For her part, Kara let out a snort of laughter and waved a hand dismissively.

     

                “No, no, it’s- it was nothing. How was work? I wasn’t expecting you home so early.”

     

                “Work was … okay,” Lena hedged, setting her bag down on the counter.

     

                Kara hummed distractedly and Lena waited for her to say something else, to move or look at her, and when she didn’t, Lena loosed a sigh. Running her hands over her face, she swallowed and was speechless for a moment, at a loss.

     

                “Pack a bag,” she suddenly instructed Kara, fishing her phone out of her coat pocket.

     

                “What?”

     

                “Pack a bag - we’re going away for a few days.”

     

                She was already dialling the private company that chartered her flights, pressing her phone to her ear as she quickly went through the process of arranging for her jet to be ready for takeoff as soon as possible. Hanging up, she raised her eyebrows at Kara, who was staring at her with wariness in her eyes.

     

                “Where are we going?”

     

                “It’s time for you to see where I grew up,” Lena replied with a wry smile.

     

                She went upstairs to pack a bag for herself then, Kara following her up and rifling through her own clothes taking up a small portion of the closet space, and they didn’t speak as they folded things into their respective bags, Lena fetching their toothbrushes and toiletries, Kara packing a sweater for Lena in case she got cold, and in short order they were ready to go.

     

                Calling her driver to pick them up, Lena made a few more calls; one to Alex, so she didn’t worry, another to her mom, and two more to Sam and Jess, rescheduling meetings and apologetically reminding them of urgent matters that she couldn’t handle over the phone. She was finished by the time the car pulled up outside, her driver fetching their bags and Athena’s things while Lena locked up and they climbed into the car.

     

                It was still light when they reached the private airstrip and by the time they were settled inside the plane, sunset was creeping in, the blue sky streaked with peach and lavender. Kara was talkative as they took to their seats, buckling in while Lena made Athena sit beside her, asking questions about Lena’s childhood home as her curiosity got the better of her.

     

                By the time they landed in Metropolis, it was late - even by West Coast standards - and Lena’s eyes were burning and heavy as she ushered Kara into the waiting car and slid in beside her. It carried the two of them out of the city limits, the dark highway illuminated by the orange glow of streetlights, before they turned off, passing through the suburbs and then out to undeveloped acres of land, with no end in sight as Kara dubiously peered out the window at the black expanse of nothingness.

     

                “How far out of the city is it?”

     

                “Well, if someone tried to murder you in the house, no one would hear you for miles around. I think the closest neighbours are a fifteen minute drive away, so … it’s pretty secluded.”

     

                “Oh. Of course . How big is the house? Like, I know you showed me when we video called, and it looked huge , but is it really that big?”

     

                “Probably bigger,” Lena snorted.

     

                “Jesus.”

     

                Casting her fiancée a nervous glance, worried that it would throw Kara off, Lena shifted restlessly in her seat. Of course Kara knew that Lena was rich, but she’d never given her an exact figure of her family’s wealth, and while she liked to live a far more modest lifestyle - or so she liked to think - the estate was the exact opposite of modest. 

     

                They pulled up to the gates thirty minutes later and Lena rubbed her palms together nervously as Kara shifted forward with anticipation, although it was too dark for her to see anything. It was still a long drive up to the house though, the tree-lined driveway blotting out most of the rolling gardens, and Lena bit back a smile at Kara’s natural excitement and curiosity.

     

                A few lights were on, yellow squares seemingly set impossibly far apart for it to be all one house, and Kara’s face crumpled with serious surprise as they pulled up outside, the car stopping as they climbed out.

     

                “I- no way this is where you grew up,” she spluttered, eyes wide as she turned to face Lena.

     

                Smiling wryly as she shrugged self-consciously, Lena let out a soft sigh. “You should see it in the daylight. But … a big house doesn’t make a happy family - or childhood.”

     

                “Are you sure you want to stay here?”

     

                “I’m sure. I thought- well, it might be nice to get out of the city for a couple of days. Plus, my mom liked it when I visit; I’m not opposed to staying a few days and making better memories for myself here.”

     

                Kara nodded slowly, falling into step beside Lena, “okay, but if it’s too much-”

     

                “If it’s too much for you ,” Lena countered with a quick laugh, squeezing Kara’s arm. 

     

                Too busy staring up at the shadowed facade of the house, the brickwork and the wide windows - too many to count - and the curving twin steps leading up to the huge front door, Kara didn’t reply. Lena knocked once they reached the front door and her mom answered a minute later, looking nervous but pleased to have them there.

     

                “Hi, mom,” Lena wearily greeted her, giving her a brief hug, “sorry for the late warning; it was a bit of a spontaneous choice.”

     

                “Nonsense. You know I’d love to get you here more often; besides, I’ve been asking you to bring Kara for weeks.”

     

                Shooting Lena an accusing look of amusement as she quietly scoffed, Kara followed her inside, “oh, you have? Someone conveniently forgot to mention that.”

     

                Rolling her eyes, Lena ushered her in, “I was waiting for the right time.”

     

                “Thank you for having me, Lillian. This place is incredible.”

     

                “Make yourself at home. Can I get you anything to eat or drink?”

     

                “It’s pretty late; I might sleep.”

     

                “Mm, I guess the tour can wait. Your room’s been made up.”

     

                Giving her a tired smile, Lena ducked her head in gratitude, “thanks, mom.”

     

                Hefting their bags, leaving Athena’s things inside the door for the time being, Lena thanked the driver as he set the last few things down and watched as her mom locked up for the night. Lillian must have been tired, but having Lena home for a few days was a good enough reason to be up so late and she bid them goodnight before slipping upstairs.

     

                Lena walked upstairs at a slower pace, talking to Kara over her shoulder as they moved up one side of the curved double staircase. 

     

                “It’s very quiet here - well, these days anyway - and the house gets a bit cold because of how it was built. It’s pretty old.”

     

                “I’ll say. It looks like something straight out of a gothic novel. It’s like- it’s like one of those old English estates in an Austen novel. I feel like we’re about to- to have some secret love affair in the linen closet and get found out for the maid.”

     

                “A fantasy of yours?”

     

                Kara rolled her eyes at Lena’s reading, poking her ass as she followed her up the steps and around to the next staircase heading up.

     

                “You know, I knew you were rich, but it was pretty easy to ignore it. But being here … how the hell did you end up with a broke journalist who literally hasn’t got a single asset?”

     

                “That’s not true; your entire personality is an asset. And you don’t have any student debt, so I guess I don’t have to find a way to sneakily pay that off for you.”

     

                Snorting, Kara shook her head as a smile pulled at the corners of her mouth and she stopped when Lena paused outside a door at the end of the long hallway, dropping the bag and turning the handle before she nudged it open with her foot.

     

                Dumping the bags on the floor as Kara fumbled for the light switch, Lena turned around and gave her a wary smile, spreading her hands.

     

                “Well, this is my room.”

     

                She watched Kara’s eyes travel around the rather bare space, taking in the ancient furniture and the clean bedding, the heavy drapes and the canopy over the bed. It was large and would have been homely even, if it had a few personal effects scattered throughout it. As it was, the bare bookshelves and empty desk made it look like it was waiting for someone to move in.

     

                “I can’t imagine you here,” Kara said after a long minute. “It feels … cold.”

     

                “Ah, well, I used to have my Britney Spears poster up over there, and all of my chess trophies and nerd shit, so it wasn’t always like this.”

     

                “I know, but … your house is so light. Tastefully modern. It suits you perfectly, but all of this old furniture …”

     

                “It suited the person I used to be.”

     

                 “A stubborn little heiress?”

     

                Laughing, Lena walked over to her and cupped Kara’s face in her hands, drawing in a deep breath before she shrugged, eyes creasing with mirth.

     

                “Yes.”

     

                Kissing her and affectionately tweaking her chin, Lena turned and unzipped her bag, pulling out pyjamas and changing. Kara followed suit while Lena dragged the drapes across the window and pulled back the sheets, turning the lamp on and climbing into bed.

     

                 Turning off the main light, Kara slipped between the covers next to her, moving across the wide bed and collapsing onto Lena’s pillow.

     

                “It’s quite cosy; I feel like I’m at Hogwarts.”

     

                Snorting, Lena caressed the length of Kara’s arm. “Go to sleep.”

     

                “Goodnight. I love you.”

     

                Turning her head to kiss her, Lena exhaled, the nervousness that had filled her fleeing as she lay in her old bed with Kara in her arms. It felt like the meshing of two worlds she never would have wanted to collide, but it didn’t seem so bad now that it had happened.

     

                “I love you too.”

     

                Sleep came surprisingly fast, the chill of the room paired with the heavy damask covers making for a perfect combination, but Lena was still up early the next morning. She was as quiet as possible as she slipped out of bed and tiptoed out of the room, sneaking down the hallway to her favourite study, a small space with a writing desk beneath a window overlooking the gardens, two bookshelves cluttered with heavy leatherbound classics and little marble busts and vases, and an old globe on a stand in the corner. Drawing out the rickety chair, she slid open the drawer and pulled out a piece of paper with the Luthor crest stamped into it at the top, rummaging around for an old MIT pen from her college orientation years ago, and started scribbling away on the paper.

     

                Finishing off the letter, she found a matching envelope and wrote Kara’s name on the front before sealing it. Making her way downstairs, the early dawn casting a blush of pink to the morning as fingers of fog lingered and birds chirped in the trees. Stepping out onto the back patio, Lena made her way down to the garden and plucked a pink rose from the bush before disappearing into the low maze.

     

                Re-emerging, she greeted her mother’s chef, who was unpacking groceries in the kitchen, and made her way upstairs. Kara was on the third floor, looking a little lost as Lena emerged from an old servant’s stairwell.

     

                “Morning,” Lena greeted her, pulling her in for a lingering kiss.

     

                “This place is a maze.”

     

                “Ah, no, the maze is in the garden.”

     

                “No, really, where are the stairs?”

     

                “This is the servant’s one - it’s the closest to my room.”

     

                Lena moved back towards her bedroom as she explained directions to the main staircase before slipping into the en-suite and showering. Dressing in jeans and a cotton shirt, she proposed going outside and enjoying the early morning weather as they overlooked the rolling acres of land, and Kara enthusiastically agreed. Lena suspected that she was eager to see the house in full and explore the grounds and she led her downstairs, holding her hand as if fearing she’d get lost.

     

                Stepping outside as they passed through a mud room, Lena gestured grandly to the view, and Kara’s eyes immediately landed on the maze.

     

                “Can I go in it?”

     

                Smiling as she gave her a gentle push of encouragement, she watched Kara rush off towards it, Athena bounding after her as she was let loose to run free. Lena followed at a slower pace, watching Kara move through the low hedges and laughing when she watched her make a wrong turn, having the entire thing memorised from years of walking the path.

     

                It only took her five minutes to make it to the centre and find the rose and letter where Lena had left it on the edge of the fountain. Winding her way down the stretch of path between the low hedges, Lena joined her in the middle and Kara smelled the rose before giving her a wide smile.

     

                “It’s beautiful, thank you.”

     

                “Aren’t you going to read the letter?”

     

                “I was hoping you would read it to me.”

     

                Wrinkling her nose as she internally cringed at the thought of rereading what she’d written and voicing it aloud, Lena was struck by the shock of realising they’d never read their letters to each other before. They’d been reserved for while Kara was gone, a way to keep a memory of their time apart, something for them to look forward to receiving, but this was the first one written while they were together.

     

                Taking the envelope from her, Lena sank down onto the edge of the fountain and patted the space beside her for Kara to join her. Smiling at her, Lena captured a fluttering lock of hair between her fingers and tucked it safely behind Kara’s ear before she turned her attention to the letter. Opening the envelope, Lena unfolded the sheets of paper and let out a soft sigh of resignation, willing her cheeks not to redden with embarrassment as she started reading it aloud.

     

                “To my dearest Kara,” Lena said, glancing sideways at her and taking in the serene look on her face, eyes closed and a small smile gracing her lips.

     

    It’s been a few months since the last letter I wrote to you, and I know we’ve had more important things to worry about, but I also promised you that it wouldn’t be the last letter I’d write to you. I should probably start by saying how proud I am of you, for everything you’ve been through and overcome. As much as I hated it, you did your job and saw it through to the very end, and saved a man’s life in the process. I know that you don’t see it that way, that those three weeks were a hellish nightmare, but I’m so grateful to you for dragging yourself through it and coming home. I don’t say that insensitively, and I know there’s still a long road ahead of us, but I just want you to know that I’m proud of how far you’ve come. Hopefully, now comes the peaceful part of life together, and I hope I can fill it with happiness for you. It’s the least I can do in return.

     

    I’ve told you in so many ways how much I love you, but I still feel like words fail me here - they’ve always been your thing, not mine, and even science can’t help me out. I don’t think I’ll ever truly be able to express what you mean to me, not in any language that exists, but I hope you know it and feel it. I know things have been difficult for you but your strength and bravery has pulled us both through it, because you make me stronger too, and I know I would be a different person without you. 

     

    With you, I’m better. Your warmth, kindness and unconditional love had affected me more than I could have ever thought, and I know with all my heart that no one else could have changed my life as much as you have. You’ve shown me what it’s like to be truly loved, and to love as well, and what it means to make a life for myself. I’m not talking about crazy adventures and travelling the world - that’s not living to me - but you gave me so many firsts, so many things to appreciate, to laugh about and fall in love with. You brought some colour back into my life and I know there are more things you’ve done and changed that I’m still unaware of, and that you probably haven’t even realised either. I want to thank you for that, and I hope that one day I’ll be able to do the same for you.

     

    But I won’t pretend it’s all been picture perfect - those three weeks say it all - but our time together has been perfect to me. We’ve been through more in eighteen months than most people do in a lifetime, and I think we’ve come out stronger because of it, even if we’re still a little broken from it. I know for a fact that there’s no one else I would want to go through life with, and that you’re it for me. You are it. I hope you never doubted that you were the only person I could ever feel this way about, even when you were telling me to move on one day and our family was doubting us too, but I want you to know that I don’t plan on ever letting you go again. If there’s one thing those three weeks taught me it’s that there are pieces of you in every part of my life.

     

    I know there’s still a lot of things for us to work on, and to help you get back on your feet, and I know it’s frustrating for us both but I also know we’ll be okay. Nothing will be able to come between us - not even death itself, apparently - and I want you to know that no matter what, in everything we do for the rest of our lives, I’ll be right beside you. There’s so much we still have left to do together, to figure out, and I can’t wait to do it all with you. I hope those days come quickly because we’ve done enough waiting to last a lifetime. Now I’m ready to start the rest of it with you.

     

    Love always,

     

    Lena x

     

                Trailing off, Lena folded the letter back up and slipped it into the envelope before looking at Kara. She was teary eyed and the look on her face was tender as she leaned over to give Lena a lingering kiss. 

     

                “Thank you.”

     

                “Thank you. I don’t think I could have done any of this without you.“

     

                “Any of what?”

     

                “Everything.”

     

                It was a simple reply and a slow smile spread across Lena’s face before she climbed to her feet and held her hand out. Pulling Kara up, she kissed her cheek and wrapped an arm around her shoulder.

     

                “Come on, time for a tour.”

     

                They stuck to the grounds at first, Lena taking Kara to the stables - reduced down to just two horses now, both of them still being broken when Lena had first left home - and then through the small thicket of trees deeper in the estate’s land, where the apple trees were. Lena climbed up one of them, ungainly and not as nimble at it as she’d been at eight. Kara improvised with the bottom of her shirt to create a basket for the ripe ones Lena picked and they made their way back to the house, the sun already higher in the sky. 

     

                Dew clung to their shoes and the hems of their jeans and they stomped their feet on the bristly mat in the mud room before depositing the apples in the kitchen. Lillian was nowhere to be found and Lena shepherded Kara through the downstairs floor, opening and closing doors on rooms as she kept up a running commentary, pointing out her favourite ones or a memory associated with another, the history behind a piece of art and which chairs were comfiest.

     

                They made their way up to the next floor, bypassing Lillian, who was heading downstairs for coffee, and then wound up on the third floor before making the reverse trip back down for breakfast.

     

                “This house is insane. I can’t even imagine what it was like to grow up here. I mean, like the house as a physical thing. Your mom must get lonely out here.”

     

                “Mm, I think so. She won’t move out though; it’s the Luthor estate, it’s been in the family for a few generations now. I guess it’s my inheritance too.”

     

                “Oh. Yeah, I guess.”

     

                Squeezing her hand, Lena led her through to the open kitchen and her mom’s chef scrambled eggs and fried back for them. Lena shooed Kara through to her favourite sitting room after they’d finished, making tea and following after her. As she came upon the open door, she paused at the sound of voices drifting out and hesitated before caving to eavesdropping.

     

                “It’s incredible here. I’d kill to live somewhere like this - and not just for the house, but the land as well. It’s beautiful. It’d be a great place to grow up.”

     

                “Would you actually move away from National City?” Lillian asked.

     

                With a nonchalant laugh, Kara replied. “I mean, I’ve lived in a few places. I was born in Tennessee originally. Moved to Midvale. Then to National City - but I guess most of my time there was while I was enlisted, so I was never really settled there. Moving wouldn’t be a new experience for me, but I just- Alex is there and I don’t know if Lena would pick up and move headquarters again, move houses. But me … I could live anywhere. National City isn’t a bad place either and we have so many good memories there too; I just think … the bad ones.”

     

                “The only time I’ve ever seen her truly happy has been there,” Lillian admitted. “And it wasn’t the place; it was you. She’d move anywhere for you - you’re her home.”

     

                “Well … she doesn’t mind being back here so much anymore, for what it’s worth. But, well, I think she’s afraid to move quickly now, after everything that happened. We rushed into an engagement, made all kinds of promises because we didn’t think we had much time, and now … we’ve got all the time in the world. I know she’s the one who’s been stalling you setting up a meeting with Cat Grant for me.”

     

                “She isn’t doing it to hurt you,” Lillian quickly jumped to Lena’s defence.

     

                Outside, Lena bit back a smile - a year ago she would never have thought her mom would be leaping to defend her. 

     

                “I know. She thinks I’ll be too overwhelmed by it all, and maybe she’s right, which is why I haven’t fought her in it yet. But … I’d like us to do more. She has all these plans - I know she does - but she won’t share them with me. I think she’s afraid it’ll be too much for me and I’ll … have some sort of breakdown.”

     

                “You really should take it slow. You can still plan for the future, but what you went through … it’s going to take time. You’ve made excellent progress though, I’ll admit. Still, take care of yourself.”

     

                “Of course I will,” Kara said with a soft laugh, “I wouldn’t take on more than I thought I could handle. I’d just like to know where she’d like to get married, and when. Where she wants us to raise kids. Has she ever told you she wants kids?”

     

                Lillian exhaled forcefully, the sound full of regret, “Lena and I … we never really had a personal relationship. Not until you came along. Even now, I don’t know if that’s a conversation she’d ever have with me. But I’m sure there’ll be plenty of time for the two of you to have it.”

     

                “She does want them,” Kara softly confessed, a smile in her voice. “Two girls, she said. I want to know what names she likes, if she’d send them to ballet lessons-“

     

                Scoffing, Lillian hummed dubiously. “I doubt the ballet lessons; she was never much of a dancer herself. Even with her ballroom lessons.”

     

                “She’s quite good.”

     

                “She’s good at everything. Something she’d want her kids to inherit, I think.”

     

                “Mm, well … first thing first is getting back to work, I think. I guess moving in is ticked off my checklist.”

     

                “I think firstly, you need to take care of yourself.”

     

                “You sound exactly like Eliza,” Kara said with a quiet groan and a chuckle.

     

                “I might not have been the best mother towards Lena, but I was a mother, nonetheless. A better one for Lex, at that’s

     

                “She’s forgiven you, you know,” Kara murmured and Lena blinked, startling slightly at her fiancée’s perception. 

     

                It was true, of course, although Lena might not have even admitted it to herself. There had been a point where even when things had become amicable, when she’d started to trust Lillian again, Lena hadn’t thought she’d be able to forgive her for the past. Move on, but not forgive . But she had. Somewhere along the way, that bitter part of her that had clung to her old wounds had healed over, so slowly, so imperceptibly that she hadn’t even realised it herself. Yet she had, and Lena felt odd at the fact that she was standing outside the living room door in her childhood home, listening to her fiancée and her mother having a conversation about her. It all felt a little surreal.

     

                “I think … I know that. I didn’t think she ever would, but … well, I’m more grateful than she knows. I love her more than she knows too; I always have.”

     

                A lump lodged itself in Lena’s throat and she had to back up a few steps, closing her eyes and holding the two cups of tea as she composed herself. Letting out a shaky breath, she cleared her throat and plastered an innocent look on her face as she smiled and briskly strode into the living room.

     

                “Oh, mom,” she said, acting surprised as she set the cups of tea down. “You’ve still got coffee?”

     

                “I’m fine.”

     

                Giving her a quick smile, Lena sat beside Kara on the loveseat and quickly slipped into their conversation, pretending like she hadn’t been eavesdropping outside for five minutes as they spoke about business. Sipping her tea, Lena watched both of them closely, but they didn’t seem to have any desire to bring up anything they’d mentioned while she was out of the room.

     

                It was a lazy day around the house, old movies, games of chess to occupy Kara’s mind, and even a few games of pool and darts - the latter of which Kara was bizarrely good at - before they ate dinner. Kara insisted on cooking for them and Lena was all too happy to let her monopolise the kitchen, drinking a glass of wine as she watched Kara move about with purpose.

     

                They had lamb shanks with all the trimmings and Lillian was more than a little impressed at her cooking skills. After cleaning up, Lena put some music on and the three of them enjoyed a drink in one of the parlours, the room cosy and warm as they chatted away, Lena feeling more at ease around the two of them together as she got over her original reservations. It seemed her mom had gotten over her misgivings too, almost genuinely fond of Kara, if Lena wasn’t mistaken.

     

                They were tired from their late night before though and had a relatively early night, the big house dark and silent as the two of them made their way upstairs. As tired as she was, Lena couldn’t fall asleep straight away though, even with Kara out cold beside her, and she made her way down to the kitchen to pour herself a glass of water.

     

                Lillian startled her as she shuffled into the kitchen with her empty wine glass, and Lena shut off the tap as she eyed her mom.

     

                “I thought you’d be asleep by now. Do you need your sleeping pills?”

     

                “I’m fine,” Lena murmured, taking a sip of water. “Just thirsty.”

     

                “Alright.”

     

                They lapsed into silence but it was clear her mom had something on her mind and it only took a moment for her to act on that urge. Setting her glass in the sink, Lillian ran her hands over the thighs of her slacks.

     

                “I need to talk to you about something.”

     

                “Oh?”

     

                “Come and sit for a moment.”

     

                Lillian moved over to the table and sank down onto a chair, while Lena took one perpendicular to her, staring at her with a flicker of unease in her green eyes. She was patient though, waiting for her mom to speak in her own time. Lillian wasn’t known for keeping her thoughts to herself for long.

     

                “Kara wants to move,” she finally said. “She wants to move on with her life, do all of those things you planned, and that includes potentially moving.”

     

                “I know. I heard.”

     

                “You hear- you were eavesdropping?” Lillian scoffed, arching an eyebrow in cool amusement.

     

                Lena shrugged indifferently and her mom rolled her eyes, sparing her the lecture. “I guess you don’t have to tell me then.”

     

                “That’s … not what I was going to tell you.”

     

                “Oh,” Lena said, frowning, at a loss. “Oh, okay. Well … what is it?”

     

                Lips pressing into a thin line, Lillian was serious and hesitant, fingers laced together on the table as she gathered her thoughts.

     

                “I know how you might react - probably not well - but … I want to give you the estate.”

     

                “You … what?”

     

                “As a wedding gift. When you get married … obviously.”

     

                Mouth opening and closing as she was completely blindsided by Lillian’s offer - the last thing she was expecting to come out of her mom’s mouth - she let out a choked laugh. 

     

                “I … don’t understand.”

     

                “The house. It’s yours when you and Kara get married. I’ll move out, obviously, but it’s the Luthor estate and it’ll be yours one day anyway. If you overhead then you know she’d like to raise kids here; maybe you could change this place for yourself. Fill it with laughter and happiness, make it a proper home, the way it never was for you. I know your opinion of the place has changed a bit already. Anyway, you don’t have to live here if you don’t want to, but … it’s your inheritance.”

     

                Lena’s mind quickly went back to the conversation that morning and she let out a sudden laugh, her face crumpling with the confusing feelings inside her.

     

                “I … well-“

     

                “Don’t say anything. Talk it over with Kara first. There’s a lot she wants to discuss, as you heard. I just thought you might like to know your options.”

     

                “Yeah. Thanks, mom.”

     

                Nodding, Lillian clapped her hands on her thighs and pushed herself to her feet. “Right, well, I’ll see you in the morning.”

     

                “Night.”

     

                “Sleep tight,” Lillian said, dropping a kiss on Lena’s head and vanishing upstairs to her room.

     

                Sipping her water in the kitchen for a minute, Lena carried her glass upstairs, turning over the new information. As she passed through the familiar hallways, past doors she could name for every room beyond, to each step that groaned and each chip in the shiny veneer of the old house - that scratch where she’d dropped her cello case, that curl of wallpaper where the window had been left open when it had rained one day, warping it. It could be theirs - all of it. It could be the fresh start she’d overheard Kara talking about with Alex, a place for them to raise the children they’d talked about, a new home to start off married life. 

     

                Slipping back into the dark bedroom and crept into bed, setting her glass down on the nightstand and pulling the covers up. Kara rolled over in her sleep, throwing an arm around Lena, as if she’d been waiting for her to come back. Smiling as she stroked a hand down Kara’s back, Lena fell asleep wondering what it would be like to live in that house again.

                They only stayed until Sunday in Metropolis and the following week passed by too fast for Lena to broach the topic of her eavesdropping. That weekend, James and Lucy were in town from Metropolis to visit Kelly and reunite with Kara again, and Winn was freshly back from his deployment.
