It was the first time Kara had been around so many familiar faces since being back, and while Lena was a little bit anxious about how she’d cope with it, it was worth it to see the joy on Kara’s face when she opened the door to Lucy.

     

                There was a bond between those that had served overseas together that those that hadn’t were on the outside of, but it made Lena’s heart soar to see the understanding between them. Kara hugged them just a little bit longer and Lena was filled with the quiet hope that it would make things easier for her, even just for one night.

     

                “I’ve missed you,” Kara said as she pulled back from Lucy and wrapped James in a tight hug.

     

                “Us?” James echoed with a loud laugh, “the last time we saw you, it was an empty box being lowered into the ground. You have some explaining to do.”

     

                Rolling her eyes, her smile a little strained, Kara ushered them inside and Lena stepped forward from where she was hovering in the doorway to the living room. Greetings were exchanged, friendly hugs and offers to take coats and fetch drinks.

     

                “It’s a long story,” Kara wearily replied.

     

                James clapped a hand on her shoulder, squeezing reassuringly. “Yeah, even Mike wouldn’t talk about it when I gave him a call. And you know how much he loved the sound of his own voice.”

     

                Kara snorted, shaking her head as she suppressed a laugh. She fetched two beers and handed them over, while Lena refilled her wine glass.

     

                “You heard from him much?” James continued.

     

                “No, not at all,” Kara murmured. “I’m not really keen to, to be honest.”

     

                Lucy nodded with understanding, rubbing Kara’s back before changing the subject. Looping her arm through Lucy’s, Kara exhaled and then drew herself up, taller and perked up.

     

                “Come on, I’ll introduce you to everyone else.”

     

                Taking a seat in between Kelly and Sam on one of the sofas, Lena took a sip of her wine and watched Kara make introductions, feeling content to sit there and nurse her drink as music played in the background and multiple conversations overlapped with laughter as everyone mingled. Some of these people she didn’t know too well and others were family, her best friends, and it was a nice mixture as Lena studied the life they’d created together.

     

                Pizza was soon delivered for dinner, boxes passed around and slices held as the ten of them split up into random pairs and they raced through round after round of Pictionary , taking it in turns to draw on the board while guesses were shouted out and the artists were heckled. Lena couldn’t remember the last time she’d laughed so much, her eyes always straying to Kara to check if she was laughing too.

     

                When Alex suggested Cards Against Humanity, Lena went to fetch new drinks and refills for people, Kelly tagging along to lend a hand as they stood in the considerably cooler kitchen, pouring wine, vodka and soda, opening beer bottles and rinsing glasses. 

     

                “How’re you doing?”

     

                Looking up at Kelly, Lena’s mild look of surprise melted into exasperation as she smiled, “just fine. You don’t have to keep checking up on me, you know.”

     

                “That’s what family does,” Kelly said, lodging a wedge of lime into the mouth of a Corona. “How were things at your mom’s? Kara seems a little more … well, herself.”

     

                “Yeah, it was good. Sometimes it’s frightening how fine she seems, but I feel like she’s keeping things from me.”

     

                “Like what?”

     

                “Like how she doesn’t want to stay here,” Lena blurted out with a tiny smile, one side of her mouth hitching higher than the other as she met Kelly’s stare. 

     

                Inhaling and opening her mouth, Kelly made a sound of confusion as she frowned. “But … what do you mean? Where does she want to go?”

     

                 “Anywhere. Away from here. I overheard her talking to my mom , of all people. And I overheard her talking to Alex before that; pretty much the same conversation.”

                

                Perplexed as she screwed the cap back onto the vodka, Kelly cocked her head to the side, “Alex doesn’t want to move anymore. She only applied for that job because … well, she was grieving for her sister. Guess she didn’t want to be stuck her either. But now … she’d never leave Kara.”

     

                With a short laugh, Lena arched an eyebrow. “Kara said the same thing. But if she did want to move, I’d pack it all up in an instant. Would you?”

     

                “Of course,” Kelly softly crowed. “If she was serious, hell yeah I would. My mom and James are both in Metropolis; I have just as much reason to move there as anyone.”

     

                Nodding, Lena pressed her lips into a flat line and poured red wine into her glass. After a moment, setting the bottle down, she furrowed her brow in deep thought. “So … if they want to go then-”

     

                “I’d wager at least one of us is moving.”

     

                Snorting, Lena had no argument for her and gathered up three drinks, carefully carrying them back through to the living room, where white cards were been shuffled out for everyone. Handing a beer to Sam and the vodka and soda to Nia, she reclaimed her seat and set her wineglass safely beneath the coffee table as she gathered up her white cards and held them close.

     

                Within ten minutes, claims of cheating and showing favouritism were being hurled back and forth. Everyone was smug when their card won and offended when it didn’t, and Lena couldn’t help but laugh, rosy cheeked and basking in the warm glow of a good night and the effects of wine as it sent a slow flush through her.

     

                It ended up being a late night, everyone claiming bedrooms for themselves as they dropped off, one by one - even Sam, who’d sent Ruby for a sleepover - and Kara was well and truly drunk as Lena helped her up to bed, along with Alex and James, the last ones standing. Lena wasn’t sure if letting her drink so much had been such a great idea, but Kara had genuinely been enjoying herself and she would have hated to spoil her fun, trusting Kara to know her limits. At any rate, Kara clumsily stripped off her clothes and collapsed into bed, passing out cold quickly, which was a rare occurrence these days.

     

                It didn’t stop the nightmares though, although there was no scream. Lena jerked away at the sudden feeling of the mattress jostling, taking in Kara’s rising and falling shoulders as she hunched over, running a hand over her face, ragged breaths quiet in the vastness of the bedroom. Reaching out, Lena laid a palm flat against her back and shifted closer.

     

                “Hey, it was just a dream.”

     

                Kara reached out to grip Lena’s leg over the blanket, squeezing gently. “I’m okay,” she whispered, a tremor in her voice. 

     

                The sheets rustled as she lay back down, the smell of beer and sweat on her skin as she stared up at the ceiling in the dark. Laying beside her, Lena listened to the sound of her breathing even out again.

     

                “It was Mike this time,” she said after a long minute of silence.

     

                “I know James asked … are you sure you don’t want to visit him? Even just a- a phone call?”

     

                It had been a few months now, and Kara hadn’t so much as heard a whisper from him, and hadn’t wanted to anyway. Even when they’d awarded her various medals and honours before discharging her, she hadn’t gone to the ceremony and had received them in the mail, wanting to avoid anything related to the military. Her close friends were the exception there.

     

                “No,” Kara heavily sighed. “We weren’t friends - weren’t even close. I don’t think going through something like that with him means that we have to be close now. I mean … I don’t think it’ll help.”

     

                “Okay.”

     

                She knew it was pointless to fight Kara on this, and Lena didn’t know him anyway, beyond the guy that had a crush on Kara and then had been lost with her. It was her decision to make and she was content for her to hold to it. Snugging up close to her, her head on her chest, Kara softly sighed as Lena cradled her and kissed the top of her head.

     

                “Tell me something,” Kara quietly hummed, the demand seeming more like a plea.

     

                Somehow, it had become a ritual for Lena to hold her close whenever Kara woke up from a nightmare and talk until she fell back asleep, which usually resulted in a poetry recital, snatches of essays and old stories.

     

                “Of course. Um … let me think,” Lena whispered, scrambling for something.

     

                It was slow going, but every day she could feel more of Kara returning to her, and Lena was grateful for the small progress she made. The small moments, like being wrapped up in each other’s arms with their poetry, stories, speeches and monologues, was a big enough reward for Lena. Each small victory made the bad days feel worth it, and she knew that eventually the day would come when there would be more good days than bad.

     

                She ended up explaining the plot of Don Quixote to her in as much detail as she could, an old classic Lena remembered reading at boarding school for her English class. It was long-winded and lulled Kara straight to sleep, but even then Lena kept talking, until she was sure she was sleeping peacefully.

     

                The next morning, everyone gathered in the kitchen to help make breakfast, nursing some degree of hangover as Kara popped Advil into hands, while Sam and Alex cooked eggs - one scrambling and the other frying - Lena brewed copious amounts of coffee and Kelly and James bickered over how much the bread should be toasted. With everyone busy doing something , it made the spacious kitchen feel full, and Lena opened the back door to let in the fresh air as Nia’s bacon started smoking while Querl flapped a dish towel in its direction.

     

                Soon enough, they were all squeezed around the table, or otherwise at the bar stools lining the counters, everyone in high spirits despite the headaches and slightly greenish complexions. Calling cabs for everyone as they trickled off in ones and twos, Lena quietly cleaned up while Kara soaked up as much time with her friends as she could.

     

                “So, have you two set the date for the wedding yet?” Lucy asked.

     

                Kara hesitated, glancing over at Lena with a sheepish look on her face. “Not yet. Next year though. And what about you two, huh? Shouldn’t you be getting hitched soon?”

     

                Rolling his eyes, James slung an arm around Lucy’s shoulder and kissed the side of her head, “all in good time. Kelly’s first; my mom’s thrilled about that, so that’s fine by me.”

     

                Patting his chest, Lucy scoffed, “he’s more focused on kids. He’s already got the baseball glove ready for little Jimmy - he’s convinced we’ll have a boy first.”

     

                “Hey, if we have a girl, you bet she’ll have that baseball glove on the moment she can,” he defensively replied. Raising his eyebrows at Lena, he smiled, “what about you? Kids in the future?”

     

                Looking over at Kara, Lena smiled lovingly, “two girls, we think.”

     

                “God, two more Danvers sisters?” James laughed. “Look out - that’s trouble.”

     

                “Hey, your sister is marrying one of them; imagine what their kid will be like.”

     

                “Spoilt as hell.”

     

                Lucy shook her head and gave Kara an expectant look. “What about yours?”

     

                “Ah, well, we’d have little geniuses, of course.”

     

                Her eyes crinkled at the corners as she turned to look at Lena, whose heart leapt at the sight of it. Forget intelligence - she hoped their child would have Kara’s smile, her eyes, her warmth . It would be years at least, but it was a comforting thought that they had the rest of their lives ahead of them, plans to be made and brought to reality. 

     

                Eventually, Lucy and James left as well and Lena took a trash bag around the house, collecting empty recyclables for the trash, before wiping down sticky surfaces while Kara tackled the mountain of dishes. They were both quiet, but it was a peaceful sort of silence, enjoying their morning as they clean up after a good night, both of them exhausted but content.

     

                Flicking suds into the sink and drying her hands, Kara groaned as she rubbed at a shoulder, “I’m aching everywhere. I can’t remember the last time I drank so much.”

     

                Lena smiled fondly at her complaints, moving over to her and cradling her waist in her hands as she chastely kissed her. “How about a nice hot bath?”

     

                Humming in agreement, Kara kissed her beforeLena made her way upstairs to run the hot water, adding bubbles and epsom salts before stripping off the pyjamas and climbing in. Kara joined her a moment later, facing her in the spacious tub, and they both enjoyed the warmth and steam. Trailing her fingers through the bubbles, Lena felt the weight of her thoughts bearing down on her and resolved to broach the subject at last.

     

                “So … I’ve been meaning to talk to you since we got back from my mom’s.”

     

                “About what?” Kara murmured, opening one eye and squinting blindly.

     

                Reaching across the space between them, Lena smoothed out the furrow between her eyebrows with a chuckle before leaning back against the rim of the tub. “I, uh, I overhead you talking to my mom.”

     

                Drumming her fingers on the edge of the tub, Kara hummed as she sighed. “And how much did you overhear?”

     

                “Well … I was eavesdropping, so the whole thing, I guess,” Lena admitted, coaxing a loud laugh of surprise from Kara.

     

                “Always so honest. Well, you don’t have to worry, because-”

     

                “My mom’s giving us the estate,” Lena blurted out, watching surprise and confusion dawn on Kara’s face as she blinked slowly. “When we get married, she’s giving it to me then.”

     

                “The estate? As in you mom’s house? The huge mansion?”

     

                “That would be the one,” Lena hummed in agreement, giving Kara a wry smile. “So, it’s mine if I want it - well, ours - and if you want to move to Metropolis, we can. I know you said you wanted a house with a big garden for kids … well, you’ve seen how big it is. The fresh start you’re looking for … I think we can find it there. It’s where L-Corp’s original headquarters is located, I’ve already got my own place there, it’s where my mom lives, Kelly’s family - James and Lucy would be there - and … just about everything we could ever want.”

     

                Kara frowned as she pursed her lips, looking down at the bubbles for a moment, deep in thought. “But … do you want to move?”

     

                “I would go … anywhere with you. I heard you say that my happiness is here, but my mom was right when she said that it’s you. We have all these memories, but they’re inside my head wherever we are, in my heart, in the photos you’ve taken. Wherever you are, it’s where I want to be. We could … move to Fiji and take up surfing or- or raise sheep in the Scottish highlands. I don’t know. Whatever you want. We can go anywhere in the world and I’ll be happy because you’re there; it’s the people that make the place.”

     

                Looking sceptical and uncertain, Kara cocked her head to the side, eyebrows knitting together. “You would really … go? If I wanted to-”

     

                Lena gripped the sides of the tub and pulled herself forwards, towards Kara, cupping her face and pressing a hard kiss to her lips. Leaning her forehead against Kara’s when she pulled back, her voice was low and oddly thick with emotion as she closed her eyes and swallowed. 

                

                “I’d leave right now if you wanted to. I’d pack a bag and get on my plane and take you … wherever you wanted to go. We can go tomorrow, or next week. Or wait until we’re married and go straight into that house.”

     

                “You really mean it,” Kara murmured, and not as a question, but as a surprised statement, stroking Lena’s cheek.

     

                “Of course . But … there is one catch.”

     

                “Oh?”

     

                “Alex and Kelly are coming too.”

     

                Kara laughed, tipping her head back and splashing as she slid down in the bath. Lena grinned and kissed her before retreating back to her end of the tub. “Well … I guess we’d better start planning out wedding then.”

    Chapter 78

                They planned for almost a year.

     

                It was a year packed with activity, with milestones and achievements and plenty of planning. Lillian had set Kara up with that meeting with Cat Grant, securing Kara a journalist gig for a fashion magazine - something she’d mocked in the past but seemed happy and grateful for now - and Lena had slowly started the transition to move L-Corp back to Metropolis, giving Sam a hefty pay rise for her to move back with her.

     

                It was a busy year, more than anything, but a good one. If it wasn’t for the scar on Kara’s abdomen, no one would know what she’d been through by looking at her. She’d made small steps in her recovery, and then big ones, until she slept through the night almost every night - save for the odd nightmare - and could slam a cupboard without flinching, without reeling back into a flashback. Lena learned to relax, confident that Kara was safe, was doing okay. 

     

                Work seemed to be the first big step, with Kara eager to prove herself as a real journalist, and not just a public affairs officer, teasing stories out of soldiers and terrified civilians from the middle of nowhere. She was busy and happy with her work, meeting Lena for lunch, animatedly talking about her articles over dinner at night, working closely with Nia, of all people, and able to be in an office full of strangers without feeling the slightest bit of panic at being somewhere so unfamiliar. 

     

                Another came when Alex and Kelly got married. It was a quick affair, both of them deciding that they didn’t want to wait any longer, and didn't need the fanfare of a big wedding. Alex called Kara one morning and told her they were eloping that afternoon, the four of them making their way to the registry office, watching as the pair said their vows and slipped rings onto each other’s fingers. Not that she needed it, but the happiness it brought to witness that special moment only reinforced Lena’s decision to marry Kara; she wanted that piece of paper, that ring and that glow of love and happiness as they were pronounced wives.

     

                They moved to Metropolis shortly after that, Lena helped get a good buyer for Kelly’s apartment and gave them the key to her one to get settled in. She didn’t need it; she and Kara would be moving into the estate shortly before their own wedding, and witnessing Alex and Kelly’s lit a fire under them to get a move on with planning their own.

     

                There were arguments and debates over the date, the location, the flowers, the colours, cake flavours and menus, and everything in between. Compromises were the usual outcome as they came to agreements by finding middle grounds. The estate’s garden was a perfectly lovely place to get married; Lena didn’t have to fly everyone to France for it. Just their close friends and family was enough; the entirety of CatCo didn’t need to be invited so no one felt left out. 

     

                Eventually, it was all planned. They each went dress shopping, taking their mom’s, Alex and Kelly and were reassured that their dresses would go well together. They’d made frequent trips to Metropolis, tasting cakes and deciding on a lemon one, tailored the menu to their tastes, even though Lillian insisted that dumplings weren’t a wedding appetiser.

     

                As the date neared, boxes started piling up in their own home, most of Lena’s things being shipped to Metropolis with them. She knew the estate would need some desperate sprucing up to feel comfortable; the bones of the place were good, and everything was well made and expensive, but surely some of the ghastly paintings could be replaced with something more contemporary, the colour scheme a little more modern. 

     

                Lillian had already packed up all of her things, taking some of her favourite pieces with her anyway, leaving the estate ready for them to move in over the coming weeks. The last time Lena had visited, it was quite bare inside compared to how it had always been growing up, and she thought that her mom might’ve felt her reservations about moving into the house when it felt frozen in the past. Instead, Lillian took it all with her, to her favourite townhouse within the city centre.

     

                Their official moving date came and went, a month before the wedding and exciting for more than one reason. The fresh start had been a good idea, but Lena knew being away from Alex so often made Kara miss her sister more than anything, and it was a good reunion - a permanent one - as they touched down in Metropolis, ahead of the rest of their things, to Alex waiting for them.

     

                Unpacking was a busy few days, choosing a bigger bedroom for themselves, splitting the space in the walk-in closet, even though Lena argued she needed more space for her clothes. They hung paintings in the walls, arranged Lena’s record collection and found homes for their books in the extensive library system scattered throughout the many rooms of the house. Each of them claimed an office, Lena taking the one that had been her dad’s and then her mom’s, and chose which furniture to remove and which vases and lamps could stay.

     

                It would take months to completely redo everything to their liking, Kara urging them to keep the Victorian feeling of the place with its dark wood and classic features. Lena was reluctant to keep some of it though, wanting light and warmth and something out of this century, making the place feel less oppressive. Even she had to admit that it wasn’t that bad being back there though; in the end, it was just a house. 

     

                She was still adjusting to being back in Metropolis though, taking Kara to her favourite places in the city, finding a new Chinese restaurant and a new coffee shop, a twinge of sadness at losing their old haunts, even though the memories were safely inside her head and an abundance of photos. Everything almost seemed too calm , considering their wedding was a few weeks away, yet all Lena felt was peace.

     

                There was a strange sense of peace in Lena’s chest. It felt like she’d been waiting forever for this one day, and the little details faded into the background when she thought about it. Who cared if the flowers weren’t exactly how she’d envisioned, who cared if some people couldn’t make it or if it was raining. It all seemed like trifling concerns in the grand scheme of marrying Kara, and maybe she was just young and naïve, just shy of twenty-seven, but Lena imagined that this would be their fresh start.

     

                As the weeks dwindled down to a handful of days, and then to the night before, she felt even more sure. Lena had always had the knack for making the hard decisions with unnerving surety, never backing down from what she’d wanted, and she was filled with conviction as she sat outside with Kara on the back patio of the estate, staring at the white marquee that had been erected earlier that day, while they enjoyed a glass of wine each and watched the stars.

     

                “Are you excited?” Kara asked.

     

                “Of course! We’ve been waiting for so long, I’m still not sure it’s actually here. Are you excited?”

     

                “If I was anymore excited, I’d be bouncing off the walls,” Kara said with a chuckle, raising her glass to her lips and taking a slow sip before she gave Lena a searching look. “Are you … nervous?”

     

                Giving her a tender look of longing, Lena smiled slightly, reaching out to squeeze her knee. “And why would I be nervous?”

     

                Shrugging nonchalantly, Kara took another sip of wine and met her patient stare. Softly sighing, Kara rolled her eyes. “Well I am.”

     

                Soothingly rubbing her arm, Lena cocked her head to the side, a gentle smile on her face. “Why?”

     

                “Because I want tomorrow to be perfect. It’s like … everything’s been building up to tomorrow, so … of course.”

     

                Leaning forward, Lena cupped Kara’s chin in her hand, her expression softening with understanding, “hey, it will be perfect - I’m marrying you. If it rains, it rains. If the photographer forgets to show up and the cake turns out to be shit … well, I’ll laugh about it with my wife.”

     

                Shoulders dropping as Kara exhaled, she reached up and gripped Lena’s wrist, pulling her chin free from her grasp and then pressing a kiss to her knuckles before holding her hand in her lap.

     

                “You know … I-” she cut off, letting out a forceful breath before giving Lena an aching look, so tender and loving, unable to find the words. “Where’s all the time gone?” she ended up asking with a sigh.

     

                Humming in agreement, Lena picked up her glass and narrowed her eyes slightly as her lips twitched with a smile. “It feels like only yesterday that we met, with a whole lifetime in between. And I know that a lot of stuff has happened and things changed, but … the one thing that hasn’t is that I love you.”

     

                “I love you too. It just- it feels weird. We’re going to be married. Wives. Isn’t that just … unbelievable?”

     

                “You’re telling me,” Lena laughed. “When we met, I thought marriage and love and all that romance bullshit was … far from my life. And now, if I had to wait one more day to marry you, I think I’d explode from impatience.”

     

                Laughing, Kara shook her head, cheeks dimpling and eyes creasing. “God, what did I do to you, huh?”

     

                “All good things,” Lena said before climbing to her feet, the metal chair legs grating against the paving stones. She tossed back the rest of her wine and smiled down at Kara, her heart aching in her chest as she held out a hand. “Come on, we need an early night.”

     

                Kara reached for her hand and climbed to her feet and they disappeared inside. The house was unusually full, their family and friends filling the empty bedrooms in anticipation of tomorrow, those out of state flying in over the past week and bringing some much needed stress relief to the two women as they all cooked dinner together and drank outside, laughing and getting a headstart on the celebration of their nuptials. 

     

                They’d slipped outside for a little break together, enjoying their drink and a private moment together before the whirlwind of tomorrow. Everyone was still awake, a little too early for bedtime, but Lena slipped away upstairs when Kara went to join the sounds of laughter and shouts coming from the games room. Giving her a parting kiss, Lena went up to her office, switching on the light and settling behind her desk as she pulled out a piece of paper and a pen, hesitating as she searched for the words.

     

                Truthfully, there were no words to put onto paper that could perfectly encapsulate the complex thoughts and feelings she had about Kara. There was so much to say that she didn’t even know where to begin but she smiled as she hunched over and started writing in her cramped print.

     

    To my beautiful wife, Mrs Kara Danvers-Luthor,

     

    I know I could easily say all of this to you myself in the morning, seeing as we’re screwing tradition, but how could I not write you a letter for the happiest day of my life? It’s our own tradition and I couldn’t imagine starting married life with you without commemorating it with one more, even if I can’t find the words to say all of the things I feel about you. I know that if I tried to say all of this to you, I’d come up with even fewer words and probably a lot of tears. Our vows are going to be fun tomorrow - I’ll be lucky if I can get through them at all. You know, I used to be pretty unemotional until I met you, but that’s just another thing you’ve changed for me.

     

    I hope I’ve changed things for you too. Maybe not as drastically as you’ve altered things for me, but maybe I’ve made you feel less alone, more loved. That’s all I really want for you. My hope is that I’ll make you happy, and if I succeed at that, I’ll consider myself a good wife, but I hope you know I’d give you the world if you asked for it. I know it hasn’t been easy, and it probably won’t always be in the future either, but I can promise you that I’ll love you unconditionally. Every day, I’ll love you more than yesterday, and that’s enough for me. You are more than enough for me, and everything I never thought I’d have or deserve. Even now, after two and a half years, I look at you and see everything that’s good in this world, and I’m still not quite sure that you’re real. But I’ll try my best to be worthy of your love, to cherish you forever and make sure you’re always safe and happy. That’s a promise I fully intend to keep.

     

    I think tomorrow is as clear as I can make it, but I love you. I really do. More than I’ve ever loved anything or anyone else. It seems surreal to me that when you read this, in just a few short hours we’ll be married, after everything we’ve been through and the sheer luck of bumping into each other in a café. Out of all the café’s in National City, and all the cities in the state, states in the country and countries in the world, we ended up at the same one at the same time. I know I’ve talked so much shit about soulmates and fate and all that crap, and I don’t think I believe in it now, even, but you were right when you said I believed in science. There may not be some higher power working hard to throw us together, but the entire order of the universe has aligned itself over and over again to bring us right to this very moment. It wasn’t fate or destiny trying to make it happen - it’s just the way things were supposed to be. It was the order of the universe, and one way or another, we were always supposed to meet and find our way to tomorrow.

     

    I’ll be waiting for you at the altar, impatient, excited and maybe a little nervous, but more sure than I’ve ever been of anything else in my life. I can’t wait to see you in your dress; you’re always beautiful to me but I know you’ll look perfect. I’ll hardly sleep at all tonight, I think, but I’ll be thinking of you the whole time. You’ll hear my vows tomorrow, but I just want you to know that I see them not as promises but as a privilege: I get to laugh with you and cry with you, care for you, build with you and live with you. How lucky am I?

                Sealing the letter, Lena sat back in her seat with a look of amusement on her face - it felt strange to write Kara’s surname before her own, but after tomorrow, she’d sign that name on everything, irrefutable proof that she was married to the love of her life, that she’d been deserving of someone’s love. They’d decided to hyphenate after much deliberation, Lena gladly willing to take Danvers as her surname but Kara arguing that it would be a shame to give up the name she’d worked so hard to change the public opinion of through her work with L-Corp.                 Sealing the letter in the envelope, she smiled to herself, thinking about how three years ago she’d been in an entirely different place, how this life she’d cultivated for herself, through hardships and heartbreak and overwhelming love, was so far away from that lonely life she’d committed herself to that it hardly seemed real at all.                 Swallowing thickly, Lena ducked her head in agreement, reaching out to trace a finger over the stones. “It’s beautiful . Thank you.”

     

                Lillian’s lips twisted ruefully as she looked at Lena, a shadow of bewilderment in her eyes as she rested her cheek in her hand. “I never used to be sure if I’d ever get the chance to give it to you for your wedding. Surprisingly, I love it when you prove me wrong, and you’re so damn good at doing that.”

     

                Letting out a choked laugh, Lena gave her a wry smile in response, closing the box. “Well, I never used to be sure if I’d ever get married - and I didn’t think you’d be at my wedding if I did. So … I guess we were both wrong.”

     

                “I’m glad that we were.”

                “No, not at all. Coming from the woman who had her reservations at first, I’m … I’m happy for you. So, so happy for you both , and grateful to be here for it. It’s … all I want for you now, and I hope you’ll both be happy together. God knows you’ve been through enough.”

     

                “Thanks, mom.”

     

                Nodding, Lillian lingered for a minute, both of them silent and wrapped up in their thoughts, before she climbed to her feet and plucked the velvet box from the desk. “I should go and hunt down my daughter-in-law before you go to bed. Are you still insisting on breaking tradition?”

     

                Snorting, Lena climbed to her feet as well, picking up her letter. “Why would I want to spend half of my wedding day without her? It seems stupid. Besides, I think we already got all of our bad luck out of the way early on.”

                Smiling tiredly, Lena made a sound of assent at the back of her throat, kissing her mom on the cheek as they stepped out into the hallway, before she made her way upstairs to her room.                 Lena didn’t manage more than a little bit of fruit and a parfait, but Kara ate with enthusiasm, beaming and proud as the palpable excitement of the room shrouded them all.                 Perhaps a tiny bit nervous, or just impatient and waiting to pass the time, Lena indulged in a glass or two of the expensive champagne Lillian had kept in the wine cellar for this day, feeling a warm glow in her chest as she laughed along with Kelly and the makeup artist as her lips were touched up.     Chapter 79

                Walking through the front door to the disjointed sound of piano keys being played by clumsy hands, Lena let out a snort of laughter, dropping her keys onto a table just inside the door and carrying her armful of grocery bags through to one of the larger living rooms, where she knew the grand piano was situated. Stepping into the open doorway, she took in the sight of Lillian sitting on the bench with a dark haired girl on her lap, playing a clumsy scale.

     

                “Already trying to turn her into a child prodigy?”

                “Mom, she’s four . Why don’t you play with dolls with her?”

                Awkwardly picking up one of the paper bags while Lillian grabbed the rest for her, Lena led her daughter out of the room and through to the kitchen. “Mom’s gone to talk to her special friend about her week; she’ll be home soon.”

     

                “Can we play Lego when she gets home?”

                “Sure, I’ll get you some grapes.”

She flipped through the photos with nostalgic fondness, even though it wasn’t that long ago, really. She pointed out familiar faces to Daisy and then moved onto another one, the one where their daughter appeared for the first time, in Kara’s arms at the hospital, taken by a nurse.

     

    It was just past midnight when they’d been woken up by a phone call from the adoption agency that the anonymous woman they were adopting from had gone into labour at Metropolis General Hospital. The two of them had rushed there immediately, the car loaded with baby things and a car seat to bring their daughter home, both of them dressed in mismatched clothes in their haste, and they spilled into the hospital looking frazzled and excited.

     

    They were both more scared than they wanted to admit, pale beneath the harsh fluorescent lights, and even though they’d been going through the adoption process for a while now, preparing themselves for motherhood with parenting books and classes, as the reality set in, Lena couldn’t help but feel woefully unprepared. She didn’t know the first thing about raising a baby and she anxiously paced back and forth in the lobby as they waited out the long labour. A part of her was terrified to acknowledge it as their baby, thinking about how the woman might back out once she was born - it was known to happen - but they were so close to starting the little family they’d dreamed of, and Lena could see the nervous excitement in the lines of Kara’s face as she nervously fiddled with her fingers from the waiting room chair.

     

    Eliza had flown into town a week ago, anticipating the baby’s due date, but they didn’t call anyone to let them know she’d gone into labour, this stranger who held the fate of this baby in her hand’s. A representative from the adoption agency was there, walking them through the process, talking them through everything while they waited. It was to be a closed adoption, at the birth mother’s request, not even wanting to meet the married couple she would be giving the baby to, and it felt so strange to Lena that she felt so much gratitude for a woman she’d never even met but was giving her everything they’d ever wanted.

     

    They waited hours, well past dawn and into the following afternoon, ignoring phone calls from their family as they waited, worrying. In the end, it all went perfectly and a healthy baby girl had been born. Kara burst into tears jsut from the announcement and Lena was sure she looked ghostly, shaking with fear before they were told they could see her, that there was no backtracking on the adoption. They were taken through to see their new daughter then, and the moment Lena laid eyes on her, she’d started crying. She was theirs. Kara held her first, the nurse snapping a photo on the Polaroid camera of the three of them together, before Kara placed the tiny bundle in Lena’s arms. She’d never felt anything like it in her life - this tiny bundle was hers. Hers and Kara’s. She loved her instantly.

     

    “Daisy,” Kara whispered, stroking the baby’s pink cheek. Eyelids fluttered open revealing blue eyes, such a clear, sky blue that they were almost the same shade as Kara’s.

     

    “Daisy,” Lena agreed, looking up at Kara, who was smiling widely with tear-filled eyes. Leaning in, Kara kissed her before bending down and pressing a kiss on the baby’s forehead.

     

                There was a whole album dedicated to Daisy’s first year of life, dozens of photos of her as a newborn pasted in; sleeping on Lena’s chest, staring up at the Kara with wide blue eyes, being held by everyone for the first time, smiling and crawling and sitting upright, holding onto the stuffed teddy bear she carried everywhere. There were ones of her standing, dark curls and dimples and Lena’s anxious hands waiting to catch her. 

     

    “Quick! Get the camera!” Lena told Kara, who was scrambling up off the floor.

     

    “Don’t let her walk until I get it!” Kara yelled behind her as she ran out of the room.

     

    Lena laughed. “What am I supposed to do? Push her over if she starts to do it?”

     

    “Yes!” Kara laughed, her voice drifting in from far away.

     

    She was back a moment later, two cameras and her phone in hand. Turning the video on, Kara arranged her phone so that they could capture Daisy’s first steps on camera. Next she took a photo on her polaroid camera as Lena let go of the little girl, who teetered slightly as she smiled at Kara.

     

    “Come on baby girl, come to mommy!” Kara said encouragingly, opening her arms wide as she laughed. 

     

    Lena laughed with delight as she watched Daisy take a step forward, and then another before faltering and falling to her knees. She didn’t cry and Kara swept her up into her arms as they both clapped and cheered, Lena filled with pride as she watched on. Soon enough, the house was filled with the sounds of little feet running around the place, followed by the sounds of heavier footfalls chasing after them.

     

                Flipping through more pages, they came to Daisy’s first birthday party. A photo of Kelly wearing a party hat as she held Daisy in her lap made Lena smile. It was no surprise that she was good with kids, doting on her niece, along with Alex, until they’d recently adopted their own daughter, Esme.

     

                There one of Daisy sitting on Athena's back, her arms thrown around the dog's neck as she wandered around the house with the toddler on her back. They'd been a bit hesitant at having a baby around such a big dog, but they knew that Athena had a mild temperament and was very protective, so they weren't at all surprised when she took up a guard position outside the baby's nursery all night. When Daisy had started walking she'd had a permanent railing next to her to catch herself on if she started to fall, and soon enough she had figured out that if she climbed on Athena's back she could get free rides around the house.

     

                A photo of Kara in the sea outside Eliza's back garden, throwing Daisy up in the air, made Lena smile. It was the first time she'd been in the ocean, and she'd loved it. Since then, they'd taken her to Eliza's almost every weekend during the summertime so she could splash around in the water and see her grandma.

     

    "Higher mommy!" the little girl squealed with laughter as Kara threw her up again, catching her as gravity brought her back down.

     

    "Not too high," Lena called from her seat on the back porch.

     

    Eliza laughed, stroking Lena's hair as she sat down next to her, handing Lena a glass of lemonade. "Look at you being all sensible. I would've thought you'd be the one daring to throw her as high as you could."

     

    "I guess marriage and motherhood has tamed me," Lena joked, rolling her eyes and giving Eliza a look of amusement. "I don't have time for arrests and nights in jail anymore."

     

    "I, for one, am relieved to hear it," Eliza laughed.

     

    "Daisy Danvers-Luthor! Did you just splash me?" Kara gasped, and there was a peal of laughter as the little girl splashed around in the water, trying to swim away with the aid of her armbands. 

     

    "No!"

     

    "I'm going to get you!"

     

    "Mommy! Help!" Daisy called out to Lena, a scream dissolving into laughter as she tried to get away from Kara.

     

    Lena set her glass down and took off her sunglasses. "Looks like it's mom to the rescue," Lena said to Eliza, before standing up and crossing the sand dunes, stepping onto the beach to splash into the shallow, cold water, still somewhere uneasy around open water but willing to brave it for her daughter.

     

                There was a photo of the night they’d decided to have another baby, Kara smiling widely out of the picture that Lena had taken as they'd toasted with a glass of water. She had asked Kara to carry the baby, because she didn’t think she’d want to. She’d never imagined that she would ever have kids, until she met Kara, but even now, Lena was hesitant to be the one to carry their baby. Of course Kara would want to anyway, because she was so maternal and Lena knew that she would love it – even the bad parts like morning sickness and an aching back.

     

    “Why can’t we just use a sperm donor though?” Lena argued, and Kara let out a heavy sigh as she gave Lena an exasperated look.

     

    “It’s fine , Lena, it’ll work! Men are basically useless now. Just picture it, a baby that’s half me and half you. Science has come so far, we don’t need a donor, we just need my egg and your DNA.”

     

    “But how safe is it, Kara? This is our baby we’re talking about. It’s still a pretty new procedure, I don’t want to risk anything going wrong. I mean … you could get ill too.”

     

    Kara let out a quick laugh, her eyes briefly crinkling at the corners as she walked over to Lena and cupped her face in her hands. “If I wasn’t convinced it was safe, I would never go through with it.”

     

    “Fine, we’ll make an appointment with the doctor,” Lena sighed. “But we’re making sure it's all completely safe before we agree on anything.”

     

    “Deal,” Kara smiled, leaning down to press a kiss on her lips.

     

                Then there was a photo of Kara and Lena, holding up an ultrasound scan, which was little more than a swirl, as they smiled widely, and Lena thought back to the day, not too long ago, when they’d found out that Kara’s idea had paid off, and they were having another baby.

     

    “Hi, baby, I don’t want to alarm you - everything’s fine, I promise-”

     

    “What’s wrong?” Lena urgently asked, dropping her pen to her desk.

     

    “Nothing. I just- I passed out for a second. I’m fine.”

     

    “Let me call my mom. Maybe she can do a quick checkup. You didn’t … bump your head? You’re okay?”

     

    “Don’t call your mom,” Kara quickly commanded before her voice softened. “Can you just … come home. Please.”

     

    “I- of course . Of course I can; I’ll be there soon.”

     

    She’d hung up and told Jess to cancel the rest of her appointments for that day, riding the elevator down to the underground parking garage and potentially earning herself a ticket as she rushed home. Walking through the front door, her face a mask of concern as her heels clicked on the tiles, she called out.

     

    “Kara?”

     

    “I’m just in the kitchen.”

     

    Briskly walking through, Lena rushed towards her at the sight of her standing at the kitchen counter, Daisy scribbling in a colouring book, oblivious to her mom’s concern as she looked up and smiled. Lena softened minutely, murmuring a greeting to her daughter and kissing her, before she anxiously crossed over to Kara.

     

    “Hey,” she murmured, her voice achingly gentle as she gave Kara a searching look, taking in her flushed cheeks and bright eyes. “What happened? Are you okay?”

     

    Letting out a strangled laugh, Kara cupped Lena’s cheek in her hand and smiled, barely able to contain her excitement as she held something out to her. Glancing down, Lena took in the stick and blanched.

     

    “We’re having a baby.”

     

    “We- oh ,” Lena stammered, speechless as her eyes widened.

     

    Her eyes prickled with tears as she let out an elated laugh, pressing a hand to her forehead as relief swept through her. “Oh my God.”

     

    Reaching down, she cupped Kara’s flat stomach over the top of her shirt and let out another laugh, shaking her head as she looked up at Kara with so much joy on her face that she felt like her heart would beat out of her chest.

     

                That was where the photos ended in the most recent album, with Kara holding the stick up as she beamed and pressed a hand to her stomach, taken by a rather dazed Lena only a month ago. They hadn’t told anyone yet, too early to be sure that it would all work out, but she was nearly out of her first trimester and they both knew they wouldn’t be able to contain their excitement over the news for much longer.

     

                It made Lena nostalgic, going through all the photos, because so much had changed over such a short period of time. It felt like it had been forever, so many memories formed together, but their photo albums together spanned less than eight years. Each moment had been filled with happiness though, and Lena’s eyes prickled with tears as she thought about how much Kara had changed her life. 

     

                There wasn’t a day that went by that Lena didn’t think about how grateful she was for that blessed day in that café. She would’ve missed so much if she’d stayed in her office instead, taken lunch at her desk and made all of her meetings, but instead, she had more than she’d ever imagined she’d have.

     

                They were flipping through the last photo album when Kara appeared in the doorway, taking the sight of her wife and daughter on the floor, surrounded by black photo albums, the last page open to the black and white swirl of a sonogram for their first scan. At the flicker of movement, Lena and Daisy looked up, and the little girl jumped up off the floor and ran over to her.

     

                “Mommy! You’re home!”

     

                Lena climbed to her feet as well, albeit at a slower pace, and walked over to Kara with a smile. She leaned down to pick Daisy up, bringing her close to Kara so that she could kiss her, and then leaned in to kiss Kara herself, lingering and full of love. Pulling back, Kara ran her hair through the little girl’s curls, her blue eyes crinkling at the corners as she stared at Lena.

     

                “I’m home.”
